full_output.methodology: Heterologous expression, gene knockout, and functional assays were used to validate the zwittermicin A biosynthetic gene cluster and characterize the zmaWXY resistance mechanism.

full_output.paper_title: Distant and new mutations in CTX-M-1 beta-lactamase affect cefotaxime hydrolysis.
The gut as reservoir of antibiotic resistance: microbial diversity of tetracycline resistance in mother and infant.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various tetracycline resistance genes, including tet(M), tet(L), erm(T), tet(W), tet(O), and tet(X), in the gut microbiota of a mother and her infant. It also discovered a novel composite transposon, Tn 6079, carrying tet(M), tet(L), and erm(T) in the infant's gut, highlighting the potential for horizontal gene transfer and maternal transmission of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic fosmid library screening, PCR, and sequencing were used to identify and characterize tetracycline resistance genes in the gut microbiota of a mother and her infant.

full_output.paper_title: Fijimycins A-C, three antibacterial etamycin-class depsipeptides from a marine-derived Streptomyces sp.
full_output.key_findings: The paper describes the isolation and structural elucidation of three new depsipeptides, fijimycins A-C, from a marine-derived Streptomyces sp. These compounds exhibit significant in vitro antibacterial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were isolated using chromatographic techniques and characterized using NMR, MS, and IR spectroscopy. Their antibacterial activities were evaluated against MRSA strains.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro antibacterial activity of NB-003 against Propionibacterium acnes.
full_output.key_findings: NB-003 was found to be bactericidal against all Propionibacterium acnes isolates, including those resistant to erythromycin, clindamycin, and/or tetracycline. The study also showed that NB-003 had no cross-resistance with known antiacne agents and exhibited synergistic effects with benzoyl peroxide.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the in vitro antibacterial activity of NB-003 against P. acnes isolates using broth microdilution methods and assessed synergy with other antiacne agents.

full_output.paper_title: Lipooligosaccharide Structure is an Important Determinant in the Resistance of Neisseria Gonorrhoeae to Antimicrobial Agents of Innate Host Defense.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies lgtD as a gene involved in lipooligosaccharide (LOS) structure, which affects resistance to normal human serum (NHS) in Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Mutations in lgtD lead to altered LOS structures and decreased NHS resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, complementation analysis, and chemical analysis of lipooligosaccharides.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, Samoa, 2007-2008.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified five MRSA genotypes in Samoa, including USA300, the Queensland clone, a sequence type 1 MRSA strain, the Southwest Pacific MRSA clone, and AK3. Resistance profiles varied among the strains, with some showing resistance to ciprofloxacin and erythromycin, while others were resistant only to β-lactams.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting S. aureus isolates from skin and soft tissue infections, performing antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and characterizing MRSA strains through molecular techniques such as multilocus sequence typing, spa typing, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cefepime-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa as a significant cause of infection with increased mortality, particularly in patients with bloodstream infections. It highlights risk factors including prior use of extended-spectrum cephalosporins, penicillins, quinolones, and transfers from outside facilities.
full_output.methodology: Case-control and retrospective cohort studies analyzing risk factors for cefepime-resistant P. aeruginosa infections and their association with mortality.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Harboring OXA-24 carbapenemase, Spain.

blaOXA-24.evidence_note: The paper states that the blaOXA-24 gene was isolated from the clone causing the outbreak (AbH12O-A2) and that carbapenem resistance in all clones was linked to a plasmid harboring the blaOXA-24 gene.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the OXA-24 carbapenemase gene in a multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii strain, highlighting its role in carbapenem resistance and its association with a hospital outbreak.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective longitudinal study, plasmid analysis, and real-time PCR for gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Macrolide resistance in Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Israel, 2010.

23S rRNA.notes: Mutation in 23S rRNA gene associated with macrolide resistance
23S rRNA.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the A2063G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene is associated with macrolide resistance in Mycoplasma pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Ciprofloxacin-resistant Salmonella enterica Serotype Typhi, United States, 1999-2008.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ciprofloxacin-resistant Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi isolates in the United States, with resistance linked to specific mutations in the gyrA and parC genes.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of the quinolone resistance-determining region (QRDR) and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Invasive Streptococcus pneumoniae in children, Malawi, 2004-2006.
full_output.key_findings: The study found chloramphenicol resistance in 27% of Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates and penicillin nonsusceptibility in 10% of isolates, with all being ceftriaxone susceptible.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 176 invasive S. pneumoniae isolates through serotyping and MIC determination using Etest.

full_output.paper_title: S-bacillithiolation protects against hypochlorite stress in Bacillus subtilis as revealed by transcriptomics and redox proteomics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ohrA and bshA as critical genes involved in protecting Bacillus subtilis against hypochlorite stress through S-bacillithiolation mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomics, redox proteomics, and mutational analysis were used to investigate the response of Bacillus subtilis to hypochlorite stress.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M, bla SHV, and bla TEM genes as the primary mechanisms of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) production in Enterobacteriaceae, with CTX-M being the most prevalent. These genes conferred resistance to several cephalosporins and aztreonam.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing of ESBL genes, along with susceptibility testing using the agar dilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-activity relationships of antitubercular nitroimidazoles. 3. Exploration of the linker and lipophilic tail of ((s)-2-nitro-6,7-dihydro-5H-imidazo[2,1-b][1,3]oxazin-6-yl)-(4-trifluoromethoxybenzyl)amine (6-amino PA-824).
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the structure-activity relationships of antitubercular nitroimidazoles, focusing on the linker and lipophilic tail of 6-amino PA-824. Modifications at various positions of the molecule were synthesized and tested for their activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis, revealing insights into the conformational preferences and substrate efficiency of the compounds.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of derivatives, MIC and enzyme kinetic assays, and computational analysis of conformational preferences.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus hominis (MRSHo): low clonality and reservoirs of SCCmec structural elements.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various SCCmec structures in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus hominis, including novel combinations of mec and ccr complexes, highlighting the genetic diversity and potential for horizontal gene transfer.
full_output.methodology: PFGE, PCR, Southern hybridization, and sequencing were used to analyze the genetic diversity and SCCmec structures in S. hominis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Role of P27 -P55 operon from Mycobacterium tuberculosis in the resistance to toxic compounds.

p55.role_in_paper: The P27-P55 operon is crucial for the survival of Mycobacterium tuberculosis during infection in mice. P55 encodes an efflux pump that has been shown to provide Mycobacterium smegmatis and Mycobacterium bovis BCG with resistance to several drugs.
p55.validation_method: Mutant strain decolorized malachite green faster than the wild type strain and was hypersensitive to both malachite green and ethidium bromide, and more susceptible to the first-line antituberculosis drugs: isoniazid and ethambutol. The pump inhibitor reserpine reversed M. tuberculosis resistance to ethidium bromide.
p55.evidence_note: The mutant strain decolorized malachite green faster than the wild type strain and was hypersensitive to both malachite green and ethidium bromide, and more susceptible to the first-line antituberculosis drugs: isoniazid and ethambutol.

full_output.key_findings: The P27-P55 operon in Mycobacterium tuberculosis contributes to resistance against toxic compounds and maintains cell wall integrity. Both P27 and P55 are essential for resistance to malachite green, SDS, and ethidium bromide, with P55 playing a key role in efflux pump activity.
full_output.methodology: Gene disruption, complementation, and susceptibility testing were used to evaluate the role of P27 and P55 in resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase genes of Escherichia coli in chicken meat and humans, The Netherlands.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-1, bla TEM-52, and bla SHV-12 as the primary extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) genes in Escherichia coli from chicken meat and humans in the Netherlands. These genes were found to be highly prevalent in chicken meat and were also commonly detected in human rectal swabs and blood cultures.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping, sequencing, and molecular analysis were used to identify and characterize ESBL genes in bacterial isolates from chicken meat, human rectal swabs, and blood cultures.
full_output.sample_size: 262 meat samples, 927 rectal swab specimens, 31 blood cultures

full_output.paper_title: An acpXL Mutant of Rhizobium leguminosarum bv. phaseoli Lacks 27-Hydroxyoctacosanoic Acid in Its Lipid A and Is Developmentally Delayed during Symbiotic Infection of the Determinate Nodulating Host Plant Phaseolus vulgaris
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes an acpXL mutant of Rhizobium leguminosarum bv. phaseoli that lacks the VLCFA 27-hydroxyoctacosanoic acid in its lipid A, leading to membrane instability and developmental delays during symbiotic infection of Phaseolus vulgaris.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, lipid A structural analysis, and transmission electron microscopy were used to evaluate the effects of the acpXL mutation.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular basis of sulfonamide and trimethoprim resistance in fish-pathogenic Aeromonas isolates.

dfrA28.validation_method: experimental validation through cloning and susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the novel trimethoprim resistance gene dfrA28 and the sulfonamide resistance gene sul1 in fish-pathogenic Aeromonas isolates, highlighting the role of class 1 integrons in the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, cloning, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Multiple targets of nitric oxide in the tricarboxylic acid cycle of Salmonella enterica serovar typhimurium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies lipoamide dehydrogenase (LpdA) as a key target of nitric oxide (NO·) in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, leading to impaired succinyl-CoA production and methionine/lysine auxotrophy under nitrosative stress.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial growth experiments, amino acid supplementation, enzyme activity assays, and microarray analysis to investigate the effects of NO· on Salmonella metabolism.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations of the Listeria monocytogenes peptidoglycan N-deacetylase and O-acetylase result in enhanced lysozyme sensitivity, bacteriolysis, and hyperinduction of innate immune pathways.
full_output.key_findings: Mutations in the Listeria monocytogenes peptidoglycan N-deacetylase (pgd) and O-acetylase (oat) result in enhanced lysozyme sensitivity, bacteriolysis, and hyperinduction of innate immune pathways.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation and characterization of L. monocytogenes mutants, along with in vitro and in vivo infection assays.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of OXA-181, a carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D beta-lactamase from Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes OXA-181, a carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D beta-lactamase from Klebsiella pneumoniae KP3, which differs from OXA-48 by four amino acid substitutions and is located on a 7.6-kb ColE-type plasmid.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, cloning, expression in E. coli, and MIC testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel streptogramin A, pleuromutilin, and lincosamide resistance gene, vga(E), in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus ST398.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SabR as a regulatory gene that enhances nikkomycin production in Streptomyces ansochromogenes by interacting with the promoter region of sanG. Disruption of sabR reduces nikkomycin production, while overexpression increases it. The study also identifies a specific DNA sequence, SARE, which is bound by SabR and plays a crucial role in this regulatory mechanism.
full_output.methodology: The study uses molecular biology techniques including S1 nuclease mapping, EMSA, DNase 1 footprinting, real-time PCR, and gene disruption to investigate the role of SabR in nikkomycin biosynthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Ceftaroline: A New Cephalosporin with Activity against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.key_findings: Ceftaroline is a novel fifth-generation cephalosporin with broad-spectrum activity against Gram-positive bacteria, including MRSA, VISA, hVISA, VRSA, and daptomycin- and linezolid-resistant strains. It shows superior efficacy against MRSA compared to other antibiotics and has a low propensity for resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The paper discusses the mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, and clinical efficacy of ceftaroline against various bacterial strains, including MRSA and other resistant organisms.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro selection of variants resistant to beta-lactams plus beta-lactamase inhibitors in CTX-M beta-lactamases: predicting the in vivo scenario?
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three types of inhibitor-resistant (IR) CTX-M mutants with mutations S130G, K234R, and S237G, which confer resistance to beta-lactams plus beta-lactamase inhibitors (BBLIs). The S130G mutation was the most frequent and provided the highest resistance levels to BBLIs, while the K234R and S237G mutations had a smaller effect. The study also shows that the S130G mutation can lead to a decrease in resistance to cephalosporins, demonstrating an antagonistic pleiotropy effect.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro evolution experiments with E. coli strains carrying various bla CTX-M genes, followed by serial passages in increasing concentrations of amoxicillin-clavulanate (AMC) and analysis of mutations through MIC determination and sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Acquired antibiotic resistance: are we born with it?
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of tetracycline resistance gene tet (M), erythromycin resistance gene ermB, sulfonamide resistance gene sul2, and beta-lactam resistance gene bla TEM in the gut microbiota of infants, indicating that antibiotic resistance genes are present in the human gut microbiota from an early age.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, real-time PCR, and DGGE analysis to identify and quantify antibiotic resistance genes in infant fecal samples.

full_output.paper_title: Persistence of antibiotic resistance: evaluation of a probiotic approach using antibiotic-sensitive Megasphaera elsdenii strains to prevent colonization of swine by antibiotic-resistant strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance genes tet(O) and tet(W) in Megasphaera elsdenii strains, which were experimentally validated to confer tetracycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used clone and MIC testing to validate the function of tetracycline resistance genes in Megasphaera elsdenii.

full_output.paper_title: Changing Italian nosocomial-community trends and heteroresistance in Staphylococcus aureus from bacteremia and endocarditis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the prevalence of heteroresistant vancomycin-intermediate Staphylococcus aureus (hVISA) in both methicillin-sensitive (MSSA) and methicillin-resistant (MRSA) strains, highlighting the challenges in detecting and managing these resistant strains in clinical settings.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 128 S. aureus isolates from bloodstream infections and endocarditis using molecular typing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and detection of hVISA through the Macro-Etest and PAP/AUC methods.

full_output.paper_title: Complete genome and comparative analysis of Streptococcus gallolyticus subsp. gallolyticus, an emerging pathogen of infective endocarditis.

tet(O/W/32/O).evidence_note: The paper mentions the presence of the mosaic tetracycline resistance gene tet(O/W/32/O) on the plasmid pSGG1, which is associated with tetracycline resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance genes tetL and tet(O/W/32/O) in the plasmid pSGG1 of Streptococcus gallolyticus subsp. gallolyticus strain BAA-2069, highlighting the role of plasmids in lateral gene transfer and tetracycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR, and tetracycline susceptibility testing were used to identify and validate tetracycline resistance genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies d-boroAla as a novel antibacterial agent targeting d-Ala-d-Ala ligase (DDL), showing broad-spectrum activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. It demonstrates that d-boroAla inhibits DDL, leading to bactericidal effects at specific concentrations.
full_output.methodology: The study determined MICs, MBCs, and evaluated the biochemical mechanism of d-boroAla through intracellular metabolite analysis and enzyme inhibition assays.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of aac(6')-Ib-cr plasmid-mediated and chromosome-encoded fluoroquinolone resistance in Enterobacteriaceae in Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the aac(6')-Ib-cr gene as a plasmid-mediated fluoroquinolone resistance determinant in Enterobacteriaceae, primarily in E. coli, and highlights its role in increasing the risk of high-level resistance through chromosomal mutations.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and MIC testing were used to characterize the aac(6')-Ib-cr gene and its impact on fluoroquinolone resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Pervasive sign epistasis between conjugative plasmids and drug-resistance chromosomal mutations.

mutations_found.protein_change: Aspartic acid to Glycine at position 87

gyrA.notes: Exhibits sign epistasis with plasmid R831

rpoB.notes: Exhibits sign epistasis with plasmid R702

mutations_found.protein_change: Lysine to Glutamic acid at position 88

rpsL.notes: Exhibits sign epistasis with plasmid RP4

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various chromosomal mutations in gyrA, rpoB, and rpsL that confer resistance to nalidixic acid, rifampicin, and streptomycin, respectively. These mutations interact with conjugative plasmids in a manner that can lead to sign epistasis, where the presence of both a mutation and a plasmid increases the fitness of the bacterial strain compared to having either the mutation or the plasmid alone.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized competition assays to measure the fitness cost of resistance determinants and analyzed epistatic interactions between chromosomal mutations and conjugative plasmids.
full_output.sample_size: 50 combinations of chromosomal mutations and conjugative plasmids

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-resistance in Staphylococcus aureus is not affected by the overexpression in trans of the mecA gene repressor: a surprising observation.

mutations_found.origin: SCC mec type II strain BK2464

mecI.notes: mutation in mecI leads to truncated repressor protein
mecI.evidence_note: The paper describes mutations in mecI that lead to non-functional truncated MecI protein and reduced mecA repression, and confirms these findings through DNA sequencing and northern blotting.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that overexpression of mecI does not significantly alter oxacillin resistance levels in most MRSA strains, indicating that other factors may influence mecA regulation and β-lactam resistance.
full_output.methodology: Northern blotting, plasmid transformation, DNA sequencing, and electrophoretic mobility shift assay.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple MRSA strains including SCC mec types I-VIII.

full_output.paper_title: Membrane integration of poliovirus 2B viroporin.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that poliovirus 2B viroporin is an integral membrane protein that integrates into the ER membrane via the translocon, with a specific topology involving two hydrophobic regions (HR1 and HR2) forming a helical hairpin structure.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized in vitro translation, membrane sedimentation, alkaline wash, urea treatments, and Triton X-114 partitioning to analyze the membrane integration and topology of the 2B viroporin.

full_output.paper_title: Microarray-based analysis of IncA/C plasmid-associated genes from multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes associated with IncA/C plasmids in multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica, including blaCMY-2, aadA, merA, merP, and aphA, which confer resistance to beta-lactams, streptomycin, mercury, and kanamycin, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Microarray-based analysis of plasmid-associated genes in 59 Salmonella enterica isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Citrobacter spp. as a source of qnrB Alleles.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies seven novel qnrB alleles (qnrB32 to qnrB38) in Citrobacter spp., demonstrating their role in fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to characterize qnrB alleles in Citrobacter isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Gonorrhea infection in women: prevalence, effects, screening, and management.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the challenges of treating gonorrhea due to the development of antimicrobial resistance, highlighting the emergence of resistance to various antibiotics including cephalosporins, tetracyclines, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and data on gonorrhea prevalence, treatment options, and resistance patterns.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that 5% of new tuberculosis cases and 24% of previously treated patients in Sudan had multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB). The CAS1_Delhi spoligotype was the most prevalent genotype.
full_output.methodology: Drug susceptibility testing was performed using the proportion method on Lowenstein-Jensen media, and spoligotyping was used for genotyping.

full_output.paper_title: Engineering microbes to sense and eradicate Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a human pathogen.

pyocin S5.validation_method: expression in E. coli and demonstration of killing activity against P. aeruginosa

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of a synthetic genetic system in E. coli that detects and kills Pseudomonas aeruginosa using pyocin S5 and the E7 lysis protein. The system was characterized and shown to effectively inhibit P. aeruginosa growth and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Genetic circuit design, plasmid construction, and functional characterization of the sensing, killing, and lysing devices in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Cross-reactivity of anthrax and C2 toxin: protective antigen promotes the uptake of botulinum C2I toxin into human endothelial cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that protective antigen (PA) from anthrax toxin can bind and translocate the enzymatic component C2I of botulinum C2 toxin into human endothelial cells, highlighting the cross-reactivity between these two binary toxins.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized lipid bilayer experiments, cell culture, and biochemical assays to investigate the interaction between anthrax toxin components and C2 toxin.

full_output.paper_title: RNAi screen reveals host cell kinases specifically involved in Listeria monocytogenes spread from cell to cell.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CSNK1A1 and CSNK2B as specifically involved in Listeria monocytogenes spread from cell to cell, with CSNK1A1 being required in sending cells for protrusion resolution into double-membrane vacuoles.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput fluorescence microscopy, computer-assisted image analysis, and siRNA kinome screen.

full_output.paper_title: Extended antimicrobial treatment of bacterial vaginosis combined with human lactobacilli to find the best treatment and minimize the risk of relapses.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the characterization of vaginal lactobacilli strains and their potential role in treating bacterial vaginosis, highlighting the importance of specific Lactobacillus strains in reducing relapse rates.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the characterization of lactobacilli through molecular typing techniques, including REP-PCR and RAPD-PCR, along with assessing their antimicrobial properties and safety profiles.

full_output.paper_title: The Bacillus subtilis GntR family repressor YtrA responds to cell wall antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies YtrA as a repressor of the ytrA and ywoB operons in response to cell wall antibiotics, highlighting its role in regulating stress responses to antibiotics that target the transglycosylation step of cell wall synthesis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized transcriptome analysis, promoter fusion assays, EMSA, and DNase I footprinting to investigate the regulatory mechanisms of YtrA in response to cell wall antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: The Bacillus subtilis extracytoplasmic function σ factor σ(V) is induced by lysozyme and provides resistance to lysozyme.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies oatA as a gene that confers resistance to lysozyme in Bacillus subtilis, and shows that its expression is induced by lysozyme stress through the σV factor.
full_output.methodology: The study used mutant analysis, complementation, and qRT-PCR to investigate the role of σV and oatA in lysozyme resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Successful control of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in endemic neonatal intensive care units--a 7-year campaign.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that implementing infection control measures, including surveillance culture and decolonization with mupirocin, significantly reduced MRSA healthcare-associated infections in neonatal intensive care units.
full_output.methodology: Infection control measures, surveillance culture, and decolonization with mupirocin were implemented to control MRSA spread.

full_output.paper_title: Dramatic transcriptional changes in an intracellular parasite enable host switching between plant and insect.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes involved in host switching of phytoplasmas, including mscL, which is upregulated in the plant host and potentially involved in osmotic stress adaptation, and PAM486, a secreted protein upregulated in the plant host.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis and qRT-PCR were used to analyze gene expression in phytoplasmas during host switching between plant and insect hosts.
full_output.sample_size: Six independent OY-M-infected plants and OY-M-infected insects

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the discovery of N-alkyl-N-(pyridin-2-yl)hydroxylamine scaffolds as selective antibacterial agents with potent activity against Micrococcus luteus and moderate activity against antibiotic-resistant strains of Staphylococcus aureus and Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.methodology: The research involved the synthesis of a diverse library of compounds using nitroso Diels-Alder and ene chemistry, followed by evaluation of their antibacterial activity through agar diffusion and broth microdilution assays.

full_output.paper_title: The Class D beta-lactamase family: residues governing the maintenance and diversity of function.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies conserved residues and motifs in Class D beta-lactamases, highlighting their role in maintaining and diversifying function, particularly focusing on the catalytic residues and potential disulfide bonds contributing to enzyme stability and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Sequence-based bioinformatics, molecular modeling, and phylogenetic analysis were used to investigate the structure-function relationships of Class D beta-lactamases.

full_output.paper_title: ArmA Methyltransferase in a Monophasic Salmonella enterica Isolate from Food.

armA.mechanism: confers resistance to aminoglycosides by methylating the 16S rRNA

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the ArmA methyltransferase in a multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica isolate from food, highlighting its role in high-level resistance to aminoglycosides and other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Molecular analysis, conjugation experiments, PCR, and S1 pulsed-field gel electrophoresis were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Development of TaqMan real-time polymerase chain reaction for the detection of the newly emerging form of carbapenem resistance gene in clinical isolates of Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Acinetobacter baumannii.

blaNDM-1.validation_method: real-time PCR assay with TaqMan probes

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a TaqMan real-time PCR assay for detecting the blaNDM-1 gene, which confers resistance to carbapenems in clinical isolates of E. coli, K. pneumoniae, and A. baumannii.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR assay using TaqMan probes for detection of blaNDM-1 gene.
full_output.sample_size: clinical isolates of E. coli (11 strains), K. pneumoniae (17 strains), and A. baumannii (6 strains)

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of CTX-Mβ-lactamases among Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from patients at Tehran hospitals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaCTX-M genes in 71.5% of ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae isolates, with CTX-M-I and CTX-M-III being the most prevalent clusters. The blaCTX-M genes were widespread among Iranian isolates of K. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: PCR and DNA sequencing were used to detect blaCTX-M genes, and PFGE was used for molecular typing of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: OXA beta-lactamase-mediated carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-23-like and blaOXA-51-like genes as the most common OXA carbapenamases, and blaVIM as the most common metallo-beta-lactamase contributing to carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.methodology: PCR, gene sequencing, and phenotypic tests including modified Hodge test and inhibitor potentiated disk diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Metallo beta lactamase producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies metallo-beta-lactamases, particularly Zn-dependent class B enzymes, in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting their resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic tests involving EDTA and zinc were used to detect metallo-beta-lactamase production.

full_output.paper_title: CTX-M-9 group extended-spectrum β-lactamases in neonatal stool isolates: emergence in India.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first identification of CTX-M-14-like and CTX-M-27-like extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs) belonging to the CTX-M-9 group in Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli isolated from neonatal stool in India. The blaCTX-M-9 group was found to be transferable via plasmids, and blaCTX-M-15 was identified as the predominant ESBL gene among the isolates.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization and plasmid transfer experiments were conducted to identify and validate the presence of ESBLs in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Human defensin 5 disulfide array mutants: disulfide bond deletion attenuates antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus.

HD5.notes: Deletion of disulfide bonds leads to reduced antibacterial activity against S. aureus.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the wild-type disulfide array of human defensin 5 is essential for its antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, while its activity against E. coli is less affected by disulfide bond deletions.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the generation of HD5 mutants through site-directed mutagenesis, overexpression in E. coli, purification, and evaluation of their antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus using colony counting and turbidity assays.

full_output.paper_title: New target for inhibition of bacterial RNA polymerase: 'switch region'.

rpoB.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

rpoC.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The paper identifies the 'switch region' of bacterial RNA polymerase as a new target for antibacterial drugs. It describes four natural products, myxopyronin, corallopyronin, ripostatin, and lipiarmycin, that inhibit bacterial RNA polymerase by targeting the switch region. The study also characterizes mutations in the rpoB and rpoC genes that confer resistance to myxopyronin.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and sequencing of myxopyronin-resistant mutants, crystallographic analysis of the RNAP-myxopyronin complex, and biochemical experiments to determine the mechanism of action.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative characterization of fungal anthracenone and naphthacenedione biosynthetic pathways reveals an α-hydroxylation-dependent Claisen-like cyclization catalyzed by a dimanganese thioesterase.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the ada gene cluster in Aspergillus niger ATCC 1015, which is responsible for the biosynthesis of the naphthacenedione compound 1. The cluster includes genes encoding a non-reducing polyketide synthase (adaA), a metallo-beta-lactamase-type thioesterase (adaB), a FAD-dependent monooxygenase (adaC), and an O-methyltransferase (adaD).
full_output.methodology: Genome mining, gene cloning, heterologous expression in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and in vitro biochemical assays were used to characterize the ada gene cluster and its role in the biosynthesis of 1.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of quinolone resistance among extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae in the Central African Republic: genetic characterization.

qnrA1.evidence_note: All CTX-M-producing strains were resistant to the tested quinolones. Two Escherichia coli strains with the highest MICs were shown to harbour an IS CR1-qnrA1 sequence.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies qnrA1 as a plasmid-borne quinolone resistance gene and a common gyrA mutation (Ser83Leu) as mechanisms of quinolone resistance in ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae in the Central African Republic.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to identify quinolone resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial and toxicological activities of five medicinal plant species from Cameroon traditional medicine.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of methanolic, ethylacetate, and hexanic extracts of five Cameroonian medicinal plants against various pathogenic microorganisms. The methanolic and ethylacetate extracts of Phyllanthus muellerianus and Piptadeniastum africana showed the highest antimicrobial activity. The in vivo acute toxicity study indicated that these plants were not toxic at the tested doses.
full_output.methodology: The antimicrobial activity was assessed using agar well-diffusion and broth microdilution methods. Acute toxicity was evaluated in albino rats.

full_output.paper_title: Expression during Host Infection and Localization of Yersinia pestis Autotransporter Proteins.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes 12 putative autotransporter proteins in Yersinia pestis CO92, demonstrating their surface localization and secretion capabilities in both E. coli and Y. pestis. Some of these proteins are processed by bacterial surface omptins and released into the supernatant.
full_output.methodology: The study uses in silico analysis, plasmid construction, Western blotting, immunofluorescence microscopy, and qRT-PCR to analyze the localization, expression, and secretion of Yersinia pestis autotransporter proteins.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic evaluation of fluoroquinolone resistance in clinical isolates of Staphylococcus aureus in Tehran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple mutations in the QRDRs region of both grlA and gyrA genes in fluoroquinolone-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates from Tehran.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing of grlA and gyrA genes, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Flo11p, drug efflux pumps, and the extracellular matrix cooperate to form biofilm yeast colonies.

PDR5.validation_method: disruption of the PDR1 gene and deletion of PDR5 and SNQ2 genes

SNQ2.validation_method: deletion of PDR5 and SNQ2 genes

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PDR5 and SNQ2 as essential multidrug resistance transporters in Saccharomyces cerevisiae biofilm colonies, highlighting their role in removing toxic compounds from surface cells.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation and fluorescence microscopy were used to investigate the roles of PDR5 and SNQ2 in biofilm colony defense.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that primary resistance to ceftazidime (CAZ) or amoxicillin-clavulanic acid (AMC) in Burkholderia pseudomallei is rare, supporting their continued use as empirical therapy for melioidosis in Thailand.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial resistance in B. pseudomallei isolates using disk diffusion and Etest methods.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baylyi strain coharboring blaSIM-1 and blaOXA-23 from China.

blaSIM-1.source: Clinical Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baylyi Strain Coharboring blaSIM-1 and blaOXA-23 from China
blaSIM-1.evidence_note: The paper states that blaSIM-1 was detected in the clinical carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baylyi strain NB09A30 and that it was located on a large plasmid.

blaOXA-23.genetic_context: bla OXA-23 was part of transposon Tn 2008 ( 1 ), which was inserted into a noncoding region and flanked by two copies of an 11-bp direct repeat (ATATTCTGTTT)
blaOXA-23.source: Clinical Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baylyi Strain Coharboring blaSIM-1 and blaOXA-23 from China
blaOXA-23.evidence_note: bla OXA-23 was detected and confirmed by sequencing

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of blaSIM-1 in China in a carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baylyi strain, along with blaOXA-23, both located on a large plasmid.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and plasmid analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Current prospects for the fluoroquinolones as first-line tuberculosis therapy.

gyrA.notes: Mutation identified in a Tanzanian study.

gyrB.notes: Mutation identified in a Taiwanese study.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the role of fluoroquinolones in tuberculosis therapy, highlighting the development of resistance through mutations in the gyrA and gyrB genes encoding DNA gyrase subunits.
full_output.methodology: Analysis of clinical isolates and sequencing of resistance-associated genes.
full_output.sample_size: Various studies mentioned, including 291 isolates from Tanzania and 420 isolates from Taiwan.

full_output.paper_title: SMB-1, a novel subclass B3 metallo-beta-lactamase, associated with ISCR1 and a class 1 integron, from a carbapenem-resistant Serratia marcescens clinical isolate.

blaSMB-1.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + susceptibility testing
blaSMB-1.evidence_note: The blaSMB-1 gene was cloned into E. coli and conferred resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SMB-1, a novel subclass B3 metallo-beta-lactamase, which confers resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics, including carbapenems, in a carbapenem-resistant Serratia marcescens clinical isolate.
full_output.methodology: The gene was cloned and expressed in E. coli, and its resistance phenotype was confirmed through susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular basis of NDM-1, a new antibiotic resistance determinant.
full_output.key_findings: NDM-1 is a metallo-beta-lactamase that confers resistance to carbapenems and other beta-lactam antibiotics. It exhibits potent hydrolytic activity against these antibiotics, making it a significant threat in clinical settings.
full_output.methodology: Homology modeling, molecular docking, and enzymatic activity assays were used to characterize NDM-1's structure and function.

full_output.paper_title: Central venous catheter-associated Nocardia bacteremia in cancer patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the role of Nocardia species, particularly N. nova complex, in causing catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSIs) in cancer patients. It also demonstrates the effectiveness of antimicrobial lock solutions, such as trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole and minocycline, in reducing Nocardia biofilm formation on central venous catheters.
full_output.methodology: The study involved retrospective analysis of clinical data, in vitro biofilm formation experiments, and susceptibility testing of Nocardia isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Ciprofloxacin-resistant Shigella sonnei among men who have sex with men, Canada, 2010.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ciprofloxacin-resistant Shigella sonnei isolates among men who have sex with men in Montreal, Canada, with resistance mechanisms involving mutations in the gyrA and parC genes.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing of gyrA and parC genes to determine resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: The surfactant of Legionella pneumophila Is secreted in a TolC-dependent manner and is antagonistic toward other Legionella species.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes involved in the biosynthesis and secretion of a surfactant in Legionella pneumophila, including lpw_24151, lpw_24111, lpw_07761, and lpw_07981. These genes are essential for surfactant production and secretion, and the surfactant exhibits antimicrobial activity against other Legionella species.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, mutant construction, complementation, and biochemical assays were used to investigate the role of specific genes in surfactant production and secretion.

full_output.paper_title: Gene expression study using real-time PCR identifies an NTR gene as a major marker of resistance to benzonidazole in Trypanosoma cruzi.

NTR.validation_method: real-time PCR and gene copy number analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the NTR gene as a major marker of resistance to benzonidazole in Trypanosoma cruzi, with reduced mRNA levels and a loss of one gene copy in the resistant phenotype.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR and gene copy number analysis were used to assess gene expression and genetic changes in benzonidazole-resistant Trypanosoma cruzi strains.

full_output.paper_title: A randomized trial of the efficacy and safety of sequential intravenous/oral moxifloxacin monotherapy versus intravenous piperacillin/tazobactam followed by oral amoxicillin/clavulanate for complicated skin and skin structure infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy and safety of moxifloxacin monotherapy versus piperacillin/tazobactam followed by amoxicillin/clavulanate for complicated skin and skin structure infections. Both treatments were found to be non-inferior in terms of clinical and bacteriological success.
full_output.methodology: Randomized, double-blind, multicenter trial comparing moxifloxacin monotherapy with piperacillin/tazobactam followed by amoxicillin/clavulanate.

full_output.paper_title: Conversion of commensal Escherichia coli K-12 to an invasive form via expression of a mutant histone-like protein.
full_output.key_findings: Expression of the mutant histone-like protein HUα E38K, V42L in E. coli K-12 leads to changes in DNA supercoiling, activation of pathogenicity-associated genes, and enables invasion of intestinal epithelial cells.
full_output.methodology: Transcription assays, invasion experiments, and genetic manipulation.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of the functional contributions of Asn233 in metallo-β-lactamase IMP-1.

mutations_found.validated_by: resistance levels measured in E. coli

IMP-1.notes: Substitutions at position 233 significantly alter the kinetic parameters of the enzyme, but most substituted enzymes are able to provide for a high level of resistance to a broad range of β-lactams.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the functional contributions of Asn233 in the metallo-β-lactamase IMP-1, showing that substitutions at this position affect resistance to β-lactam antibiotics, with varying impacts depending on the antibiotic and the nature of the substitution.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, immunoblot analysis, MIC determinations, and kinetic parameter analysis were used to assess the effects of amino acid substitutions at position 233 of IMP-1 on β-lactam resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic basis for in vivo daptomycin resistance in enterococci.
full_output.key_findings: Mutations in the genes encoding LiaF and a GdpD-family protein were necessary and sufficient for the development of resistance to daptomycin in Enterococcus faecalis. Additionally, an Arg218 Gln substitution in the Cls enzyme was found in daptomycin-resistant E. faecium isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, allelic replacement, and MIC testing were used to identify and validate the genetic changes associated with daptomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a ViI-like phage specific to Escherichia coli O157:H7.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the ViI-like phage CBA120, highlighting its unique genetic features, including a putative thymidylate synthase and dNMP kinase, which suggest a novel DNA base substitution mechanism involving hmdUra instead of thymidine.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, BLAST analysis, and proteomic studies were conducted to analyze the genetic and biochemical characteristics of CBA120.

full_output.paper_title: Modulation of NKp30- and NKp46-mediated natural killer cell responses by poxviral hemagglutinin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies vaccinia virus (VV) and ectromelia virus (ECTV) hemagglutinin (HA) as novel ligands for the natural killer (NK) cell receptors NKp30 and NKp46. HA from VV and ECTV was shown to block NKp30-mediated activation while stimulating NKp46-mediated activation, leading to reduced NK cell lysis of infected cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used immunofluorescence staining, flow cytometry, and functional assays to investigate the interaction between poxviral HA and NK cell receptors.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas evades immune recognition of flagellin in both mammals and plants.

aprA.mechanism: degrades flagellin monomers, preventing TLR5 and FLS2 activation
aprA.validation_method: cloning and expression in E. coli, purification, and functional assays

aprI.validation_method: cloning and expression in E. coli, purification, and functional assays

full_output.key_findings: Pseudomonas aeruginosa uses the alkaline protease AprA to degrade flagellin monomers, preventing immune recognition by TLR5 and FLS2. The inhibitor AprI blocks AprA activity, protecting flagellin in the flagellar structure.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, expression, and purification of AprA and AprI, followed by functional assays in HEK/TLR5 cells and Arabidopsis.

full_output.paper_title: Serratia marcescens Utilizes a Non-Canonical Autophagic Pathway to Facilitate Intracellular Survival and Replication
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that Serratia marcescens utilizes a non-canonical autophagic pathway to facilitate its intracellular survival and replication, involving the recruitment of LC3 and Rab7 to Serratia-containing vacuoles (SeCVs).
full_output.methodology: The research utilized in vitro infection assays with epithelial cells, confocal microscopy, and biochemical analyses to investigate the interaction between Serratia marcescens and the autophagy pathway.

full_output.methodology: Molecular detection and analysis of resistance genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Presence of RD149 deletions in M. tuberculosis Central Asian Strain 1 isolates affect growth and TNFα induction in THP-1 monocytes.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that RD149 deletions in M. tuberculosis Central Asian Strain 1 (CAS1) isolates affect growth and TNFα induction in THP-1 monocytes. CAS1 strains with RD149 deletions showed reduced intracellular growth and increased TNFα secretion compared to strains without deletions and the reference strain H37Rv.
full_output.methodology: The study compared growth and cytokine induction in THP-1 monocytes between CAS1 strains with and without RD149 deletions, using broth growth assays and cytokine measurement techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Exploiting bacterial DNA gyrase as a drug target: current state and perspectives.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the current state and future perspectives of exploiting bacterial DNA gyrase as a drug target, focusing on various inhibitors such as quinolones, aminocoumarins, and other small molecules. It highlights the mechanisms of action, resistance, and potential for developing new antibacterial agents targeting gyrase.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature and research on DNA gyrase inhibitors and their mechanisms of action.

full_output.paper_title: Thiostrepton inhibits stable 70S ribosome binding and ribosome-dependent GTPase activation of elongation factor G and elongation factor 4.

full_output.methodology: GTP hydrolysis assays, ribosome binding assays, and chemical footprinting were used to analyze the effects of thiostrepton on EF-G and EF4.

full_output.paper_title: Intergenic Sequence Comparison of Escherichia coli Isolates Reveals Lifestyle Adaptations but Not Host Specificity.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed intergenic regions of E. coli isolates to identify molecular signatures related to host adaptation and lifestyle, but no host-specific AMR genes or mutations were found.
full_output.methodology: Phylogenetic analysis, PCR, and phenotypic testing were used to compare E. coli isolates from various hosts.

full_output.paper_title: Partial Genome Assembly for a Candidate Division OP11 Single Cell from an Anoxic Spring (Zodletone Spring, Oklahoma).

full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR was used to analyze gene expression in ileal biopsies.

full_output.paper_title: Biological consequences of ancient gene acquisition and duplication in the large genome of Candidatus Solibacter usitatus Ellin6076.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the large genome of Candidatus Solibacter usitatus Ellin6076, highlighting extensive gene duplication and paralogy, but no specific antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes or mutations were identified as being experimentally validated in this paper.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, comparative genomics, and phylogenetic analysis were employed to examine the genomic features of Candidatus Solibacter usitatus Ellin6076.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and regulation of the osmolyte betaine synthesizing enzymes GSMT and SDMT from halophilic methanogen Methanohalophilus portucalensis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the betaine synthesizing genes gsmt and sdmt from Methanohalophilus portucalensis, demonstrating their functionality in E. coli and their role in osmoadaptation under high salt conditions.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, heterologous expression in E. coli, biochemical assays, and in vivo betaine accumulation analysis.

full_output.paper_title: RNA-mediated reciprocal regulation between two bacterial operons is RNase III dependent.

aad9.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + spectinomycin resistance assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Qs and X RNA as small RNAs that reciprocally regulate gene expression in Enterococcus faecalis through RNase III-mediated processing, revealing a novel mechanism of gene regulation.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a combination of molecular biology techniques including Northern blotting, Western blotting, RACE, and in vitro cleavage assays to investigate the role of Qs and X RNA in regulating gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Necrotic enteritis-derived Clostridium perfringens strain with three closely related independently conjugative toxin and antibiotic resistance plasmids.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three closely related independently conjugative plasmids in a necrotic enteritis strain of Clostridium perfringens, including plasmids carrying the netB toxin gene, tetracycline resistance gene tetA(P), and the beta2 toxin gene cpb2.
full_output.methodology: Conjugation experiments, PCR analysis, and plasmid sequencing were used to characterize the resistance genes and plasmids.

full_output.paper_title: High-resolution melting-curve analysis of ligation-mediated real-time PCR for rapid evaluation of an epidemiological outbreak of extended-spectrum-beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized CTX-M and TEM beta-lactamase genes and the O25b-ST131 clone in extended-spectrum-beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli isolates during an outbreak.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, amplicon sequencing, and high-resolution melting analysis were used to detect and characterize AMR genes and clones.

full_output.paper_title: In-roads to the spread of antibiotic resistance: regional patterns of microbial transmission in northern coastal Ecuador.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that resistance to ampicillin and sulphamethoxazole is the most frequent profile among E. coli isolates, with higher prevalence in less remote communities. The research highlights the impact of environmental transmission and introduction rates of resistant bacteria on regional antibiotic resistance patterns.
full_output.methodology: The study involved analyzing E. coli isolates from 2210 samples using disc-diffusion methods to assess antibiotic susceptibility, alongside statistical modeling to evaluate the influence of remoteness and antibiotic use on resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: MexEF-OprN efflux pump exports the Pseudomonas quinolone signal (PQS) precursor HHQ (4-hydroxy-2-heptylquinoline).

mexEF-oprN.validation_method: mutant analysis and efflux pump inhibitor experiments

mexE.mechanism: constitutive expression leads to increased resistance

mutations_found.validated_by: mutant construction and efflux pump inhibitor assay

mexS.notes: mutations in mexS lead to overexpression of mexEF-oprN

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the MexEF-OprN efflux pump as a key player in exporting the Pseudomonas quinolone signal (PQS) precursor HHQ, affecting quorum sensing and virulence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, efflux pump inhibitor experiments, and LC-MS/MS for HAQ quantification.

full_output.paper_title: XpertÂ® MTB/RIF assay: development, evaluation and implementation of a new rapid molecular diagnostic for tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance.

rpoB.validation_method: detection of mutations in the rpoB gene through molecular beacon technology and real-time PCR

full_output.key_findings: The Xpert MTB/RIF assay detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance by targeting the rpoB gene, which is crucial for rifampicin resistance detection.
full_output.methodology: The Xpert MTB/RIF assay uses molecular beacon technology and real-time PCR to detect mutations in the rpoB gene of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Subtilase Cytotoxin-Coding Genes in Verotoxin-Producing Escherichia coli Strains from Sheep and Goats Differ from Those from Cattle.

subAB1.mechanism: encoding two closely linked, cotranscribed genes (subA and subB)

subAB2.mechanism: encoding two closely linked, cotranscribed genes (subA and subB)

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two variants of the subAB gene, subAB1 and subAB2, in verotoxin-producing Escherichia coli (VTEC) strains from sheep, goats, and cattle, highlighting their potential role in virulence.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and cytotoxicity assays in CHO cells were used to analyze the presence and characteristics of subAB genes.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative genomics study of multi-drug-resistance mechanisms in the antibiotic-resistant Streptococcus suis R61 strain.

pbp2x.notes: Mutations in the active site of PBP2x contribute to β-lactam resistance.

pbp2b.notes: Mutations in PBP2b contribute to β-lactam resistance.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in the QRDR of GyrA contribute to quinolone resistance.

parC.notes: Mutations in the QRDR of ParC contribute to quinolone resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes and mutations in the multidrug-resistant S. suis R61 strain, including pbp2x, pbp2b, gyrA, parC, tet(W), and mef(E), contributing to resistance against β-lactams, quinolones, tetracyclines, and macrolides.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, sequence analysis, structural modeling, and MIC testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.
full_output.sample_size: Two S. suis strains (R61 and A7) were analyzed.

full_output.paper_title: The eukaryotic-type serine/threonine protein kinase Stk is required for biofilm formation and virulence in Staphylococcus epidermidis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Stk as a critical regulator of biofilm formation and virulence in Staphylococcus epidermidis, highlighting its role in biofilm development, PIA production, and stress response.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic mutants, complementation analyses, and biochemical assays to investigate the role of Stk in S. epidermidis.

full_output.paper_title: PhoQ mutations promote lipid A modification and polymyxin resistance of Pseudomonas aeruginosa found in colistin-treated cystic fibrosis patients.

mutations_found.validated_by: experimental validation through mutagenesis and resistance testing

full_output.methodology: Experimental validation through mutagenesis, resistance testing, and lipid A analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of fusB-mediated fusidic acid resistance islands in Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates.

fusB.mechanism: direct binding to EF-G and protection of the drug target site

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies fusB-mediated fusidic acid resistance islands in Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates, highlighting the association of fusB with phage-related resistance islands and its role in conferring resistance to fusidic acid.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, Southern hybridization, and PFGE analysis were used to characterize fusB and its resistance islands.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteremia due to extended-spectrum-β-lactamase-producing Aeromonas spp. at a medical center in Southern Taiwan.

blaPER-3.evidence_note: The bla PER-3 gene was located in both chromosomes and plasmids, as demonstrated by Southern hybridization.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla PER-3 as an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase gene in two Aeromonas caviae isolates, which conferred resistance to cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and phenotypic testing were used to identify and characterize the ESBL genes.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance to ceftazidime involving loss of penicillin-binding protein 3 in Burkholderia pseudomallei.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the loss of the penicillin-binding protein 3 gene (BPSS1219) as a mechanism of ceftazidime resistance in Burkholderia pseudomallei, leading to a severe growth defect and high-level resistance to ceftazidime.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial genotyping, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and genomic analysis to investigate the mechanism of ceftazidime resistance in Burkholderia pseudomallei.

full_output.paper_title: A TetR-like regulator broadly affects the expressions of diverse genes in Mycobacterium smegmatis.
full_output.key_findings: Ms6564, a TetR-like transcriptional regulator, was identified as a key player in the regulation of DNA repair and cell cycle genes in Mycobacterium smegmatis. It binds to the promoters of these genes and acts as a positive regulator, affecting mutation frequencies and rates.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial one-hybrid assays, ChIP, EMSA, qRT-PCR, and mutation frequency/rate analyses were used to investigate the role of Ms6564 in gene regulation.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of quinolone-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the gyrA and parC genes of quinolone-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from Brazil, which are associated with increased resistance to ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and molecular methods, including analysis of mutations in the gyrA and parC genes through PCR and direct DNA sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 11 Staphylococcus aureus isolates with heterogeneous intermediate-level resistance to vancomycin (hVISA) in the United States, indicating a low prevalence of hVISA among S. aureus isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used the Etest GRD method for screening and PAP-AUC analysis for confirming hVISA isolates.

mutations_found.validated_by: virus replication and transmission studies in ferrets

NA.evidence_note: The I223R mutation in the neuraminidase gene confers resistance to neuraminidase inhibitors.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the I223R mutation in the neuraminidase gene of a 2009 pandemic A/H1N1 influenza virus, which confers resistance to neuraminidase inhibitors (oseltamivir, zanamivir, and peramivir). The mutant virus retains its virulence and transmissibility in ferrets.
full_output.methodology: The study used ferret models to assess the replication, pathogenicity, and transmissibility of the I223R mutant virus compared to a reference virus.

full_output.paper_title: Characterisation and manipulation of docetaxel resistant prostate cancer cell lines.

NF-kappa-B.notes: NF-κB activity was increased in response to Docetaxel treatment in the resistant sublines.

P-glycoprotein.notes: P-gp was overexpressed in DU-145 R and 22RV1 R sublines.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NF-κB activation and P-glycoprotein overexpression as key mechanisms of Docetaxel resistance in prostate cancer cell lines.
full_output.methodology: Western blotting, luciferase assay, and flow cytometry were used to analyze gene expression and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Ruminant rhombencephalitis-associated Listeria monocytogenes alleles linked to a multilocus variable-number tandem-repeat analysis complex.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified distinct alleles of the actA and inlJ genes in Listeria monocytogenes isolates associated with ruminant rhombencephalitis, which were linked to specific MLVA complexes and clinical origins.
full_output.methodology: MLVA, PCR, and DNA sequencing were used to analyze genetic variation in L. monocytogenes isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium smegmatis RoxY is a repressor of oxyS and contributes to resistance to oxidative stress and bactericidal ubiquitin-derived peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies RoxY as a repressor of oxyS and shows that RoxY, OxyS, and AhpD contribute to Mycobacterium smegmatis resistance to oxidative stress and bactericidal ubiquitin-derived peptides.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, mutant analysis, complementation, qRT-PCR, and EMSA were used to investigate the role of RoxY, OxyS, and AhpD in oxidative stress and Ub-peptide resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Deletion of the aconitase gene in Corynebacterium glutamicum causes strong selection pressure for secondary mutations inactivating citrate synthase.

gltA.notes: A mutation in gltA leading to loss of citrate synthase activity was identified in Δ acn mutants.

full_output.key_findings: The deletion of the aconitase gene in Corynebacterium glutamicum leads to secondary mutations in the gltA gene, resulting in the inactivation of citrate synthase.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, sequencing, and enzymatic activity assays were used to identify mutations in gltA and assess their impact on citrate synthase activity.

zwf.mechanism: confers resistance to tellurite by increasing NADPH levels, which helps in neutralizing reactive oxygen species (ROS) and protecting the cell from oxidative stress
zwf.validation_method: experimental validation through gene overexpression and knockout studies showing increased sensitivity to tellurite in Δzwf strains and restoration of resistance upon genetic complementation

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the zwf gene, encoding glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PDH), as crucial for E. coli's resistance to tellurite. G6PDH increases NADPH levels, which helps mitigate oxidative stress caused by tellurite.
full_output.methodology: Gene overexpression, knockout, and complementation studies combined with biochemical assays to measure NADPH levels, ROS, and enzyme activities.

full_output.paper_title: The Staphylococcus aureus two-component regulatory system, GraRS, senses and confers resistance to selected cationic antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the GraRS two-component regulatory system in Staphylococcus aureus is involved in resistance to cationic antimicrobial peptides (CAPs). Mutations in graR and vraG lead to increased susceptibility to CAPs, highlighting the importance of this system in sensing and responding to these peptides.
full_output.methodology: The study used isogenic graR and vraG mutant strains of S. aureus Mu50 and COL to investigate the role of GraRS and VraFG in CAP resistance through susceptibility testing, transcriptional analysis, and membrane lipid profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanism-based inactivation by aromatization of the transaminase BioA involved in biotin biosynthesis in Mycobaterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a mechanism-based inhibitor (compound 1) targeting the transaminase BioA involved in biotin biosynthesis in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Compound 1 irreversibly inactivates BioA through an aromatization mechanism, demonstrating selectivity and providing insights into the enzymatic pathway.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the synthesis and biochemical evaluation of a mechanism-based inhibitor of BioA, including kinetic analysis, mass spectrometry, and X-ray crystallography to confirm the mechanism of inactivation.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogenetic groups and cephalosporin resistance genes of Escherichia coli from diseased food-producing animals in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes, including bla CTX-M-2, bla CTX-M-25, bla CTX-M-15, and bla SHV-2, as well as the AmpC beta-lactamase gene bla CMY-2, in Escherichia coli isolates from diseased food-producing animals in Japan.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Recombinase-mediated cassette exchange as a novel method to study somatic hypermutation in Ramos cells.

organisms_observed_in: Ramos human Burkitt’s lymphoma cell line

AID.notes: The C-to-G mutation in WT B introduces a nonsense mutation in the VDJ region.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the use of recombinase-mediated cassette exchange (RMCE) to introduce a cluster of WGCW hot spots into the endogenous heavy chain gene of Ramos cells, increasing the frequency of mutations in the V region without altering their characteristics or distribution.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RMCE to modify the IgH V region in Ramos cells, followed by sequencing to analyze mutation frequencies and characteristics.

full_output.paper_title: Divergent Rifamycin Susceptibilities of Clostridium difficile Strains in Canada and Italy and Predictive Accuracy of Rifampin Etest for Rifamycin Resistance

rpoB.notes: Two new rpoB mutations were identified in rifamycin-resistant isolates.
rpoB.evidence_note: The paper states that 'two new rpoB mutations were identified in rifamycin-resistant isolates' and describes the molecular analysis performed to identify these mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified two new rpoB mutations (S488P and S498T) in rifamycin-resistant Clostridium difficile isolates, along with previously described mutations (H502N and R505K).
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing by agar dilution and Etest, molecular analysis of rpoB mutations.

full_output.paper_title: IMP-producing carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in the United States.

blaIMP.mechanism: hydrolyzes carbapenems and other beta-lactam antibiotics

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IMP-4, a metallo-beta-lactamase, as a novel mechanism of carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae in the United States.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PFGE, and plasmid analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SCORD3 (EDS5) and SCORD5 (AtGCN20/AtABCF3) as crucial genes involved in salicylic acid (SA) biosynthesis and bacterium-triggered stomatal closure in Arabidopsis.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screen, T-DNA insertion analysis, mutant phenotyping, and complementation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Drosophila melanogaster as an animal model for the study of Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm infections in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that P. aeruginosa forms biofilms in the Drosophila crop, which are composed of microcolonies, EPS, and DNA. The pelB gene was found to be essential for in vivo biofilm formation, while the psl gene was associated with increased EPS production in a hyperbiofilm-forming mutant.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a Drosophila melanogaster oral infection model to investigate P. aeruginosa biofilm formation and its effects on host immune responses, including AMP gene expression and survival outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: A clonal group of nontypeable Haemophilus influenzae with two IgA proteases is adapted to infection in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a clonal group of nontypeable Haemophilus influenzae with the igaB gene, which encodes a type 2 IgA1 protease, and shows that these strains are adapted for colonization and infection in COPD.
full_output.methodology: Molecular typing, sequencing, PCR, and MLST analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Carbon storage regulator A (CsrA(Bb)) is a repressor of Borrelia burgdorferi flagellin protein FlaB.

csrA Bb.mechanism: binds to the flaB transcript leader sequence and inhibits translation initiation

full_output.key_findings: CsrA Bb represses the synthesis of FlaB, the major flagellin protein of Borrelia burgdorferi, by binding to the flaB transcript and inhibiting translation initiation.
full_output.methodology: Genetic, biochemical, and cryo-electron tomography approaches were used to investigate the regulatory mechanism of CsrA Bb on flagellar synthesis and motility.

full_output.paper_title: Global spread of Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the global spread of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae, including KPC, NDM-1, OXA-48, VIM, and IMP, highlighting their resistance to carbapenems and the challenges in detection and management.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews literature and provides insights into the detection and epidemiology of carbapenemase-producing bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial ointments and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus USA300.
full_output.key_findings: Resistance to bacitracin and neomycin was found only in USA300 MRSA isolates, suggesting that the use of over-the-counter antimicrobial drugs may select for the USA300 clone.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing of MRSA isolates to bacitracin and neomycin using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method and agar dilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Nosocomial outbreak of VIM-1-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates of multilocus sequence type 15: molecular basis, clinical risk factors, and outcome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaVIM-1 as a gene responsible for carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates during a nosocomial outbreak. The gene was found in a class 1 integron and was associated with multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Molecular epidemiology, PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the ROB-1 beta-lactamase gene from Haemophilus influenzae plasmid RRob, identifying it as a class A beta-lactamase with low homology to other beta-lactamases and showing its evolutionary relationship with beta-lactamases from gram-positive bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Insights into the CtrA regulon in development of stress resistance in obligatory intracellular pathogen Ehrlichia chaffeensis.
full_output.key_findings: E. chaffeensis CtrA regulates the expression of ompA, bolA, and surE, which contribute to stress resistance in the bacterium. full_output.methodology: Quantitative RT-PCR, EMSA, lacZ reporter assays, and osmotic stress resistance assays were used to characterize the roles of ompA, bolA, and surE in E. chaffeensis.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative study on occurrence of class A and class C β-lactamase genes and their co-occurrence in Indian Enterobacteriaceae during years 2009 and 2010.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the occurrence and co-occurrence of class A (bla CTX-M, bla SHV, bla TEM) and class C (bla ampC) β-lactamase genes in Indian Enterobacteriaceae isolates, highlighting a decrease in the co-existence of bla ESBLs with bla ampC from 2009 to 2010.

full_output.paper_title: C4-alkylthiols with activity against Moraxella catarrhalis and Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design, synthesis, and testing of novel monocyclic β-lactams with alkyl- and aryl-thio groups at C4, showing activity against β-lactamase-producing Moraxella catarrhalis and Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of β-lactams with C4 substitutions, followed by antibacterial activity testing using Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion and MIC/MBC assays.

full_output.paper_title: Aqueous and organic solvent-extracts of selected south African medicinal plants possess antimicrobial activity against drug-resistant strains of Helicobacter pylori: inhibitory and bactericidal potential.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of aqueous and organic solvent extracts from selected South African medicinal plants against drug-resistant strains of Helicobacter pylori, demonstrating significant inhibitory and bactericidal effects.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar well diffusion and micro broth dilution methods to assess the antimicrobial activity of plant extracts against H. pylori strains.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of a Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate of sequence type 258 producing KPC-2 carbapenemase in Korea.

blaKPC-2.evidence_note: The paper describes the isolation of a KPC-2-producing K. pneumoniae isolate and confirms the presence of the blaKPC-2 gene through PCR and DNA sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the isolation of a KPC-2-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate of sequence type 258 in Korea, which exhibits resistance to multiple antibiotics including carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify the KPC-2 carbapenemase and determine the resistance profile of the isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid metagenome reveals high levels of antibiotic resistance genes and mobile genetic elements in activated sludge.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes, including tetB(P), aadA5, ampC, macB, IS Pps1, and IS Sm2, in the plasmid metagenome of activated sludge, highlighting the presence of diverse resistance mechanisms in environmental microbial communities.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput sequencing and metagenomic analysis were used to identify and characterize antibiotic resistance genes in the plasmid metagenome of activated sludge.
