full_output.paper_title: Substrate recognition by β-ketoacyl-ACP synthases.

ecFabB.notes: Mutants of ecFabB (R62Q, K63Q, R66Q, K151Q) were created via site-directed mutagenesis and characterized kinetically.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and comparative genomic analysis of a novel bacteriophage, SFP10, simultaneously inhibiting both Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli O157:H7.

full_output.paper_title: Roles of DNA sequence and sigma A factor in transcription of the vraSR operon.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the roles of DNA sequence and the sigma A factor in the transcription of the vraSR operon in Staphylococcus aureus, focusing on the binding mechanisms of VraR and its impact on gene expression under stress conditions.
full_output.methodology: The research employed electromobility shift assays, DNase I footprinting, KMnO4 footprinting, and in vitro transcription experiments to analyze the interactions between VraR, DNA, and the sigma A factor.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular basis of lipopolysaccharide heterogeneity in Escherichia coli: envelope stress-responsive regulators control the incorporation of glycoforms with a third 3-deoxy-α-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid and rhamnose.

waaZ.notes: waaZ mutants contain only glycoform I and no glycoform IV derivatives.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies waaZ and waaS as the structural genes responsible for the incorporation of the third Kdo and rhamnose in the LPS of E. coli, highlighting their roles in LPS heterogeneity and outer membrane integrity.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized mass spectrometry, genetic mutagenesis, and biochemical analyses to characterize the roles of waaZ and waaS in LPS biosynthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis not due to noncompliance but to between-patient pharmacokinetic variability.

rpoB.encodes: β subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
rpoB.notes: Mutations in rpoB gene are associated with rifampin resistance

katG.notes: Mutations in katG gene are associated with isoniazid resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study found that nonadherence alone is not sufficient for the emergence of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB). Instead, pharmacokinetic variability among patients plays a significant role in the development of MDR-TB. Mutations in the rpoB gene (Ser531Leu) and katG gene (Ser315Thr) were identified as causes of rifampin and isoniazid resistance, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The study used hollow fiber system (HFS) experiments to simulate the effects of nonadherence on drug resistance emergence and conducted Monte Carlo simulations to assess the impact of pharmacokinetic variability on MDR-TB development.

full_output.paper_title: The anti-sigma factor TcdC modulates hypervirulence in an epidemic BI/NAP1/027 clinical isolate of Clostridium difficile.

tcdC.validation_method: Western immunoblotting, Vero cell cytotoxicity assays, qRT-PCR

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the tcdC gene in Clostridium difficile BI/NAP1/027 isolates acts as a negative regulator of toxin production. Complementation of the tcdC mutation reduces toxin production and virulence, showing that the tcdC mutation is a key factor in the hypervirulence of these strains.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, Western immunoblotting, Vero cell cytotoxicity assays, qRT-PCR, and animal model experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Mainstreams of horizontal gene exchange in enterobacteria: consideration of the outbreak of enterohemorrhagic E. coli O104:H4 in Germany in 2011.

tetA.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + disk diffusion

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various genomic islands (GIs) in enterobacteria, including those carrying antibiotic resistance genes such as beta-lactamase (bla), tetracycline efflux protein (tet), and mercury resistance operon (mer). These GIs were found to be horizontally transferred and contributed to the virulence and resistance profiles of the strains analyzed.

full_output.paper_title: Hypervirulent Clostridium difficile PCR-ribotypes exhibit resistance to widely used disinfectants.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance gene abundances correlate with metal and geochemical conditions in archived Scottish soils.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotics shaping bacterial genome: deletion of an IS91 flanked virulence determinant upon exposure to subinhibitory antibiotic concentrations.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of a novel and potent class of F. tularensis enoyl-reductase (FabI) inhibitors by molecular shape and electrostatic matching.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel FabI inhibitors through a ligand-based virtual screening approach combining molecular shape and electrostatic matching, leading to the discovery of compounds with sub-micromolar enzyme inhibition and whole-cell antibacterial activity against various bacterial species.

full_output.paper_title: International spread of MDR TB from Tugela Ferry, South Africa.

rpoB.notes: rpoB mutation associated with rifampin resistance

full_output.paper_title: Salivaricin D, a novel intrinsically trypsin-resistant lantibiotic from Streptococcus salivarius 5M6c isolated from a healthy infant.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid colorimetric testing for pyrazinamide susceptibility of M. tuberculosis by a PCR-based in-vitro synthesized pyrazinamidase method.

full_output.methodology: PCR amplification of pncA gene, in-vitro synthesis of PZase, and colorimetric activity assay.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical outcome of pneumococcal meningitis during the emergence of pencillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae: an observational study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that penicillin resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae was associated with higher case-fatality rates in patients with pneumococcal meningitis, even when initial antibiotic therapy included ceftriaxone.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed clinical data from 548 patients with culture-confirmed pneumococcal meningitis, examining the impact of penicillin resistance on outcomes through proportional hazards regression.

full_output.paper_title: Global analysis of the Staphylococcus aureus response to mupirocin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ileS as a gene that is significantly induced in response to mupirocin treatment in Staphylococcus aureus, indicating its potential role in the bacterial response to this antibiotic.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of proteomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic analyses to investigate the response of Staphylococcus aureus to mupirocin.

full_output.paper_title: PmrB mutations promote polymyxin resistance of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from colistin-treated cystic fibrosis patients.

pmrB.notes: Multiple pmrB mutations were identified in clinical isolates, including single and double missense mutations in the periplasmic and DHP domains.
pmrB.evidence_note: The paper describes pmrB mutations in clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa that confer resistance to colistin and polymyxin B.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various pmrB mutations that confer polymyxin resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from cystic fibrosis patients treated with colistin.
full_output.methodology: Episomal expression of pmrB alleles in PAK wild-type and Δ pmrAB strains, along with lipid A analysis and susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of galacturonosyl transferase genes rgtA, rgtB, rgtC, rgtD, and rgtE responsible for lipopolysaccharide synthesis in nitrogen-fixing endosymbiont Rhizobium leguminosarum: lipopolysaccharide core and lipid galacturonosyl residues confer membrane stability.

These genes are involved in the addition of galacturonic acid (GalA) residues to the LPS core and lipid A, contributing to membrane stability and resistance to polymyxin B (PmxB).
full_output.methodology: Genetic mutagenesis, lipid analysis, and biochemical assays were used to characterize the functions of the rgt genes in LPS synthesis and membrane stability.

full_output.paper_title: Fatal S. aureus hemorrhagic pneumonia: genetic analysis of a unique clinical isolate producing both PVL and TSST-1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the genetic organization of PVL and TSST-1 toxin genes in a unique clinical isolate of Staphylococcus aureus, MSSA68111. The PVL genes were found in a novel temperate prophage, ФPVLv68111, and the TSST-1 gene was located on a unique staphylococcal pathogenicity island, SaPI68111.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, PCR, ELISA, and sequencing were used to characterize the PVL and TSST-1 genes in MSSA68111.

full_output.paper_title: Thermostable hexameric form of Eis (Rv2416c) protein of M. tuberculosis plays an important role for enhanced intracellular survival within macrophages.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified that the hexameric form of the Eis protein, which has aminoglycoside acetyltransferase activity, is thermostable and contributes to the enhanced intracellular survival of Mycobacterium tuberculosis within macrophages.
full_output.methodology: Biophysical and biochemical methods including size exclusion chromatography, circular dichroism, fluorescence spectroscopy, and aminoglycoside acetyltransferase activity assays were used to characterize the structural and functional properties of the Eis protein.

full_output.paper_title: A case of wound dual infection with Pasteurella dagmatis and Pasteurella canis resulting from a dog bite -- limitations of Vitek-2 system in exact identification of Pasteurella species.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a case of dual infection with Pasteurella dagmatis and Pasteurella canis following a dog bite, highlighting the limitations of the Vitek 2 system in accurately identifying these species. All isolates were found to be highly susceptible to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The isolates were identified through morphological, biochemical, and genetic analysis, including 16S rRNA sequencing, and their antimicrobial susceptibility was determined using the Vitek 2 AST-N025 panels.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization and antimicrobial susceptibility of nasal Staphylococcus aureus isolates from a Chinese medical college campus.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mupA as a gene conferring resistance to mupirocin in MRSA isolates from a Chinese medical college campus, highlighting the presence of mupirocin-resistant strains among nasal S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Listeria monocytogenes infection in macrophages induces vacuolar-dependent host miRNA response.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies miR-155, miR-146a, miR-125a-3p, miR-125a-5p, and miR-149 as significantly upregulated miRNAs in L. monocytogenes-infected macrophages, highlighting their role in the host's innate immune response.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized TaqMan Rodent miRNA Arrays and RT-qPCR to analyze miRNA expression in bone marrow-derived macrophages infected with L. monocytogenes.

full_output.paper_title: The role of catalase in gonococcal resistance to peroxynitrite.

katA.validation_method: experimental validation through construction of a katA mutant and restoration of resistance via IPTG induction of a cloned katA gene

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies katA as a gene encoding catalase that provides resistance to peroxynitrite in Neisseria gonorrhoeae. The resistance is attributed to the catalytic activity of KatA, which detoxifies peroxynitrite, and the study shows that the absence of katA leads to increased sensitivity to peroxynitrite.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic manipulation, including construction of a katA mutant, and experimental validation through catalase activity assays and survival analysis after exposure to peroxynitrite.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic antibacterial and antibiotic effects of bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloids on clinical isolates of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloids tetrandrine (Tet) and demethyltetrandrine (d-Tet) enhance the in vitro antibacterial efficacy of cefazolin (CFZ) against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates, showing significant synergistic effects.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution, chequerboard, and time-kill tests were used to evaluate the antibacterial activity of Tet, d-Tet, and antibiotics against MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of blaCTX-M in Enterobacteriaceae isolates from the Kingdom of Bahrain.

blaCTX-M.validation_method: multiplex PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaCTX-M as the most prevalent extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) in Enterobacteriaceae isolates from the Kingdom of Bahrain, particularly in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, contributing to resistance against various beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR was used to detect blaCTX-M genes, and antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed to assess resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: NONO and RALY proteins are required for YB-1 oxaliplatin induced resistance in colon adenocarcinoma cell lines.

NONO.mechanism: Regulates YB-1 expression and contributes to oxaliplatin resistance
NONO.validation_method: siRNA knockdown and oxaliplatin sensitivity assays

RALY.mechanism: Regulates YB-1 expression and contributes to oxaliplatin resistance
RALY.validation_method: siRNA knockdown and oxaliplatin sensitivity assays

full_output.paper_title: Bisubstrate adenylation inhibitors of biotin protein ligase from Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the essentiality of the birA gene encoding biotin protein ligase (Mt BPL) in Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Mycobacterium smegmatis, and characterizes a bisubstrate inhibitor, Bio-AMS, that effectively targets Mt BPL, showing potent antitubercular activity against drug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of Bio-AMS, kinetic inhibition assays, isothermal titration calorimetry, and genetic studies to validate the essentiality of birA and the mechanism of action of Bio-AMS.

vraFG.role_in_paper: essential component of the five-component system

full_output.paper_title: Mechanism of amphotericin B resistance in clinical isolates of Leishmania donovani.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MDR1, PgPA, and SCMT B as key players in amphotericin B resistance in Leishmania donovani, with MDR1 showing increased expression in resistant strains and SCMT B being overexpressed in resistant parasites.

full_output.paper_title: Novel gene cassettes and integrons in antibiotic-resistant bacteria isolated from urban wastewaters.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three new gene cassettes, including a novel aadA variant (aadA17), a gene putatively involved in cell signaling (dcyA), and an open reading frame of unknown function interrupted by a novel insertion sequence (orfER.17::ISAs12). Thirteen different gene cassette arrays were detected, four of which represent novel integrons.
full_output.methodology: The study used dot blot hybridization and molecular techniques to screen for integrons and characterize their genetic structure in antibiotic-resistant bacteria isolated from urban wastewaters.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotics in feed induce prophages in swine fecal microbiomes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies antibiotic resistance genes in swine fecal viromes, showing that in-feed antibiotics induce prophages and alter microbial community structures.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and analysis of phage and bacterial communities in swine feces.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of the naturally occurring genes encoding carbapenem-hydrolysing oxacillinases from Acinetobacter haemolyticus, Acinetobacter johnsonii, and Acinetobacter calcoaceticus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three novel carbapenem-hydrolysing oxacillinase genes, blaOXA-211, blaOXA-213, and blaOXA-214, in Acinetobacter species. These genes confer resistance to penicillins and carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: PCR screening, sequencing, and MIC determination.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanisms of resistance to chloramphenicol in Pseudomonas putida KT2440.

full_output.key_findings: Pseudomonas putida KT2440 exhibits resistance to chloramphenicol through the coordinated expression of genes involved in efflux pumps, oxidative stress responses, and physiological adaptations. Key genes identified include pp2669, pp2668, pp2667, pqqC, pqqB, and agmR, which contribute to chloramphenicol resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis, mutant screening, and gene expression studies were conducted to identify genes involved in chloramphenicol resistance in Pseudomonas putida KT2440.

full_output.paper_title: Use of recombinase-based in vivo expression technology to characterize Enterococcus faecalis gene expression during infection identifies in vivo-expressed antisense RNAs and implicates the protease Eep in pathogenesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified in vivo-expressed antisense RNAs and implicated the protease Eep in pathogenesis of Enterococcus faecalis. Deletion of eep resulted in severe attenuation in a rabbit model of endocarditis, which was rescued by complementation with the wild-type gene.
full_output.methodology: RIVET screen, deletion mutant analysis, complementation, and biofilm assays.

full_output.paper_title: Cost of antibiotic resistance and the geometry of adaptation.

rpsL.notes: Mutation in rpsL confers streptomycin resistance.

K43N.notes: This mutation was experimentally validated and confers resistance to streptomycin.

K88E.notes: This mutation was experimentally validated and confers resistance to streptomycin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the rpsL K43N mutation as a cause of streptomycin resistance in E. coli, demonstrating its impact on fitness and compensatory evolution.
full_output.methodology: Experimental evolution, competition fitness assays, and microsatellite frequency measurement were used to analyze mutations and their effects on resistance and fitness.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the metabolic reprogramming in Pseudomonas fluorescens under nitrosative stress, highlighting the role of citrate lyase (CL) in degrading citrate and circumventing stress through a novel metabolic network.

full_output.paper_title: The Streptomyces-produced antibiotic fosfomycin is a promiscuous substrate for archaeal isopentenyl phosphate kinase.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of antibiotic combinations against multidrug-resistant strains of Acinetobacter baumannii and the effects of their antibiotic resistance determinants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several β-lactamase genes (blaPER, blaTEM, blaADC, blaOXA-Ab), aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes (aphA6, aadA1, aadB, aacC1, aacC2), and the adeR gene involved in efflux pump regulation, along with fluoroquinolone resistance mutations in gyrA and parC. full_output.methodology: Analytical isoelectric focusing, PCR, and direct sequencing of PCR products were used to characterize antibiotic resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Genes involved in immunity to and secretion of aureocin A53, an atypical class II bacteriocin produced by Staphylococcus aureus A53.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes involved in immunity to and secretion of aureocin A53, an atypical class II bacteriocin produced by Staphylococcus aureus A53. Key genes include aucA, aucE, aucF, aucG, aucIB, aucIA, and orf8, which are crucial for immunity and secretion mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, transformation, and mutant analysis were used to characterize the roles of these genes in immunity and secretion of aureocin A53.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of spores on the comparative efficacies of five antibiotics for treatment of Bacillus anthracis in an in vitro hollow fiber pharmacodynamic model.

full_output.methodology: The study used an in vitro hollow fiber pharmacodynamic model to assess antibiotic efficacy against Bacillus anthracis, including spore-forming and non-spore-forming strains.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of isolates with reduced glycopeptide susceptibility in persistent or recurrent bloodstream infections due to methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.paper_title: High-level cefixime- and ceftriaxone-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae in France: novel penA mosaic allele in a successful international clone causes treatment failure.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the blaGES-5 gene, encoding a carbapenem-hydrolyzing beta-lactamase, on plasmids pRSB113 and pRSB115 recovered from a sewage treatment plant. The gene was shown to confer resistance to carbapenems, ceftazidime, and aztreonam.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid isolation, sequencing, and transformation experiments were conducted to characterize the blaGES-5 gene and its resistance profile.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology over an 11-year period (2000 to 2010) of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli causing bacteremia in a centralized Canadian region.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaCTX-M-15 and blaCTX-M-14 as the dominant extended-spectrum beta-lactamase genes in Escherichia coli isolates causing bacteremia in Calgary, Canada, between 2000 and 2010.
full_output.methodology: Molecular epidemiology, PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Effective antibiotics in combination against extreme drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa with decreased susceptibility to polymyxin B.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies metallo-beta-lactamase genes (blaIMP and blaVIM) and other resistance genes (VEB-1 and OXA-10) in XDR-PA isolates, highlighting the need for combination therapies against these resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR assay and susceptibility testing were used to characterize resistance genes and mechanisms in XDR-PA isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies methicillin-susceptible ST398 Staphylococcus aureus isolates responsible for bloodstream infections, highlighting their increasing incidence and unique characteristics compared to pig-borne clones.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a longitudinal survey of bloodstream infections, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, MLST, and molecular typing techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Severe infection in a lung transplant recipient caused by donor-transmitted carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaOXA-23 gene as a major determinant of carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii, which was responsible for severe infection in a lung transplant recipient following donor transmission.
full_output.methodology: Polymerase chain reaction assay, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and strain typing techniques including RAPD and PFGE were used to analyze the isolates.

mecA.validation_method: chip-based array with colorimetric intensity changes

full_output.key_findings: The study describes Staph ID/R, a rapid method for identifying Staphylococcus species and detecting the mecA gene directly from positive blood cultures, demonstrating high specificity and sensitivity for methicillin resistance detection.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized helicase-dependent amplification (HDA) combined with a chip-based array for rapid detection of Staphylococcus species and the mecA gene.

full_output.paper_title: Population structure of multi- and extensively drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains in South Africa.

inhA.notes: Mutations in the inhA promoter were associated with increased resistance to isoniazid and ethionamide.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified inhA promoter mutations as a significant factor in the development of extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB) in South Africa, particularly in the Western and Eastern Cape provinces.
full_output.methodology: The study used spoligotyping and sequencing to analyze the genetic diversity and resistance mechanisms of Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multidrug-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype 6D clones in South Korea, highlighting genetic recombination events involving the cps locus leading to the emergence of these clones.
full_output.methodology: The study involved antimicrobial susceptibility testing and sequencing of genes around the cps locus in various S. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and diversity evaluation of tetracycline resistance genes in grassland-based production systems in Colombia, South america.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a wide distribution of tetracycline resistance genes, particularly tet(W) and tet(Q), in both animal and environmental samples from grassland-based production systems in Colombia. These genes were found to be prevalent in feces and ruminal fluid, with some genes like tet(B) and tet(Z) being detected in environmental samples.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection and DGGE analysis were used to identify and characterize tetracycline resistance genes in animal and environmental samples.

full_output.paper_title: Glutamate dehydrogenase affects resistance to cell wall antibiotics in Bacillus subtilis.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that glutamate dehydrogenase RocG affects resistance to cell wall antibiotics in Bacillus subtilis by regulating the σ W regulon. Mutations in gudB can restore resistance to CEF and fosfomycin in a rocG mutant.
full_output.methodology: Disk diffusion assays, microarray analysis, and DNA sequencing were used to investigate the role of glutamate dehydrogenase in antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Evolutionary paths to antibiotic resistance under dynamically sustained drug selection.

dhfr.notes: mutations restricted to the target enzyme dihydrofolate reductase

full_output.paper_title: The TCA cycle is not required for selection or survival of multidrug-resistant Salmonella.

mutations_found.validated_by: whole genome sequencing and site-directed mutagenesis

ramR.notes: mutation in ramR confers multidrug resistance

full_output.paper_title: Total synthesis of [Ψ[C(═S)NH]Tpg4]vancomycin aglycon, [Ψ[C(═NH)NH]Tpg4]vancomycin aglycon, and related key compounds: reengineering vancomycin for dual D-Ala-D-Ala and D-Ala-D-Lac binding.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the total synthesis of [Ψ[C(=S)NH]Tpg4]vancomycin aglycon and [Ψ[C(=NH)NH]Tpg4]vancomycin aglycon, which exhibit dual binding affinity for d-Ala-d-Ala and d-Ala-d-Lac ligands and potent antimicrobial activity against vancomycin-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, binding affinity assays, and antimicrobial activity testing.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of clarithromycin resistance in Helicobacter pylori following noncryogenic storage of rapid urease tests for 30 days.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the 23S rRNA gene (A2142G and A2143G) as the primary mechanism of clarithromycin resistance in H. pylori, demonstrating that these mutations can be detected through molecular testing of gastric biopsies stored in rapid urease tests for 30 days.
full_output.methodology: Molecular testing including PCR and allele-specific primer-PCR for detection of 23S rRNA gene mutations and clarithromycin susceptibility testing via E-test strips.

full_output.paper_title: Small-molecule modulators of Listeria monocytogenes biofilm development.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies small molecules that modulate biofilm development in Listeria monocytogenes, including sphingosine and palmitoyl-d,l-carnitine, which inhibit biofilm formation at sub-MIC concentrations.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput biofilm assay and structure-activity studies of compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Cellular response of Campylobacter jejuni to trisodium phosphate.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies nhaA1 and nhaA2 genes in Campylobacter jejuni that function as cation/proton antiporters, contributing to tolerance against trisodium phosphate (TSP). These genes partially restore TSP, alkaline, and sodium resistance in an E. coli mutant lacking cation/proton antiporters.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, functional complementation in E. coli, and growth assays were used to validate the role of nhaA1 and nhaA2 in TSP tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Large-scale screening of a targeted Enterococcus faecalis mutant library identifies envelope fitness factors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several genes involved in the interaction between enterococci and their host environments, highlighting the importance of cell envelope glycopolymers in E. faecalis host adaptation.
full_output.methodology: Large-scale screening of targeted mutants in E. faecalis V583 for resistance to oxidative stress, antibiotic resistance, opsonophagocytosis, adherence, and virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genome-wide analysis of an antibiotic-resistant small colony variant (SCV) of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

mexAB-oprM.mechanism: Contributes to resistance to aminoglycosides and cephalosporines

mexXY.mechanism: Contributes to resistance to aminoglycosides and fluoroquinolones

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple genes and mutations involved in antibiotic resistance in a Pseudomonas aeruginosa SCV, including overexpression of efflux pumps, LPS modification genes, and mutations in phoP, phoQ, and mexZ.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide transcriptional profiling, proteome analysis, and genome sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Zn(II)-responsive ribosomal proteins YkgM and L31 in E. coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes Zn(II)-responsive ribosomal proteins YkgM and L31 in E. coli, identifying their roles in Zn(II) homeostasis and their metal-binding properties.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR, cDNA microarrays, protein over-expression, purification, and metal analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Frequency of antibiotic resistance in Helicobacter pylori strains isolated from the northern population of Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high rates of antibiotic resistance in Helicobacter pylori isolates from northern Iran, including resistance to amoxicillin (23.9%), ciprofloxacin (34.5%), clarithromycin (45.2%), furazolidone (61.4%), metronidazole (65.5%), and tetracycline (37.1%).
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method on 197 H. pylori isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Reevaluation of the critical concentration for drug susceptibility testing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis against pyrazinamide using wild-type MIC distributions and pncA gene sequencing.

pncA.mechanism: mutations in pncA lead to pyrazinamide resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study reevaluates the critical concentration for pyrazinamide susceptibility testing in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, highlighting the importance of pncA gene mutations in conferring resistance. It suggests adjusting the resistance cutoff to >128 mg/liter based on wild-type MIC distributions.
full_output.methodology: The study determined PZA MICs using the Bactec MGIT 960 system, performed pncA sequencing, and conducted pyrazinamidase tests to assess resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Trends in the susceptibility of clinically important resistant bacteria to tigecycline: results from the Tigecycline In Vitro Surveillance in Taiwan study, 2006 to 2010.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that tigecycline maintained good in vitro activity against most clinically important drug-resistant bacteria in Taiwan, except for Acinetobacter baumannii, which showed decreasing susceptibility over time.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the in vitro susceptibility of various drug-resistant bacteria to tigecycline using broth microdilution methods and evaluated trends over a five-year period.

full_output.paper_title: Differences in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains isolated from pediatric and adult patients from hospitals in a large county in California.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified spa types t008, t242, and t002 as the predominant MRSA strains in Orange County, with t008 (USA300) being significantly more common in pediatric patients compared to adults.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted a prospective cohort study of inpatients, characterizing MRSA isolates using spa typing and molecular techniques.

rpoB.notes: The I572F mutation was associated with rifampin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated a new line probe assay (LiPA) kit for identifying Mycobacterium species and detecting drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It identified mutations in rpoB, katG, pncA, and gyrA associated with resistance to rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and levofloxacin, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The study used a line probe assay (LiPA) kit combined with DNA sequencing to detect mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of isolates of Salmonella enterica serovar Stanley, a serovar endemic to Asia and associated with travel.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the bla CMY-2 gene as a major contributor to extended-spectrum cephalosporin resistance in Salmonella enterica serovar Stanley isolates, along with the qnrS1 gene associated with plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis were used to characterize resistance mechanisms and genetic diversity.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli bacteriocins: antimicrobial efficacy and prevalence among isolates from patients with bacteraemia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the antimicrobial efficacy of colicins and microcins against uroseptic E. coli strains and highlights the prevalence of these bacteriocins among isolates from patients with bacteraemia.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based screening, susceptibility testing, and statistical analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Differences in genotype and virulence among four multidrug-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates belonging to the PMEN1 clone.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified genic differences in the blp bacteriocin locus and erythromycin resistance genes among PMEN1 strains, contributing to variations in virulence and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: The chemistry of peptidyltransferase center-targeted antibiotics: enzymatic resistance and approaches to countering resistance.

full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the enzymatic resistance mechanisms targeting the peptidyltransferase center of the bacterial ribosome, focusing on the roles of erm and cfr genes in mediating resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Review of literature and experimental studies on antibiotic resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of the Pseudomonas aeruginosa regulon controlled by the sensor kinase KinB and sigma factor RpoN.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the regulon controlled by the sensor kinase KinB and sigma factor RpoN in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, highlighting their roles in alginate production, motility, and virulence.
full_output.methodology: Microarray and proteomic analyses were performed on P. aeruginosa strains to identify genes regulated by KinB and RpoN.

full_output.paper_title: MpeR regulates the mtr efflux locus in Neisseria gonorrhoeae and modulates antimicrobial resistance by an iron-responsive mechanism.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MpeR as a regulator of the mtr efflux locus in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, showing that it modulates antimicrobial resistance through iron-responsive mechanisms. Key genes involved include mtrF, mtrR, and terC, which contribute to resistance against hydrophobic antimicrobials and tellurium.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized gene expression analysis, mutant construction, complementation, and susceptibility testing to investigate the role of MpeR in regulating antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

full_output.paper_title: Pneumococcal gene complex involved in resistance to extracellular oxidative stress.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a gene complex consisting of tlpA, spd0571, and msrAB that is crucial for Streptococcus pneumoniae's resistance to extracellular oxidative stress. Deletion of these genes significantly reduces survival under hydrogen peroxide stress, and their expression restores resistance.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, and survival assays under oxidative stress conditions were conducted to evaluate the role of the identified genes in oxidative stress resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibitors of aminoglycoside resistance activated in cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies aminoglycoside N-6'-acetyltransferase (AAC(6')-Ii) as a key enzyme responsible for resistance to kanamycin A in Enterococcus faecium and reports the development of prodrug compounds that can potentiate the antibacterial activity of kanamycin A against resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Enzyme inhibition assays, biosynthetic in vitro assays, and checkerboard MIC assays were used to evaluate the activity of the compounds and their effect on resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypes and genotypes of erythromycin-resistant Streptococcus pyogenes strains isolated from invasive and non-invasive infections from Mexico and the USA during 1999-2010.

mef A.evidence_note: The paper describes mef A as encoding an efflux system for resistance to 14- and 15-membered, but not 16-membered, ring macrolides, and associates it with the M phenotype of erythromycin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mef A, erm B, and erm TR as the primary genes responsible for erythromycin resistance in Streptococcus pyogenes isolates from Mexico and the USA. The M phenotype was linked to mef A, while the cMLS and iMLS phenotypes were associated with erm B and erm TR, respectively.
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic analysis of erythromycin-resistant isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Cloning of SHV-2, OHIO-1, and OXA-6 beta-lactamases and cloning and sequencing of SHV-1 beta-lactamase.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the cloning and sequencing of the SHV-1, SHV-2, OHIO-1, and OXA-6 beta-lactamase genes, highlighting their roles in conferring resistance to penicillins and cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Molecular cloning and sequencing of beta-lactamase genes.

full_output.paper_title: Dominance of serotype Ia among group B Streptococci causing invasive infections in nonpregnant adults in Portugal.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the erm(TR) gene as the most frequently found among erythromycin-resistant isolates and the bovine-associated tet(O) gene in a minority of tetracycline-resistant isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study involved antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR for detecting resistance genes, and molecular typing methods such as PFGE and MLST.

full_output.paper_title: Multisite reproducibility of the broth microdilution method for susceptibility testing of Nocardia species.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the reproducibility of broth microdilution susceptibility testing for Nocardia species and identified issues with certain antimicrobial agents like ceftriaxone, imipenem, sulfamethoxazole, and tigecycline. It also proposed N. nova ATCC BAA-2227 as a quality control organism.
full_output.methodology: The study involved six laboratories performing broth microdilution testing on Nocardia isolates, evaluating antimicrobial susceptibility and reproducibility.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of plasmid mediated bla(TEM-1) and bla(CTX-M-15) type extended spectrum beta-lactamases in patients with sepsis.

full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and conjugation experiments were used to detect and validate the presence of bla(TEM-1) and bla(CTX-M-15) genes.

full_output.paper_title: Structure and function of OprD protein in Pseudomonas aeruginosa: from antibiotic resistance to novel therapies.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the OprD protein in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, highlighting its role in carbapenem resistance through deficiencies and mutations affecting its structure and function.
full_output.methodology: Functional studies and structural analysis of the OprD protein.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity of genotypes in CTX-M-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated in different hospitals in Brazil
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized CTX-M, TEM, and SHV beta-lactamase genes in CTX-M-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Brazil, highlighting the diversity of genotypes and the frequent association of different ESBL types.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and PFGE analysis were used to characterize the genes and genomic diversity of the isolates.

full_output.key_findings: All Mycobacterium massiliense isolates were susceptible to amikacin and clarithromycin but resistant to cefoxitin, ciprofloxacin, doxycycline, tobramycin, and sulfamethoxazole.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanisms of action of escapin, a bactericidal agent in the ink secretion of the sea hare Aplysia californica: rapid and long-lasting DNA condensation and involvement of the OxyR-regulated oxidative stress pathway.

full_output.paper_title: A novel membrane protein, VanJ, conferring resistance to teicoplanin.

full_output.paper_title: First national survey of antibiotic susceptibility of the Bacteroides fragilis group: emerging resistance to carbapenems in Argentina.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the cfiA gene in 8 out of 23 isolates of the Bacteroides fragilis group, which conferred resistance to carbapenems.

full_output.paper_title: Persistence of Borrelia burgdorferi in rhesus macaques following antibiotic treatment of disseminated infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that Borrelia burgdorferi can persist in rhesus macaques despite antibiotic treatment, suggesting the existence of antibiotic-tolerant persisters.
full_output.methodology: The study used nonhuman primates to evaluate the efficacy of antibiotic treatments against disseminated Borrelia burgdorferi infection through various detection methods including xenodiagnosis, culture, PCR, and immunofluorescence.

full_output.paper_title: Cell wall antibiotics provoke accumulation of anchored mCherry in the cross wall of Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that cell wall antibiotics like penicillin and moenomycin cause the accumulation of mCherry-fused proteins at the cross wall of Staphylococcus aureus, highlighting the role of SrtA in this process.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized fluorescent protein fusions, microscopy, and genetic manipulations to analyze protein localization and the effects of antibiotics on cell wall structure.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of multidrug resistance in bacterial uropathogens from Kathmandu, Nepal.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of multidrug resistance in bacterial uropathogens, particularly in Escherichia coli and Citrobacter spp., with resistance to multiple antibiotic classes including beta-lactams, quinolones, and sulfonamides.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed bacterial isolates from urine samples, determined antibiotic resistance patterns, and examined plasmid profiles and conjugation for resistance transfer.

full_output.paper_title: MRSA USA300 at Alaska Native Medical Center, Anchorage, Alaska, USA, 2000-2006.
full_output.key_findings: The study documents the emergence and dominance of MRSA USA300 among clinical isolates in Anchorage, Alaska, from 2000 to 2006. USA300 became the exclusive genotype by 2006, indicating a significant shift in the MRSA population.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed MRSA isolates through genotyping, MLST, SCC mec typing, and PVL detection, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Diverse mobilized class 1 integrons are common in the chromosomes of pathogenic Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies diverse mobilized class 1 integrons in the chromosomes of pathogenic Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates, highlighting the role of genomic islands and lateral gene transfer in the dissemination of resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the integrons and their genetic contexts.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic polymorphisms and drug susceptibility in four isolates of Leishmania tropica obtained from Canadian soldiers returning from Afghanistan.

PTR1.notes: PTR1 mutations observed in L. tropica isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified genetic polymorphisms in the pteridine reductase 1 (PTR1) gene of Leishmania tropica isolates from Canadian soldiers, with some SNPs showing conservation. All isolates were sensitive to amphotericin B, miltefosine, Pentostam, and paromomycin, but resistant to fluconazole.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization via PFGE and sequencing of PTR1 and other genes, along with in vitro drug susceptibility testing using THP-1 cells.

full_output.paper_title: Hierarchy of protection against lethal systemic F. tularensis LVS challenge after vaccination of mice with LVS or the variants LVS-G, LVS-R, and heat-killed LVS
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes such as IFN-γ, IL-6, TNF-α, and others whose expression levels correlate with the degree of protection conferred by different Francisella vaccines in mice.
full_output.methodology: The study uses in vitro co-culture experiments and qRT-PCR to analyze gene expression in splenocytes from vaccinated mice.

full_output.paper_title: Purification and activity testing of the full-length YycFGHI proteins of Staphylococcus aureus.

YycG.validation_method: activity testing in detergent-micelle-model and phospholipid-liposome-model

mutations_found.effect_on_function: higher activity in the liposome system compared to the wild-type
mutations_found.validated_by: activity tests in detergent-micelle-model and phospholipid-liposome-model

yycG.notes: The YycG(Y306N) mutant showed higher activity in the liposome system compared to the wild-type.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: increased activity in the liposome system

YycG.notes: point mutation in the putative signal sensing PAS domain
YycG.evidence_note: The paper describes a point mutation (T916A) in the cytoplasmic PAS domain of YycG, which leads to a Y306N amino acid change. This mutation was shown to increase the activity of the kinase in a phospholipid-liposome model.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the full-length YycG and YycF proteins of Staphylococcus aureus, focusing on their activity and interactions. A mutation in YycG (Y306N) was found to affect kinase activity, suggesting a potential role in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Protein expression, purification, and activity testing in detergent-micelle and phospholipid-liposome models.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and characterization of a novel polysaccharide deacetylase C (PdaC) from Bacillus subtilis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes PdaC, a novel polysaccharide deacetylase from Bacillus subtilis, which exhibits both MurNAc and GlcNAc deacetylase activities, playing a role in peptidoglycan modification and lysozyme resistance.
full_output.methodology: Gene disruption, enzymatic activity assays, and structural analysis were used to characterize PdaC.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and virulence factors in Escherichia coli from Swedish dairy calves.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that antimicrobial resistance was common in E. coli from preweaned dairy calves, especially in calves from herds with neonatal diarrhea problems. The virulence genes espP, irp, and fyuA were more commonly found in resistant E. coli isolates compared to fully susceptible ones.
full_output.methodology: The study involved analyzing E. coli isolates from fecal samples of calves using PCR for virulence genes and determining antimicrobial susceptibility through MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Feedback inhibition by thiols outranks glutathione depletion: a luciferase-based screen reveals glutathione-deficient γ-ECS and glutathione synthetase mutants impaired in cadmium-induced sulfate assimilation.

mutations_found.validated_by: root elongation assays and HPLC-MS analysis

At4g23100.evidence_note: The mutation in At4g23100 (nrc1) was identified as a C→T mutation in the fourth exon causing a Pro → Leu (P214L) change in the amino acid sequence of γ-ECS.

mutations_found.validated_by: root elongation assays and HPLC-MS analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the γ-glutamylcysteine synthetase (At4g23100) and glutathione synthetase (At5g27380) genes that impair cadmium-induced sulfate assimilation in Arabidopsis. These mutations lead to reduced responsiveness to cadmium, highlighting the importance of glutathione biosynthesis in the plant's response to heavy metal stress.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screen using a cadmium-inducible luciferase reporter, mutagenesis, HPLC-MS analysis, and root elongation assays.

full_output.paper_title: A novel non-homologous recombination-mediated mechanism for Escherichia coli unilateral flagellar phase variation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the flnA gene encoding the H17 flagellin and reveals that the unilateral flagellar phase variation in the H17 strain is caused by the excision of the flnA region, mediated by the tyrosine recombinase Int1157 through non-homologous recombination.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR, and mutagenesis experiments were used to identify the flnA gene and analyze the mechanism of flagellar phase variation.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of OXA-48-Type Carbapenemase-Producing Enterobacteriaceae in German Hospitals
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the emergence of OXA-48 and OXA-162 carbapenemases in Enterobacteriaceae isolates in Germany, highlighting their role in carbapenem resistance and the potential for horizontal gene transfer.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, conjugation assays, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Extending the Definition of the GyrB Quinolone Resistance-Determining Region in Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA Gyrase for Assessing Fluoroquinolone Resistance in M. tuberculosis.

gyrB.validation_method: DNA gyrase inhibition assays and MIC measurements

mutations_found.validated_by: DNA gyrase inhibition assays and MIC measurements
DNA gyrase inhibition assays and MIC measurements
DNA gyrase inhibition assays and MIC measurements
DNA gyrase inhibition assays and MIC measurements

gyrB.notes: All mutations were experimentally validated and shown to confer fluoroquinolone resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies four GyrB mutations (D500A, N538T, T539P, and E540V) that contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, expanding the defined quinolone resistance-determining region of GyrB.
full_output.methodology: Experimental validation through DNA gyrase inhibition assays and MIC measurements.
full_output.sample_size: 4 clinical isolates with GyrB substitutions and 1 reference strain

full_output.paper_title: First description of KPC-2-producing Pseudomonas putida in Brazil.

arr-6.genetic_context: class 1 integron containing the dhfr XVb gene and the new allele arr-6
arr-6.evidence_note: The paper states that the arr-6 allele codes for resistance to rifampin.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first case of a KPC-2-producing Pseudomonas putida isolate in Brazil, highlighting the presence of the blaKPC-2 gene and a novel rifampin resistance allele arr-6.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic and biochemical characterization of a novel metallo-β-lactamase, TMB-1, from an Achromobacter xylosoxidans strain isolated in Tripoli, Libya.

blaTMB-1.source: Achromobacter xylosoxidans strain isolated in Tripoli, Libya
blaTMB-1.evidence_note: The TMB-1 β-lactamase has lower k cat values than both DIM-1 and GIM-1 with cephalosporins and carbapenems.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TMB-1, a novel metallo-β-lactamase from Achromobacter xylosoxidans, which confers resistance to carbapenems and cephalosporins through hydrolytic activity.
full_output.methodology: Genetic and biochemical characterization including purification, kinetic analysis, and sequence analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Antigen 85C inhibition restricts Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth through disruption of cord factor biosynthesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies I3-AG85 as a novel inhibitor of Ag85C, which restricts Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth by disrupting cord factor biosynthesis. I3-AG85 shows activity against drug-susceptible and drug-resistant M. tuberculosis strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used NMR spectroscopy, resazurin assay, and lipid synthesis assays to characterize the inhibitory effects of I3-AG85 on Ag85C and its impact on M. tuberculosis growth and lipid synthesis.

full_output.paper_title: IMP-29, a novel IMP-type metallo-β-lactamase in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

blaIMP-29.validation_method: expression in E. coli and biochemical analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IMP-29, a novel IMP-type metallo-β-lactamase in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which efficiently hydrolyzes carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, cloning, and biochemical analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Two novel class I integron arrays containing IMP-18 metallo-β-lactamase gene in Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates from Puerto Rico.

blaIMP-18.genetic_context: class I integron containing bla IMP-18 and bla OXA-224 in nine isolates, and bla IMP-18 and bla OXA-2 in a new arrangement in two isolates
blaIMP-18.source: Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates from Puerto Rico
blaIMP-18.evidence_note: The paper describes the identification of blaIMP-18 in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates and its association with class I integrons.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two novel class I integron arrays containing the IMP-18 metallo-β-lactamase gene and a new variant, blaOXA-224, in Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates from Puerto Rico.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis were used to analyze the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Deletion of TnAbaR23 results in both expected and unexpected antibiogram changes in a multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii strain.

sul1.validation_method: experimental validation through deletion mutant analysis

aacC1.validation_method: experimental validation through deletion mutant analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that deletion of TnAbaR23 in Acinetobacter baumannii leads to increased susceptibility to sulfamethoxazole and gentamicin, highlighting the role of this transposon in multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genetic deletion of TnAbaR23 and subsequent antimicrobial susceptibility testing of mutants.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem resistance in Elizabethkingia meningoseptica is mediated by metallo-β-lactamase BlaB.

blaB.validation_method: expression in E. coli, enzymatic activity assays, and immunoassays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies BlaB as the primary metallo-β-lactamase responsible for carbapenem resistance in Elizabethkingia meningoseptica, demonstrating its functional role in hydrolyzing imipenem and meropenem.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, enzymatic activity assays, Western blotting, and immunoassays were used to characterize BlaB's role in carbapenem resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and SNP analyses demonstrate a distant separation of the hospital and community-associated clades of Enterococcus faecium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies core genomic differences between hospital-associated (HA) and community-associated (CA) clades of Enterococcus faecium, highlighting a 3.5-4.2% divergence in concatenated gene sequences and clade-specific SNPs.
full_output.methodology: Genomic and SNP analysis of 100 genes from 21 E. faecium genomes to determine core genomic differences between HA and CA clades.

full_output.paper_title: The G671V variant of MRP1/ABCC1 links doxorubicin-induced acute cardiac toxicity to disposition of the glutathione conjugate of 4-hydroxy-2-trans-nonenal.

MRP1.validation_method: expression in HEK293 cells and transport assays

MRP1.notes: associated with increased doxorubicin-induced cardiac toxicity

full_output.key_findings: The G671V variant of MRP1 is associated with increased doxorubicin-induced cardiac toxicity due to reduced efflux of GS-HNE, leading to increased intracellular accumulation of doxorubicin and oxidative stress.
full_output.methodology: Expression of MRP1 variants in HEK293 cells, transport assays, cytotoxicity studies, and measurement of GSH/GSSG ratios.

full_output.paper_title: Distinguishing colonization from infection with Staphylococcus aureus in diabetic foot ulcers with miniaturized oligonucleotide arrays: a French multicenter study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies lukDE as a strong predictor of favorable outcomes in uninfected diabetic foot ulcers caused by Staphylococcus aureus, highlighting its potential utility in guiding clinical decisions.
full_output.methodology: Use of oligonucleotide DNA arrays to analyze S. aureus strains for virulence and resistance genes, along with statistical analysis of associations between gene presence and wound outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Longitudinal study of the persistence of antimicrobial-resistant campylobacter strains in distinct Swine production systems on farms, at slaughter, and in the environment.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that antimicrobial-resistant Campylobacter coli strains persisted in both antimicrobial-free (ABF) and conventional swine production systems on farms, at slaughter, and in the environment. High levels of resistance to tetracycline, ciprofloxacin, and macrolides were observed, with significant associations between antimicrobial use and resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting and analyzing Campylobacter isolates from swine and their environments across multiple production stages, with antimicrobial susceptibility testing and statistical analysis of resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Ribosome clearance by FusB-type proteins mediates resistance to the antibiotic fusidic acid.

fusB.mechanism: binds to elongation factor G (EF-G) and promotes the dissociation of stalled ribosome⋅EF-G⋅GDP complexes
fusB.validation_method: binding studies, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), crystallography, and biochemical experiments

fusC.mechanism: binds to elongation factor G (EF-G) and promotes the dissociation of stalled ribosome⋅EF-G⋅GDP complexes
fusC.validation_method: binding studies, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), crystallography, and biochemical experiments

full_output.key_findings: FusB-type proteins mediate resistance to fusidic acid by binding to elongation factor G (EF-G) and promoting the dissociation of stalled ribosome-EF-G-GDP complexes, thus allowing ribosomes to resume translation.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical and biophysical studies, including binding assays, isothermal titration calorimetry, crystallography, and kinetic experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports a multidrug-resistant HBV strain in a Turkish patient, showing resistance to lamivudine, adefovir, entecavir, and tenofovir. Key mutations identified include rtM204V, rtN236T, rtL180M, rtV173L, rtA181V, rtL80V, and rtQ215H.
full_output.methodology: Direct sequencing, line probe assay, and clonal analysis were used to detect polymerase gene mutations in HBV.

full_output.paper_title: Wild coastline birds as reservoirs of broad-spectrum-β-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae in Miami Beach, Florida.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified CMY-2 and CTX-M-15 as the most common resistance determinants in broad-spectrum-beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae isolated from wild birds in Miami Beach, Florida.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Using nucleic acid microarrays to perform molecular epidemiology and detect novel β-lactamases: a snapshot of extended-spectrum β-lactamases throughout the world.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two novel β-lactamase variants, bla SHV-129 and bla KPC-11, in clinical isolates. These genes confer resistance to various β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized nucleic acid microarrays combined with PCR-sequencing to detect and characterize β-lactamase genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: High efficiency recombineering in lactic acid bacteria.

ddl.mechanism: mutation in active site reduces vancomycin resistance
ddl.validation_method: mutation of active site residue F258Y led to decreased vancomycin resistance

ddl.notes: mutation in active site reduces vancomycin resistance
ddl.evidence_note: The paper describes the mutation of the ddl gene in Lactobacillus reuteri, resulting in a single amino acid change (F258Y) that reduces vancomycin resistance. The mutation was validated through mutagenesis and MIC testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the use of ssDNA recombineering to introduce targeted mutations in Lactobacillus reuteri, reducing its intrinsic vancomycin resistance through a single amino acid change in the d-Ala-d-Ala ligase (Ddl) enzyme.
full_output.methodology: ssDNA recombineering was used to introduce targeted mutations in L. reuteri, with validation through PCR, sequencing, and vancomycin susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: O157:H7 and O104:H4 Vero/Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli outbreaks: respective role of cattle and humans.

ter.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The O104:H4 E. coli strain is a chimeric pathogen combining characteristics of VTEC and EAggEC, including the presence of the Vtx2a gene, the absence of AE lesion genes, and the presence of aggR, aafA, and set1 genes. Additionally, it produces a CTX-M15 ESBL.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis and molecular techniques were used to characterize the O104:H4 strain.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of bacterial virulence: drug-like molecules targeting the Salmonella enterica PhoP response regulator.
full_output.key_findings: Eight compounds were identified that inhibit the formation of the PhoP-DNA complex necessary for gene regulation in Salmonella enterica by disrupting DNA binding through an allosteric mechanism.
full_output.methodology: A hybrid approach combining computational virtual screening and experimental validation using EMSA, native PAGE, SEC, and FRET assays was employed to identify and characterize PhoP inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: The TPR domain in the host Cyp40-like cyclophilin binds to the viral replication protein and inhibits the assembly of the tombusviral replicase.

CPR7.mechanism: Inhibits TBSV replication by binding to the RNA-binding region of p33 replication protein
CPR7.validation_method: Cell-free replication assay with purified recombinant Cpr7p and its domains

CPR6.mechanism: Interacts with p33 replication protein but does not significantly inhibit TBSV replication

At5g48570.mechanism: Inhibits TBSV replication by interacting with p33 and p92 replication proteins
At5g48570.validation_method: CFE-based TBSV replication assay with purified recombinant At5g48570 and its TPR domain

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CPR7 and its TPR domain as potent inhibitors of TBSV replication, demonstrating that Cyp40-like cyclophilins and their TPR domains can interfere with viral RNA recruitment and replicase assembly. Additionally, plant-derived Cyp40-like proteins, such as At5g48570, exhibit similar antiviral effects.
full_output.methodology: Cell-free replication assays, MYTH assays, and deletion studies in yeast.

full_output.paper_title: Specialized peptidoglycan hydrolases sculpt the intra-bacterial niche of predatory Bdellovibrio and increase population fitness.

bd3459.validation_method: deletion mutagenesis, electron microscopy, and in vitro activity assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bd0816 and bd3459 as peptidoglycan hydrolases critical for Bdellovibrio's predatory invasion, enabling prey cell rounding and preventing double invasions.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomics, RT-PCR, deletion mutagenesis, electron microscopy, and in vitro enzymatic assays.

full_output.paper_title: Independent large scale duplications in multiple M. tuberculosis lineages overlapping the same genomic region.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple independent large-scale duplications in the same genomic region of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, occurring in strains from different lineages and showing varied boundaries, suggesting potential genomic instability or selective advantages.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and PCR validation were used to analyze the duplications in various M. tuberculosis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Over-expression of a cytochrome P450 is associated with resistance to pyriproxyfen in the greenhouse whitefly Trialeurodes vaporariorum.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CYP4G61 as a cytochrome P450 gene strongly associated with pyriproxyfen resistance in Trialeurodes vaporariorum, with high over-expression levels observed in resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis and quantitative PCR were used to identify and validate the over-expression of CYP4G61 in pyriproxyfen-resistant strains.

full_output.paper_title: A molecular study on the prevalence and virulence potential of Aeromonas spp. recovered from patients suffering from diarrhea in Israel.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various virulence genes in Aeromonas isolates from Israeli patients with diarrhea, including ahyB, pla, lip, lipH3, apl-1, fla, lafA, aexU, act, aerA, hlyA, alt, ast, TTSS ascV, TTSS ascF-ascG, and aexT. Most isolates were resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics but susceptible to third-generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify virulence genes and assess antibiotic resistance in Aeromonas isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Borrelia burgdorferi requires the alternative sigma factor RpoS for dissemination within the vector during tick-to-mammal transmission.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies RpoS as essential for Borrelia burgdorferi dissemination during tick-to-mammal transmission, and shows that ospC functions exclusively within the mammal.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, phenotypic analysis, qRT-PCR, and microscopy techniques were used to investigate the role of RpoS and ospC in spirochete dissemination.

full_output.paper_title: High-resolution melting analysis of the single nucleotide polymorphism hot-spot region in the rpoB gene as an indicator of reduced susceptibility to rifaximin in Clostridium difficile.

mutations_found.protein_change: amino acid substitutions associated with reduced susceptibility to rifaximin

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 16 different rpoB sequence-types and 24 SNPs, with 15 SNPs located in the rpoB hot-spot region, leading to 11 different HRM curve profiles. Eleven SNPs resulted in amino acid substitutions associated with reduced susceptibility to rifaximin.
full_output.methodology: High-resolution melting analysis and sequencing of the rpoB gene in 348 C. difficile strains.

full_output.paper_title: Hospital and community ampicillin-resistant Enterococcus faecium are evolutionarily closely linked but have diversified through niche adaptation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes and mutations associated with ampicillin resistance in Enterococcus faecium, including the pbp5 gene with mutations in the C-terminal region, and unique genes in canine isolates involved in xylopolysaccharide metabolism.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, MLST, Southern blot analysis, PCR, and DNA sequence analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Peritoneal dialysis-related peritonitis due to Staphylococcus aureus: a single-center experience over 15 years.

mecA.validation_method: detection of the mecA gene via PCR

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the mecA gene in 11.3% of Staphylococcus aureus isolates, which is associated with oxacillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and susceptibility testing were used to detect the mecA gene and evaluate oxacillin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Genes that influence swarming motility and biofilm formation in Variovorax paradoxus EPS.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Varpa_4680 (wbuB) and Varpa_5900 (pilY1) as genes influencing swarming motility and biofilm formation in Variovorax paradoxus EPS. Additionally, the two-component system shkRS is implicated in regulating these surface behaviors.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, complementation experiments, qPCR, and biofilm/swarm assays were used to investigate the roles of identified genes in surface behaviors.

full_output.paper_title: Contribution of a genomic accessory region encoding a putative cellobiose phosphotransferase system to virulence of Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates a genomic island in Streptococcus pneumoniae that includes a putative cellobiose phosphotransferase system (PTS), a ROK family protein, and a putative sulfatase. Deletion of this island led to reduced virulence in murine models, indicating its role in pneumococcal pathogenesis and colonization.
full_output.methodology: The study used mutational analysis and in vivo virulence models to assess the role of the genomic island in Streptococcus pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: 3-aminopiperidine-based peptide analogues as the first selective noncovalent inhibitors of the bacterial cysteine protease IdeS.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of piperidine-containing peptide analogues as noncovalent inhibitors of the bacterial cysteine protease IdeS, demonstrating their effectiveness in inhibiting IdeS activity with varying degrees of selectivity towards other proteases.
full_output.methodology: Peptide analogues were synthesized and tested for inhibitory activity against IdeS using SDS-PAGE and surface plasmon resonance spectroscopy.

full_output.paper_title: A new approach for pyrazinamide susceptibility testing in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

mutations_found.validated_by: measured POA efflux rate and BACTEC460 susceptibility

pncA.notes: Mutations in pncA were associated with reduced pyrazinamidase activity and increased pyrazinamide resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the pncA gene, which encodes pyrazinamidase, as a cause of pyrazinamide resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. These mutations were linked to reduced enzymatic activity and increased resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study measured pyrazinoic acid (POA) efflux rates and used BACTEC460 susceptibility testing to evaluate pyrazinamide resistance in M. tuberculosis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Genome sequence of Staphylococcus aureus strain 11819-97, an ST80-IV European community-acquired methicillin-resistant isolate.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the genome sequence of a European community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolate, ST80-IV, and identifies the fusidic acid resistance gene fusB on a plasmid.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and annotation using Illumina and Roche platforms.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a highly transmissible animal-independent Staphylococcus aureus ST398 clone with distinct genomic and cell adhesion properties.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the ST398 MSSA clone as a highly transmissible strain with distinct genomic features, including the presence of immune evasion genes chp and scn, and cadmium resistance genes cadX, cadD, and ermT. These genes contribute to the adaptability and persistence of the ST398 MSSA clone in human populations.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR, and comparative genomic analysis were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in the ST398 MSSA clone.
full_output.sample_size: 48 ST398 MSSA clinical isolates and 5 LA-ST398 MRSA isolates

full_output.paper_title: VP16 Is Expressed in Phase I but Remains in the Cytoplasm
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that VP16 is expressed during Phase I of HSV-1 reactivation but remains in the cytoplasm, and its transactivation function is crucial for Phase II reactivation. Human Oct-1 enhances VP16-mediated transactivation during Phase II.
full_output.methodology: The study used qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence microscopy, and gel-shift assays to analyze VP16 and Oct-1 function during HSV-1 reactivation.

full_output.paper_title: Fructose-bisphophate aldolase exhibits functional roles between carbon metabolism and the hrp system in rice pathogen Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola.
full_output.key_findings: The fbaB gene is required for full virulence and growth of Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola in rice, and its mutation reduces the ability to utilize fructose, pyruvate, and malate. The gene is negatively regulated by HrpG and HrpX.
full_output.methodology: Mutant construction, complementation, growth assays, EPS production analysis, and RT-PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Long-range transcriptional control of an operon necessary for virulence-critical ESX-1 secretion in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the espACD-Rv3613c-Rv3612c operon as a five-gene unit necessary for ESX-1 secretion in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It characterizes the major transcription start site of espA at -67 bp and demonstrates that EspR activates this promoter through enhancer-like sequences located far upstream, specifically within the e spA a ctivating r egion (EAR).
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RT-PCR, qRT-PCR, 5'-RACE, primer extension, RNA-seq, and site-directed mutagenesis to analyze the transcriptional regulation of the espACD-Rv3613c-Rv3612c operon and the role of EspR in its activation.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular mechanisms of drug resistance in natural Leishmania populations vary with genetic background.

CBS.validation_method: quantitative PCR and gene expression profiling

GCS.validation_method: quantitative PCR and gene expression profiling

MST.validation_method: Western blot analysis and gene expression profiling

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies variations in molecular mechanisms of antimonial resistance in Leishmania donovani populations, highlighting differences in gene expression and thiol levels between resistant and susceptible isolates.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR, Western blot analysis, HPLC-based thiol quantification, and in vitro stress phenotyping were used to analyze gene expression, protein levels, thiol content, and stress susceptibility.
