full_output.paper_title: Quorum-sensing and BvrR/BvrS regulation, the type IV secretion system, cyclic glucans, and BacA in the virulence of Brucella ovis: similarities to and differences from smooth brucellae.

bacA.notes: Inactivation of bacA did not affect splenic colonization in mice or behavior in J774.A1 murine macrophages.

cgs.notes: Defects in the synthesis of cyclic ß-1,2 glucans reduced the uptake of B. ovis PA in macrophages.

vjbR.notes: The Δ vjbR mutant was impaired in intracellular replication and showed strong attenuation in mice.

virB2.notes: Mutants with mutations in the type IV secretion system were severely attenuated in the mouse model.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: severe attenuation in the mouse model

virB.notes: A polar mutation in the virB operon resulted in severe attenuation in the mouse model.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the roles of bacA, cgs, vjbR, and the type IV secretion system in the virulence of Brucella ovis. Inactivation of these genes led to reduced macrophage uptake, impaired intracellular replication, and strong attenuation in mice.
full_output.methodology: The study used mutant strain construction, susceptibility assays, and intracellular survival experiments in macrophages to analyze the roles of specific genes in B. ovis virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence and characteristics of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) producing Enterobacteriaceae in food producing animals, minced meat and raw milk.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) genes, including CTX-M-1, CTX-M-14, CTX-M-15, CTX-M-117, CTX-M-186, SHV-12, TEM-1, and TEM-52, in Enterobacteriaceae isolated from food-producing animals, minced meat, and raw milk in Switzerland.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.sample_size: 334 fecal samples, 100 raw milk samples, 104 minced meat samples, and 67 E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Infection prevention and control interventions in the first outbreak of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infections in an equine hospital in Sweden.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes interventions to control the first outbreak of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in an equine hospital in Sweden, focusing on infection prevention and control measures.
full_output.methodology: The study involved environmental sampling, genotyping of isolates, and implementation of infection control protocols.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of extended-spectrum β-lactamase genes found among Escherichia coli isolates from duck and environmental samples obtained on a duck farm.

blaCTX-M-105.genetic_context: bla CTX-M-105 was located in a Tn 1721 -like element on pHNDD81-1 and is associated with an IS Ecp1-bla CTX-M -IS 903D-iroN Δ structure which has been seen in several cases associated with bla CTX-M-65 ( 7 , 33 ), bla CTX-M-24 ( 26 ), bla CTX-M-19 ( 24 ), and bla CTX-M-14 ( 17 ).

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) genes, including bla CTX-M-105, bla CTX-M-27, bla CTX-M-55, bla CTX-M-24e, and others, in Escherichia coli isolates from ducks and environmental samples. These genes confer resistance to various β-lactam antibiotics and other antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to identify and characterize ESBL genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and characterization of a lipopolysaccharide α,2,3-sialyltransferase from the human pathogen Helicobacter bizzozeronii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes two novel sialyltransferases, Hb-ST1 and Hb-ST2, in Helicobacter bizzozeronii, which are involved in the biosynthesis of sialylated lipopolysaccharides (LPS).
full_output.methodology: Genome analysis, PCR, cloning, expression in E. coli, biochemical assays, and structural analysis of LPS.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiological evaluation of water quality from urban watersheds for domestic water supply improvement.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes including blaTEM, aadA1, and tetC in pathogenic E. coli isolates from urban and agricultural sources in the Santa Ana River watershed.
full_output.methodology: PCR screening for antimicrobial resistance genes and disk diffusion assays for antimicrobial susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial-resistant strains of Clostridium difficile from North America.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial resistance in Clostridium difficile isolates from North America, with notable resistance to clindamycin, moxifloxacin, and rifampin, especially among PCR ribotype 027 strains.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using Etest strips against 316 C. difficile isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Sorting nexin 27 interacts with multidrug resistance-associated protein 4 (MRP4) and mediates internalization of MRP4.
full_output.key_findings: SNX27 interacts with MRP4 and mediates its internalization, leading to reduced cell surface expression and transport function of MRP4.
full_output.methodology: GST pull-down assays, co-immunoprecipitation, cell surface biotinylation, and siRNA knockdown experiments.

blaOXA-201.evidence_note: The paper describes blaOXA-201 as a variant of blaOXA-51-like genes associated with carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii.

blaOXA-113.evidence_note: The paper describes blaOXA-113 as a variant of blaOXA-51-like genes associated with carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii.

blaOXA-219.evidence_note: The paper describes blaOXA-219 as a variant of blaOXA-51 with an amino acid substitution (L167→V) and notes that IS Aba1 is associated with blaOXA-51-like genes, which can lead to carbapenem resistance.

blaOXA-200.evidence_note: The paper describes blaOXA-51 variants in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates and their correlation with clonal lineages.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes various blaOXA-51 variants in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates, showing their correlation with DiversiLab-defined clonal lineages and their role in carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of blaOXA-51-like genes and phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of terminal dimethylation on the resistance profile of α-N-heterocyclic thiosemicarbazones.

ABCG2.validation_method: genomic analyses (arrayCGH and FISH) revealed amplification of the ABCC1 gene on double minute chromosomal DNA in KP1089-resistant cells as well as overexpression of ABCC1 and ABCG2 on the protein level. KP1089 was further confirmed as a substrate of ABCC1 and ABCG2

full_output.key_findings: The study identified ABCC1 and ABCG2 as key mediators of resistance to KP1089, with ABCC1 showing significant amplification and overexpression in resistant cells. GSH depletion enhanced KP1089 activity, suggesting a role for GSH in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analyses (arrayCGH and FISH), Western blotting, and drug sensitivity assays were used to characterize resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: The RNA chaperone Hfq regulates antibiotic biosynthesis in the rhizobacterium Pseudomonas aeruginosa M18.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Hfq as a crucial regulator of antibiotic biosynthesis in Pseudomonas aeruginosa M18, influencing the production of pyoluteorin (Plt) and phenazine-1-carboxylic acid (PCA) through posttranscriptional and transcriptional mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study employed genetic manipulation, lacZ reporter assays, EMSA, and biochemical analyses to investigate Hfq's role in regulating antibiotic biosynthesis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the critical roles of IL-12p40, IL-12p35, and IFN-γ in survival of primary SchuS4 infection, highlighting their necessity for effective immune responses against virulent F. tularensis.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of cytokine profiling, flow cytometry, and genetic knockout models to assess immune responses in mice infected with F. tularensis SchuS4.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that ertapenem susceptibility was significantly associated with sepsis-related mortality in patients with bacteremia caused by ESBL-producing E. coli or K. pneumoniae. Isolates with ertapenem MICs >0.25 μg/ml had worse clinical outcomes compared to those with MICs ≤0.25 μg/ml.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective study analyzing carbapenem susceptibility and clinical outcomes in patients with ESBL-producing E. coli or K. pneumoniae bacteremia.

full_output.paper_title: Genome sequence of E. coli O104:H4 leads to rapid development of a targeted antimicrobial agent against this emerging pathogen.

EGR74047.validation_method: synthesis and fusion to R-type pyocin tail fiber, bactericidal activity against E. coli O104 strains

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a P22-like bacteriophage tailspike protein from E. coli O104:H4, which was engineered into an R-type pyocin to create AvR2-O104.1, a bactericidal agent specific for E. coli O104 strains.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, gene synthesis, plasmid construction, and bactericidal activity assays.

katG.mechanism: activation of isoniazid
katG.validation_method: MIC 90 determination, catalase activity assay, IVT assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the loss of the sigma factor SigI leads to isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis through reduced expression of katG, which is responsible for activating isoniazid. Despite this resistance, the ΔsigI mutant does not show reduced virulence or fitness.
full_output.methodology: Generation of ΔsigI mutant and complemented strain, MIC 90 determination, catalase activity assay, IVT assay, and in vivo infection models in mice.

full_output.paper_title: A unique modification of the eukaryotic initiation factor 5A shows the presence of the complete hypusine pathway in Leishmania donovani.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes deoxyhypusine hydroxylase (DOHH) from Leishmania donovani, demonstrating its role in the hypusine biosynthetic pathway and highlighting structural differences from the human homolog that could be exploited for drug development.
full_output.methodology: Sequence analysis, protein expression, purification, and activity assays were conducted to characterize DOHH.

full_output.paper_title: Novel conjugative transferable multiple drug resistance plasmid pAQU1 from Photobacterium damselae subsp. damselae isolated from marine aquaculture environment.

blaCARB-9 -like.validation_method: sequence analysis and homology to known beta-lactamases
blaCARB-9 -like.evidence_note: The paper describes blaCARB-9-like as a beta-lactamase gene with homology to known carbenicillinase genes.

floR.validation_method: sequence analysis and homology to known drug transporters
floR.evidence_note: The plasmid pAQU1 was shown to carry the floR gene, which encodes a drug transporter of the major facilitator superfamily known as chloramphenicol and florfenicol resistance proteins.

mef (A)-like.validation_method: sequence analysis and homology to known macrolide resistance genes

sul2.validation_method: sequence analysis and homology to known sulfonamide resistance genes

tet (M).evidence_note: The paper describes the presence of tet(M) in a plasmid from Photobacterium damselae subsp. damselae and its transfer to E. coli, with confirmation via PCR and MIC testing.

tet (B).validation_method: sequence analysis and homology to known tetracycline resistance genes
tet (B).evidence_note: The paper mentions that the plasmid pAQU1 contains tet (M) and tet (B) genes, which are associated with tetracycline resistance. The plasmid was transferred to E. coli, and the presence of these genes was confirmed through sequencing and hybridization.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes on the plasmid pAQU1, including bla CARB-9 -like, floR, mef (A)-like, sul2, tet (M), and tet (B), which confer resistance to various antibiotics such as carbenicillin, chloramphenicol, florfenicol, erythromycin, sulfonamide, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing, PCR, and MIC testing were used to identify and validate the AMR genes on the plasmid pAQU1.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and characterization of antibacterial dental monomers and composites.
full_output.key_findings: The study synthesized and characterized antibacterial methacrylate and methacrylamide monomers containing long-chain quaternary ammonium fluoride. Monomer II showed superior antibacterial activity against Streptococcus mutans compared to monomers I and III. Dental composites containing 3% monomer II effectively inhibited S. mutans biofilm formation without major adverse effects on mechanical properties.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of monomers, cytotoxicity and bactericidal tests, formulation and characterization of dental composites.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic analysis of the Cronobacter sakazakii O4 to O7 O-antigen gene clusters and development of a PCR assay for identification of all C. sakazakii O serotypes.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the O-antigen gene clusters of Cronobacter sakazakii O4 to O7 and developed a multiplex PCR assay for serotyping all C. sakazakii O serotypes.
full_output.methodology: Genomic DNA extraction, PCR amplification, sequencing, and bioinformatic analysis were used to analyze the O-antigen gene clusters and develop a PCR assay for serotyping.

full_output.paper_title: Polymorphisms in rpoS and Stress Tolerance Heterogeneity in Natural Isolates of Cronobacter sakazakii.

rpoS.notes: Mutations in rpoS lead to loss of function

full_output.paper_title: Ceftazidime resistance in Burkholderia pseudomallei: first report from India.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reports the first case of ceftazidime-resistant Burkholderia pseudomallei in India, highlighting the need for monitoring resistance trends in this pathogen.
full_output.methodology: Case report of a diabetic patient with disseminated melioidosis, including microbiological identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant Proteus mirabilis bloodstream infections: risk factors and outcomes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several TEM-type beta-lactamase genes (bla TEM-52, bla TEM-11, bla TEM-72, bla TEM-93, and bla TEM-111) in multidrug-resistant Proteus mirabilis isolates causing bloodstream infections, which confer resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing of bla genes in P. mirabilis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Dissemination of pCT-like IncK plasmids harboring CTX-M-14 extended-spectrum β-lactamase among clinical Escherichia coli isolates in the United Kingdom.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pCT-like IncK plasmids carrying the CTX-M-14 extended-spectrum beta-lactamase in clinical Escherichia coli isolates in the UK, highlighting their dissemination among diverse strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and PFGE analysis were used to detect and characterize the plasmids and their resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Functional role of the sarcin-ricin loop of the 23S rRNA in the elongation cycle of protein synthesis.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: mutant ribosomes were completely inactive in luciferase synthesis
mutations_found.origin: mutant ribosomes were purified to homogeneity and analyzed using kinetic assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that mutations in the sarcin-ricin loop (SRL) of the 23S rRNA, including G2655C, A2660U, and U2653Δ-C2667Δ, lead to defects in ribosome function, particularly affecting the binding of EF-G and translocation of the mRNA-tRNA complex. These mutations do not impair GTP hydrolysis on EF-Tu but significantly reduce the efficiency of translocation.
full_output.methodology: Kinetic assays, subunit association experiments, and in vitro translation assays were used to analyze the effects of SRL mutations on ribosome function.

full_output.paper_title: Presence and characterization of Campylobacter jejuni in organically raised chickens in Quebec.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 44% of Campylobacter jejuni isolates were resistant to tetracycline, 6% to erythromycin, 6% to azithromycin, and 2% to clindamycin. Intrinsic resistance to bacitracin and ceftiofur was also observed.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial resistance was evaluated using agar dilution, and phenotypic characteristics such as autoagglutination and chemotaxis were analyzed.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of intermediate in evolutionary model of enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli O157.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies strain LSU-61 as an intermediate in the evolutionary model of enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli O157, bridging the gap between O55:H7 and both sorbitol-fermenting (SF) and non-sorbitol-fermenting (NSF) O157 strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) typing and genomic analysis to characterize the evolutionary relationships among EHEC O157 strains.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of Escherichia coli ST131 pulsotypes, by epidemiologic traits, 1967-2009.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple pulsotypes of Escherichia coli ST131, with pulsotype 968 being the most prevalent, associated with fluoroquinolone resistance but not with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase production or bla CTX-M-15. Certain pulsotypes showed distinct temporal, geographic, and source-specific distributions.
full_output.methodology: PFGE analysis, statistical comparisons, and multivariable logistic regression were used to analyze the distribution and resistance traits of E. coli ST131 pulsotypes.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus ST398, New York and New Jersey, USA.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes 8 infections with methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus ST398 in the New York City area, highlighting the emergence of clinical infections with two distinct CC398 sequence types. Some isolates showed resistance to clindamycin and erythromycin, and one isolate was reported as oxacillin resistant despite lacking the mecA gene.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective typing of clinical S. aureus isolates, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PFGE, spa typing, and multilocus sequence typing.

full_output.paper_title: Update on resistance status of Anopheles gambiae s.s. to conventional insecticides at a previous WHOPES field site, "Yaokoffikro", 6 years after the political crisis in Côte d'Ivoire.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high-frequency mutations in the L1014F kdr and ace-1 G119S genes, which contribute to resistance against pyrethroids, DDT, carbamates, and organophosphates in Anopheles gambiae s.s. populations from Yaokoffikro. Additionally, increased enzymatic activities of NSE and GST were observed, indicating potential metabolic resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: PCR analysis and biochemical assays were used to detect resistance genes and enzymatic activities in Anopheles gambiae s.s. populations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MntC as a highly conserved cell surface protein in Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis that elicits protective immunity. MntC is expressed early during infection and is a promising candidate for a multiantigen vaccine against staphylococcal diseases.
full_output.methodology: The study involved cloning and characterizing MntC, assessing its expression in vivo, and evaluating its protective effects through active vaccination and passive immunization models in mice and infant rats.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic organization, tissue distribution and functional characterization of the rat Pate gene cluster.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the rat Pate gene cluster, showing that Pate exhibits antibacterial activity while Pate-F does not. Both genes are expressed in the male reproductive tract and respond to endotoxin challenges.
full_output.methodology: In silico analyses, RT-PCR, recombinant protein expression, and antibacterial activity assays.
full_output.sample_size: n=3 for tissue collection, n=5 for androgen ablation experiments

full_output.paper_title: Extensive genetic diversity, unique population structure and evidence of genetic exchange in the sexually transmitted parasite Trichomonas vaginalis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two distinct types of Trichomonas vaginalis (type 1 and type 2) with differences in metronidazole sensitivity and TVV infection rates. Evidence of genetic exchange is suggested, indicating a potential sexual life cycle.
full_output.methodology: Genetic diversity and population structure were analyzed using microsatellite markers and SNP data from T. vaginalis isolates collected globally.

full_output.paper_title: Spanish multicenter study of the epidemiology and mechanisms of amoxicillin-clavulanate resistance in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various beta-lactamase genes, including bla TEM-1, bla TEM-30, bla TEM-40, bla OXA-1, and plasmid-mediated AmpC beta-lactamases (bla CMY-2, bla DHA-1, bla CIT, bla ACC, bla EBC, bla MOX, and bla FOX) responsible for amoxicillin-clavulanate resistance in Escherichia coli. Additionally, a novel inhibitor-resistant TEM variant, TEM-185, was characterized.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to identify and characterize the resistance mechanisms in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A new family of membrane electron transporters and its substrates, including a new cell envelope peroxiredoxin, reveal a broadened reductive capacity of the oxidative bacterial cell envelope.

scsB.validation_method: genetic analysis and redox state assessment

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a new family of membrane electron transporters, ScsB, and characterizes its substrates, including a novel periplasmic peroxiredoxin, PprX, and a protein disulfide isomerase, ScsC. ScsB is essential for maintaining these proteins in a reduced state in the bacterial cell envelope.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, redox state assessment, purification, and in vitro activity assays were used to characterize the function of ScsB and its substrates.

full_output.paper_title: Structural evidence that colicin A protein binds to a novel binding site of TolA protein in Escherichia coli periplasm.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structural interaction between colicin A and TolA protein in E. coli, identifying the binding region of colicin A (residues 58-96) and detailing the molecular interactions involved in this complex formation.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, and surface plasmon resonance were used to analyze the structural and binding properties of the TA 53-107 -TolAIII complex.

full_output.paper_title: Contribution of efflux to the emergence of isoniazid and multidrug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

mutations_found.protein_change: STOP codon in position 1314 of the katG gene (codon 438)

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the katG gene, including a total deletion and a STOP codon, as contributing to isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Efflux pump overexpression plays a significant role in the development of resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used DNA sequencing, MIC determination, and efflux activity assays to investigate resistance mechanisms in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.sample_size: Four M. tuberculosis strains were studied.

full_output.paper_title: Macrolide resistance determination and molecular typing of Mycoplasma pneumoniae in respiratory specimens collected between 1997 and 2008 in The Netherlands.
full_output.key_findings: The study found no macrolide-resistant (MLr) Mycoplasma pneumoniae genotypes in the Netherlands between 1997 and 2008, despite the global rise in MLr strains. The pyrosequencing system was effective for determining MLr and molecular typing of M. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Pyrosequencing and nested PCR were used to detect macrolide resistance-associated mutations in the 23S rRNA gene and to determine M. pneumoniae subtypes.

full_output.paper_title: Drug and multidrug resistance among Mycobacterium leprae isolates from Brazilian relapsed leprosy patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in rpoB, folP1, and gyrA genes associated with drug resistance in Mycobacterium leprae isolates from Brazilian relapsed leprosy patients.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing of rpoB, folP1, and gyrA genes from skin biopsy samples.

full_output.paper_title: Group A Streptococcus secreted esterase hydrolyzes platelet-activating factor to impede neutrophil recruitment and facilitate innate immune evasion.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SsE, a secreted esterase from Group A Streptococcus (GAS), as a PAF acetylhydrolase that inactivates PAF, thereby reducing neutrophil recruitment and facilitating immune evasion.
full_output.methodology: Enzyme activity assays, TLC, LC-MS, neutrophil activation and chemotaxis assays, and in vivo infection models.

full_output.paper_title: Sialyl residues modulate LPS-mediated signaling through the Toll-like receptor 4 complex.
full_output.key_findings: Desialylation of TLR4 and MD2 enhances LPS-mediated NFκB signaling, and N-linked glycosylation sites on TLR4 are critical for its function.
full_output.methodology: Transfection, luciferase assay, immunoprecipitation, and FRET analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Role of the two component signal transduction system CpxAR in conferring cefepime and chloramphenicol resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae NTUH-K2044.

full_output.key_findings: The CpxAR two-component system contributes to resistance against cefepime and chloramphenicol in Klebsiella pneumoniae NTUH-K2044 by modulating efflux pump expression and outer membrane protein profiles.

full_output.methodology: Cloning, expression in E. coli, biochemical analysis, and MIC testing were used to characterize OXA-229.

full_output.paper_title: Characterizations of clinical isolates of clostridium difficile by toxin genotypes and by susceptibility to 12 antimicrobial agents, including fidaxomicin (OPT-80) and rifaximin: a multicenter study in Taiwan.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the gyrA and gyrB genes of Clostridium difficile isolates that conferred resistance to moxifloxacin, ciprofloxacin, and levofloxacin. Specifically, the Thr82→Ile mutation in gyrA and the Ser416→Ala and Glu466→Lys mutations in gyrB were found to independently confer resistance to moxifloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using agar dilution and broth microdilution methods. Partial sequencing of gyrA and gyrB genes was conducted for moxifloxacin-nonsusceptible isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study compares the transmissibility of different MRSA clones, highlighting that the Asian ST239-TW clone had a higher reproduction number than non-TW MRSA in ICU2, suggesting enhanced transmissibility.
full_output.methodology: The study used probabilistic tree reconstruction and maximum likelihood methods to estimate reproduction numbers and analyze MRSA transmission dynamics in two ICU settings.

full_output.paper_title: Intraspecies variation in the emergence of hyperinfectious bacterial strains in nature.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hyperinfectious Salmonella strains that exhibit increased virulence following in vivo passage, with variations in virulence characteristics among different serovars.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized virulence assays, transcriptome analysis, and bacterial culture techniques to investigate the development of hyperinfectious strains in Salmonella.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial drug resistance in Escherichia coli from humans and food animals, United States, 1950-2002.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a significant increase in antimicrobial resistance in E. coli isolates from humans and food animals between 1950 and 2002, with notable resistance to tetracycline, sulfonamide, and streptomycin. Multidrug resistance increased substantially over time.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of E. coli isolates from human and animal sources using antimicrobial susceptibility testing and statistical trend analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and mechanism of evolution of new alleles coding for the AIDA-I autotransporter of porcine pathogenic Escherichia coli.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of clonal complex 5 (CC5) methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates susceptible to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole in a Brazilian hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the emergence of clonal complex 5 (CC5) methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates susceptible to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (SXT) in a Brazilian hospital, highlighting shifts in MRSA epidemiology and the importance of SXT susceptibility as a marker for new MRSA clones.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial profile and drug susceptibility pattern of urinary tract infection in pregnant women at University of Gondar Teaching Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens causing urinary tract infections in pregnant women, with Escherichia coli being the most common isolate. High levels of resistance were observed to ampicillin, amoxicillin, tetracycline, and co-trimoxazole.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that the presence of the nalC mutation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa is associated with oxacillin resistance through the overproduction of the MexAB-OprM efflux system.

full_output.paper_title: Bacillus licheniformis BlaR1 L3 loop is a zinc metalloprotease activated by self-proteolysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the BlaR1 L3 loop as a zinc metalloprotease that is activated by self-proteolysis. Key residues in the L3 loop, including H212, E213, H216, D221, E253, D257, E274, Y272, and R304/R305, are critical for zinc binding and β-lactamase induction. Mutations in these residues disrupt the function of BlaR1, leading to reduced or absent β-lactamase induction.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, zinc-blot analysis, Western blotting, and β-lactamase induction assays were used to characterize the role of the BlaR1 L3 loop in β-lactam resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia infections in a general hospital: patient characteristics, antimicrobial susceptibility, and treatment outcome.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolates showed high susceptibility to colistin, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, and netilmicin, but low susceptibility to ticarcillin/clavulanic acid and ceftazidime.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility was tested using the agar dilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic synergy interaction against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from an abattoir effluent environment.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the synergistic efficacy of antibiotic combinations against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains isolated from an abattoir effluent. It found that cefepime, imipenem, and meropenem combined with amikacin showed significant in vitro synergy, suggesting potential therapeutic applications.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar dilution and Etest procedures for susceptibility and synergy testing, along with PCR for bacterial identification.

full_output.paper_title: Increase of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii infection in acute care hospitals in Taiwan: association with hospital antimicrobial usage.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a significant increase in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) infections in Taiwanese hospitals, correlating with the use of anti-pseudomonal carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed data from the Taiwan Nosocomial Infections Surveillance system and National Health Insurance claims to investigate the association between antimicrobial usage and CRAB infections.

full_output.paper_title: The antibiotic CJ-15,801 is an antimetabolite that hijacks and then inhibits CoA biosynthesis.
full_output.key_findings: CJ-15,801 is an antimetabolite that targets CoA biosynthesis by being phosphorylated by PanK II in S. aureus, forming P-CJ which inhibits PPCS, a key enzyme in the CoA biosynthesis pathway.
full_output.methodology: In vitro activity analyses, HPLC, and kinetic studies were used to characterize the interaction of CJ-15,801 with pantothenate kinase and phosphopantothenoylcysteine synthetase.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the PIB-Type ATPases present in Thermus thermophilus.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes three PIB-type ATPases in Thermus thermophilus, including CopA, CopB, and a putative Zn2+/Cd2+-ATPase, which are involved in heavy metal transport and resistance.
full_output.methodology: The genes were cloned, expressed, and functionally analyzed in both Thermus thermophilus and E. coli, with biochemical assays assessing ATPase and phosphatase activities.

full_output.paper_title: OmpA is the principal nonspecific slow porin of Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies OmpA as the principal nonspecific slow porin in Acinetobacter baumannii, which contributes to the low permeability of the outer membrane and plays a critical role in the intrinsic resistance to antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study characterizes the pore-forming function of OmpA through reconstitution assays and evaluates the impact of OmpA deficiency on antibiotic permeability and resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of RarA, a novel AraC family multidrug resistance regulator in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies RarA, a novel AraC-family transcriptional regulator in Klebsiella pneumoniae, which contributes to multidrug resistance by upregulating the oqxAB efflux pump. Overexpression of RarA leads to increased MICs for multiple antibiotics, including chloramphenicol, tetracycline, ciprofloxacin, norfloxacin, tigecycline, and olaquindox.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, mutagenesis, MIC testing, and real-time RT-PCR were used to analyze the role of RarA in multidrug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Pneumococcal interactions with epithelial cells are crucial for optimal biofilm formation and colonization in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that pneumococci form structured biofilms during nasopharyngeal colonization, which exhibit increased antibiotic resistance. Biofilms formed on epithelial cells show greater resistance to antibiotics compared to those on abiotic surfaces, highlighting the importance of bacterial-epithelial interactions in biofilm development and colonization.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized scanning electron microscopy, biofilm formation assays, and antibiotic susceptibility testing to analyze pneumococcal biofilm formation and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Coordinated phenotype switching with large-scale chromosome flip-flop inversion observed in bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a reversible large-scale chromosome flip-flop inversion in S. aureus strain Mu50Ω that drives coordinated phenotype switching between small colony variants (SCVs) and normal colony variants (NCVs).
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, PFGE, Southern blotting, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the genetic and phenotypic characteristics of the variants.

full_output.paper_title: A modular and optimized single marker system for generating Trypanosoma brucei cell lines expressing T7 RNA polymerase and the tetracycline repressor.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes a modular single marker plasmid (SmOx) for generating Trypanosoma brucei cell lines expressing T7 RNA polymerase and the tetracycline repressor. The plasmid was validated for expression of both transgenes in different strains and life cycle stages of T. brucei.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid construction, codon optimization, transfection, western blot analysis, and flow cytometry were used to validate the expression of T7 RNA polymerase and tetracycline repressor in T. brucei cell lines.

full_output.paper_title: Aminoglycoside multiacetylating activity of the enhanced intracellular survival protein from Mycobacterium smegmatis and its inhibition.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the aminoglycoside acetyltransferase activity of the enhanced intracellular survival (Eis) protein from Mycobacterium smegmatis (Eis_Msm) and compares its substrate specificity and acetylation profiles with those of Eis_Mtb. It identifies differences in the ability of Eis_Msm and Eis_Mtb to acetylate various aminoglycosides, highlighting the structural basis for these differences.
full_output.methodology: The study uses spectrophotometric assays, mass spectrometry, and kinetic analyses to characterize the acetylation activity of Eis_Msm and compare it with Eis_Mtb.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of isoniazid resistance-conferring mutations on the clinical presentation of isoniazid monoresistant tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Contribution of urease to colonization by Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli.

full_output.paper_title: Secretion of Clostridium difficile toxins A and B requires the holin-like protein TcdE.

full_output.paper_title: Pollutant-induced modulation in conformation and β-lactamase activity of human serum albumin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies increased expression of vraSR, dltA, and mprF genes in vancomycin-tolerant MRSA strains following exposure to vancomycin, daptomycin, and telavancin, indicating altered gene regulation in response to antimicrobial agents.

full_output.paper_title: Larval midgut modifications associated with Bti resistance in the yellow fever mosquito using proteomic and transcriptomic approaches.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes and proteins differentially expressed in a Bti-resistant Aedes aegypti strain, including proteases, alkaline phosphatases, and V-ATP synthase subunits, which may be involved in Bti resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses using microarrays and 2D-DIGE to compare gene and protein expression in Bti-resistant and susceptible Aedes aegypti strains.

full_output.paper_title: Biosynthesis of albomycin δ(2) provides a template for assembling siderophore and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase inhibitor conjugates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the abmE and abmI genes involved in the biosynthesis of albomycin δ2, a natural product antibiotic with potent antimicrobial activity. abmE encodes a carbamoyltransferase responsible for N-carbamoylation of the cytosine nucleoside, while abmI encodes an S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM)-dependent methyltransferase that methylates the N3 of the cytosine in albomycins.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation experiments, and biochemical characterization were used to determine the function of abmE and abmI.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that nine out of ten S. aureus strains developed reduced susceptibility to the nonoxinol-9 iodine complex, while only one strain showed reduced susceptibility to chlorhexidine digluconate. No cross-resistance to antibiotics was observed in any of the strains, though all isolates showed high resistance to penicillin G.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth macrodilution and agar disk diffusion methods to assess antimicrobial susceptibility and induced resistance through repeated passages with sub-lethal concentrations of disinfectants.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several genes associated with ExPEC plasmid pathogenicity islands (PAIs) that differentiate neonatal meningitis-associated Escherichia coli (NMEC) from fecal E. coli isolates (HFEC). These genes include aec35, ompTp, hlyF, cvaC, etsA, cvaA, etsB, cvaB5', iss, sfaS, iutA, 2093, 2101, cdtB, tsh, 2103, 2095, cvaB3', 2078, and papG1*. These genes were found to be more prevalent in NMEC isolates compared to HFEC isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used multiplex PCR genotyping and plasmid replicon typing to analyze the genetic differences between NMEC and HFEC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Predicting risk for death from MRSA bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that vancomycin MICs for most MRSA isolates were 1-2 µg/mL, and neither VISA nor hVISA strains were independently associated with increased risk for death. Patient factors such as age, cirrhosis, renal insufficiency, and nursing home residence were significant predictors of mortality.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing 699 episodes of MRSA bacteremia, including vancomycin MIC testing and clinical data analysis.

full_output.paper_title: On the origin of Mycobacterium ulcerans, the causative agent of Buruli ulcer.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that Mycobacterium ulcerans and other mycolactone-producing mycobacteria (MPM) form a single clonal group that evolved from a common Mycobacterium marinum progenitor. Key findings include the acquisition of the pMUM plasmid, which encodes mycolactone biosynthesis, and extensive gene loss, particularly in cell wall-related functions, which are under adaptive selection.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing of 35 mycobacterial isolates from diverse sources, followed by comparative genomic analysis to determine phylogenetic relationships and identify genetic variations.

full_output.paper_title: Polyclonal non multiresistant methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates from clinical cases of infection occurring in Palermo, Italy, during a one-year surveillance period.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified non-multiresistant MRSA isolates carrying SCC mec IV or V, with resistance to ciprofloxacin, macrolides, and tetracycline. ST22, ST8, and ST398 were the predominant sequence types.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, MLST, PCR for SCC mec, agr groups, ACME, and PVL genes, MLVF, and PFGE.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 47 Beijing family strains out of 55 M. tuberculosis isolates and found no significant correlation between drug resistance and the Beijing family genotype. It also reported 36.2% of Beijing family strains and 2.5% of non-Beijing family strains showing resistance to at least one drug.
full_output.methodology: MIRU-VNTR genotyping and drug susceptibility testing using the proportion method on Lowenstein-Jensen culture media.

full_output.paper_title: Studies on New Delhi Metallo-Beta-Lactamse-1 producing Acinetobacter baumannii isolated from donor swab in a tertiary eye care centre, India and structural analysis of its antibiotic binding interactions.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of biofilm formation, quorum sensing and infection in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by natural products-inspired organosulfur compounds.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized microplate-based screening assays, biofilm inhibition tests, quorum sensing reporter systems, and Drosophila infection models to evaluate the effects of organosulfur compounds on P. aeruginosa.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that alkaloid compounds from Cienfuegosia digitata Cav. exhibit potent antibacterial activity against methicillin and ampicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA/ARSA) strains, showing synergistic effects when combined with conventional antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study employed disc diffusion, MIC, MBC, time-kill assays, and FICI evaluation to assess the antibacterial efficacy of alkaloid compounds against MRSA/ARSA strains.

full_output.paper_title: Transmission dynamics of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae in the tertiary care hospital and the household setting.

full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and molecular typing techniques were used to characterize ESBL genes and their resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of extended-spectrum β-lactamase and Klebsiella pneumoniae Carbapenemase genes directly from blood cultures by use of a nucleic acid microarray.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates a nucleic acid microarray for detecting bla ESBL and bla KPC genes directly from blood cultures, showing high concordance with phenotypic testing.

full_output.paper_title: Stimulation of host immune defenses by a small molecule protects C. elegans from bacterial infection.

full_output.paper_title: Footprint of positive selection in Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum genome sequences suggests adaptive microevolution of the syphilis pathogen.

full_output.paper_title: Cationic antimicrobial peptides disrupt the Streptococcus pyogenes ExPortal.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that cationic antimicrobial peptides (CAPs) such as polymyxin B and human neutrophil peptide-1 (HNP-1) disrupt the ExPortal of Streptococcus pyogenes, leading to altered secretion of virulence factors like SpeB and SLO, but not SIC.
full_output.methodology: The study used fluorescence microscopy, electron microscopy, and biochemical assays to investigate the effects of CAPs on the ExPortal of S. pyogenes.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis WhiB4 regulates oxidative stress response to modulate survival and dissemination in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: WhiB4 is a redox-sensitive transcription factor that regulates the oxidative stress response in Mtb, affecting its survival and dissemination in vivo.
full_output.methodology: Genetic disruption, complementation, and biochemical analyses were used to study WhiB4's role in Mtb.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of acquired antimicrobial resistance genes.

sul1.evidence_note: The paper mentions 'sul1' in the context of resistance to sulfamethoxazole in the table of results.

mecA.mechanism: Altered binding site for beta-lactam antibiotics

catB9.evidence_note: The catB9 gene was found in all four K. pneumoniae isolates with an ID = 100%, but not in full length, consistent with all four testing phenotypically susceptible to chloramphenicol. One V. cholera isolate contained part of floR and tested phenotypically susceptible to florfenicol.

dfrA31.evidence_note: The paper mentions that 'dfrA1 , dfrA31 TMP TMP' in the context of V. cholerae isolate Vchole-002, indicating that dfrA31 is associated with trimethoprim resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents ResFinder, a web-based tool for identifying acquired antimicrobial resistance genes in whole-genome data. It successfully identifies resistance genes with high accuracy and agrees with phenotypic testing. The tool detects various resistance genes across different bacterial species, including beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, tetracycline resistance genes, and others.
full_output.methodology: ResFinder uses BLAST to identify acquired antimicrobial resistance genes in whole-genome data. It was evaluated on GenBank files and de novo-sequenced isolates, comparing in silico predictions with phenotypic testing.
full_output.sample_size: 1862 GenBank files, 23 de novo-sequenced isolates, 30 isolates from NCBI genomes database

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PanM as a GNAT homologue that lacks acetyltransferase activity but functions as an acetyl-CoA sensor, crucial for the maturation of pro-PanD into active PanD.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biochemical assays, genetic manipulations, and structural analysis to investigate the role of PanM in pro-PanD maturation.

full_output.paper_title: EGL-9 controls C. elegans host defense specificity through prolyl hydroxylation-dependent and -independent HIF-1 pathways.

egl-9.notes: egl-9(sa307) mutants exhibit enhanced susceptibility to S. aureus
egl-9.evidence_note: The paper states that egl-9(sa307) mutants exhibit enhanced susceptibility to S. aureus, and the mutation is a premature stop codon. The organism observed is Caenorhabditis elegans.

hif-1.notes: hif-1(ia4) mutants exhibit near wild-type susceptibility
hif-1.evidence_note: The paper describes hif-1(ia4) mutants as exhibiting near wild-type susceptibility, indicating that the mutation does not confer resistance.

vhl-1.notes: vhl-1(ok161) mutants exhibit near wild-type susceptibility
vhl-1.evidence_note: The paper states that vhl-1(ok161) mutants exhibit near wild-type susceptibility to S. aureus.

swan-1.notes: swan-1(ok267) mutants exhibit enhanced susceptibility to S. aureus
swan-1.evidence_note: The paper states that 'swan-1(ok267) mutants exhibit enhanced susceptibility to S. aureus' and describes the mutation as a loss-of-function.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies EGL-9, HIF-1, VHL-1, and SWAN-1 as critical regulators of host defense against S. aureus in C. elegans. Loss of egl-9 or swan-1 leads to enhanced susceptibility, while loss of hif-1 or vhl-1 does not significantly alter susceptibility. The findings highlight the dual role of HIF-1 in both inducing and repressing host defense genes.
full_output.methodology: Survival analysis, qRT-PCR, and genetic manipulation of C. elegans mutants.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity and mechanism of a scorpion venom peptide derivative in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: Kn2-7, a scorpion venom peptide derivative, exhibits enhanced antibacterial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including antibiotic-resistant strains, by binding to LTA and LPS.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity testing, MIC determination, transmission electron microscopy, and biolayer interferometry.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of E. officinalis on the cariogenic properties of Streptococcus mutans: a novel and alternative approach to suppress quorum-sensing mechanism.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that Emblica officinalis extracts inhibit the cariogenic properties of Streptococcus mutans by reducing biofilm formation, adherence, glucan synthesis, and cell surface hydrophobicity, as well as suppressing the expression of virulence-related genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used GC-MS, biofilm assays, adherence tests, and qRT-PCR to evaluate the effects of E. officinalis extracts on S. mutans.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance to paclitaxel in a cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer cell line is mediated by P-glycoprotein.

ABCB1.validation_method: Western blot and epirubicin accumulation assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies P-glycoprotein (encoded by ABCB1) as a key mediator of paclitaxel resistance in the cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer cell line IGROVCDDP. Overexpression of P-glycoprotein was confirmed at both the gene and protein levels, and its functional activity was demonstrated through epirubicin accumulation assays.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a TaqMan low-density array (TLDA) to analyze gene expression, Western blotting for protein validation, and epirubicin accumulation assays to assess P-glycoprotein functionality.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a Rifampin-Inactivating Glycosyltransferase from a Screen of Environmental Actinomycetes.

rgt1438.validation_method: disruption in the bacterial chromosome, resulting in a loss of antibiotic inactivation and a 4-fold decrease in MIC
rgt1438.genetic_context: located on a 43-kb contig (accession number JX028276) which showed 72% nucleotide and 69% protein identity to the N. brasiliensis element
rgt1438.source: Characterization of a Rifampin-Inactivating Glycosyltransferase from a Screen of Environmental Actinomycetes
rgt1438.evidence_note: The role of rgt1438 in rifampin resistance was confirmed by its disruption in the bacterial chromosome, resulting in a loss of antibiotic inactivation and a 4-fold decrease in MIC.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies rgt1438 as a rifampin resistance determinant from WAC1438 that inactivates rifampin through glycosylation, demonstrating a new mechanism of rifampin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, gene disruption, complementation, and enzyme activity assays were used to characterize the role of rgt1438 in rifampin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Altering the Proclivity towards Daptomycin Resistance in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Using Combinations with Other Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that combining daptomycin (DAP) with oxacillin (OXA) or clarithromycin (CLR) can significantly reduce the development of DAP resistance in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro antibiotic combination exposures and evaluated changes in DAP MICs, cell wall thickness, and membrane properties.

full_output.paper_title: Restricted gene flow among hospital subpopulations of Enterococcus faecium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hospital-associated lineages of Enterococcus faecium, including lineage 78, which exhibits ampicillin resistance and the presence of the esp virulence gene. These lineages are significantly associated with hospital isolates and show distinct evolutionary histories.
full_output.methodology: Bayesian population genetic analysis, MLST, and phylogenomic analysis were used to investigate the population structure of E. faecium.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and Functional Analysis of Nematocida Microsporidia
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies unique genomic features of Nematocida microsporidia, including the absence of certain metabolic pathways and the presence of specific gene families involved in host-parasite interactions.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, RNA-seq, and functional assays were employed to analyze the genomic and metabolic characteristics of Nematocida microsporidia.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and mechanistic basis for the inhibition of Escherichia coli RNA polymerase by T7 Gp2.

rpo.notes: The R1174A mutation in the β′ jaw domain of Eσ70 reduces RPo formation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the R1174A mutation in the β′ jaw domain of Eσ70 reduces RPo formation, highlighting the importance of this region in RNA polymerase function and its interaction with DNA.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis using NMR spectroscopy, biochemical assays, and genetic experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Expression, purification and characterization of enoyl-ACP reductase II, FabK, from Porphyromonas gingivalis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the FabK enzyme from Porphyromonas gingivalis, an enoyl-ACP reductase involved in the fatty acid synthesis pathway, and provides insights into its biochemical properties and potential as a drug target.
full_output.methodology: Molecular cloning, expression, purification, and enzymatic characterization of the FabK enzyme.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the organic hydroperoxide resistance system of Brucella abortus 2308.

ohr.validation_method: isogenic mutants and lacZ promoter fusions

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the organic hydroperoxide resistance system in Brucella abortus 2308, identifying Ohr as a detoxifier of organic hydroperoxides and OhrR as a transcriptional repressor of ohr and ohrR.
full_output.methodology: Generation of isogenic mutants, lacZ promoter fusions, and biochemical assays to assess resistance and gene regulation.

full_output.paper_title: Geographic variability and anti-staphylococcal activity of the chrysophaentins and their synthetic fragments.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies new chrysophaentin analogs, E2 and E3, and evaluates the antibacterial activity of natural chrysophaentins and synthetic fragments against various Staphylococcus aureus strains, highlighting their potential as antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial evaluation via microbroth dilution assay, determination of MIC 50, MIC 90, and MBC.

full_output.paper_title: Characterisation of MRSA strains isolated from patients in a hospital in Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple MRSA strains in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with a high prevalence of Panton-Valentine leukocidin (PVL) genes and various resistance genes including mecA, blaZ, erm(C), aacA-aphD, aadD, dfrA, tet(M), tet(K), msr(A), mph(C), qacA, and fusC.
full_output.methodology: DNA microarray analysis was used to characterize MRSA isolates for resistance and virulence genes.

full_output.paper_title: A Potential Substrate Binding Conformation of β-Lactams and Insight into the Broad Spectrum of NDM-1 Activity

blaNDM-1.role_in_paper: The paper discusses the role of NDM-1 in hydrolyzing β-lactam antibiotics.
blaNDM-1.validation_method: The paper uses docking simulations to analyze the binding of β-lactams to NDM-1.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the NDM-1 metallo-beta-lactamase, which hydrolyzes a broad spectrum of β-lactam antibiotics, providing insights into its substrate binding conformation and mechanism of action.
full_output.methodology: Computational docking simulations and structural analysis of NDM-1 in complex with various β-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Reduced expression of the rplU-rpmA ribosomal protein operon in mexXY-expressing pan-aminoglycoside-resistant mutants of pseudomonas aeruginosa.

rplU-rpmA.notes: mutation in the promoter region of rplU-rpmA leads to reduced expression and increased mexXY expression, contributing to aminoglycoside resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a mutation in the promoter region of the rplU-rpmA ribosomal protein operon that reduces its expression, leading to increased mexXY efflux pump expression and pan-aminoglycoside resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa mutants.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, real-time quantitative PCR, and growth assays were used to analyze the relationship between rplU-rpmA expression and mexXY overexpression in Pseudomonas aeruginosa mutants.

full_output.paper_title: Systematic analysis of pyrazinamide-resistant spontaneous mutants and clinical isolates of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

pncA.mechanism: mutations in the pncA gene lead to loss of pyrazinamidase activity, resulting in pyrazinamide resistance
pncA.validation_method: sequencing of the pncA gene and its promoter region, correlation with phenotypic resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the pncA gene as the primary mechanism of pyrazinamide resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with 87.5% of spontaneous mutants showing pncA mutations. Additionally, 12% of pyrazinamide-resistant mutants did not have pncA mutations, indicating other resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of the pncA gene and its promoter region, phenotypic resistance testing, and structural analysis of the PncA protein.

full_output.paper_title: A ten year analysis of multi-drug resistant blood stream infections caused by Escherichia coli & Klebsiella pneumoniae in a tertiary care hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a significant increase in multidrug-resistant E. coli and K. pneumoniae, particularly highlighting the rise in ESBL producers and carbapenemase production, especially in K. pneumoniae. It also found a correlation between antibiotic use and resistance.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of blood culture samples and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular detection and drug resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex from cattle at a dairy farm in the Nkonkobe region of South Africa: a pilot study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) in cattle milk, with 10 out of 11 samples showing resistance to both isoniazid (INH) and rifampicin (RIF). The most frequent RIF resistance mutation was H526Y in the rpoB gene, and all INH-resistant samples had the T8A mutation in the inhA gene.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection and drug susceptibility testing using PCR-based assays and the GenoType MTBDR plus assay.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates from patients newly identified as nasal carriers.

mecA.mechanism: confers resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics by altering penicillin-binding protein 2a

mupA.mechanism: confers resistance to mupirocin by modifying the target site

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the molecular and microbiological features of MRSA isolates from newly identified nasal carriers, identifying mecA, mupA, PVL, and USA300 genes. It found no high-level mupirocin resistance but noted low-level resistance in some cases. The study suggests that expanded MRSA surveillance for mupA, USA300, or PVL may not be necessary.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR, disk diffusion susceptibility testing, and Xpert MRSA PCR were used to analyze MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Subtractive hybridization yields a silver resistance determinant unique to nosocomial pathogens in the Enterobacter cloacae complex.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a silver resistance determinant (sil) in the Enterobacter cloacae complex, which is present in a significant proportion of clinical isolates and contributes to silver resistance.
full_output.methodology: Subtractive hybridization, PCR, and phenotypic tests were used to identify and validate the silver resistance determinant.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of β-lactamase phenotypes and carriage of selected β-lactamase genes among Escherichia coli strains obtained from Kenyan patients during an 18-year period.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several β-lactamase genes, including bla TEM-1, bla SHV-1, bla CTX-M-14, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-9, bla CTX-M-8, bla CTX-M-3, bla CTX-M-1, bla SHV-5, bla SHV-12, bla TEM-52, bla TEM-125, bla TEM-50, bla TEM-78, bla TEM-152, bla TEM-158, bla TEM-103, bla TEM-109, and bla CMY-2, which are responsible for resistance to various β-lactam antibiotics in E. coli isolates from Kenya.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and sequencing to detect and characterize β-lactamase genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Increased expression of the yeast multidrug resistance ABC transporter Pdr18 leads to increased ethanol tolerance and ethanol production in high gravity alcoholic fermentation.

PDR18.mechanism: PDR18 expression decreases intracellular ethanol accumulation and ethanol-induced plasma membrane permeabilization in yeast
PDR18.validation_method: spot assays, growth curve analysis, 3H-ethanol accumulation assays, membrane permeability measurements
PDR18.evidence_note: PDR18 expression was found to confer resistance to growth inhibitory concentrations of ethanol.

full_output.key_findings: Over-expression of the PDR18 gene in Saccharomyces cerevisiae increases ethanol tolerance and ethanol production during high gravity alcoholic fermentation.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, plasmid-based expression, ethanol susceptibility assays, 3H-ethanol accumulation, membrane permeability measurements, HPLC for ethanol and glucose quantification.

full_output.paper_title: Characterisation of a natural variant of the γ-butyrolactone signalling receptor.

scbR.validation_method: proteomic analysis, sequencing, gel retardation assay

mutations_found.validated_by: proteomic analysis, sequencing, gel retardation assay

scbR.notes: The scbR M600 variant exhibits reduced DNA binding ability compared to scbR M145.

full_output.key_findings: A natural variant of the γ-butyrolactone receptor ScbR (ScbR M600) was identified in Streptomyces coelicolor M600, differing from ScbR M145 by a single amino acid change (R120S). This mutation impairs DNA binding and alters the expression of antibiotic biosynthesis genes.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis, sequencing, gel retardation assays, and qRT-PCR were used to characterize the ScbR variants and their effects on gene expression.
full_output.sample_size: 16 S. coelicolor strains and 1 S. lividans strain

full_output.paper_title: Factors related to increasing prevalence of resistance to ciprofloxacin and other antimicrobial drugs in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, United States.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that ciprofloxacin resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae increased rapidly among men who have sex with men (MSM) compared to heterosexual men. Triple resistance (to ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, and penicillin) was the fastest-growing class of ciprofloxacin-resistant types among MSM. The study also highlighted the role of travel and antimicrobial drug use in the spread of resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed data from the Gonococcal Isolate Surveillance Project (GISP) to investigate trends in antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

full_output.paper_title: Klebsiella pneumoniae Carbapenemase-producing enterobacteria in hospital, Singapore.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a KPC-producing K. pneumoniae isolate carrying the blaKPC-2 gene, which confers resistance to carbapenems.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in genes such as rpoB, inhA, katG, embB, gyrA, pncA, and rrs that confer resistance to various anti-tuberculosis drugs including rifampin, isoniazid, ethambutol, ofloxacin, pyrazinamide, and amikacin in two families affected by multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Membrane Disruption by Antimicrobial Fatty Acids Releases Low-Molecular-Weight Proteins from Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that specific fatty acid structures, such as 16:1Δ9, inhibit the growth of Staphylococcus aureus by disrupting the cytoplasmic membrane, leading to the release of solutes and low-molecular-weight proteins. It also highlights the role of wall teichoic acids in determining the structural specificity of fatty acid toxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution assays, flow cytometry, metabolic labeling, and lipid extraction techniques to investigate the effects of fatty acids on S. aureus.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies nine mutations in rpoB and rpoC genes that confer resistance to squaramide RNA polymerase inhibitors in Haemophilus influenzae. These mutations are located in the switch region of RNA polymerase, which is the binding site for natural antibiotics like myxopyronin and fidaxomicin.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening, mutant isolation, MIC testing, and structural analysis were used to identify and characterize the resistance mutations in rpoB and rpoC.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular identification and antimicrobial susceptibility of Staphylococcus aureus nasal isolates from medical students in Cartagena, Colombia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of mecA, which confers methicillin resistance, and PVL genes (lukF-PV and lukS-PV) in Staphylococcus aureus nasal isolates from medical students in Cartagena, Colombia.
full_output.methodology: PCR assays and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and characterize the isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes, including cat, blaT, SulI, dhfrI, aadA, StrA, StrB, and qacE, in multidrug-resistant S. Typhimurium strains from Malawi, highlighting the genetic basis of their resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and comparative analysis of 27 multidrug-resistant S. Typhimurium strains.

full_output.paper_title: Synergy between vancomycin and nafcillin against Staphylococcus aureus in an in vitro pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the combination of vancomycin and nafcillin showed synergy against heterogeneously vancomycin-intermediate Staphylococcus aureus (hVISA), methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), and methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA).
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the synergy between vancomycin and nafcillin using time-kill experiments and an in vitro pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model.

full_output.paper_title: Hal Is a Bacillus anthracis Heme Acquisition Protein.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and biochemical characterization of a trapped coenzyme A adduct of Caenorhabditis elegans glucosamine-6-phosphate N-acetyltransferase 1.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: not directly involved in the reaction mechanism

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structural and biochemical properties of Caenorhabditis elegans GNA1 (Ce GNA1) and its homologue in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Sc GNA1), focusing on the role of a conserved active-site cysteine (Cys141 in Ce GNA1 and Cys135 in Sc GNA1) in the reaction mechanism. A covalent CoA adduct was observed, which can be reactivated under reducing conditions. Mutation of the cysteine (C141S in Ce GNA1 and C135S in Sc GNA1) resulted in altered kinetic parameters but did not eliminate activity, indicating that the cysteine is not directly involved in catalysis.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, steady-state kinetics, mass spectrometry, and mutagenesis were used to analyze the structure and function of GNA1 enzymes.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a novel genomic island conferring resistance to multiple aminoglycoside antibiotics in Campylobacter coli.
full_output.key_findings: A novel genomic island containing multiple aminoglycoside resistance genes, including aadE, aphA-3, aacA-aphD, and sat4, was identified in Campylobacter coli strains, conferring resistance to multiple aminoglycoside antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, PFGE, MLST, and natural transformation experiments were used to characterize the genomic island and its resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: DNA microarray profiling of a diverse collection of nosocomial methicillin-resistant staphylococcus aureus isolates assigns the majority to the correct sequence type and staphylococcal cassette chromosome mec (SCCmec) type and results in the subsequent identification and characterization of novel SCCmec-SCCM1 composite islands.

aacA-aphD.evidence_note: The paper states that 'aacA-aphD, encoding resistance to amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, and tobramycin' was detected in 53% of isolates.

fusA.notes: Three different combinations of mutations were identified in these isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes novel SCCmec-SCCM1 composite islands in MRSA isolates, highlighting the presence of various AMR genes such as blaZ, erm(A), aadD, qacA, qacC, merA, merB, fosB, sdrM, aacA-aphD, far1 (fusB), Q6GD50 (fusC), and cat-pC194 (pMC524).
full_output.methodology: DNA microarray profiling and whole-genome sequencing were used to analyze AMR genes and characterize novel SCCmec-SCCM1 composite islands in MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A case of postoperative endophthalmitis by extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The case report describes a 75-year-old female who developed postoperative endophthalmitis caused by extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli, which exhibited resistance to penicillins, cephalosporins, aminoglycosides, and levofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial identification test and analysis of antibiotic resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: A novel 5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase from Rahnella aquatilis with significantly reduced glyphosate sensitivity.

aroA.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + enzyme activity assay

mutations_found.protein_change: Thr38Lys, Arg40Val, Arg222Gln, Ser224Val, Ile225Val, Gln226Lys

AroA_R.aquatilis.notes: Mutations in subdomain 3 and subdomain 5 of AroA R.aquatilis reduced glyphosate sensitivity.

aroA.notes: Mutations in subdomain 5 and hinge region of AroA R.aquatilis and AroA E.coli contribute to glyphosate resistance.

full_output.key_findings: A novel glyphosate-tolerant EPSPS gene from Rahnella aquatilis, AroA R.aquatilis, was identified and shown to confer higher glyphosate tolerance than E. coli EPSPS. Mutations in subdomain 3 and subdomain 5 of AroA R.aquatilis reduced glyphosate sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, site-directed mutagenesis, functional analysis in E. coli, and transgenic tobacco experiments.
full_output.sample_size: 1 strain isolated from grape rhizosphere in glyphosate-contaminated vineyards

full_output.paper_title: Identification of MrtAB, an ABC transporter specifically required for Yersinia pseudotuberculosis to colonize the mesenteric lymph nodes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mrtAB, an ABC transporter, as essential for Yersinia pseudotuberculosis to colonize the mesenteric lymph nodes, highlighting its role in virulence and efflux pump functionality.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screen, transposon mutagenesis, complementation experiments, and in vivo infection assays.

full_output.paper_title: The role of the C8 proton of ATP in the catalysis of shikimate kinase and adenylate kinase.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: The mutation of Thr17 in shikimate kinase (SK) significantly reduces enzyme activity, with the SK-T17I mutant showing a 4.5 to 6 fold reduction in enzyme activity at low ATP concentrations.
The mutation of Thr23 in AK1 significantly affects the enzyme's activity, leading to a substantial decrease in specific activity.
The mutation of Thr39 in AK1 significantly affects the enzyme's activity, leading to a substantial decrease in specific activity.
The mutation of Arg128 in AK1 significantly affects the enzyme's activity, leading to a substantial decrease in specific activity.
The mutation of Arg97 in AK1 significantly affects the enzyme's activity, leading to a substantial decrease in specific activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies critical residues in the 'push' mechanism of shikimate kinase (SK) and adenylate kinase 1 (AK1) that affect ATP C8-H lability and catalytic efficiency. Mutations in these residues alter enzyme activity and kinetic properties, demonstrating their roles in phosphoryl transfer mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis and kinetic analysis of wild-type and mutant SK and AK1 enzymes.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative transcriptomics of H. pylori strains AM5, SS1 and their hpyAVIBM deletion mutants: possible roles of cytosine methylation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hpyAVIBM as a phase-variable C5 cytosine methyltransferase in H. pylori, which influences gene expression related to motility, pathogenesis, and LPS synthesis.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, RT-PCR, and mutagenesis were used to analyze the impact of hpyAVIBM deletion on gene expression in H. pylori strains AM5 and SS1.
full_output.sample_size: 75 adult patients with duodenal ulcer and 30 healthy volunteers

full_output.paper_title: The small regulatory RNA FasX controls pilus expression and adherence in the human bacterial pathogen group A Streptococcus.

cpa.mechanism: base-pairing with FasX sRNA to inhibit translation and reduce mRNA stability
cpa.validation_method: quantitative RT-PCR, Western blot, in vitro translation

sipA1.mechanism: regulated by FasX through base-pairing with cpa mRNA

tee1.mechanism: regulated by FasX through base-pairing with cpa mRNA

srtC1.mechanism: part of the pilus biosynthesis operon regulated by FasX

fasX.mechanism: regulates pilus expression by base-pairing with cpa mRNA
fasX.validation_method: microarray, quantitative RT-PCR, Western blot, EMSA

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies FasX as a small regulatory RNA that negatively regulates pilus expression in Group A Streptococcus by base-pairing with the 5'-UTR of cpa mRNA, thereby inhibiting translation and reducing mRNA stability.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, quantitative RT-PCR, Western blot, EMSA, in vitro translation, and mutational analysis.

rpoB.notes: mutations in rpoB gene associated with rifampicin resistance

mabA-inhA.notes: mutations in mabA-inhA promoter region associated with isoniazid resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the use of capillary electrophoresis-single strand conformation polymorphism (CE-SSCP) for detecting mutations in the rpoB gene and mabA-inhA promoter region associated with rifampicin and isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: Capillary electrophoresis-single strand conformation polymorphism (CE-SSCP) was used to detect mutations in the rpoB gene and mabA-inhA promoter region.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Amp C genes encoding for beta-lactamases in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study detected Amp C genes in 29.87% of the study isolates, with the majority co-producing ESBL. The most common Amp C was the CIT family.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR was used to detect Amp C genes after phenotypic testing.

full_output.paper_title: The β-Lactam Resistance Protein Blr, a Small Membrane Polypeptide, Is a Component of the Escherichia coli Cell Division Machinery.

blr.mechanism: component of the cell division machinery

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Blr, a small membrane polypeptide, as a novel component of the E. coli cell division machinery, showing that it localizes to the division septum and is involved in stabilizing the divisome under low-osmotic-stress conditions.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial two-hybrid screening, fluorescent tagging, and localization studies.

full_output.paper_title: Crystal structures of the Cid1 poly (U) polymerase reveal the mechanism for UTP selectivity.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: diminished Cid1’s activity for UTP addition and improved ATP incorporation

Cid1.notes: Mutation of H336 to asparagine reduces UTP selectivity and increases ATP incorporation.
Cid1.evidence_note: The paper describes the mutation of H336 to asparagine in Cid1 and its effect on UTP and ATP incorporation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the molecular mechanisms underlying UTP selectivity in Cid1, a poly(U) polymerase, revealing that a histidine residue in the active site is crucial for UTP discrimination. Mutating this residue to asparagine alters substrate preference towards ATP.
