full_output.key_findings: The study presents a microarray-based serogenotyping assay for Salmonella, demonstrating high correlation between genotypic and phenotypic characteristics. Several AMR genes were identified and validated, showing strong association with AMR phenotypes.
full_output.methodology: Microarray-based serogenotyping and AMR gene detection using hybridization and comparative analysis with classical serotyping and AMR phenotyping.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and characterization of two novel bla(KLUC) resistance genes through large-scale resistance plasmids sequencing.

blaKLUC-3.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + MIC testing
blaKLUC-3.evidence_note: The paper states that bla KLUC-3 shows resistance to several extend-spectrum β-lactams, including ceftriaxone, cefazolin and cefotaxime, but not ceftazidime. It also mentions that the amino acid change at position 167 (R167L) in Kluc-4 leads to the disappearance of resistance activity.

full_output.key_findings: Two novel bla(KLUC) resistance genes, blaKLUC-3 and blaKLUC-4, were identified and characterized. blaKLUC-3 conferred resistance to several extended-spectrum beta-lactams, while blaKLUC-4 did not show resistance to the tested antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput sequencing of plasmids followed by cloning, sequencing, and MIC testing of the genes in E. coli.

full_output.key_findings: Nilotinib enhances the effectiveness of anticancer drugs in multidrug-resistant xenograft models by inhibiting ABCB1, ABCG2, and ABCC10 transporters.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo studies using cell lines and xenograft models to assess the effect of nilotinib on drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of increased azithromycin resistance during unsuccessful treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection with azithromycin (Portland, OR, 2011).

mtrR.encodes: transcriptional repressor of the mtrCDE efflux pump

mutations_found.nucleotide_change: deletion of adenine (A) within the 13-base-pair inverted repeat
mutations_found.validated_by: genotypic characterization via PCR and sequencing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of azithromycin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae variants during unsuccessful treatment with azithromycin, highlighting the role of mutations in the mtrR promoter and 23S rRNA genes in increasing resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genotypic characterization through PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) was conducted.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activities of antibiotics and antimicrobial cationic peptides alone and in combination against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the in vitro activities of antibiotics and antimicrobial cationic peptides against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) biofilms, highlighting synergistic effects of combinations and the effectiveness of peptides in inhibiting biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution techniques and checkerboard assays to evaluate antimicrobial activities against MRSA biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the polymyxin B resistome of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the polymyxin B resistome of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, revealing that only one resistant mutant and 17 different susceptibility determinants were identified. The phoQ gene was found to be involved in increased mutational resistance to polymyxin B.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening of the Harvard transposon mutant library of P. aeruginosa strain PA14 to identify genes involved in polymyxin B resistance.

full_output.paper_title: A mutation of the RNA polymerase β′ subunit (rpoC) confers cephalosporin resistance in Bacillus subtilis.

mutations_found.validated_by: genetic reconstruction experiments and MIC determination

full_output.key_findings: A single point mutation (G1122D) in the rpoC gene of Bacillus subtilis confers high-level resistance to cefuroxime by increasing the activity of ECF σ factors (σ M, σ W, and σ X).
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome resequencing, genetic reconstruction, and MIC determination were used to validate the role of the rpoC G1122D mutation in cefuroxime resistance.

full_output.paper_title: novel 6'-n-aminoglycoside acetyltransferase AAC(6')-Iaj from a clinical isolate of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

aac(6')-Iaj.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + MIC testing
aac(6')-Iaj.evidence_note: The aac(6′)-Iaj gene was cloned into E. coli and conferred resistance to aminoglycosides, as shown by MIC testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel aminoglycoside 6′-N-acetyltransferase, AAC(6′)-Iaj, which confers resistance to multiple aminoglycosides including amikacin, arbekacin, gentamicin, netilmicin, and tobramycin in Pseudomonas aeruginosa NCGM1588.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, heterologous expression in E. coli, and MIC testing were used to validate the resistance phenotype conferred by AAC(6′)-Iaj.

full_output.paper_title: Surveillance and molecular epidemiology of Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates that produce carbapenemases: first report of OXA-48-like enzymes in North America.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of OXA-48-like enzymes in North America and identifies various carbapenemase genes (blaKPC, blaNDM, blaVIM, blaOXA-48, and blaIMP) in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, highlighting their molecular epidemiology and geographic distribution.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, PFGE, and MLST were used to characterize carbapenemase-producing K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies risk factors for the isolation of KPC-producing carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (KPC-CR-Kp) and Porin-ER-Kp strains, highlighting the association of KPC-CR-Kp with carbapenem exposure and endoscopy, while Porin-ER-Kp was linked to second- and third-generation cephalosporins, carbapenems, acute renal failure, and endoscopy.
full_output.methodology: Case-case-control study analyzing risk factors for KPC-CR-Kp and Porin-ER-Kp isolation in hospitalized patients.

full_output.paper_title: The TolC-like protein HgdD of the cyanobacterium Anabaena sp. PCC 7120 is involved in secondary metabolite export and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The TolC-like protein HgdD in Anabaena sp. PCC 7120 is involved in secondary metabolite export and antibiotic resistance, particularly in the export of ethidium bromide and erythromycin.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic mutants, ethidium bromide uptake assays, and biochemical analyses to investigate the role of HgdD in metabolite export and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Catecholate siderophores protect bacteria from pyochelin toxicity.
full_output.key_findings: Enterobactin, a catecholate siderophore, protects Escherichia coli from pyochelin toxicity by reducing reactive oxygen species (ROS).
full_output.methodology: MIC testing, ROS measurements, and genetic manipulation of E. coli strains.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative genomics of community-acquired ST59 methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in Taiwan: novel mobile resistance structures with IS1216V.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes, including ermB, aph(3')-IIIa, aadE, and cat, within a novel mobile element structure (MES PM1) in a multidrug-resistant ST59 CA-MRSA strain, highlighting the role of IS1216V-mediated genetic mobility in resistance acquisition.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR, and susceptibility testing were used to analyze the AMR genes and mechanisms in the ST59 CA-MRSA strain.

full_output.paper_title: A two-step mechanism for the activation of actinorhodin export and resistance in Streptomyces coelicolor.

mutations_found.validated_by: mutant construction and promoter induction assays

actR.notes: The T142W mutation in ActR responds to (S)-DNPA but not actinorhodin in living cells.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a two-step mechanism for the activation of actinorhodin export and resistance in Streptomyces coelicolor, involving the actAB operon and the transcriptional repressor ActR. The T142W mutation in ActR alters its ligand responsiveness, affecting the induction of actAB by biosynthetic intermediates.
full_output.methodology: The study uses genetic mutants, reporter assays, and live/dead cell-staining assays to investigate the role of actAB and actR in actinorhodin production and resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Intrinsic and acquired resistance mechanisms in enterococcus.

aac(6')-Ii.mechanism: Intrinsic resistance in E. faecium is attributed to the aminoglycoside 6′ acetyltransferase [AAC(6′)-Ii], which confers resistance to tobramycin with MICs as high as 1000 µg/ml and to kanamycin.
aac(6')-Ii.role_in_paper: Described as an intrinsic resistance mechanism in E. faecium.
aac(6')-Ii.validation_method: Described in the context of intrinsic resistance mechanisms.
aac(6')-Ii.evidence_note: The paper states that the aminoglycoside 6′ acetyltransferase [AAC(6′)-Ii] confers resistance to tobramycin and kanamycin in E. faecium.

vanA.mechanism: The acquisition of glycopeptide resistance by enterococci has been an epidemiological and antimicrobial dilemma for the past 25 years.
vanA.role_in_paper: The paper reviews the mechanisms underlying antibiotic resistance in enterococci, including the VanA resistance mechanism.
vanA.validation_method: The paper describes the VanA resistance mechanism and its regulation by the VanR and VanS two-component sensor-transducer system.
vanA.evidence_level: The paper provides detailed descriptions of the VanA resistance mechanism and its genetic basis.
vanA.genetic_context: The VanA cassette is part of the Tn1546 transposon and is regulated by the VanR and VanS two-component system.
vanA.evidence_note: The paper describes the VanA resistance mechanism and its role in glycopeptide resistance in enterococci.

msrC.evidence_note: The paper states that the msrC gene is intrinsic to E. faecium and confers low-level resistance to streptogramin B compounds.

cfr.role_in_paper: described as a gene conferring resistance to linezolid, lincosamides, and streptogramin A
cfr.validation_method: identification in clinical isolates and plasmid analysis
cfr.genetic_context: located on a plasmid (pEF-01) and flanked by IS 1216
cfr.evidence_note: The cfr gene was identified in S. aureus as the source of resistance to linezolid, lincosamides and streptogramin A compounds, among others. In 2011, cfr was identified in an E. faecalis strain (designated EF-01) from a cattle farm in China. This was the first enterococcus harboring cfr to be reported in the literature.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: accumulation of point mutations in the penicillin binding region

pbp5.notes: accumulation of point mutations in the penicillin binding region

pbp4.notes: accumulation of point mutations in the penicillin binding region

full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews intrinsic and acquired resistance mechanisms in Enterococcus, focusing on beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, glycopeptides, and other antibiotics. Key findings include the identification of various AMR genes such as bla, aac(6')-Ii, efmM, aph(3')-IIIa, ant(4')-Ia, vanA, vanH, vanX, vanY, lsa, msrC, vatD, vatE, ermA, ermB, and cfr, along with mutations in pbp5, pbp4, rRNA, cls, gdpD, and liaF contributing to resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed resistance mechanisms in Enterococcus through experimental data, including gene characterization, MIC testing, and mutation analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Lipophilic prodrugs of FR900098 are antimicrobial against Francisella novicida in vivo and in vitro and show GlpT independent efficacy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the GlpT homologs in Francisella and shows that compound 1 exhibits GlpT-independent antimicrobial activity against F. novicida.
full_output.methodology: The study used a 96-well plate assay to determine MICs and EC50s, and tested the effects of compounds on intracellular F. novicida in cell lines and a Galleria mellonella model.

full_output.paper_title: pSK41-like plasmid is necessary for Inc18-like vanA plasmid transfer from Enterococcus faecalis to Staphylococcus aureus in vitro.

pSK41.mechanism: facilitates transfer of Inc18-like vanA plasmid

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pSK41-like plasmid as essential for the in vitro transfer of Inc18-like vanA plasmid from Enterococcus faecalis to Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Conjugation experiments, PCR analysis, and plasmid characterization.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple MRSA isolates from VRSA cases.

full_output.paper_title: Biochemical and structural analysis of aminoglycoside acetyltransferase Eis from Anabaena variabilis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes Eis_ Ava, a non-mycobacterial aminoglycoside acetyltransferase from Anabaena variabilis, which exhibits resistance to kanamycin through multi-acetylation of aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical and structural analysis, UV-Vis and mass spectrometry assays, molecular modeling.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and genotypic analysis of plasmid-mediated β-lactamases among urinary Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates in Moroccan community.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the prevalence of plasmid-mediated β-lactamases, including blaCTX-M-15, blaSHV-28, blaSHV-12, and novel blaEBC-1464, among urinary Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates in Morocco. It also identifies qnr and aac(6′)-Ib-cr genes associated with quinolone and aminoglycoside resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and characterize AMR genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Vitamin D and the human antimicrobial peptide LL-37 enhance group a streptococcus resistance to killing by human cells.

hasB.evidence_note: The paper describes a deletion mutant of hasB in Streptococcus pyogenes and notes that the mutant shows reduced capsule production.

slo.evidence_note: The paper describes a deletion mutant of slo in Streptococcus pyogenes and notes that the mutant shows reduced hemolytic activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that LL-37 signaling through the CsrRS system enhances Group A Streptococcus (GAS) resistance to killing by human cells, primarily through upregulation of streptolysin O (SLO) and the hyaluronic acid capsule. Vitamin D treatment of macrophages increases GAS survival by enhancing LL-37 production, leading to increased resistance to phagocytic killing.
full_output.methodology: The study used mutant analysis, antibiotic protection assays, and cytotoxicity assays to investigate the role of CsrRS-regulated virulence factors in GAS resistance to human cells.

qnrB.validation_method: experimental validation through SOS response activation

full_output.methodology: Review of global surveillance studies and experimental validations of resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting the cell wall of Mycobacterium tuberculosis: structure and mechanism of L,D-transpeptidase 2.

full_output.methodology: Structural analysis, isothermal titration calorimetry, and kinetic measurements were used to investigate the properties of Ldt Mt2.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of the enzyme responsible for N-Acetylation of Norfloxacin by Microbacterium sp. Strain 4N2-2.

glnA.validation_method: cloning and heterologous expression in E. coli, enzyme activity assays, and disk diffusion assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies glutamine synthetase (glnA) from Microbacterium sp. strain 4N2-2 as the enzyme responsible for N-acetylation of norfloxacin, leading to low-level resistance against fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, heterologous expression, enzyme activity assays, and disk diffusion assay were used to validate the role of glnA in norfloxacin resistance.

APH(3')-IIIa.mechanism: phosphorylates aminoglycoside antibiotics, leading to their inactivation
APH(3')-IIIa.validation_method: kinetic studies and transient kinetics analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the aminoglycoside phosphotransferase(3')-IIIa (APH(3')-IIIa) enzyme, showing that ADP release is the rate-limiting step in its reaction pathway, which contributes to bacterial resistance against aminoglycoside antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Transient kinetics and steady-state kinetic analyses using various biochemical methods including quench flow and stopped flow techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and antimicrobial activity of some novel cross-linked chitosan hydrogels.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis of novel cross-linked chitosan hydrogels and their enhanced antimicrobial activity against various bacteria and fungi compared to parent chitosan.
full_output.methodology: The hydrogels were synthesized via cross-linking reactions and their antimicrobial activities were evaluated using agar well diffusion and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) methods.

full_output.paper_title: Increased mutability of Staphylococci in biofilms as a consequence of oxidative stress.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that staphylococcal biofilms exhibit increased mutability compared to planktonic cultures, which is linked to oxidative stress. The up-regulation of the superoxide dismutase gene sodA and the inactivation of the pyruvate oxidase gene cidC contribute to this increased mutability.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of mutation frequency determinations, transcriptome analysis, and genetic manipulation to investigate the role of oxidative stress in biofilm mutability.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of bla(OXA-199), a chromosome-based bla(OXA-48)-like variant, in Shewanella xiamenensis.

bla(OXA-199).genetic_context: both bla OXA-48b and bla OXA-199 were adjacent to genes encoding a peptidase (indicated as orf), a protein of unknown function ( sprT ), an endonuclease I ( endA ), and a ribosomal RNA methyl transferase ( rsmE ) upstream and to transcriptional regulator gene lysR and an acetyl-CoA carboxylase-encoding gene downstream
bla(OXA-199).evidence_note: The bla OXA-199 gene had five nucleotide differences from both bla OXA-48a and bla OXA-48b (99.4% identity), specifying the OXA-199 protein with three amino acid substitutions (H37Y, V44A and D153G) compared to OXA-48.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a new variant of the bla(OXA-48) gene, designated bla(OXA-199), in Shewanella xiamenensis, which confers resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to identify and characterize the bla(OXA-199) gene.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Extended Spectrum B-Lactamases in Urinary Isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae in Relation to Bla, Bla and Bla Gene Carriage.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaSHV, blaTEM, and blaCTX-M genes in urinary isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae, which are associated with resistance to various β-lactam antibiotics. However, no direct correlation was found between the presence of these genes and ESBL production.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing via disc diffusion and MIC, PCR for gene detection, and ESBL detection via double disc synergy test.

full_output.paper_title: FIM-1, a new acquired metallo-β-lactamase from a Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolate from Italy.

blaFIM-1.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes FIM-1, a new acquired metallo-β-lactamase from a multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate, which confers resistance to various β-lactam antibiotics including carbapenems, penicillins, and cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, sequencing, and MIC testing were used to characterize the FIM-1 enzyme.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of OXA-204, a carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D β-lactamase from Klebsiella pneumoniae.

blaOXA-204.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + MIC testing
blaOXA-204.genetic_context: bla OXA-204 gene was located on a ca. 150-kb IncA/C-type plasmid, which also carried the bla CMY-4 gene. The bla OXA-204 gene was associated with an IS Ecp1 element
blaOXA-204.evidence_note: The bla OXA-204 gene was associated with an IS Ecp1 element, whereas the bla OXA-48 genes are usually associated with IS 1999.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes OXA-204, a carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D β-lactamase from Klebsiella pneumoniae, which shows resistance to carbapenems and is associated with the blaCMY-4 gene on an IncA/C-type plasmid.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, MIC testing, and sequence analysis were used to characterize the β-lactamase.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative genomics of IncL/M-type plasmids: evolution by acquisition of resistance genes and insertion sequences.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the evolution of IncL/M-type plasmids, highlighting the acquisition of resistance genes such as blaNDM-1, blaOXA-48, blaCTX-M-3, and armA, which confer resistance to carbapenems, beta-lactams, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid sequencing and comparative genomic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of recombinant fluoroquinolone-resistant pneumococcus-like isolates.

parC.notes: Mutation in parC gene associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.

parE.notes: Mutations in parE gene associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA gene associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes fluoroquinolone-resistant pneumococcus-like isolates, identifying mutations in parC, parE, and gyrA genes that confer resistance to ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic analysis, including PCR, sequencing, and MLST, were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Complete nucleotide sequences of blaKPC-4- and blaKPC-5-harboring IncN and IncX plasmids from Klebsiella pneumoniae strains isolated in New Jersey.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the complete sequences of blaKPC-4- and blaKPC-5-harboring IncN and IncX plasmids from Klebsiella pneumoniae strains, highlighting the genetic diversity and mobility of these plasmids.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid sequencing, PCR, and functional analysis were used to characterize the resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal structure, extended-spectrum β-lactamases, and acquired AmpC-type cephalosporinases of Escherichia coli populations colonizing patients in rehabilitation centers in four countries.

blaSHV-5.role_in_paper: The gene was identified as a contributor to resistance in E. coli isolates.
blaSHV-5.genetic_context: blaSHV-5 is a variant of the SHV β-lactamase gene.
blaSHV-5.source: The paper mentions blaSHV-5 in the context of ESBL production in E. coli isolates.
blaSHV-5.evidence_note: The paper describes blaSHV-5 as an ESBL gene in E. coli.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple β-lactamase genes, including blaCTX-M-15, blaCTX-M-14, blaCTX-M-27, blaCTX-M-1, blaCTX-M-2, blaCTX-M-9, blaCTX-M-32, blaCTX-M-55, blaCTX-M-39, blaCTX-M-100, blaSHV-5, blaSHV-12, blaTEM-24, blaTEM-52, blaCMY-2, blaCMY-4, blaCMY-42, and blaDHA-1, which confer resistance to extended-spectrum cephalosporins in Escherichia coli isolates from rehabilitation centers in four countries.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and sequencing to identify and characterize β-lactamase genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: An improved small-molecule inhibitor of FtsZ with superior in vitro potency, drug-like properties, and in vivo efficacy.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: rendered the strain insensitive to PC190723
mutations_found.validated_by: isolation and characterization of compound-resistant mutants

ftsZ.notes: The G196A mutation in ftsZ gene renders the strain insensitive to PC190723.
ftsZ.evidence_note: The paper states that the G196A mutation in ftsZ gene renders the strain insensitive to PC190723.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes an improved small-molecule inhibitor of FtsZ, compound 1, which shows potent antibacterial activity against staphylococcal species, including methicillin- and multidrug-resistant strains. It also demonstrates efficacy against an FtsZ G196A mutant, indicating that the compound can overcome resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study involved in vitro and in vivo evaluations of compound 1, including MIC testing, cell division phenotype assays, and resistance frequency experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Persistent catheter-related Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia after catheter removal and initiation of antimicrobial therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 21% of catheter-related Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (CRSAB) cases persisted for more than 3 days after catheter removal and initiation of appropriate antimicrobial therapy. Methicillin resistance, presence of non-catheter prosthetic devices, and renal failure were independently associated with persistent CRSAB.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 220 episodes of CRSAB, examining clinical characteristics, risk factors, and outcomes. It also evaluated microbiological and genotypic characteristics of MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of methicillin-susceptible and -resistant staphylococci in the clinical setting: a multicentre study in Nigeria.

mecA.validation_method: detection of the mecA gene through PCR and confirmation by antibiotic susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA gene as responsible for methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci (CNS). It also found that 72.5% of CNS and 82.3% of S. aureus isolates were resistant to cotrimoxazole. The study highlights the importance of species-level identification of staphylococci for understanding their clinical relevance and resistance patterns.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of the mecA gene, antibiotic susceptibility testing using the VITEK 2 system, and molecular typing techniques such as SCC mec typing, spa typing, and MLST.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Aminoglycoside 2"-Phosphotransferase Identified in a Gram-Negative Pathogen.

APH(2\"-If.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: A novel aminoglycoside 2"-phosphotransferase, APH(2"-If, was identified in Campylobacter jejuni and shown to confer resistance to several 4,6-disubstituted aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, protein expression, purification, and MIC testing were performed to characterize the resistance mechanism.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in nasal surveillance swabs at an intensive care unit: an evaluation of the LightCycler MRSA advanced test.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the LightCycler MRSA advanced test for detecting methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and found that the mecA gene was responsible for methicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR to confirm the presence of the mecA gene in specimens with discrepant results between the LightCycler MRSA advanced test and enrichment culture.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal spread of carbapenem non-susceptible Acinetobacter baumannii in an intensive care unit in a teaching hospital in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaOXA-23 as the primary carbapenem resistance determinant in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates, alongside aacA4, catB8, and aadA1 contributing to aminoglycoside and chloramphenicol resistance. The clonal complex CC92, particularly ST92 and ST75, was prevalent in carbapenem-non-susceptible isolates.
full_output.methodology: MLST, PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze genetic diversity and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution and quantification of antibiotic resistant genes and bacteria across agricultural and non-agricultural metagenomes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes various antibiotic resistance genes across agricultural and non-agricultural metagenomes, highlighting the widespread occurrence of resistance mechanisms such as beta-lactamases, MDR efflux pumps, fluoroquinolone resistance, tetracycline resistance, and glycopeptide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis using MG-RAST to classify and quantify antibiotic resistance genes in various environmental samples.

full_output.paper_title: Effectiveness of an antimicrobial treatment scheme in a confined glanders outbreak.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that a 12-week antimicrobial treatment regimen consisting of enrofloxacin, trimethoprim-sulfadiazine, and doxycycline effectively eliminated Burkholderia mallei from infected horses, preventing disease recurrence and ensuring the health of the treated animals.
full_output.methodology: The study involved administering a combination of antibiotics to 23 culture-positive glanders-affected horses, followed by clinical and microbiological evaluations to assess treatment efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative drug resistance of Mycobacterium abscessus and M. chelonae isolates from patients with and without cystic fibrosis in the United Kingdom.
full_output.key_findings: The study compared drug resistance profiles of Mycobacterium abscessus and M. chelonae isolates from patients with and without cystic fibrosis, highlighting varying resistance patterns to multiple antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution and disc diffusion methods for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic profiling of microbial composition and antibiotic resistance determinants in Puget Sound.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a significant increase in antibiotic resistance gene signals from the open Sound to the marina to the WWTP effluent, suggesting a potential link to human impacts. Tetracycline resistance genes were the most represented among the detected resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomics combined with pyrosequencing was used to analyze the taxonomic and antibiotic resistance determinant composition of surface water bacterial communities in Puget Sound and a wastewater treatment plant effluent.
full_output.sample_size: Six sites in Puget Sound and one wastewater treatment plant effluent

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that Trichomonas vaginalis isolates carrying endosymbiotic Trichomonasvirus (TVV) activate TLR3-dependent proinflammatory responses in human epithelial cells, leading to increased production of interferon type I and proinflammatory cytokines. Metronidazole treatment exacerbates these responses.
full_output.methodology: The study uses human epithelial cell culture models, TLR3 signaling assays, and analysis of cytokine production to investigate the interaction between TVV-infected Trichomonas vaginalis and the human immune system.

full_output.paper_title: Structures of SHV-1 β-lactamase with penem and penam sulfone inhibitors that form cyclic intermediates stabilized by carbonyl conjugation.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the SHV-1 β-lactamase and its interactions with penem 1, SA1-204, and SA3-53 inhibitors, revealing structural details of covalent adducts and their roles in β-lactam resistance.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, MIC testing, and kinetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Fast test for assessing the susceptibility of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to isoniazid and rifampin by real-time PCR.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated a real-time PCR assay for detecting resistance to isoniazid and rifampin in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, identifying specific mutations in the katG, inhA, and rpoB genes associated with resistance.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR and DNA sequencing were used to detect mutations in the katG, inhA, and rpoB genes associated with isoniazid and rifampin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal composition and community clustering of drug-susceptible and -resistant Escherichia coli isolates from bloodstream infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of bla CTX-M genes in E. coli isolates, which confer resistance to multiple antibiotics including cephalosporins and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and characterize bla CTX-M genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-associated multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii are sensitised by aztreonam in combination with polyamines.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several OXA-type carbapenemase genes (bla OXA-23, bla OXA-24, bla OXA-51, and bla OXA-58) in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii strains, which contribute to resistance against beta-lactam antibiotics. The combination of aztreonam with polyamines was found to sensitize these multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, time-killing assays, and checkerboard assays were used to evaluate the effects of polyamines on antibiotic resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug resistance genes, including blaKPC and blaCTX-M-2, among Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated in Recife, Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC and blaCTX-M-2 genes in multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Recife, Brazil, highlighting the emergence of carbapenem and cephalosporin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, phenotypic testing, ERIC-PCR, and plasmid profiling were used to analyze resistance genes and genetic relationships among isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 2-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinones as selective inhibitors of ThyX, a flavin-dependent thymidylate synthase, and demonstrates their ability to inhibit bacterial growth by mimicking a genetic knockout of thymidylate synthase.
full_output.methodology: The research involved screening chemical libraries, determining inhibition mechanisms, and solving the crystal structure of a ThyX-inhibitor complex.

full_output.paper_title: New perspectives for natural antimicrobial peptides: application as antinflammatory drugs in a murine model.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that a combination of two chemically modified antimicrobial peptides, temporin B (TB-KK) and royal jellein I (RJI-C), exhibits both antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activities against Staphylococcus epidermidis. The MIX (RJI-C and TB-KK) showed synergistic antimicrobial effects and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine production.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activities of the peptides using in vitro and in vivo models, including disk diffusion, MIC testing, hemolytic assays, and animal infection models.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular analysis of human and canine Staphylococcus aureus strains reveals distinct extended-host-spectrum genotypes independent of their methicillin resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Staphylococcus aureus strains from humans and dogs, including bla, aadD, erm(C), tet(M), tet(K), and qacC, which confer resistance to beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, macrolides, tetracyclines, and quaternary ammonium compounds, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized DNA-microarray hybridization and molecular typing techniques to analyze AMR genes in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Partial complementation of Sinorhizobium meliloti bacA mutant phenotypes by the Mycobacterium tuberculosis BacA protein.
full_output.key_findings: The Mycobacterium tuberculosis BacA protein partially restores the ability of a Sinorhizobium meliloti bacA mutant to form bacteroids and protects it against antimicrobial peptides, indicating a role in peptide uptake and resistance.
full_output.methodology: Expression of M. tuberculosis bacA in S. meliloti mutants, assessment of symbiotic defects, and evaluation of resistance to antimicrobial peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Role of the Mmr efflux pump in drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

mmr.validation_method: drug susceptibility assays and fluorometric detection of ethidium bromide efflux

full_output.key_findings: The Mmr efflux pump in Mycobacterium tuberculosis was found to contribute to resistance against ethidium bromide, tetraphenylphosphonium, safranin O, and cetyltrimethylammonium bromide. However, it did not significantly affect isoniazid resistance.
full_output.methodology: Construction of Mmr knockout and overexpression mutants, drug susceptibility assays, and fluorometric detection of ethidium bromide efflux.

full_output.paper_title: Identifying genetic susceptibility to sensitization to cephalosporins in health care workers.
full_output.key_findings: The FcεR1β -109T > C polymorphism was significantly associated with IgE sensitization to cephalosporins in health care workers, with the T allele showing increased promoter activity.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping of SNPs and functional assays in human mast cells.

full_output.paper_title: The nonantibiotic small molecule cyslabdan enhances the potency of β-lactams against MRSA by inhibiting pentaglycine interpeptide bridge synthesis.

fema.mechanism: inhibits FemA, thereby suppressing pentaglycine interpeptide bridge synthesis
fema.validation_method: binding assay and enzymatic activity assay
fema.evidence_note: The paper identifies FemA as a target of cyslabdan and describes its role in the synthesis of the pentaglycine interpeptide bridge of the peptidoglycan of MRSA.

full_output.key_findings: Cyslabdan enhances the potency of β-lactams against MRSA by inhibiting FemA, which is involved in the synthesis of the pentaglycine interpeptide bridge of the peptidoglycan.
full_output.methodology: Binding assay, enzymatic activity assay, and HPLC analysis.

full_output.paper_title: A truncated AdeS kinase protein generated by ISAba1 insertion correlates with tigecycline resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii.

adeS.validation_method: cloning and expression in a knockout strain

adeR.notes: Mutations in AdeR were found in all TGC resistant isolates except for the two TGC sensitive isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a truncated AdeS kinase protein generated by ISAba1 insertion, which leads to tigecycline resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii by constitutively activating the AdeABC efflux pump.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, cloning, and expression analysis in a knockout strain.

full_output.paper_title: Modulation of antimicrobial host defense peptide gene expression by free fatty acids.
full_output.key_findings: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) such as acetate, propionate, and butyrate strongly induce the expression of antimicrobial host defense peptides (HDPs) like AvBD9 and cathelicidin B1 in chicken cells, enhancing resistance against Salmonella enteritidis.
full_output.methodology: Real-time RT-PCR and HDAC activity assays were used to analyze gene expression and the mechanism of HDP induction by free fatty acids.

full_output.paper_title: An altered immune response, but not individual cationic antimicrobial peptides, is associated with the oral attenuation of Ara4N-deficient Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium in mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pmrF as a critical gene for Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium virulence, as its deletion leads to a virulence defect in mice upon oral infection due to increased sensitivity to cationic antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.methodology: Generation of pmrF mutant strains and assessment of their virulence in mice.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the challenges of eradicating Helicobacter pylori in India, highlighting the impact of antibiotic resistance on treatment success and emphasizing the need for region-specific treatment regimens.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and clinical data on H. pylori infection and antibiotic resistance in India.

full_output.paper_title: Interaction of lipocalin 2, transferrin, and siderophores determines the replicative niche of Klebsiella pneumoniae during pneumonia.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the siderophores enterobactin (Ent) and yersiniabactin (Ybt) play critical roles in the pathogenesis of Klebsiella pneumoniae, with Ent being counteracted by lipocalin 2 (Lcn2) and Ybt supporting bacterial replication in the presence of Lcn2. Transferrin inhibits Ybt-dependent growth, highlighting the importance of iron acquisition mechanisms in bacterial virulence.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized isogenic mutants of K. pneumoniae, murine pneumonia models, histopathological analysis, and in vitro growth assays to investigate the roles of siderophores and host defense mechanisms in bacterial infection.

full_output.paper_title: 'Transient' genetic suppression facilitates generation of hexose transporter null mutants in Leishmania mexicana.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LmxPIFTC3 as a transient suppressor that facilitates the generation of hexose transporter null mutants in Leishmania mexicana, but is not essential for their long-term survival.
full_output.methodology: Targeted gene replacement, cosmid library construction, plasmid shuffling, and Southern blot analysis were used to characterize the role of LmxPIFTC3 in genetic suppression.

full_output.paper_title: First clinical cases of OXA-48-producing carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in the United States: the "menace" arrives in the new world.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first clinical cases of OXA-48-producing carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in the United States, highlighting the emergence of OXA-48 and OXA-181 as significant carbapenemases in Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the carbapenemases.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a ferritin-like protein of Listeria monocytogenes as a mediator of β-lactam tolerance and innate resistance to cephalosporins.

fri.mechanism: mediates β-lactam tolerance and innate resistance to cephalosporins

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the ferritin-like protein Fri as a mediator of β-lactam tolerance and innate resistance to cephalosporins in Listeria monocytogenes. Disruption of the fri gene increases sensitivity to penicillin G, ampicillin, cefalotin, and cephradine.
full_output.methodology: Promoter-trap system, transcriptional analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of deletion mutants.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a BioMAP screening method to identify and classify natural product antibiotics, leading to the discovery of a novel naphthoquinone antibiotic called arromycin with unique structural features and antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a panel of 15 bacterial strains and BioMAP profiling to analyze the activity of antibiotics and natural product extracts, leading to the identification of arromycin.

full_output.key_findings: The FER gene delivery via electroporation improved survival in a murine model of trauma-related pneumonia by enhancing innate immune responses and reducing bacterial loads.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility profiles of Mycoplasma sp. 1220 strains isolated from geese in Hungary.

full_output.paper_title: Distinct Salmonella Enteritidis lineages associated with enterocolitis in high-income settings and invasive disease in low-income settings.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the blaIMP-4 gene in Citrobacter freundii B38, which confers resistance to carbapenems. The gene is part of a class 1 integron on plasmid pOZ172, along with other resistance determinants.
full_output.methodology: Genome and plasmid sequencing using PacBio SMRT technology.

full_output.paper_title: Cefazolin and Ertapenem, a Synergistic Combination Used To Clear Persistent Staphylococcus aureus Bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the combination of cefazolin (CZ) and ertapenem (ETP) exhibits synergistic activity against methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) and some methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) strains, enhancing bactericidal effects and reducing heteroresistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro checkerboard assays, time-kill assays, disk diffusion, and in vivo murine skin infection models to evaluate the synergistic effects of CZ and ETP against S. aureus strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the identification of antibiotic resistance genes from preterm infant gut metagenomic libraries through functional selection and sequencing.
full_output.methodology: Functional selection of antibiotic resistance genes from metagenomic libraries, followed by PCR amplification, sequencing, and bioinformatics analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes florfenicol and linezolid resistance genes, including cfr, optrA, floR, fexA, and fexB, in soils adjacent to swine feedlots, highlighting their prevalence and association with florfenicol usage.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR, metagenomic sequencing, and UPLC-MS/MS were used to analyze the abundance and distribution of florfenicol resistance genes in soil samples.

full_output.paper_title: Network analysis identifies Rv0324 and Rv0880 as regulators of bedaquiline tolerance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Rv0324 and Rv0880 as regulators of bedaquiline tolerance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Knockout of these transcription factors increases the susceptibility of MTB to bedaquiline, suggesting their role in mediating tolerance.
full_output.methodology: The study uses systems-level network models (EGRIN and PROM) to analyze transcriptional responses to bedaquiline, along with experimental validation through transcription factor knockout mutants and time-kill assays.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Analysis Reveals Multi-Drug Resistance Clusters in Group B Streptococcus CC17 Hypervirulent Isolates Causing Neonatal Invasive Disease in Southern Mainland China.

tetO.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

ermB.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

ant6.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

aphA.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

ant9.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

lnuB.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple antibiotic resistance genes, including tetO, ermB, ant6, aphA, ant9, and lnuB, in Group B Streptococcus CC17 isolates from China, highlighting the emergence of multi-drug resistance in these hypervirulent strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify and characterize the antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: High Gastrointestinal Colonization Rate with Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase-Producing Enterobacteriaceae in Hospitalized Patients: Emergence of Carbapenemase-Producing K. pneumoniae in Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a high gastrointestinal colonization rate with extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacteriaceae, including ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae and E. coli, and identifies the emergence of carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae in Ethiopia.
full_output.methodology: The study used chromogenic agar, Vitek 2 system, and Neo-Sensitabs for bacterial identification, ESBL detection, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro and in vivo bactericidal activity of Tinospora sagittata (Oliv.) Gagnep. var. craveniana (S.Y.Hu) Lo and its main effective component, palmatine, against porcine Helicobacter pylori.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Tinospora sagittata (TSG) and its main component, palmatine, exhibit bactericidal activity against Helicobacter pylori in vitro and in vivo. The MIC and MBC of TSG against H. pylori SCYA201401 and SS1 were both 6250 μg/mL, while palmatine had lower MIC values of 6.25 μg/mL and 3.12 μg/mL for SCYA201401 and SS1, respectively. In vivo, TSG achieved an 80% eradication rate, and palmatine achieved a 50% eradication rate, comparable to triple therapy.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar cup diffusion, MIC/MBC tests, time-kill curves, and in vivo experiments in mice to assess the bactericidal activity of TSG and palmatine against H. pylori.

full_output.paper_title: Triclosan Resistome from Metagenome Reveals Diverse Enoyl Acyl Carrier Protein Reductases and Selective Enrichment of Triclosan Resistance Genes
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies diverse enoyl acyl carrier protein reductases (ENRs) from metagenomic sources that confer triclosan resistance in Escherichia coli through complementation analysis.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic library screening, subcloning, complementation analysis, and phylogenetic analysis were used to identify and characterize triclosan resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Colistin- and Carbapenem-Resistant Escherichia coli Harboring mcr-1 and blaNDM-5, Causing a Complicated Urinary Tract Infection in a Patient from the United States.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the isolation of an Escherichia coli strain harboring both mcr-1 and blaNDM-5, which conferred resistance to colistin and carbapenems, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid transfer experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: A High-Content, Phenotypic Screen Identifies Fluorouridine as an Inhibitor of Pyoverdine Biosynthesis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa Virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 5-fluorouridine (FUR) as a potent antivirulent compound that inhibits pyoverdine biosynthesis in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, thereby reducing its virulence. FUR does not exhibit bactericidal or bacteriostatic activity, distinguishing it as a specific antivirulent agent.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput phenotypic screening using a C. elegans model to identify compounds that inhibit P. aeruginosa virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Propargyl-Linked Antifolates Are Potent Inhibitors of Drug-Sensitive and Drug-Resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies propargyl-linked antifolates (PLAs) as potent inhibitors of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including drug-sensitive and drug-resistant strains. These compounds show high activity against MDR and XDR strains, with some compounds having MIC values as low as 0.03 μg/mL. The research highlights the potential of PLAs as novel antitubercular agents.
full_output.methodology: The study involved screening PLAs for antibacterial activity against M. tuberculosis, evaluating enzyme inhibition, and determining MIC values. Crystallographic analysis was conducted to understand the molecular interactions of PLAs with MtbDHFR.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of new diketopiperazines inhibiting Burkholderia cenocepacia quorum sensing in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies four diketopiperazine derivatives (8a, 8b, 8c, and 6a) that inhibit the quorum sensing (QS) enzyme CepI of Burkholderia cenocepacia, reducing the production of virulence factors such as proteases and siderophores, and affecting biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study used recombinant CepI enzyme purification, enzymatic activity assays, and structural bioinformatics predictions to identify and characterize the inhibitory effects of diketopiperazine derivatives on CepI.

full_output.paper_title: Time-resolved, single-cell analysis of induced and programmed cell death via non-invasive propidium iodide and counterstain perfusion.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a non-invasive, real-time method for analyzing cell death using propidium iodide (PI) and counterstains in a microfluidic device. It observed antibiotic tolerance in wild-type Corynebacterium glutamicum and analyzed programmed cell death in E. coli and S. cerevisiae.
full_output.methodology: Microfluidic cultivation with dynamic PI staining and counterstains for real-time single-cell analysis of cell death and antibiotic tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-Genome Characterization and Strain Comparison of VT2f-Producing Escherichia coli Causing Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes VT2f-producing E. coli strains from human patients and pigeons, identifying a phage carrying the vtx2f genes and highlighting differences in virulence gene profiles between strains causing different disease severities.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and bioinformatics analyses were used to characterize the strains and their virulence profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical relevance of molecular identification of microorganisms and detection of antimicrobial resistance genes in bloodstream infections of paediatric cancer patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of mecA, vanA, blaCTX, and blaSPM genes in various pathogens associated with bloodstream infections in paediatric cancer patients, highlighting the significance of molecular detection for rapid and accurate identification of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized qPCR for molecular detection of microorganisms and antimicrobial resistance genes, alongside conventional phenotypic methods for comparison.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology of carbapenem resistant gram-negative bacilli from infected pediatric population in tertiary - care hospitals in Medellín, Colombia: an increasing problem.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified KPC carbapenemase as the primary resistance mechanism in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, with KPC-2 and KPC-3 variants detected. VIM-2 carbapenemase was found in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, and KPC-3 was detected in Enterobacter cloacae.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing for detection of carbapenemase genes, PFGE, and MLST for molecular typing.

full_output.paper_title: A novel method for investigating Burkholderia cenocepacia infections in patients with cystic fibrosis and other chronic diseases of the airways.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a novel model using human A549 lung carcinoma cells (HLCCs) in 60% artificial sputum medium (ASMDM) to investigate Burkholderia cenocepacia infections, demonstrating that B. cenocepacia can associate with and damage HLCC monolayers in this environment.
full_output.methodology: The study used human A549 lung carcinoma cells cultured in gas-permeable plates with varying concentrations of ASMDM to assess cell viability and B. cenocepacia growth and invasion.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes of Salmonella enterica isolated from pet dogs and cats.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella enterica isolates from pet dogs and cats, including dfrA12, aadA2, cmlA, strA, strB, tetA, tetB, dfrA1, dfrA10, dfrA12, aadA1, aadA2, sul1, sul2, sul3, blaTEM, blaCTX-M, and qnrS. These genes were associated with resistance to trimethoprim, chloramphenicol, streptomycin, tetracycline, sulfamethoxazole, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella enterica isolates.

full_output.paper_title: ABCB1 and ABCC11 confer resistance to eribulin in breast cancer cell lines.

ABCB1.validation_method: overexpression in HEK293T cells and knockdown in breast cancer cell lines

ABCC11.validation_method: overexpression in HEK293T cells and knockdown in breast cancer cell lines

full_output.key_findings: ABCB1 and ABCC11 confer resistance to eribulin in breast cancer cell lines through their efflux pump activities, as demonstrated by overexpression and knockdown experiments.
full_output.methodology: Overexpression and knockdown experiments in breast cancer cell lines and HEK293T cells, along with WST assays to measure drug sensitivity.
full_output.sample_size: 7 breast cancer cell lines and HEK293T cells

full_output.paper_title: Global Mapping of Small RNA-Target Interactions in Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents RIL-seq, a method for identifying Hfq-bound small RNA (sRNA)-target interactions in bacteria. It reveals numerous sRNA-target interactions, expands the known sRNA targets, and provides insights into the mechanisms of sRNA regulation.
full_output.methodology: RIL-seq combines experimental and computational approaches to identify Hfq-bound sRNA-target interactions in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Reverse Chemical Genetics: Comprehensive Fitness Profiling Reveals the Spectrum of Drug Target Interactions.

dfr1.notes: Mutations were identified through high-throughput screening and validated through growth assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple point mutations in the DFR1 gene that confer resistance to methotrexate, demonstrating the utility of functional variomics in identifying drug-resistant variants.
full_output.methodology: Functional variomics combined with deep sequencing and Bayesian statistical modeling was used to identify and validate methotrexate-resistant DFR1 mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of Novel Bacterial Cell-Penetrating Phylloseptins in Defensive Skin Secretions of the South American Hylid Frogs, Phyllomedusa duellmani and Phyllomedusa coelestis.
full_output.key_findings: Two novel phylloseptin peptides, PS-Du and PS-Co, were identified from the skin secretions of Phyllomedusa duellmani and Phyllomedusa coelestis. These peptides exhibited antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria as well as a pathogenic yeast.
full_output.methodology: The study involved cloning of cDNAs, structural characterization via HPLC and mass spectrometry, and evaluation of antimicrobial and hemolytic activities of the synthesized peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Essential Genes for In Vitro Growth of the Endophyte Herbaspirillum seropedicae SmR1 as Revealed by Transposon Insertion Site Sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: This study identified 395 genes essential for the in vitro growth and survival of Herbaspirillum seropedicae SmR1 using transposon insertion site sequencing (Tn-seq).
full_output.methodology: Transposon insertion site sequencing (Tn-seq) was used to analyze the essential genes for in vitro growth of H. seropedicae SmR1.

full_output.paper_title: Streptococcus pneumoniae Senses a Human-like Sialic Acid Profile via the Response Regulator CiaR.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies nanA, satA, and ciaR as genes involved in Streptococcus pneumoniae's response to Neu5Ac, a human-like sialic acid profile, contributing to increased virulence and resistance to oxidative stress.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptional analysis, bacterial growth assays, and mouse infection models were used to investigate the role of nanA, satA, and ciaR in S. pneumoniae's response to Neu5Ac.

full_output.paper_title: Two lytic transglycosylases in Neisseria gonorrhoeae impart resistance to killing by lysozyme and human neutrophils.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LtgA and LtgD lytic transglycosylases as critical for Neisseria gonorrhoeae survival against lysozyme and neutrophil antimicrobials, highlighting their role in maintaining envelope integrity.
full_output.methodology: Ex vivo survival assays, genetic complementation, and biochemical analyses were used to assess the role of LtgA and LtgD in Gc resistance to neutrophil antimicrobials.

full_output.paper_title: PSM-Mec-A Virulence Determinant that Connects Transcriptional Regulation, Virulence, and Antibiotic Resistance in Staphylococci.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PSM-mec as a virulence determinant in staphylococci, highlighting its role in regulating virulence and antibiotic resistance through both a cytolytic peptide and a regulatory RNA.
full_output.methodology: Expression studies, functional assays, and genetic manipulation of PSM-mec in Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance Profile of Planktonic and Biofilm Cells of Staphylococcus aureus and Coagulase-Negative Staphylococci.
full_output.key_findings: The study determined the antimicrobial resistance profiles of planktonic and biofilm cells of Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS). It found that biofilm cells exhibited significantly higher minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) compared to planktonic cells, particularly for vancomycin and erythromycin. Linezolid was the most effective drug against biofilm cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution method to determine MICs and MBCB for various antibiotics against planktonic and biofilm cells of Staphylococcus spp.

full_output.paper_title: Low Enteric Colonization with Multidrug-Resistant Pathogens in Soldiers Returning from Deployments- Experience from the Years 2007-2015.

vanA.mechanism: alteration of peptidoglycan precursors

full_output.key_findings: The study found low levels of enteric colonization with multidrug-resistant pathogens in soldiers returning from deployments, with the most common resistance mechanisms being bla TEM, bla SHV, bla CTX-M group 1, and bla CTX-M group IV beta-lactamases, as well as vanA-mediated glycopeptide resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used culture screening, PCR, Sanger sequencing, and phenotypic resistance testing to identify and characterize multidrug-resistant pathogens in stool samples from soldiers.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and burden of multidrug-resistant bacterial infection in a developing country.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial infections in Thailand, with significant excess mortality attributed to MDR bacteria in hospital-acquired infections.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of microbiology and hospital databases from nine public hospitals in northeast Thailand.

full_output.paper_title: Silver-nanoparticles-modified biomaterial surface resistant to staphylococcus: new insight into the antimicrobial action of silver.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that silver nanoparticle-modified titanium surfaces reduced the expression of biofilm-related genes icaA, icaR, fnbA, and fnbB in Staphylococcus epidermidis and Staphylococcus aureus, thereby inhibiting biofilm formation and bacterial adhesion.
full_output.methodology: The study used SEM, CLSM, qRT-PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to evaluate the effects of silver nanoparticle-modified surfaces on biofilm formation and gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Chemicals Are Associated with Elevated Antibiotic Resistance Genes in the Indoor Dust Microbiome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several antibiotic resistance genes, including tet(W), blaSRT-1, erm(B), erm(X), erm(33), tet(K), vga(A), and cmr, which are associated with elevated levels of antimicrobial chemicals in indoor dust.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenome sequencing and chemical analysis were used to characterize the resistome and antimicrobial chemical concentrations in dust samples.

full_output.paper_title: Abundance of Class 1 Integron-Integrase and Sulfonamide Resistance Genes in River Water and Sediment Is Affected by Anthropogenic Pressure and Environmental Factors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the abundance of class 1 integron-integrase gene (intI1) and sulfonamide resistance genes (sul1 and sul2) in river water and sediment, highlighting the impact of anthropogenic pressure and environmental factors on their distribution.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR was used to quantify the abundance of intI1, sul1, and sul2 genes in water and sediment samples.

full_output.paper_title: Pyrazinamide Resistance Assays and Two-Month Sputum Culture Status in Patients with Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated pyrazinamide resistance in multidrug-resistant tuberculosis patients using various assays and identified pncA mutations as a factor in resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used phenotypic drug susceptibility testing, Bactec MGIT 960 method, and pncA gene sequencing to assess pyrazinamide resistance.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and complementation experiments were used to validate the role of identified mutations in colistin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Fluorescence-Based Flow Sorting in Parallel with Transposon Insertion Site Sequencing Identifies Multidrug Efflux Systems in Acinetobacter baumannii.

adeIJK.validation_method: transposon insertion sequencing and flow cytometry

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the AdeABC, AdeIJK, and AmvA efflux systems and their regulators, AdeRS, AdeN, and AmvR, as critical for ethidium accumulation and resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.methodology: The study used fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) in combination with transposon insertion site sequencing (TraDIS) to identify genes involved in ethidium efflux and resistance.
full_output.sample_size: More than 100,000 unique transposon insertion mutants

full_output.paper_title: aroA-Deficient Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhimurium Is More Than a Metabolically Attenuated Mutant.
full_output.key_findings: Deletion of aroA in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium leads to increased immunogenicity and pathogenicity, along with altered metabolic and gene expression profiles, highlighting the importance of the shikimate pathway in bacterial physiology and host interactions.
full_output.methodology: Genetic deletion, transcriptome analysis, phenotypic characterization, and in vivo infection experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Horizontal Transfer of the Salmonella enterica Serovar Infantis Resistance and Virulence Plasmid pESI to the Gut Microbiota of Warm-Blooded Hosts.

mutations_found.position_in_molecule: upstream of traC and pil genes
mutations_found.effect_on_function: positive transcriptional regulator of the conjugative pilus genes

traB.evidence_note: The paper states that traB is a transcriptional regulator of pESI conjugation and that an in-frame deletion of traB resulted in decreased pilV transcription and pESI conjugation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the plasmid pESI, which confers multidrug resistance and virulence in Salmonella enterica serovar Infantis, and demonstrates its horizontal transfer to the gut microbiota of warm-blooded hosts, including commensal E. coli and Lactobacillus reuteri, highlighting the role of the microbiota in the spread of resistance and virulence genes.
full_output.methodology: The study uses molecular techniques such as PCR, qRT-PCR, conjugation assays, and whole-genome sequencing to analyze the structure, function, and transferability of the pESI plasmid.

full_output.paper_title: Design, synthesis, and characterization of (1-(4-aryl)- 1H-1,2,3-triazol-4-yl)methyl, substituted phenyl-6-methyl-2-oxo-1,2,3,4-tetrahydropyrimidine-5-carboxylates against Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of novel (1-(4-aryl)-1H-1,2,3-triazol-4-yl)methyl, substituted phenyl-6-methyl-2-oxo-1,2,3,4-tetrahydropyrimidine-5-carboxylates against Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Compound 7d showed promising antitubercular activity against H37Rv and multidrug-resistant strains of M. tuberculosis at 10 and 15 μg/mL, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized using a click reaction and evaluated for antitubercular activity using the resazurin microplate assay method.

full_output.paper_title: Loss of phosphodiesterase 4D mediates acquired triapine resistance via Epac-Rap1-Integrin signaling.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PDE4D as a critical gene in triapine resistance, where its loss leads to increased cAMP levels and subsequent activation of the Epac-Rap1-integrin signaling pathway, contributing to acquired triapine resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic characterization, aCGH, Western blotting, and cell viability assays were used to analyze triapine resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and Characterization of Oxacillin Susceptible mecA-Positive Clinical Isolates of Staphylococcus aureus Causing Bovine Mastitis in India.

mecA.validation_method: PCR amplification and SCC mec typing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified oxacillin-susceptible mecA-positive Staphylococcus aureus (OS-MRSA) strains in bovine mastitis cases in India, highlighting the importance of combining genetic and phenotypic tests for accurate detection.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, SCC mec typing, MLST, spa typing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology of Staphylococcus aureus in the General Population in Northeast Germany: Results of the Study of Health in Pomerania (SHIP-TREND-0).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains, primarily belonging to the HA-MRSA-ST22 lineage, and detected one livestock-associated MRSA ST398 isolate. It also found that MRSA carriage was associated with frequent healthcare contacts.
full_output.methodology: The study used spa genotyping, MLST, and multiplex PCR for detecting virulence and resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Bioinformatic Characterization of Detected T. pallidum Proteins
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the proteome of T. pallidum, identifying 557 proteins, with a focus on their functional categories, cellular localization, and abundance. It highlights the presence of various virulence factors and provides insights into the unique nature of the T. pallidum proteome.
full_output.methodology: Mass spectrometry and bioinformatic analyses were used to characterize the T. pallidum proteome, including protein identification, functional categorization, and subcellular localization prediction.

full_output.paper_title: Development of Recombinant Lactococcus lactis Displaying Albumin-Binding Domain Variants against Shiga Toxin 1 B Subunit.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two albumin-binding domain variants, S1B22 and S1B26, which effectively bind to Shiga toxin 1B (Stx1B) and interfere with its retrograde transport, potentially offering a strategy for toxin neutralization.
full_output.methodology: Recombinant Stx1B was produced in E. coli and used to select ABD variants via ribosome display. The selected variants were characterized using ELISA, SPR, and MST.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic interaction mapping reveals a strain-dependent underlying genomic network
full_output.key_findings: The study identified genes involved in daptomycin resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae strains T4 and 19F, highlighting strain-specific differences in genetic networks and mechanisms of resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transposon insertion sequencing (Tn-Seq) and deletion mutant analysis were used to identify genes involved in daptomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Gammaproteobacteria as essential primary symbionts in the striped shield bug, Graphosoma Lineatum (Hemiptera: Pentatomidae).
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the gut symbiotic bacterium in Graphosoma lineatum, identifying it as a Gram-negative Gammaproteobacterium closely related to Pantoea agglomerans and Erwinia herbicola. The symbiont is essential for the host's development and reproduction.
full_output.methodology: Molecular phylogeny, real-time PCR, light and electron microscopy, and qPCR were used to analyze the symbiotic bacterium and its relationship with the host.
full_output.sample_size: 100 adult insects and 10 individuals of each nymphal stage

full_output.paper_title: Prodigiosin - A Multifaceted Escherichia coli Antimicrobial Agent.
full_output.key_findings: Prodigiosin acts as a bacteriostatic agent in E. coli, affecting multiple physiological processes such as protein and RNA synthesis, cell division, and metabolic activity. It does not confer resistance to antibiotics but rather enhances survival when combined with certain antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Experimental analysis of prodigiosin's effects on E. coli physiology, including membrane integrity, DNA damage, and antibiotic survival assays.

full_output.paper_title: Colonization of Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli and Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli in chickens and humans in southern Vietnam.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-function analysis of Avian β-defensin-6 and β-defensin-12: role of charge and disulfide bridges.

full_output.paper_title: Multiplication of Legionella pneumophila Sequence Types 1, 47, and 62 in Buffered Yeast Extract Broth and Biofilms Exposed to Flowing Tap Water at Temperatures of 38°C to 42°C.

full_output.methodology: The study used buffered yeast extract broth and biofilm experiments to analyze the growth of different L. pneumophila sequence types at various temperatures.

Additionally, the paper mentions that "the wild-type amino acid residue at these positions was substituted by the second most frequently occurring amino acid and/or those with similar physicochemical properties as the wild-type residue" and that "the imipenem resistance levels (minimum inhibitory concentrations, MIC) of E. coli cells transformed with empty vector and the wild-type CphA expression vector were determined to be 0.25 μg/ml and 2 μg/ml, respectively."

full_output.methodology: Structural and biochemical analyses, including X-ray crystallography and DNA cleavage assays, were used to investigate the resistance mechanisms of the fluoroquinolones.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel livestock-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strain (CC9/CC398) that has adapted to humans and is transmitted through poultry meat, highlighting potential foodborne transmission routes.

blaSHV-2.source: The first bla SHV-2 gene was identified in the 1970s in E. coli (Pitton, 1972). The encoded enzyme SHV−1 (sulfhydryl reagent variable) proved its activity against penicillins and first generation cephalosporins (Matthew et al., 1979) and was confirmed part of the conjugative plasmid p453 (Barthélémy et al., 1988 ; Table 1 ). The most likely ancestor of the plasmid-mediated SHV−1 is a chromosomal species-specific penicillinase detected in fecal K. pneumoniae isolates from neonates (Haeggman et al., 1997 ).
blaSHV-2.evidence_note: The first report of SHV-mediated resistance to third-generation cephalosporins was in 1983 with the isolation and characterization of bla SHV-2 , encoded by plasmid pBP60 in a German clinical isolate of Klebsiella ozaenae and showing only a few nucleotide mismatches with bla SHV-1 (Kliebe et al., 1985 ).

full_output.paper_title: Longitudinal Comparison of Antibiotic Resistance in Diarrheagenic and Non-pathogenic Escherichia coli from Young Tanzanian Children.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high prevalence of antibiotic resistance in both pathogenic and non-pathogenic E. coli isolates from young Tanzanian children, with resistance to ampicillin and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole being particularly common. full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple S. Typhi genotypes in Nigeria, with a focus on antimicrobial resistance genes and plasmids. full_output.paper_title: Ethyl Pyruvate: An Anti-Microbial Agent that Selectively Targets Pathobionts and Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: Ethyl pyruvate (EP) selectively targets pathobionts and biofilms, demonstrating broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against various fungal and bacterial pathogens, including Candida species, dermatophytes, and Aspergillus fumigatus, without affecting beneficial Lactobacillus species.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity of EP was assessed using broth microdilution, agar macrodilution, and biofilm formation assays, with MIC and MBC/MFC determined for various microbial isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes two fully sequenced multi-drug resistant plasmids, pP10164-2 and pP10164-3, from Leclercia adecarboxylata. These plasmids harbor numerous resistance genes conferring resistance to multiple antibiotic classes, including beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, quinolones, tetracyclines, and others. The plasmids also contain mobile elements such as transposons and integrons, contributing to the spread of resistance.
full_output.methodology: The plasmids were sequenced using high-throughput shotgun sequencing and PCR-based gap closure. Resistance genes and mobile elements were identified through bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation.

full_output.paper_title: A 5-year Surveillance Study on Antimicrobial Resistance of Acinetobacter baumannii Clinical Isolates from a Tertiary Greek Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 92.89% of Acinetobacter baumannii isolates were multidrug resistant (MDR), with resistance to multiple antibiotic classes. Colistin remained the most effective antibiotic, but resistance to it increased significantly in 2014.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Vitek 2 automated system and E-test method for selected antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Two case reports: Whole genome sequencing of two clinical macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae isolates with different responses to azithromycin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified A2063G mutations in the 23S rRNA gene of two macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae isolates, which are associated with resistance to macrolide antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted on the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infection in a Child with Cystic Fibrosis.

ceftolozane.mechanism: enhanced in vitro activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa

full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing and pharmacokinetic modeling were used to evaluate the effectiveness of ceftolozane/tazobactam.
