full_output.methodology: The paper is a review article discussing the epidemiology, risk factors, and management of antibacterial resistance in HSCT recipients.

full_output.paper_title: Model systems for the study of Enterococcal colonization and infection.

vanA.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

vanB.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews various animal models for studying Enterococcal colonization and infection, focusing on virulence factors and resistance mechanisms such as vanA and vanB for vancomycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Review of animal models and experimental studies on Enterococcal virulence factors and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Draft Genome Sequences of Pandrug-Resistant Serratia marcescens Clinical Isolates Harboring blaNDM-1.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the draft genome sequences of two pandrug-resistant Serratia marcescens clinical isolates carrying multiple antibiotic resistance genes, including blaNDM-1, blaSHV-12, blaTEM-1B, blaCMY-6, sul1, sul2, rmtC, aacA4, aac(6')Ib-c, strA, strB, dfrA18, qnrA1, catA2, aac(6')-Ic, tet(41), and ampC.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and analysis using the CGE platform and RAST annotation tool.

full_output.paper_title: Shigatoxin encoding Bacteriophage ϕ24(B) modulates bacterial metabolism to raise antimicrobial tolerance.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the Shiga toxin-prophage ϕ24 B increases antimicrobial tolerance in E. coli MC1061 to chloroxylenol and 8-hydroxyquinoline without encoding traditional antimicrobial resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used Biolog phenotype microarrays, metabolite profiling, and sub-inhibitory concentration tests to assess the impact of ϕ24 B on E. coli metabolism and antimicrobial tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Overexpression of MoSM1, encoding for an immunity-inducing protein from Magnaporthe oryzae, in rice confers broad-spectrum resistance against fungal and bacterial diseases.

MoSM1.mechanism: modulates SA- and JA-mediated signaling pathways
MoSM1.validation_method: transgenic rice lines with overexpression of MoSM1 showed improved resistance against M. oryzae and X. oryzae pv. oryzae

full_output.paper_title: Experimental and In-Silico Investigation of Anti-Microbial Activity of 1-Chloro-2-Isocyanatoethane Derivatives of Thiomorpholine, Piperazine and Morpholine.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of 1-chloro-2-isocyanatoethane derivatives of thiomorpholine (CTC), piperazine (CPC), and morpholine (CMC). CMC showed some antimicrobial activity against certain Gram-negative bacteria, while CTC and CPC were inactive against all Gram-negative organisms tested. The compounds exhibited varying levels of activity against Gram-positive bacteria and none were effective against yeast strains.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using agar well diffusion and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) assays, along with molecular docking simulations to investigate the interaction of the compounds with DNA gyrase.

full_output.paper_title: Changes in Molecular Characteristics of Mycoplasma pneumoniae in Clinical Specimens from Children in Beijing between 2003 and 2015.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified macrolide resistance mutations in the 23S rRNA gene of Mycoplasma pneumoniae, with the A2063G mutation being the most prevalent. There was a significant association between the MLVA type M4-5-7-2 and macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Molecular typing and detection of macrolide resistance mutations through PCR and sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Nasal Carriage of Staphylococcus aureus among Children in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified nasal carriage of Staphylococcus aureus among children in the Ashanti region of Ghana, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) isolates and methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA). High prevalence of Panton-Valentine leukocidin (PVL) was noted, raising concerns about potential for virulent MRSA clones.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting nasal swabs from children, characterizing S. aureus isolates through antimicrobial susceptibility testing, spa-typing, and molecular detection of virulence factors.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic discovery throughout the Small World Initiative: A molecular strategy to identify biosynthetic gene clusters involved in antagonistic activity.

mutations_found.position_in_molecule: gene encoding a pyridoxal phosphate-dependent aminotransferase

aminotransferase.notes: The gene was identified as part of a biosynthetic gene cluster involved in antagonistic activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) in Pseudomonas strain SWI36 that is involved in antagonistic activity against various pathogens, including Bacillus cereus, Listeria monocytogenes, and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). A transposon insertion in a gene encoding a pyridoxal phosphate-dependent aminotransferase leads to loss of antagonistic activity.
full_output.methodology: The study uses transposon mutagenesis, genome sequencing, and linkage-mediated PCR to identify and characterize the BGC involved in antagonistic activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that carbon sources like fumarate and glyoxylate modulate tobramycin susceptibility in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by affecting the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and respiratory activity, thereby influencing drug uptake and lethality.
full_output.methodology: The study used metabolic screening, gene expression analysis, metabolite profiling, and respiratory activity measurements to investigate the impact of carbon sources on tobramycin susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: The Resistome of Farmed Fish Feces Contributes to the Enrichment of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Sediments below Baltic Sea Fish Farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antibiotic resistance genes in the intestinal contents of farmed fish, including aadA1, aadA2, catA1, dfrA1, intI1, qacEΔ1, sul1, emrB, tet(32), tetM, tetO, tetW, and tnpA. These genes were found to be enriched in the sediments below fish farms, suggesting that farmed fish feces contribute to the enrichment of antibiotic resistance genes in the environment.
full_output.methodology: The study used a WaferGen qPCR array with 364 primer sets to detect and quantify antibiotic resistance genes in the intestinal contents of 20 fish from two Baltic Sea farms.

full_output.paper_title: ABCF2, an Nrf2 target gene, contributes to cisplatin resistance in ovarian cancer cells.

ABCF2.encodes: cytosolic member of the ABC superfamily of transporters
ABCF2.mechanism: NRF2 target gene with functional antioxidant response element (ARE) in its promoter region
ABCF2.validation_method: Stable overexpression and knockdown experiments, luciferase reporter assay, ChIP assay, cell viability and apoptosis assays

full_output.key_findings: ABCF2 is identified as a novel NRF2 target gene that contributes to cisplatin resistance in ovarian cancer cells. Its expression is regulated by NRF2, and modulation of ABCF2 levels affects cisplatin sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: Stable overexpression and knockdown of NRF2, luciferase reporter assays, ChIP assays, cell viability and apoptosis assays.
full_output.sample_size: 9 pairs of high-grade serous ovarian cancer tissues

full_output.paper_title: Superior Multiplexing Capacity of PlexPrimers Enables Sensitive and Specific Detection of SNPs and Clustered Mutations in qPCR.

23S rRNA.notes: mutations in 23S rRNA gene associated with azithromycin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study introduces a novel method using PlexPrimers and PlexZymes for the sensitive and specific detection of SNPs and clustered mutations, demonstrating high concordance with existing methods.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized qPCR with PlexPrimers and PlexZymes for the detection of SNPs and mutations in ADME genes and the 23S rRNA gene of Mycoplasma genitalium.

full_output.paper_title: Recombinant production of the antibody fragment D1.3 scFv with different Bacillus strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the recombinant production and secretion of the antibody fragment D1.3 scFv in various Bacillus strains, highlighting the importance of protease-deficient strains for improved protein stability and secretion.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic engineering techniques to construct plasmids for the expression of D1.3 scFv in different Bacillus strains, along with cultivation and analysis methods to assess protein production and secretion.

full_output.paper_title: Perturbations of Phosphatidate Cytidylyltransferase (CdsA) Mediate Daptomycin Resistance in Streptococcus mitis/oralis by a Novel Mechanism.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the cdsA gene as a novel mechanism of daptomycin resistance in Streptococcus mitis/oralis, demonstrating that loss-of-function mutations in cdsA lead to reduced phospholipid synthesis and resistance to daptomycin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, gene replacement, and complementation experiments were used to validate the role of cdsA mutations in daptomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Cyclic Boronates Inhibit All Classes of β-Lactamases.
full_output.key_findings: Cyclic boronates inhibit all classes of β-lactamases, including class A ESBLs like CTX-M-15, class C AmpC, and class D OXA enzymes, showing potent inhibition against various β-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: Fluorogenic assays, NMR spectroscopy, and crystallization were used to evaluate the inhibitory effects of cyclic boronates on β-lactamases.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Class IIa Bacteriocin Resistance in Enterococcus faecium.

manB.mechanism: confers resistance to class IIa bacteriocins by facilitating their uptake
manB.validation_method: heterologous expression in L. lactis and susceptibility testing

manC.mechanism: confers resistance to class IIa bacteriocins by facilitating their uptake
manC.validation_method: heterologous expression in L. lactis and susceptibility testing

manD.mechanism: confers resistance to class IIa bacteriocins by facilitating their uptake
manD.validation_method: heterologous expression in L. lactis and susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mannose phosphotransferase system (ManPTS) as a critical determinant of resistance to class IIa bacteriocins in Enterococcus faecium. Disruption of ManPTS components, including manB, manC, and manD, leads to reduced susceptibility to these bacteriocins. Mutations in sigma54 and manR also contribute to resistance by downregulating ManPTS expression.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, qRT-PCR, heterologous expression in L. lactis, and susceptibility testing were used to validate the role of ManPTS in bacteriocin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Formulation of Biocides Increases Antimicrobial Potency and Mitigates the Enrichment of Nonsusceptible Bacteria in Multispecies Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that formulation of the biocide benzalkonium chloride (BAC) increased antimicrobial potency, leading to greater reductions in viable bacteria compared to BAC in a simple aqueous solution. It also showed that BAC formulation significantly suppressed bacteria with reduced BAC and antibiotic susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study used domestic drain biofilm microcosms exposed to varying concentrations of BAC in simple aqueous solutions or complex formulations, followed by analysis of bacterial viability, susceptibility, and community composition through culture, 16S rRNA sequencing, and high-throughput sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Infection Dynamics and Antimicrobial Resistance Profile of Salmonella Paratyphi B d-tartrate Positive (Java) in a Persistently Infected Broiler Barn.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial resistance in Salmonella Paratyphi B d-tartrate positive (Java) isolates, including resistance to tetracycline, fluoroquinolones, trimethoprim, and cefoxitin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using agar diffusion and microdilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Phloretin Exerts Anti-Tuberculosis Activity and Suppresses Lung Inflammation.

mtKASIII.encodes: beta-ketoacyl acyl carrier protein synthase III

full_output.key_findings: Phloretin exhibits anti-tuberculosis activity by binding to and inhibiting the function of mtKASIII, a key enzyme in the fatty acid biosynthesis pathway of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: Binding affinity and docking studies, RT-PCR, Western blot, ELISA, and in vivo mouse model experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Identifying components required for OMP biogenesis as novel targets for antiinfective drugs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies BamB and SurA as critical components for outer membrane protein biogenesis and virulence in Yersinia enterocolitica. Knockout of these genes leads to increased antibiotic susceptibility and reduced virulence, highlighting their potential as targets for anti-infective drugs.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockout, complementation, disk diffusion assay, western blot, and mass spectrometry were used to evaluate the role of BamB and SurA in outer membrane integrity and virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of Quinolone Resistance in Escherichia coli Isolates from Humans, Animals, and the Environment in the Czech Republic.

aac(6')-Ib-cr.role_in_paper: aac(6′)-Ib-cr was the second most common PMQR gene in human PMQR-positive clinical isolates
aac(6')-Ib-cr.genetic_context: aac(6′)-Ib-cr was found in 82% of human PMQR-positive clinical isolates
aac(6')-Ib-cr.source: The gene aac(6′)-Ib-cr was the second most common PMQR gene in E. coli from humans
aac(6')-Ib-cr.evidence_note: aac(6′)-Ib-cr was found in 82% of human PMQR-positive clinical isolates

gyrA.notes: Common mutation in quinolone-resistant isolates

parC.notes: Common mutations in quinolone-resistant isolates

parE.notes: Less common mutation in quinolone-resistant isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified qnrS1, aac(6')-Ib-cr, and qnrB19 as the most prevalent plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance genes in E. coli isolates from various sources in the Czech Republic. Key mutations in gyrA, parC, and parE were associated with high-level quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Emerging Perils of Extended Spectrum β-Lactamase Producing Enterobacteriaceae Clinical Isolates in a Teaching Hospital of Nepal.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae, particularly E. coli and Klebsiella spp., with bla-CTX-M being the most prevalent gene followed by bla-TEM and bla-SHV.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and molecular analysis via PCR for ESBL genes.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic correlates of daptomycin-resistant methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus clinical isolates.

mprF.notes: mutations in mprF are associated with daptomycin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study reports a decrease in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infection rates in several hospital departments between 2008 and 2014, along with reduced resistance to multiple antibiotics, except for sulfamethoxazole/triprim. No specific AMR genes or mutations were characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of S. aureus isolates from various hospital departments using automated microbiological systems and CLSI standards.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance profiles and molecular characterization of Escherichia coli strains isolated from healthy adults in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-9 and bla CTX-M-1 genes as the primary contributors to extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) production in E. coli strains from healthy adults in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Additionally, bla TEM genes were found in some strains, contributing to resistance against multiple beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized multiplex PCR and sequencing to identify ESBL genes, along with disk diffusion methods for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of Serotype Prevalence of Pneumococci Isolated from Middle Ear, Lower Respiratory Tract and Invasive Disease Prior to Vaccination in Iceland.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that serotype 19F was the most common pneumococcal serotype, with a high prevalence of penicillin non-susceptible isolates. Multiresistant isolates of serotype 19F were highly prevalent, particularly from middle ear infections in young children.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed pneumococcal isolates from middle ear, lower respiratory tract, and invasive disease through serotyping and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Silver ion-mediated killing of a food pathogen: Melting curve analysis data of silver resistance genes and growth curve data.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified silver resistance genes (silA, silE, silS) in Salmonella Typhimurium and determined the minimum inhibitory concentration of silver ions as 375 μg/ml.
full_output.methodology: Melting curve analysis and growth curve experiments were conducted to evaluate silver resistance genes and their impact on bacterial growth.

full_output.paper_title: High-throughput automated microfluidic sample preparation for accurate microbial genomics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific genetic mutations in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates that correlate with resistance to imipenem, ciprofloxacin, and ceftazidime, demonstrating the utility of low-input, high-throughput WGS for predicting antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study employs low-input, high-throughput WGS combined with phenotypic susceptibility assays to identify antibiotic resistance-associated mutations in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Laboratory confirmed miltefosine resistant cases of visceral leishmaniasis from India.

LdMT.notes: Mutations in LdMT gene associated with miltefosine resistance.

full_output.key_findings: Two laboratory confirmed cases of miltefosine resistant visceral leishmaniasis caused by L. donovani were reported. Mutations in the LdMT gene (354 Tyr↔Phe and 1078 Phe↔Tyr) were identified as potential molecular markers for miltefosine resistance.
full_output.methodology: In vitro drug susceptibility tests, genetic analysis, and SNPs typing of LdMT and LdRos genes.

full_output.paper_title: Structure and Function of the PiuA and PirA Siderophore-Drug Receptors from Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Ab-PiuA and Ab-PirA as critical TonB-dependent receptors for the antimicrobial activity of BAL30072 and MC-1 in Acinetobacter baumannii. Deletion of these genes reduces susceptibility, while their overexpression increases susceptibility to the siderophore-drug conjugates.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, susceptibility testing, and structural analysis of PiuA and PirA from P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Dual Targeting of Epithelial Ovarian Cancer Via Folate Receptor α and the Proton-Coupled Folate Transporter with 6-Substituted Pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine Antifolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the antifolates AGF94 and AGF154 as potent inhibitors of epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) cell lines through dual targeting of folate receptor alpha (FRα) and the proton-coupled folate transporter (PCFT).
full_output.methodology: Real-time RT-PCR, immunohistochemistry, and cell proliferation assays were used to evaluate FRα and PCFT expression and the anti-proliferative effects of AGF94 and AGF154 in EOC cell lines.
full_output.sample_size: 41 EOC specimens and 7 normal ovary specimens

full_output.paper_title: Gut symbiont enhances insecticide resistance in a significant pest, the oriental fruit fly Bactrocera dorsalis (Hendel).
full_output.key_findings: The gut symbiont Citrobacter sp. (CF-BD) enhances resistance to the organophosphate insecticide trichlorphon in Bactrocera dorsalis by degrading trichlorphon. Five phosphatase genes (gene IDs 0086, 1012, 1747, 2752, and 4498) were identified as potentially involved in trichlorphon degradation.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, 16S rDNA sequencing, PCR, and enzyme activity assays were used to identify and characterize the phosphatase genes involved in trichlorphon degradation.

full_output.paper_title: Cj1199 Affect the Development of Erythromycin Resistance in Campylobacter jejuni through Regulation of Leucine Biosynthesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that Cj1199 affects the development of erythromycin resistance in Campylobacter jejuni by regulating leucine biosynthesis. The deletion of Cj1199 leads to a decrease in erythromycin resistance and a growth disadvantage under erythromycin pressure and in leucine-free medium.
full_output.methodology: Construction of a Cj1199 deletion mutant, microarray analysis, qRT-PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and growth assays.

full_output.paper_title: Prediction of in vivo and in vitro infection model results using a semimechanistic model of avibactam and aztreonam combination against multidrug resistant organisms.
full_output.key_findings: The study develops a semimechanistic PK/PD model to predict the efficacy of aztreonam-avibactam against multidrug-resistant organisms, demonstrating that avibactam enhances aztreonam's antibacterial activity by reducing its EC50.
full_output.methodology: Development of a semimechanistic pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model using time-kill kinetic studies and MIC data.

full_output.paper_title: TDtest: easy detection of bacterial tolerance and persistence in clinical isolates by a modified disk-diffusion assay.

vapBC.notes: Mutation 8 in the vapBC toxin-antitoxin module confers tolerance.

hipA.notes: hipA7 mutation leads to high persistence.

full_output.key_findings: The TDtest enables the detection of bacterial tolerance and persistence by modifying the standard disk-diffusion assay. It identifies strains with varying levels of tolerance to antibiotics, including those with mutations in vapBC, metG, and hipA.
full_output.methodology: The TDtest involves a modified disk-diffusion assay with an additional step involving nutrient disks to detect tolerant and persistent bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Alanine 501 Mutations in Penicillin-Binding Protein 2 from Neisseria gonorrhoeae: Structure, Mechanism, and Effects on Cephalosporin Resistance and Biological Fitness.

penA.notes: Mutations in penA gene lead to resistance to cephalosporins.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific mutations in the penA gene of Neisseria gonorrhoeae that confer resistance to cephalosporins, with particular emphasis on the A501V, A501T, A501S, A501R, and A501P mutations. These mutations increase resistance to cefixime and ceftriaxone while maintaining essential transpeptidase function.
full_output.methodology: The study involved transforming N. gonorrhoeae with mutated penA alleles, determining MICs, and analyzing the structural effects of the mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of new-generation aminoglycoside promoting premature termination codon readthrough in cancer cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes NB124, a synthetic aminoglycoside derivative, which effectively promotes readthrough of premature termination codons (PTCs) in tumor suppressor genes such as p53 and APC, leading to restoration of full-length p53 protein and subsequent apoptosis in cancer cells.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a dual reporter system, quantitative PCR, Western blot analysis, and flow cytometry to evaluate the effects of NB124 on PTC readthrough, mRNA stabilization, and p53 functionality.

full_output.paper_title: Comparisons of Transcriptional Profiles of Gut Genes between Cry1Ab-Resistant and Susceptible Strains of Ostrinia nubilalis Revealed Genes Possibly Related to the Adaptation of Resistant Larvae to Transgenic Cry1Ab Corn.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified differentially expressed gut genes in Cry1Ab-resistant and susceptible strains of Ostrinia nubilalis, highlighting potential genes involved in adaptation to Cry1Ab toxin, such as contig[1398] and contig[4776].
full_output.methodology: Microarray and RT-qPCR analyses were used to compare gene expression profiles in gut tissues of larvae fed transgenic and non-transgenic corn leaves.

full_output.paper_title: Toxin Mediates Sepsis Caused by Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the PSM-mec peptide toxin as a major mediator of sepsis caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis, demonstrating its role in increasing mortality and cytokine expression in a mouse sepsis model.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized isogenic psm-mec deletion mutants and a start codon mutant in clinical strains of S. epidermidis, along with mouse sepsis models and cytokine measurements to investigate the role of the PSM-mec toxin.

full_output.paper_title: A new subclass of intrinsic aminoglycoside nucleotidyltransferases, ANT(3")-II, is horizontally transferred among Acinetobacter spp. by homologous recombination.

ant(3\")-IIa.validation_method: functional expression in E. coli and mutational analysis in A. baumannii

ANT(3\")-IIa.mechanism: modifies streptomycin by adding a phosphate group, reducing its antibacterial activity
ANT(3\")-IIa.validation_method: expression in E. coli and determination of MIC

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a new subclass of intrinsic aminoglycoside nucleotidyltransferases, ANT(3")-II, which provides resistance to streptomycin and spectinomycin in Acinetobacter species. These genes are horizontally transferred among different Acinetobacter species through homologous recombination.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics screening, functional expression in E. coli, mutational analysis in A. baumannii, and biochemical assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant bacterial enteropathogens, including extended spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli (DEC).
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method and molecular characterization of DEC strains.

full_output.paper_title: Surface mediated cooperative interactions of drugs enhance mechanical forces for antibiotic action.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mechanism by which drug-target interactions in resistant bacteria can be enhanced through surface-mediated cooperative interactions, demonstrating that oritavancin exhibits significantly stronger binding affinity against drug-resistant targets compared to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Cantilever force-based technology was used to measure mechanical responses and binding affinities of antibiotics against bacterial targets.

full_output.paper_title: Retrospective and prospective evaluation of the Carbapenem inactivation method for the detection of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the Carbapenem Inactivation Method (CIM) for detecting carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (CPE). It identifies several carbapenemase genes, including blaIMP, blaKPC, blaGES, blaNDM, blaVIM, blaIMI, blaFRI, blaNMC-A, blaSME, blaOXA-48, blaOXA-181, blaOXA-204, blaOXA-244, blaOXA-162, blaOXA-232, and blaOXA-372, which confer resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic testing and molecular methods were used to identify and characterize carbapenemase genes in Enterobacteriaceae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of appropriate empirical antibiotic treatment on recurrence and mortality in patients with bacteraemia: a population-based cohort study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that inappropriate empirical antibiotic treatment (EAT) was associated with an increased risk of bacteraemia recurrence and long-term mortality, but not short-term mortality.
full_output.methodology: A population-based cohort study analyzing the impact of EAT on patient outcomes in bacteraemia patients.

full_output.paper_title: Can Ceftazidime-Avibactam and Aztreonam Overcome β-Lactam Resistance Conferred by Metallo-β-Lactamases in Enterobacteriaceae?
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effectiveness of combining ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) with aztreonam (ATM) against carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae harboring metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs). The combination showed improved in vitro and in vivo activity against MBL-producing strains, particularly those with blaNDM and blaIMP genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used disk diffusion, agar dilution MIC testing, time-kill assays, and a murine neutropenic thigh infection model to assess the efficacy of CAZ-AVI and ATM against MBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem MICs in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella Species Producing Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamases in Critical Care Patients from 2001 to 2009.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC as a gene conferring resistance to multiple carbapenems in ESBL-producing E. coli and Klebsiella species.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection of KPC gene in ESBL-producing isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Multicenter Clinical and Molecular Epidemiological Analysis of Bacteremia Due to Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) in the CRE Epicenter of the United States.

ompK36.notes: associated with high-level carbapenem resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC-2 and blaKPC-3 as the most common carbapenemases in CRE, along with blaNDM-1 in E. coli and blaOXA-48 in K. pneumoniae. Mutations in ompK35 and ompK36 were associated with high-level carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Molecular genotyping, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and analysis of clinical data from multiple medical centers.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of high-level gentamicin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis and Enterococcus faecium in an Iranian hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of high-level gentamicin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis and Enterococcus faecium in an Iranian hospital, with the aac(6')-Ie-aph(2'')-Ia gene being the most common aminoglycoside resistance gene.
full_output.methodology: PCR and multiplex PCR-based methods were used to screen for antimicrobial resistance genes, and RAPD-PCR was used for genetic diversity analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Antifungal resistance mechanisms in fungi: A comprehensive review
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses various mechanisms of antifungal resistance in fungi, including overexpression of efflux pumps like CDR1, CDR2, and MDR1, mutations in ERG11 leading to azole resistance, and mutations in FKS1 contributing to echinocandin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews experimental studies and literature on antifungal resistance mechanisms in fungi.

full_output.paper_title: TgPRELID, a Mitochondrial Protein Linked to Multidrug Resistance in the Parasite Toxoplasma gondii.

TgPRELID.notes: Deletion in exon 4 leads to resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TgPRELID as a mitochondrial protein involved in multidrug resistance in Toxoplasma gondii, with mutations in the PRELI domain conferring resistance to both F3215-0002 and I-BET151.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, drug resistance assays, and CRISPR/CAS9 editing were used to identify and validate TgPRELID mutations associated with resistance.

full_output.paper_title: The Antituberculosis Drug Ethambutol Selectively Blocks Apical Growth in CMN Group Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Ethambutol (EMB) selectively blocks apical cell wall synthesis in CMN group bacteria, leading to a bacteriostatic effect without killing the cells. EMB treatment results in the loss of mycolic acid (MA) layers and arabinose polymers from the cell envelope, while cell division continues through the divisome.
full_output.methodology: Microfluidic chambers, fluorescence microscopy, and biochemical analyses were used to study the effects of EMB on cell growth and cell wall composition in C. glutamicum and M. phlei.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Molecular Epidemiology of ESBL-Producing Escherichia coli Isolated from Outpatients in Town Hospitals of Shandong Province, China.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC, blaTEM, and blaCTX-M genes as significant contributors to carbapenem resistance in Enterobacter spp. Additionally, alterations in outer membrane proteins and the presence of the efflux pump gene acrART were noted as contributing factors.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, PFGE, and MIC testing were used to analyze resistance mechanisms in Enterobacter isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Generation of Small Colony Variants in Biofilms by Escherichia coli Harboring a Conjugative F Plasmid.

hemB.notes: Mutation in hemB leads to small colony variant phenotype and aminoglycoside resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the insertion of Tn 1000 into the hemB gene in E. coli leads to the emergence of small colony variants (SCVs) with increased resistance to aminoglycoside antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, complementation experiments, and MIC testing were used to validate the role of hemB mutation in SCV formation and aminoglycoside resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Peptides and Their Interaction with Lipopolysaccharides
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the interaction of antimicrobial peptides KYE21 and WWWKYE21 with lipopolysaccharides (LPS) and their effects on bacterial membranes and immune responses.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized various biophysical techniques including ellipsometry, NMR spectroscopy, CD spectroscopy, and lipid bilayer studies to analyze the interaction of peptides with LPS and their effects on membrane integrity and immune cell responses.

full_output.paper_title: A Descriptive Study of Open Fractures Contaminated by Seawater: Infection, Pathogens, and Antibiotic Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that seawater-contaminated wounds had a higher infection rate and different bacterial spectra compared to non-seawater-contaminated wounds. Most pathogens in seawater-contaminated wounds were sensitive to levofloxacin and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing open fractures contaminated by seawater and comparing infection rates, bacterial spectra, and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Beta-Lactamase Inhibitors: Unlocking Their Potential in Therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the development and evaluation of novel beta-lactamase inhibitors, including avibactam, vaborbactam, and relebactam, highlighting their effectiveness against various beta-lactamases such as KPC and OXA-48. It also notes the emergence of resistance mechanisms, such as mutations in blaKPC-3, which can render these inhibitors ineffective.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews preclinical and clinical studies on the efficacy and safety of novel beta-lactamase inhibitors, focusing on their ability to restore the activity of beta-lactam antibiotics against resistant bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Mutation pattern in the genome of Neisseria gonorrhoeae and its association with multidrug-resistant isolates from Delhi, India.
full_output.key_findings: Mutations in PenA, PorB, MtrE, and MtrR genes were identified in 27 drug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates, with specific mutations linked to resistance against penicillin, tetracycline, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of drug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates to identify mutations associated with antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Activity of Imipenem-Relebactam against Gram-Negative ESKAPE Pathogens Isolated by Clinical Laboratories in the United States in 2015 (Results from the SMART Global Surveillance Program).
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of imipenem-relebactam against Gram-negative ESKAPE pathogens, demonstrating that relebactam restored imipenem susceptibility against carbapenem-nonsusceptible isolates of P. aeruginosa, K. pneumoniae, and Enterobacter spp.
full_output.methodology: The study used CLSI-defined broth microdilution methodology to assess the in vitro activity of imipenem-relebactam and other antimicrobial agents against clinical isolates of ESKAPE pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Piperacillin-Tazobactam versus Other Antibacterial Agents for Treatment of Bloodstream Infections Due to AmpC β-Lactamase-Producing Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the presence and genetic diversity of ampC genes in AmpC β-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae, highlighting the importance of these genes in conferring resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and sequencing to detect and analyze ampC alleles in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Primary Clofazimine and Bedaquiline Resistance among Isolates from Patients with Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Rv0678 mutations as a primary mechanism of clofazimine and bedaquiline resistance in MDR-TB isolates, with additional findings of Rv1979c mutations associated with clofazimine resistance without cross-resistance to bedaquiline.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and microplate alamarBlue assay (MABA) for MIC determination.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of Mutations at Arg220 and Thr237 in PER-2 β-Lactamase on Conformation, Activity, and Susceptibility to Inhibitors.

PER-2.notes: Mutations at Arg220 and Thr237 in PER-2 β-lactamase significantly reduce the susceptibility to mechanism-based inhibitors such as clavulanic acid and tazobactam.

full_output.key_findings: Mutations at Arg220 and Thr237 in PER-2 β-lactamase significantly reduce the susceptibility to mechanism-based inhibitors such as clavulanic acid and tazobactam, impacting the enzyme's activity and hydrolytic efficiency towards various β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Kinetic analysis, MIC determination, and structural studies were used to evaluate the impact of mutations on PER-2 β-lactamase activity and inhibitor susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance acquired through a DNA damage-inducible response in Acinetobacter baumannii

recA.validation_method: experimental validation via knockout and complementation

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the role of the recA gene in the DNA damage-inducible response leading to antibiotic resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockout, complementation, and expression analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MRL-436, a novel small molecule that binds to and inhibits E. coli RNA polymerase (RNAP). Mutations in the rpoC gene (encoding the RNAP beta' subunit) and rpoZ gene (encoding the RNAP omega subunit) confer resistance to MRL-436.
full_output.methodology: Affinity selection-mass spectrometry (AS-MS), whole-genome sequencing, and broth microdilution MIC assays were used to identify MRL-436 and characterize resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence for natural gene transfer from gram-positive cocci to Escherichia coli.

ermBC.validation_method: expression in E. coli and B. subtilis, comparison of amino acid differences

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the ermBC gene on plasmid pIP1527 as responsible for high-level MLS resistance in E. coli BM2570, showing it is similar to erm genes from Streptococcus sanguis and Enterococcus faecalis but expresses constitutively due to mutations in its regulatory region.
full_output.methodology: Cloning and expression analysis of the ermBC gene in E. coli and B. subtilis, comparison of amino acid sequences.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and plant-derived antimicrobials (PDA(m)s) as an alternative drug line to control infections.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and explores plant-derived antimicrobials (PDAs) as potential alternatives to combat resistant infections. It highlights the role of efflux pumps and the importance of synergistic actions between PDAs and conventional antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature on AMR mechanisms, including plasmid-mediated resistance, efflux pumps, and the role of plant-derived compounds in combating resistant pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic diversity and genotypic flexibility of Burkholderia cenocepacia during long-term chronic infection of cystic fibrosis lungs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several genes associated with motility and biofilm formation in Burkholderia cenocepacia, highlighting the genetic basis of phenotypic diversity during chronic infection in cystic fibrosis patients.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, phenotypic analysis, and genetic association testing were used to identify genes linked to motility and biofilm formation.

full_output.paper_title: Bactericide, Immunomodulating, and Wound Healing Properties of Transgenic Kalanchoe pinnata Synergize with Antimicrobial Peptide Cecropin P1 In Vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antimicrobial peptide Cecropin P1 (CecP1) expressed in transgenic Kalanchoe pinnata plants, demonstrating its bactericidal and wound-healing properties in vivo.
full_output.methodology: Production of K. pinnata extracts, immunoblotting, antimicrobial activity testing, and in vivo wound healing experiments.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of tedizolid and linezolid against Staphylococcus epidermidis isolated from prosthetic joint infections.
full_output.key_findings: Tedizolid showed higher efficacy against Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates from prosthetic joint infections compared to linezolid, with lower MIC values.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing via disc diffusion and Etest for tedizolid, linezolid, and vancomycin.

full_output.paper_title: Combinations of avibactam and carbapenems exhibit enhanced potencies against drug-resistant Mycobacterium abscessus.
full_output.key_findings: Avibactam enhances the potency of carbapenems against drug-resistant Mycobacterium abscessus by reducing their minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs).
full_output.methodology: The study determined MICs of carbapenems with and without avibactam against 28 M. abscessus clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Preliminary evaluation of anti-tuberculosis potential of siderophores against drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis by mycobacteria growth indicator tube-drug sensitivity test.
full_output.key_findings: Exo-MS and DFO-B showed activity against drug-resistant Mtb isolates, suggesting their potential as adjuncts to antibiotics in treating drug-resistant TB.
full_output.methodology: MGIT-DST was used to assess the anti-TB activity of Exo-MS and DFO-B against MDR and PZA-R Mtb isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Ten MDR and seven PZA-R Mtb isolates

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and molecular characterization of antimicrobial resistance in Enterobacter spp. isolates from companion animals in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Enterobacter spp. isolates from companion animals in Japan, including blaCTX-M-15, blaSHV-12, blaCTX-M-3, blaCMY-2, blaDHA-1, blaTEM-1, blaOXA-1, qnrB, aac(6')-Ib-cr, and qnrS. These genes were associated with resistance to various antibiotics such as ceftazidime, cefotaxime, ampicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and DNA sequencing to characterize AMR genes in Enterobacter spp. isolates.

full_output.paper_title: High Burden of Antimicrobial Resistance and Mortality Among Adults and Children With Community-Onset Bacterial Infections in India.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high burden of community-onset antimicrobial-resistant infections among patients with acute febrile illness in India, with multidrug-resistant (MDR) infections being associated with prior antibiotic use and an increased risk of mortality.
full_output.methodology: Prospective study of adults and children hospitalized for acute febrile illness, with analysis of bacterial isolates and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance and biofilm production among the strains of Staphylococcus aureus isolated from pus/wound swab samples in a tertiary care hospital in Nepal.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high rates of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) and inducible clindamycin resistance among S. aureus isolates. High levels of susceptibility to linezolid and vancomycin were observed, while biofilm production was prevalent among the isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method, D-test for inducible clindamycin resistance, and microtiter plate method for biofilm detection.

full_output.paper_title: Defining a Core Genome Multilocus Sequence Typing Scheme for the Global Epidemiology of Vibrio parahaemolyticus.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a core genome multilocus sequence typing (cgMLST) scheme for Vibrio parahaemolyticus, identifying 2,254 core genes for improved strain differentiation and epidemiological analysis.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of 92 V. parahaemolyticus strains and evaluation of 142 additional genomes from NCBI to establish a cgMLST scheme.
full_output.sample_size: 92 strains sequenced in this study, 142 additional genomes from NCBI

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Susceptibility Testing of Tedizolid against Nontuberculous Mycobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Tedizolid showed greater in vitro potency than linezolid against nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), with lower MIC values for various NTM species including Mycobacterium abscessus, Mycobacterium chelonae, and Mycobacterium fortuitum.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution susceptibility testing was performed according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: High Incidence of Virulence Factors Among Clinical Enterococcus faecalis Isolates in Southwestern Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of virulence factors among E. faecalis isolates, including efa, asa1, esp, ace, gelE, cylA, and hyl. Vancomycin resistance was observed in 45.1% of isolates, while no isolates were resistant to fosfomycin or linezolid.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Cross-resistance to lincosamides, streptogramins A and pleuromutilins in Streptococcus agalactiae isolates from the USA.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies lsa(C), lnu(B), and lsa(E) as genetic determinants of cross-resistance to lincosamides, streptogramin A, and pleuromutilins in Streptococcus agalactiae isolates from the USA.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and read mapping were used to identify AMR genes in GBS isolates with specific resistance phenotypes.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that a triple combination of polymyxin B, meropenem, and ampicillin/sulbactam can eradicate polymyxin-resistant, carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, which lacks individual activity against the resistant isolate.
full_output.methodology: The study used a hollow-fiber infection model (HFIM) to simulate the patient's colistin regimen and evaluate the efficacy of antibiotic combinations against the resistant A. baumannii isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution of antimicrobial resistance determinants, virulence-associated factors and clustered regularly interspaced palindromic repeats loci in isolates of Enterococcus faecalis from various settings and genetic lineages.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized antimicrobial resistance genes such as aac(6')-aph(2"), ant(6')-Ia, tet(M), and erm(B) in Enterococcus faecalis isolates from various settings, highlighting their association with hospital-acquired infections and multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and analyze resistance genes, virulence factors, and CRISPR loci in Enterococcus faecalis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotics trigger initiation of SCCmec transfer by inducing SOS responses.
full_output.key_findings: Antibiotics induce SOS responses, leading to the expression of ccrC1 and ccrAB, which promote SCC mec excision and transfer, contributing to methicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transcript analysis, EMSA, and RT-PCR were used to investigate the role of ccrC1 and ccrAB in SCC mec excision.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Variants Contributing to Colistin Cytotoxicity: Identification of TGIF1 and HOXD10 Using a Population Genomics Approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TGIF1 and HOXD10 as genetic factors contributing to colistin cytotoxicity, with the SNP chr18:3417240 being significantly associated with resistance to colistin cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a genome-wide association study (GWAS) and functional validation through siRNA knockdown experiments in renal cells.

full_output.paper_title: 3-Substituted N-Benzylpyrazine-2-carboxamide Derivatives: Synthesis, Antimycobacterial and Antibacterial Evaluation.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of 3-substituted N-benzylpyrazine-2-carboxamide derivatives for antimycobacterial and antibacterial activity. Compounds 1a and 9a showed the highest activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv, while compound 5 exhibited potent activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, in vitro antimycobacterial and antibacterial evaluations, and molecular docking studies were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: The aacA-aphD gentamicin and kanamycin resistance determinant of Tn4001 from Staphylococcus aureus: expression and nucleotide sequence analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Analysis of the IncX4 Plasmids: Implications for a Unique Pattern in the mcr-1 Acquisition.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mcr-1 gene as a key factor in colistin resistance in Enterobacteriaceae, particularly in E. coli, and characterizes its genetic context within IncX4 plasmids.
full_output.methodology: PCR screening, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, S1-PFGE, Southern blotting, and sequencing of plasmids.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis using ResFinder 2.1, PlasmidFinder 1.3, and CGE server.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, antimicrobial resistance and genetic diversity of Campylobacter coli and Campylobacter jejuni in Ecuadorian broilers at slaughter age.
full_output.key_findings: High resistance rates to ciprofloxacin, nalidixic acid, and tetracycline were observed in both C. coli and C. jejuni. C. coli showed higher resistance to erythromycin compared to C. jejuni. The study identified novel sequence types (STs) for both species.
full_output.methodology: Microbiological isolation, PCR, MIC testing, RFLP-flaA typing, and MLST were used to assess antimicrobial resistance and genetic diversity.

full_output.paper_title: N6', N6'''', and O4' Modifications to Neomycin Affect Ribosomal Selectivity without Compromising Antibacterial Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates how modifications to neomycin, specifically N6'- and O4'-substitutions, affect ribosomal selectivity and antibacterial activity. It finds that these modifications enhance selectivity for bacterial ribosomes without reducing antibacterial efficacy, and that certain derivatives show improved resistance to aminoglycoside modifying enzymes.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of neomycin derivatives, cell-free translation assays, and evaluation of antibacterial activity against various microbial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial clonal diagnostics as a tool for evidence-based empiric antibiotic selection.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the use of a 7-SNP test for clonotyping E. coli to guide empiric antibiotic selection, showing that clonal diagnostics can improve antibiotic prescribing by reducing mismatch rates between prescribed antibiotics and bacterial resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a 7-SNP test for clonotyping E. coli and compares resistance profiles with local and multi-national reference datasets to assess the effectiveness of clonal diagnostics in guiding antibiotic selection.

full_output.paper_title: Short-term increase in prevalence of nasopharyngeal carriage of macrolide-resistant Staphylococcus aureus following mass drug administration with azithromycin for trachoma control.

msr.validation_method: detection in isolates showing resistance to azithromycin but sensitivity to clindamycin

erm(C).validation_method: detection in isolates showing resistance to azithromycin with iMLS B phenotype

erm(T).validation_method: detection in isolates showing resistance to azithromycin with iMLS B phenotype

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of macrolide resistance genes msr, erm(C), and erm(T) in Staphylococcus aureus isolates following mass drug administration with azithromycin, contributing to increased prevalence of macrolide-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed S. aureus isolates using a DNA microarray to detect antibiotic resistance determinants.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of MupP as a New Peptidoglycan Recycling Factor and Antibiotic Resistance Determinant in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mupP as a new gene involved in peptidoglycan recycling and beta-lactam resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Deletion of mupP leads to increased ampC expression and beta-lactam resistance, similar to other PG recycling mutants.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, deletion mutant analysis, complementation, and beta-galactosidase assays were used to characterize the role of mupP in PG recycling and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of Quinolone Resistance in Salmonella spp. Isolates from the Food Chain in Brazil.

qnrB.evidence_note: The paper mentions that qnr genes were found in 15 isolates, including 6 qnr B, 8 qnr S, and 1 qnr D.

qnrS.evidence_note: The paper mentions that qnr genes are plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance determinants and that they reduce quinolone binding affinity.

qnrD.evidence_note: The paper mentions that qnrD was found in 15 isolates, including one isolate (ID: 55/13) that carried the qnrD gene and showed resistance to ciprofloxacin, nalidixic acid, enrofloxacin, levofloxacin, and ofloxacin.

aac(6')-Ib.evidence_note: The aac(6′)-Ib gene was detected in 23 isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified qnrB, qnrS, qnrD, and aac(6')-Ib genes as contributors to quinolone resistance in Salmonella spp. isolates from Brazil, highlighting the role of plasmid-mediated resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection and susceptibility testing were used to identify quinolone resistance genes and assess resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo Host Environment Alters Pseudomonas aeruginosa Susceptibility to Aminoglycoside Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the host environment increases the susceptibility of Pseudomonas aeruginosa to tobramycin, and identifies waaP as a gene involved in this process.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome analysis, real-time PCR, and susceptibility testing

full_output.paper_title: Structure of the AcrAB-TolC multidrug efflux pump in complex with the inhibitor MBX3132
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structure and function of the AcrAB-TolC multidrug efflux pump, revealing its conformational changes during drug transport and providing insights into its allosteric mechanism.
full_output.methodology: Cryo-electron microscopy and structural analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic effects of antimicrobial peptide DP7 combined with antibiotics against multidrug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ermA, ermB, and ermC as azithromycin resistance genes in multidrug-resistant bacterial isolates, showing that isolates with more erm genes exhibit higher azithromycin MICs and greater synergy with DP7.
full_output.methodology: qPCR for gene detection and MIC determination for assessing antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.sample_size: 13 P. aeruginosa and 11 S. aureus isolates

full_output.paper_title: Identification and Characterization of a Chemical Compound that Inhibits Methionyl-tRNA Synthetase from Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified isopomiferin as an inhibitor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa methionyl-tRNA synthetase (MetRS), demonstrating antibacterial activity against several pathogens, though it showed limited efficacy against wild-type and efflux pump mutant strains of P. aeruginosa and E. coli.
full_output.methodology: The study involved cloning and characterizing P. aeruginosa MetRS, performing kinetic analyses, and screening chemical compound libraries using scintillation proximity assay technology.

full_output.paper_title: Strain Improvement Is Correlated to Transcriptional Landscape Remodeling in P. chrysogenum and A. chrysogenum
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pcbC as a gene involved in beta-lactam antibiotic production in P. chrysogenum and A. chrysogenum, highlighting its role in the evolutionary conservation of beta-lactam biosynthesis.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq, phylogenetic analysis, and bioinformatics tools were used to analyze gene expression and identify AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Cooperative Actions of CRP-cAMP and FNR Increase the Fosfomycin Susceptibility of Enterohaemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EHEC) by Elevating the Expression of glpT and uhpT under Anaerobic Conditions.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the expression of glpT and uhpT, which are fosfomycin transporters, is regulated by CRP-cAMP and FNR under anaerobic conditions, leading to increased fosfomycin susceptibility in EHEC.
full_output.methodology: The study used MIC assays, promoter assays, qPCR, and gel-shift assays to analyze the regulation of glpT and uhpT by CRP-cAMP and FNR.

full_output.paper_title: The Prevalence of Antibiotic-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Nasal Carriage among Industrial Hog Operation Workers, Community Residents, and Children Living in Their Households: North Carolina, USA.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a higher prevalence of S. aureus, MRSA, and MDRSA nasal carriage among IHO workers and their children compared to community residents. The presence of mecA and mecC genes was associated with methicillin-resistant S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of S. aureus-specific genes (spa, mecA, mecC, scn, pvl) and antibiotic susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes methodologies for studying horizontal gene transfer in Staphylococcus aureus, focusing on the transmission of the cfr gene, which confers resistance to multiple antibiotics including Phenicols, Lincosamides, Oxazolidinones, Pleuromutilins, and Streptogramin A.
full_output.methodology: The study outlines protocols for conjugation, phage transduction, and natural transformation to investigate the transmission of the cfr gene in S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Chitosan-propolis nanoparticle formulation demonstrates anti-bacterial activity against Enterococcus faecalis biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that chitosan-propolis nanoparticles effectively inhibit biofilm formation and disrupt existing biofilms of Enterococcus faecalis, reducing bacterial counts by up to 90% and altering the expression of biofilm-related genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized HPLC analysis, nanoparticle preparation, biofilm assays, and quantitative PCR to evaluate the anti-bacterial and anti-biofilm effects of chitosan-propolis nanoparticles against E. faecalis.

full_output.paper_title: A randomised, double-blind, phase 3 study comparing the efficacy and safety of ceftazidime/avibactam plus metronidazole versus meropenem for complicated intra-abdominal infections in hospitalised adults in Asia.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrated that ceftazidime/avibactam plus metronidazole was non-inferior to meropenem in treating complicated intra-abdominal infections in Asian populations, including against ceftazidime-non-susceptible pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Phase 3 randomized, double-blind trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of ceftazidime/avibactam plus metronidazole versus meropenem in patients with complicated intra-abdominal infections.

full_output.paper_title: Performance and microbial community variations of anaerobic digesters under increasing tetracycline concentrations.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the abundance of tetracycline resistance genes tetW and tetQ increased significantly in the reactor exposed to high tetracycline concentrations, indicating the development of tetracycline resistance in the microbial community.
full_output.methodology: The study used quantitative PCR to analyze the abundance of tetracycline resistance genes in anaerobic digesters under different tetracycline concentrations.

full_output.paper_title: High-Level Resistance of Staphylococcus aureus to β-Lactam Antibiotics Mediated by Penicillin-Binding Protein 4 (PBP4).

pbp4.mechanism: Overexpression of PBP4 leads to increased transpeptidase activity, resulting in high-level resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.
pbp4.role_in_paper: The study demonstrates that mutations in PBP4 and its promoter lead to high-level resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.
pbp4.validation_method: Experimental validation through genetic manipulation and antibiotic susceptibility testing.
pbp4.genetic_context: Mutations in the pbp4 structural gene and its promoter region were identified in the CRB strain.
pbp4.evidence_note: The study shows that overexpression of mutant PBP4 is associated with high-level resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.

The paper explicitly states that mutations E183A and F241R in PBP4 confer resistance to ceftobiprole and ceftaroline. The organism observed is Staphylococcus aureus. The effect on function is increased transpeptidase activity. The mutation type is missense. The validated methods are MIC testing and Bocillin-FL labeling. The origin of the mutation is the mutant strain CRB.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the pbp4 gene, specifically E183A and F241R, which lead to high-level resistance to β-lactam antibiotics, including ceftobiprole and ceftaroline, in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MIC testing, Bocillin-FL labeling, and genetic manipulation to investigate the role of PBP4 in β-lactam resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Structural Modification of Lipopolysaccharide Conferred by mcr-1 in Gram-Negative ESKAPE Pathogens.

mcr-1.validation_method: MIC assays and mass spectrometry analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the mcr-1 gene confers colistin resistance in various Gram-negative ESKAPE pathogens, including E. coli, K. pneumoniae, A. baumannii, and P. aeruginosa, through the modification of lipid A with phosphoethanolamine.
full_output.methodology: MIC assays and mass spectrometry were used to analyze the effects of mcr-1 on colistin resistance and lipid A structure.

full_output.key_findings: The case report describes a severe infection caused by multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica serotype Choleraesuis expressing extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Clinical case report and microbiological analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial resistance of Campylobacter jejuni and Campylobacter coli isolated from children and environmental sources in urban and suburban areas.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial resistance in Campylobacter jejuni and Campylobacter coli isolates from various sources, including poultry meat, pets, and surface water. High resistance rates to ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, and erythromycin were observed, highlighting the potential for multidrug-resistant strains to spread through environmental sources.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using E-test and PCR-based identification of Campylobacter species.

full_output.paper_title: Expansion of highly stable bla (OXA-10) β-lactamase family within diverse host range among nosocomial isolates of Gram-negative bacilli within a tertiary referral hospital of Northeast India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-10, blaOXA-14, and blaOXA-16 genes in various Gram-negative bacilli, highlighting their role in resistance to extended-spectrum cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the β-lactamase genes.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic polymorphisms in Plasmodium falciparum chloroquine resistance genes, pfcrt and pfmdr1, in North Sulawesi, Indonesia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the 76T mutation in pfcrt and the 86Y mutation in pfmdr1 as prevalent in Plasmodium falciparum isolates from North Sulawesi, Indonesia, indicating continued chloroquine resistance despite drug withdrawal.
full_output.methodology: PCR-RFLP and multiplex amplicon sequencing were used to analyze genetic polymorphisms in pfcrt and pfmdr1.

full_output.paper_title: Bactericidal permeability-increasing proteins shape host-microbe interactions
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies EsBPI2 and EsBPI4 as bactericidal/permeability-increasing proteins involved in host-microbe interactions, demonstrating their antimicrobial activity against Vibrio fischeri.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity assays, immunocytochemistry, and sequencing were used to characterize EsBPI2 and EsBPI4.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Molecular Characterization of Staphylococcus aureus Causing Childhood Pneumonia in Shanghai.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates to erythromycin, fosfomycin-trometamol, and clindamycin among S. aureus isolates causing childhood pneumonia in Shanghai. It also highlighted the prevalence of specific clones such as ST59-SCCmec IV-t172 and ST59-SCCmec IV-t437, which exhibited high resistance to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study involved antimicrobial susceptibility testing, molecular typing (spa, agr, MLST), and detection of toxin genes in S. aureus isolates from children with pneumonia.

full_output.paper_title: A Pan-Genomic Approach to Understand the Basis of Host Adaptation in Achromobacter.

blaOXA-258.validation_method: presence in genomes and association with resistance

blaOXA-243.validation_method: presence in genomes and association with resistance

MexW.evidence_note: The paper mentions that MexW is the multidrug transporter of a RND-type efflux pump and that it is under positive selection in the clinical lineage, but does not explicitly state that it confers resistance to specific drugs.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several beta-lactamase genes (blaOXA-114a, blaOXA-258, blaOXA-243) and efflux pump systems (AxyABM, AxyXY-OprZ) associated with antibiotic resistance in Achromobacter species, particularly in group 5 isolates.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, pan-genome analysis, and resistome analysis using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD).
full_output.sample_size: 55 publicly available genomes and 4 newly sequenced genomes

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial Isolates and Their Antimicrobial Susceptibility Patterns of Wound Infections among Inpatients and Outpatients Attending the University of Gondar Referral Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: High prevalence of bacterial isolates was found, with Staphylococcus aureus being the most dominant. High rates of multiple drug resistance pathogens to the commonly used antimicrobial agents were isolated.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using disk diffusion technique following Kirby-Bauer method.

full_output.paper_title: Scaffold of Selenium Nanovectors and Honey Phytochemicals for Inhibition of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Quorum Sensing and Biofilm Formation.
full_output.key_findings: SeNPs@HP inhibits quorum sensing (QS) in P. aeruginosa PAO1 by targeting the LasR receptor, reducing virulence factor production and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: RT-qPCR, molecular docking, and in vitro QS assays.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) in stool specimens submitted for Clostridium difficile toxin testing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanA as the gene responsible for vancomycin and teicoplanin resistance in Enterococcus faecium isolates from stool samples.
full_output.methodology: PCR and Etest for detection of vanA gene and vancomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Biophysical and Pharmacological Characterization of Energy-Dependent Efflux of Sb in Laboratory-Selected Resistant Strains of Leishmania (Viannia) Subgenus.

GSH1.validation_method: real time qRT-PCR and Sb uptake assays

AQP1.validation_method: gene sequencing and Sb uptake assays

ABCI4.validation_method: real time qRT-PCR and Sb uptake assays

ARM58.validation_method: real time qRT-PCR and Sb uptake assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identified and characterized genes such as MRPA, GSH1, AQP1, ABCI4, and ARM58 involved in antimony resistance in Leishmania (Viannia) strains. Additionally, a point mutation (G133D) in AQP1 was found to reduce antimony uptake in L. guyanensis.
full_output.methodology: Real-time qRT-PCR, Sb uptake and efflux assays, and gene sequencing were used to analyze gene expression and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence for the evolutionary steps leading to mecA-mediated β-lactam resistance in staphylococci.

mecA.mechanism: low affinity to β-lactams
mecA.validation_method: genomic analysis and oxacillin susceptibility testing

mecA1.mechanism: structural alteration in the active site of the PBP encoded by mecA1 homologues

mecA2.validation_method: protein structure modeling and western blotting

mutations_found.validated_by: western blotting and promoter sequence analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mecA homologues in Staphylococcus sciuri, S. vitulinus, and S. fleurettii, demonstrating that mecA contributes to β-lactam resistance through structural variations and promoter modifications.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, oxacillin susceptibility testing, and structural modeling of PBP proteins.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance Markers in Burkholderia pseudomallei Strain Bp1651 Identified by Genome Sequence Analysis.

blaP.evidence_note: The paper describes mutations in the penA gene that contribute to ceftazidime resistance in Burkholderia pseudomallei.

amrB.notes: The deletion in amrB leads to susceptibility to gentamicin and failure to grow on Ashdown's agar.

amrR.notes: The deletion in amrR leads to constitutive expression of the AmrAB-OprA efflux pump.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three point mutations in penA (T147A, D240G, V261I) that confer resistance to β-lactam antibiotics in B. pseudomallei strain Bp1651. Additionally, mutations in folA (I99L and A145T) are linked to trimethoprim resistance. The amrB and amrR genes show deletions that result in a nonfunctional efflux pump and constitutive expression, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, mutagenesis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to validate the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Prescription Patterns for Tigecycline in Severely Ill Patients for Non-FDA Approved Indications in a Developing Country: A Compromised Outcome.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated tigecycline use in off-label indications for severely ill patients, highlighting its frequent prescription in critical care settings despite limited data on its efficacy against multidrug-resistant organisms like Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective chart review of tigecycline use in 153 adult patients over two years, analyzing clinical outcomes, microbiological success, and mortality rates.

full_output.paper_title: Hydrodynamics of the VanA-type VanS histidine kinase: an extended solution conformation and first evidence for interactions with vancomycin.
full_output.key_findings: VanS, a histidine kinase involved in vancomycin resistance, was purified and characterized. The study demonstrated that vancomycin interacts directly with VanS, leading to changes in its conformation and oligomeric state.
full_output.methodology: Protein purification, analytical ultracentrifugation, circular dichroism, and autophosphorylation assays.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and molecular study of pneumococci causing respiratory tract infections. A 3-year prospective cohort.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified resistance genes pbp2x, pbp2b, pbp1a, mefA, and ermB in pneumococci causing respiratory tract infections, highlighting high resistance rates to beta-lactams and macrolides.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR was used to detect resistance genes in pneumococcal isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The recent emergence in hospitals of multidrug-resistant community-associated sequence type 1 and spa type t127 methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus investigated by whole-genome sequencing: Implications for screening.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the ileS2 gene as a key factor in high-level mupirocin resistance in multidrug-resistant ST1-MRSA-IV-t127 isolates, which were found to carry a conjugative plasmid encoding this gene.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, DNA microarray profiling, and plasmid conjugation and curing experiments were used to characterize the AMR genes and mutations in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Frequent isolation of methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) ST398 among healthy pigs in Portugal.

mecA.mechanism: alters penicillin-binding protein 2a to reduce affinity for β-lactam antibiotics
mecA.validation_method: PCR detection of the mecA gene

lsaE.mechanism: modifies ribosomes to prevent binding of streptogramin A
lsaE.validation_method: identification of the lsaE gene in porcine MRSA

full_output.paper_title: Imipenem/cilastatin encapsulated polymeric nanoparticles for destroying carbapenem-resistant bacterial isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that imipenem/cilastatin encapsulated in polymeric nanoparticles (PCL and PLGA) effectively enhances the antimicrobial activity against carbapenem-resistant isolates, reduces bacterial adhesion, and prevents the emergence of resistant colonies.
full_output.methodology: The study used nanoparticle formulation techniques, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and biofilm assays to evaluate the effectiveness of imipenem/cilastatin-loaded nanoparticles against carbapenem-resistant bacteria.
full_output.sample_size: Various clinical isolates from Mansoura University Hospitals

full_output.paper_title: Within-Host Evolution of Burkholderia pseudomallei during Chronic Infection of Seven Australasian Cystic Fibrosis Patients.

gyrA.evidence_note: The paper states that a Y77S amino acid change in DNA gyrase subunit A (GyrA) is a putative mechanism for ciprofloxacin resistance.

ptr1.notes: Ptr1 mutations contribute to TMP/SMX resistance.

full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and MIC testing of sequentially collected isolates from seven chronically infected cystic fibrosis patients.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriophages from ExPEC Reservoirs Kill Pandemic Multidrug-Resistant Strains of Clonal Group ST131 in Animal Models of Bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes bacteriophages from avian and canine reservoirs that effectively kill multidrug-resistant ST131 ExPEC strains in animal models, demonstrating therapeutic potential against these superbugs.
full_output.methodology: Phages were isolated from fecal samples, characterized through sequencing, and tested for lytic activity against multidrug-resistant ST131 ExPEC strains in murine models of bacteremia.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistant airborne bacteria and their multidrug resistance pattern at University teaching referral Hospital in South Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high rates of antibiotic resistance among airborne bacterial isolates in a hospital setting, including multidrug-resistant strains of Coagulase-negative staphylococci, Staphylococcus aureus, Enterococci, Acinetobacter, Escherichia coli, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Airborne bacterial isolates were collected using passive air sampling and subjected to antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer diffusion method.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the Carba NP test for detecting carbapenemase production in Gram-negative bacilli, highlighting its reproducibility and effectiveness across multiple sites when using standardized CLSI methodology.
full_output.methodology: The Carba NP test was performed according to CLSI procedures, with validation through multicenter trials and genomic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Development and Validation of a Lateral Flow Immunoassay for Rapid Detection of NDM-Producing Enterobacteriaceae.

blaNDM-4.validation_method: detection of NDM-4-producing strains using lateral flow immunoassay
