full_output.paper_title: Redox-Sensitive MarR Homologue BifR from Burkholderia thailandensis Regulates Biofilm Formation.
full_output.key_findings: BifR, a redox-sensitive MarR homologue, regulates biofilm formation in Burkholderia thailandensis by repressing the expression of emrB and ecsC. Oxidation of BifR leads to the formation of a dimer-of-dimers, enhancing its repressive activity.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of macrolide and fluoroquinolone resistance-mediating mutations in Mycoplasma genitalium in five cities in Russia and Estonia.

Fluoroquinolone resistance-associated mutations were detected in 6.2% of Russian samples and 5% of Estonian samples, with S83I, S83N, and D87N being the most common.

full_output.paper_title: Nucleotide sequence analysis of tetracycline resistance gene tetO from Streptococcus mutans DL5.

full_output.methodology: Cloning of the tetracycline resistance gene tetO from Streptococcus mutans DL5 and its expression in Streptococcus sanguis Challis to assess resistance phenotype.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of enterococci, their antimicrobial susceptibility patterns and associated factors among patients attending at the University of Gondar Teaching Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) and multidrug-resistant (MDR) enterococci among clinical samples, highlighting the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in enterococci isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Design, synthesis, and evaluation of novel 2-phenylpropionic acid derivatives as dual COX inhibitory-antibacterial agents.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of CTX-M-15 beta-lactamases in Enterobacteriaceae causing hospital- and community-acquired urinary tract infections as early as 2004, in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.

blaSHV-12.evidence_note: The paper states that bla SHV-12 was detected in 2 isolates, both from hospital-acquired infections.

full_output.paper_title: Outbreak by Hypermucoviscous Klebsiella pneumoniae ST11 Isolates with Carbapenem Resistance in a Tertiary Hospital in China.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the production of a recombinant antimicrobial polymeric protein, BCN-E 50-52, and evaluates its synergistic effects with thymol against various foodborne pathogens. The combination of BCN-E 50-52 and thymol demonstrated strong synergistic effects, particularly against S. aureus and L. monocytogenes.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance and Virulence Phenotypes of Recent Bacterial Strains Isolated from Urinary Tract Infections in Elderly Patients with Prostatic Disease.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii contamination in an intensive care unit.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Livestock-Associated Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Bloodstream Infections in Denmark.

full_output.paper_title: Uncovering Differences in Virulence Markers Associated with Achromobacter Species of CF and Non-CF Origin.

full_output.paper_title: Ease of use of tobramycin inhalation powder compared with nebulized tobramycin and colistimethate sodium: a crossover study in cystic fibrosis patients with pulmonary Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study compared the ease of use of tobramycin inhalation powder (TIP) with nebulized tobramycin (TIS) and colistimethate sodium (COLI) in cystic fibrosis patients with Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections. TIP was found to be easier to use, required less administration time, and was less prone to contamination compared to nebulized formulations.
full_output.methodology: A real-world, open-label, crossover, interventional phase IV study was conducted in cystic fibrosis patients with chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection.

full_output.paper_title: Multi-drug resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains circulating in hospital setting: whole-genome sequencing and Bayesian phylogenetic analysis for outbreak investigations.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multi-drug resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains carrying carbapenem resistance genes, particularly KPC, and analyzed their genetic diversity and transmission dynamics in a hospital setting.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and Bayesian phylogenetic analysis were used to investigate the genetic diversity and transmission dynamics of multi-drug resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the host methyltransferase gene Mt2 as a critical factor in Wolbachia-mediated antiviral resistance against Sindbis virus in Drosophila melanogaster.

full_output.paper_title: Streptococcus pyogenes quinolinate-salvage pathway-structural and functional studies of quinolinate phosphoribosyl transferase and NH(3)-dependent NAD(+) synthetase.

full_output.methodology: Structural and functional characterization of proteins using techniques such as X-ray crystallography, kinetic assays, and biochemical analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of Indeno[1,2-c]quinoline Derivatives as Potent Dual Antituberculosis and Anti-Inflammatory Agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several indeno[1,2-c]quinoline derivatives with potent anti-tuberculosis and anti-inflammatory activities. Additionally, these compounds exhibited dual inhibitory effects on neutrophil elastase release and superoxide anion generation.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility profiles among Campylobacter isolates obtained from international travelers between 2007 and 2014.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of ciprofloxacin resistance (60.9%) among Campylobacter isolates from international travelers, with the highest resistance rates in Asia. full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the E-test method for ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, azithromycin, erythromycin, tetracycline, doxycycline, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, and meropenem.

full_output.methodology: The study determined MICs in various broths and pig serum, analyzed the chemical composition of growth matrices, and assessed bacterial growth rates in different environments.

SElX.validation_method: host protein binding assays, glycan array screening, SPR, and mutagenesis studies

full_output.key_findings: SElX is a unique superantigen with features of both staphylococcal superantigens and SSLs, binding to sialylated glycans and modulating host immune responses through interactions with myeloid cells and MHC class II.
full_output.methodology: Host protein binding assays, glycan array screening, SPR, mutagenesis studies, and structural analysis.

full_output.paper_title: From Farms to Markets: Gram-Negative Bacteria Resistant to Third-Generation Cephalosporins in Fruits and Vegetables in a Region of North Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several 3GC-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, including Citrobacter murliniae, Enterobacter cloacae, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, Acinetobacter spp., Pseudomonas spp., and Ochrobactrum intermedium, in fruits and vegetables from North Africa. These isolates showed resistance to multiple antibiotics, including third-generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: The study involved sampling fruits, vegetables, soil, and irrigation water, followed by microbial isolation and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using disk diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance acquisition after international travel in U.S. travelers.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that international travel was associated with the acquisition of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing E. coli, with 9% of participants acquiring new strains post-travel. Resistance to multiple antibiotics, including TMP/SMX, tetracycline, and cefazolin, was observed in E. coli isolates from travelers.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed bacterial colonization in U.S. travelers before and after international travel using culture swabs and susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Secondary bacterial infections and antibiotic resistance among tungiasis patients in Western, Kenya.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antibiotic resistance in bacteria isolated from tungiasis lesions, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) resistant to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolates were tested for drug susceptibility using the Kirby Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence of Extended-Spectrum and AmpC-Type β-Lactamase Genes in Escherichia coli Isolated from Water Environments in Northern Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaCTX-M-group 1 and blaCTX-M-group 9 as the most common extended-spectrum β-lactamase genes in cefotaxime-resistant E. coli isolates from water environments in northern Thailand, along with blaCMY-2, an AmpC-type β-lactamase gene.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and characterize β-lactamase genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-Based Design and Synthesis of Apramycin-Paromomycin Analogues: Importance of the Configuration at the 6'-Position and Differences between the 6'-Amino and Hydroxy Series.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the synthesis and evaluation of apramycin-paromomycin analogs, emphasizing the significance of the 6'-hydroxyl group's configuration in enhancing antibacterial activity and reducing toxicity. The research highlights the importance of conformational constraints in improving ribosomal selectivity and overcoming resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The paper describes the synthesis of aminoglycoside analogs and evaluates their antibacterial and antiribosomal activities through cell-free translation assays and MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance in Africa: a systematic review.
full_output.key_findings: This systematic review highlights the high levels of antimicrobial resistance in Africa, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Klebsiella spp., and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Significant resistance rates were observed to commonly used antibiotics including amoxicillin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and ciprofloxacin. The study also notes the lack of comprehensive data from many African countries and emphasizes the need for improved surveillance and standardized reporting.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review of peer-reviewed articles published between 2013 and 2016, focusing on antimicrobial resistance patterns in African countries.

full_output.paper_title: Nosocomial Outbreak of Extensively Drug-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Isolates Containing blaOXA-237 Carried on a Plasmid.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the isolates and identify the blaOXA-237 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis Subculture Results in Loss of Potentially Clinically Relevant Heteroresistance

Certain resistance-associated variants, such as rpoB 515-518 deletion and gyrA 94GGC, were selected for during subculture.
full_output.methodology: Ultradep sequencing using SMOR approach to analyze resistance-associated variants in M. tuberculosis isolates before and after subculture.

full_output.paper_title: Aminoglycoside Concentrations Required for Synergy with Carbapenems against Pseudomonas aeruginosa Determined via Mechanistic Studies and Modeling.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the minimum aminoglycoside concentrations required for synergy with carbapenems against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, highlighting the outer membrane-permeabilizing effect of aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Mechanistic studies, static concentration time-kill experiments, electron microscopy, confocal imaging, and a mechanism-based model were used to determine the synergistic effects of aminoglycosides with carbapenems.

full_output.paper_title: Small RNAs in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium involved in daptomycin response and resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several small RNAs (sRNAs) in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium that are involved in daptomycin response and resistance. Specifically, sRNA_0160, sRNA_0560, sRNA_1420, sRNA_2290, sRNA_0120, sRNA_0280, and sRNA_2210 were found to be differentially expressed under daptomycin subinhibitory concentrations and in stepwise daptomycin-resistant mutants, suggesting their involvement in daptomycin resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RNA-seq, Northern blot, and qPCR to analyze the transcriptome of Enterococcus faecium under daptomycin exposure and in daptomycin-resistant mutants.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting the Type II Secretion System: Development, Optimization, and Validation of a High-Throughput Screen for the Identification of Small Molecule Inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies gspD and lipA as critical components of the Type II Secretion System (T2SS) in A. baumannii, with gspD playing a role in serum resistance and lipA contributing to colonization.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening (HTS) assay based on secreted lipase activity to identify small molecule inhibitors of the T2SS.

full_output.paper_title: Faecal carriage of CTX-M extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae among street children dwelling in Mwanza city, Tanzania.

full_output.paper_title: MALDI-TOF-MS based identification and molecular characterization of food associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mecA gene as a key determinant of methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from food samples, confirming its role in resistance to oxacillin and penicillin.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance among pathogenic bacteria from mink (Neovison vison) in Denmark.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes in coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) from wild birds in Spain, including blaZ, mecA, erm(B), erm(C), erm(43), msr(A), mph(C), lnu(A), lsa(B), vga(A), aac(6')-Ie-aph(2'')-Ia, ant(4')-Ia, str, tet(K), tet(L), tet(M), fexA, fusB, fusD, dfrK, and tst. These genes were associated with resistance to penicillin, methicillin, erythromycin, clindamycin, gentamicin, tobramycin, streptomycin, tetracycline, chloramphenicol, fusidic acid, trimethoprim, and others. Additionally, two S. sciuri isolates were found to carry the tst gene, indicating potential virulence.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR, disk diffusion, and MALDI-TOF for identifying and characterizing antimicrobial resistance genes and virulence factors in CoNS isolates from wild birds.

full_output.paper_title: Promiscuous Enzyme Activity as a Driver of Allo and Iso Convergent Evolution, Lessons from the β-Lactamases.

bla.validation_method: phylogenetic analysis and functional domain identification

full_output.key_findings: The study explores the convergent evolution of β-lactamase activity, highlighting the promiscuous activity of ancestral sequences and the role of positive selection in the development of resistance mechanisms against β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Sequence selection, functional domain identification, and phylogenetic tree construction.

full_output.paper_title: Biological Activity and Antibiofilm Molecular Profile of Citrus aurantium Essential Oil and Its Application in a Food Model.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the chemical composition, antioxidant, antimicrobial, and antibiofilm activity of Citrus aurantium essential oil (CAEO). CAEO showed significant antibiofilm activity against Stenotrophomonas maltophilia and Bacillus subtilis, as well as antifungal activity against Penicillium species.
full_output.methodology: Chemical composition analysis, DPPH radical scavenging assay, agar disc diffusion method, MBIC analysis, and MALDI-TOF MS profiling were used to evaluate the biological activity of CAEO.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular insights into the genome dynamics and interactions between core and acquired genomes of Vibrio cholerae.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the stability and interactions of genomic islands (GIs), integrative conjugative elements (ICEs), and prophages in Vibrio cholerae, highlighting their roles in genome plasticity and adaptation.
full_output.methodology: Genome engineering, reporter strain construction, PCR, and proteomics analysis were used to study the stability and integration efficiency of GIs, ICEs, and prophages in V. cholerae.

full_output.paper_title: Structure and Function of the FtsE ATP-Binding Domain in Streptococcus pneumoniae
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structural features of the essential cell division protein FtsE and its interaction with FtsX in Streptococcus pneumoniae, highlighting the importance of their interaction for cell growth and morphology.
full_output.methodology: Structural biology techniques including X-ray crystallography and microscale thermophoresis were employed to analyze FtsE and its interaction with FtsX.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDH) and pyruvate formate-lyase (PFL) as essential for V. cholerae growth on mucin, highlighting their roles in aerobic and anaerobic metabolism respectively.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis screens, growth experiments, and in vivo colonization assays in infant mice were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Post-transcriptional modulation of cytochrome P450s, Cyp6g1 and Cyp6g2, by miR-310s cluster is associated with DDT-resistant Drosophila melanogaster strain 91-R.

Cyp6g1.validation_method: microinjection of miR-310s mimics and RT-qPCR

Cyp6g2.validation_method: microinjection of miR-310s mimics and RT-qPCR

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that miR-310s cluster regulates the expression of Cyp6g1 and Cyp6g2, which are associated with DDT resistance in Drosophila melanogaster strain 91-R.
full_output.methodology: Microinjection of miR-310s mimics, RT-qPCR, and luciferase reporter assays.

full_output.paper_title: An Investigation of Potential Health Risks from Zoonotic Bacterial Pathogens Associated with Farm Rats.
full_output.key_findings: Farm rats were found to carry multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens, including high resistance to penicillins and β-lactams among Gram-positive bacteria, and over 50% resistance to several antibiotics among Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolates were identified using the Vitek 2 compact automated system, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed with AST cards.

full_output.paper_title: The large universal Pantoea plasmid LPP‐1 plays a major role in biological and ecological diversification.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the Pantoea plasmid LPP-1 and its role in the biological and ecological diversification of Pantoea species, focusing on its genetic content and potential functions.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and comparative genomics analysis.

full_output.paper_title: BACTIBASE second release: a database and tool platform for bacteriocin characterization
full_output.key_findings: The paper introduces BACTIBASE, a database and tool platform for the characterization of bacteriocins, focusing on their classification, structural features, and functional properties.
full_output.methodology: The paper describes the development and features of BACTIBASE, a database for bacteriocin characterization.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that metabolites like mannitol can enhance the effectiveness of aminoglycoside antibiotics against Gram-negative pathogens at lower concentrations, reducing their toxic side effects. It also demonstrates that this approach does not increase aminoglycoside resistance and can improve treatment of bacterial biofilms.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial cultures, metabolite supplementation, and various microbiological techniques to assess the effects of metabolites on aminoglycoside efficacy and toxicity.

full_output.paper_title: Potential of 2-Chloro-N-(4-fluoro-3-nitrophenyl)acetamide Against Klebsiella pneumoniae and In Vitro Toxicity Analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antibacterial activity of 2-chloro-N-(4-fluoro-3-nitrophenyl)acetamide (A2) against Klebsiella pneumoniae, demonstrating its bactericidal effect and potential as a novel antibacterial agent.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of acetamide derivatives, MIC and MBC determination, molecular docking analysis, and in vitro toxicity assessments.

full_output.paper_title: Where to Biopsy to Detect Helicobacter pylori and How Many Biopsies Are Needed to Detect Antibiotic Resistance in a Human Stomach.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Network and Culture Media Variation Reveal a Complex Metabolic Profile in Pantoea cf. eucrina D2 Associated with an Acidified Marine Sponge.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the production of surfactins and lipoamino acids by Pantoea cf. eucrina D2, highlighting the impact of culture conditions on metabolite profiles. Specific surfactin derivatives and lipoamino acid variants were identified, with some showing moderate antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The research employed molecular networking, HPLC-MS/MS, NMR spectroscopy, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to analyze the metabolome of Pantoea cf. eucrina D2 under various culture conditions.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the Micronaut-S carbapenemase detection microtiter plate for detecting and differentiating carbapenemase classes, including OXA-48-like enzymes, in Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. It identifies several carbapenemase genes such as blaOXA-48, blaKPC-2, blaVIM-1, and others, demonstrating the assay's effectiveness in detecting various carbapenemase producers.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a Micronaut-S carbapenemase detection microtiter plate assay to evaluate the detection of carbapenemases in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra assay detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex DNA in white rhinoceros (Ceratotherium simum) and African elephants (Loxodonta africana).
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra assay for detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) DNA in white rhinoceros and African elephants, showing its effectiveness in identifying MTBC DNA in various sample types.
full_output.methodology: The study used the Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra assay to detect MTBC DNA in respiratory and tissue samples from white rhinoceros and African elephants, comparing results with mycobacterial culture and PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Vibrio cholerae isolates from freshwater sources in northwest Ohio.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae isolates from freshwater sources in northwest Ohio, highlighting their potential virulence factors and antibiotic resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: PCR, biofilm assays, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to analyze the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and Characterization of the Novel Bacteriophage AXL3 against Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the isolation and characterization of the novel bacteriophage AXL3, which targets Stenotrophomonas maltophilia. AXL3 uses the type IV pilus as its receptor for infection, highlighting its potential as a phage therapy candidate against multidrug-resistant S. maltophilia.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, electron microscopy, host range analysis, and genomic characterization were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the Bacteriophage vB_EfaS-271 Infecting Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the bacteriophage vB_EfaS-271, which infects Enterococcus faecalis. The phage has a Siphoviridae morphology, a 40,197 bp genome, and lacks antimicrobial resistance genes and virulence factor homologs. It exhibits lytic activity against specific E. faecalis strains and effectively destroys biofilms.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, electron microscopy, mass spectrometry, and biofilm disruption assays were used to characterize the phage.

full_output.paper_title: Insights into the resistance of a synthetically-derived wheat to Septoria tritici blotch disease: less is more.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies differences in the transcriptomic response to Zymoseptoria tritici between the resistant wheat cultivar Stigg and the susceptible cultivar Longbow, highlighting the molecular basis of Stigg's exceptional resistance to Septoria tritici blotch disease.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing and differential expression analysis were used to compare the transcriptomic responses of the wheat cultivars Stigg and Longbow to Zymoseptoria tritici infection.

full_output.paper_title: LSTrAP-Crowd: prediction of novel components of bacterial ribosomes with crowd-sourced analysis of RNA sequencing data.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel components of bacterial ribosomes using co-expression analysis of RNA-seq data from 17 bacterial pathogens. It highlights the potential of these components as targets for developing species-specific antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Co-expression analysis of RNA-seq data from 17 bacterial pathogens was conducted to identify novel components of ribosomes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in Campylobacter isolates, particularly to ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, and erythromycin. Multiple virulence genes were found to be prevalent in the isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility tests were conducted using the gradient strip method, and virulence genes were analyzed through monoplex and multiplex PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterisation of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolated from patients at a tertiary care hospital in Hyderabad, South India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various MRSA strains including HA-MRSA and CA-MRSA, highlighting the genetic diversity of MRSA in a tertiary care hospital in Hyderabad, India. It also noted the presence of SCCmec type IV as the most frequent type among HA-MRSA.
full_output.methodology: The study employed antibiotic susceptibility testing, PFGE, spa typing, multilocus sequence typing, and SCCmec typing.

full_output.paper_title: Yersinia pestis strains from Latvia show depletion of the pla virulence gene at the end of the second plague pandemic.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a depletion of the pla gene in Yersinia pestis strains from Latvia, suggesting a potential link to the decline of the second plague pandemic.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of ancient DNA from human remains to detect Yersinia pestis strains and assess genetic variations.

full_output.paper_title: Acinetobacter baumannii Sequence Types Harboring Genes Encoding Aminoglycoside Modifying Enzymes and 16SrRNA Methylase; a Multicenter Study from Pakistan.

full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to identify aminoglycoside resistance genes in clinical isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports an increasing proportion of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium bacteraemias in Switzerland from 2013 to 2018, with a steady rise from 2% to 3.9% annually. No specific genetic resistance mechanisms were characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational analysis of enterococcal bacteraemias using data from the Swiss Centre for Antibiotic Resistance (ANRESIS).

full_output.paper_title: nosX is essential for whole-cell N(2)O reduction in Paracoccus denitrificans but not for assembly of copper centres of nitrous oxide reductase.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the nosX gene is essential for whole-cell N2O reduction in Paracoccus denitrificans, and that NosX is not involved in the assembly of copper centers of nitrous oxide reductase (N2OR).
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation and complementation, spectroscopic analysis, and enzymatic activity assays were used to investigate the role of nosX in N2O reduction.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequence of multi-drug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains UY1PSABAL and UY1PSABAL2 isolated from human broncho-alveolar lavage, Yaoundé, Cameroon.

full_output.paper_title: Synergy of the Bacteriocin AS-48 and Antibiotics against Uropathogenic Enterococci.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the effectiveness of the bacteriocin AS-48 against uropathogenic Enterococcus strains, demonstrating significant synergy when combined with antibiotics like vancomycin, gentamicin, and amoxicillin/clavulanate, even against antibiotic-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study characterized clinical isolates of uropathogenic Enterococcus, determined their antibiotic susceptibility, and evaluated the synergistic effects of AS-48 with various antibiotics through MIC testing and FICI analysis.

full_output.paper_title: 8-Deoxy-Rifamycin Derivatives from Amycolatopsis mediterranei S699 ΔrifT Strain.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the deletion of the rifT gene in Amycolatopsis mediterranei S699, leading to the production of 8-deoxy-rifamycin derivatives. The rifT gene was validated through gene complementation experiments.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion and complementation experiments were conducted using PCR, Gibson assembly, and electroporation. Metabolic profiles were analyzed via HPLC and LC-ESI-HRMS.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptomic Analysis of Streptococcus suis in Response to Ferrous Iron and Cobalt Toxicity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified pmtA as a gene significantly up-regulated in response to both ferrous iron and cobalt toxicity in Streptococcus suis, suggesting its role in metal efflux.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing and qRT-PCR analysis were used to examine transcriptomic changes in S. suis under ferrous iron and cobalt exposure.
full_output.sample_size: Three biological replications for each treatment

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial Diversity and Antibiotic Susceptibility of Sparus aurata from Aquaculture.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the qnrB19 gene in a Leclercia adecarboxylata strain with reduced susceptibility to ciprofloxacin and non-synonymous mutations in the parC gene of a Klebsiella pneumoniae strain, contributing to ciprofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, susceptibility testing, and sequencing were used to identify resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial and Amyloidogenic Activity of Peptides Synthesized on the Basis of the Ribosomal S1 Protein from Thermus Thermophilus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified peptides derived from the ribosomal S1 protein of Thermus thermophilus with antimicrobial activity, particularly R23I, which exhibited strong antimicrobial effects comparable to commercial antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Peptides were synthesized and tested for antimicrobial activity using spectrophotometry, electron microscopy, and proteomic analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the molecular mechanisms of C. jejuni infection and its impact on the intestinal immune response, focusing on the role of the CiaD protein in triggering inflammation and neutrophil recruitment.
full_output.methodology: The study used a pig ligated intestinal loop model, RNA-seq, proteomics, and in vitro cell culture experiments to analyze gene expression, protein abundance, and immune responses during C. jejuni infection.

full_output.paper_title: Mutant and Recombinant Phages Selected from In Vitro Coevolution Conditions Overcome Phage-Resistant Listeria monocytogenes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in Listeria phages and phage-resistant L. monocytogenes isolates that enhance host range and resistance to phage infection, demonstrating the utility of in vitro coevolution for improving phage-based control strategies.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, phenotypic analysis, and efficiency of plaquing assays were used to identify mutations and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Bacillus thuringiensis Cry1Ab Domain III β-22 Mutants with Enhanced Toxicity to Spodoptera frugiperda (J. E. Smith)
full_output.key_findings: The Cry1AbS587A mutant exhibited increased toxicity against various Spodoptera frugiperda populations, with enhanced binding affinity to midgut receptors such as APN, ALP, and CAD.
full_output.methodology: Alanine scanning mutagenesis, bioassays, binding assays, and gene silencing experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Outbreak of multi-drug-resistant (MDR) Shigella flexneri in northern Australia due to an endemic regional clone acquiring an IncFII plasmid.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes in a multi-drug-resistant Shigella flexneri strain, including bla DHA, bla OXA-1, tet(B), catA1, dfrA1, mph(A), ermB, qnrB, aadA, and qacEΔ1, which confer resistance to various antibiotics such as beta-lactams, tetracyclines, chloramphenicol, trimethoprim, macrolides, quinolones, aminoglycosides, and quaternary ammonium compounds.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and plasmid characterization were used to identify AMR genes in the Shigella flexneri strains.

full_output.paper_title: BdWRKY38 is required for the incompatible interaction of Brachypodium distachyon with the necrotrophic fungus Rhizoctonia solani.

full_output.paper_title: Concordance of disk diffusion, broth microdilution, and whole-genome sequencing for determination of in vitro antimicrobial susceptibility of Mannheimia haemolytica.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes and mutations in Mannheimia haemolytica isolates, including floR, bla-OXA2, bla-ROB1, tetH/R, erm42, msrE, mphE, and fluoroquinolone resistance mutations in gyrA and parC.

full_output.paper_title: Predictive Analysis of the Side Chain Conformation of the Higher Carbon Sugars: Application to the Preorganization of the Aminoglycoside Ring 1 Side Chain for Binding to the Bacterial Ribosomal Decoding A Site.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the conformational analysis of the side chain of aminoglycoside antibiotics and how it affects their binding to the bacterial ribosome. It shows that the conformation of the exocyclic bond in higher carbon sugars can be predicted based on the configuration of the sugar's structure, which influences the activity of aminoglycosides.

full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the role of type IV coupling proteins (T4CPs) in bacterial conjugation and their potential as targets for inhibiting the spread of antibiotic resistance. full_output.paper_title: WGS-Based Prediction and Analysis of Antimicrobial Resistance in Campylobacter jejuni Isolates From Israel.

The cmeABC multidrug efflux transporter was also found to be prevalent.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) and AMRFinderPlus analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in C. jejuni isolates.

full_output.paper_title: S. aureus Colonization, Biofilm Production, and Phage Susceptibility in Peritoneal Dialysis Patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified S. aureus colonization in peritoneal dialysis patients and evaluated biofilm production and phage susceptibility. full_output.methodology: The study involved S. aureus isolation, biofilm formation testing using microtiter plate assays, and phage susceptibility testing with commercial phage cocktails.

full_output.paper_title: Uncovering the cytochrome P450-catalyzed methylenedioxy bridge formation in streptovaricins biosynthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility signatures identify potential antimicrobial targets in the Acinetobacter baumannii cell envelope.

full_output.paper_title: The type VII secretion system protects Staphylococcus aureus against antimicrobial host fatty acids.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Diversity and Virulence Factors of S. aureus Isolated from Food, Humans, and Animals.

full_output.paper_title: Review of therapeutic options for infections with carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: The Chlamydia trachomatis secreted effector TmeA hijacks the N-WASP-ARP2/3 actin remodeling axis to facilitate cellular invasion.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified seven resistance genes and several mutations associated with antimicrobial resistance in Campylobacter jejuni isolates, demonstrating the effectiveness of whole-genome sequencing in predicting resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing combined with phenotypic susceptibility testing was used to identify resistance genes and mutations in Campylobacter jejuni isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogenetic and genomic analysis reveals high genomic openness and genetic diversity of Clostridium perfringens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 18 antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in Clostridium perfringens, with mprF being the most prevalent, followed by tetA(P) and tetB(P). The number of ARGs increased over time, suggesting exposure to antibiotic selection pressures.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in silico analysis of 173 C. perfringens genomes to identify ARGs and analyze their distribution and transfer networks.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of Potential ARG Packaging by Two Environmental T7-Like Phage during Phage-Host Interaction.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified potential packaging of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) by two T7-like phages, HZP2 and HZ2R8, during phage-host interaction. Six ARGs were detected in HZP2 DNA and four in HZ2R8 DNA, including qnrS, cmlA, tetM, bla TEM, sul3, mcr-1, and others. The abundance of these genes varied, with bla TEM being the most prevalent.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, qPCR, and genome sequencing to analyze ARG packaging by phages.

full_output.paper_title: The Household Resistome: Frequency of β-Lactamases, Class 1 Integrons, and Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria in the Domestic Environment and Their Reduction during Automated Dishwashing and Laundering.

blaCMY-2.validation_method: quantitative real-time PCR and phenotypic resistance testing
blaCMY-2.evidence_note: The paper mentions that bla CMY-2 was the most frequently detected ARG, and it is associated with beta-lactam resistance.

intI1.validation_method: quantitative real-time PCR and phenotypic resistance testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CMY-2, bla ACT/MIR, and bla OXA-48 as the most prevalent β-lactamase genes in household environments, with shower drains showing the highest abundance of antibiotic-resistant bacteria and ARGs.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR, bacterial isolation, and antibiotic susceptibility testing using the Vitek 2 system.

full_output.paper_title: Lactobacillus spp. attenuate antibiotic-induced immune and microbiota dysregulation in honey bees.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies tetB as a tetracycline resistance gene that increases in abundance in the gut microbiota of honey bees following oxytetracycline treatment. Supplementation with Lactobacillus strains (LX3) mitigates antibiotic-associated microbiota dysbiosis and immune deficits.
full_output.methodology: qPCR, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and zone-of-inhibition assays were used to assess microbial and immune responses in honey bees.
full_output.sample_size: n = 6 hives for OTC treatment, n = 4 hives per treatment group for supplementation

full_output.paper_title: The Pseudomonas aeruginosa protease LasB directly activates IL-1β.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LasB, a Pseudomonas aeruginosa protease, as a direct activator of IL-1β, bypassing the need for host caspases. LasB cleaves the pro-domain of IL-1β, leading to its activation and subsequent neutrophilic inflammation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized transgenic reporter cells, protease inhibitors, and bacterial mutants to investigate the role of LasB in IL-1β activation.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of antibiotic-resistant, toxic metal-tolerant and biofilm-forming bacteria in hospital surroundings.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several antibiotic-resistant bacteria, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Bacillus sp., Achromobacter spanius, and Cedecea davisae, which show resistance to multiple antibiotics and heavy metals. These isolates also demonstrate the production of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) enzymes.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and characterization of bacteria from hospital effluents, molecular identification using 16S rDNA sequencing, and determination of antibiotic resistance patterns using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion technique.

full_output.paper_title: Pyrolyzed biowastes deactivated potentially toxic metals and eliminated antibiotic resistant genes for healthy vegetable production.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that pyrolysis of biowastes effectively reduced the abundance of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) such as tetracycline resistance genes (tetC, tetG, tetM, tetO, tetW), sulfonamide resistance genes (sul1, sul2), and class 1 integron-integrase gene (intI1) in swine manure and sewage sludge.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR was used to analyze the abundance of microbial genes and ARGs in biowastes before and after pyrolysis.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of ST15 Klebsiella pneumoniae Clinical Isolates Producing Plasmids-Mediated RmtF and OXA-232 in China.
full_output.key_findings: Three ST15 Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates producing plasmid-mediated RmtF and OXA-232 were identified in China, highlighting the emergence of multidrug-resistant clones.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, cloning experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of mcr-8 in Clinical Isolates From Qatar and Evaluation of Their Antimicrobial Profiles.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mcr-8.1 in Klebsiella pneumoniae and mcr-1.1 in Escherichia coli, both contributing to colistin resistance. Chromosomal mutations in mgrB and phoP were also associated with colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MIC testing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify and characterize AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified aminoglycoside resistance gene aac(6')-Iaa, streptomycin resistance genes strA and strB, sulfonamide resistance gene sul2, tetracycline resistance gene tet(A), and a quinolone resistance mutation in parC (p.T57S) in Salmonella Weltevreden isolates from shrimp and tilapia in Vietnam and China.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella Weltevreden isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Genome Analysis and Phenotypic Characterization of Clostridium gasigenes CGAS001 Isolated From Chilled Vacuum-Packed Lamb Meat.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that Clostridium gasigenes CGAS001 exhibits resistance to polymyxin B and streptomycin.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, disk diffusion assay, and biochemical characterization.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive Determination of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Nontuberculous Mycobacteria From Targeted Capture Sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: Targeted capture sequencing was used to identify drug resistance mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis and nontuberculous mycobacteria, revealing mutations in genes such as katG, embB, embA, embC, rrs, gyrA, rpsL, pncA, rpsA, and rpoB associated with resistance to isoniazid, ethambutol, streptomycin, fluoroquinolones, pyrazinamide, and rifampicin.
full_output.methodology: Targeted capture sequencing was used to analyze the genetic backgrounds of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and nontuberculous mycobacteria strains, identifying drug resistance mutations through sequencing and comparison with a mutation library.

full_output.paper_title: N-terminal Myristoylation Enhanced the Antimicrobial Activity of Antimicrobial Peptide PMAP-36PW.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that N-terminal myristoylation of PMAP-36PW enhances its antimicrobial activity against Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, including S. aureus ATCC 25923 and P. aeruginosa GIM 1.551, with improved stability and effectiveness in reducing bacterial load and inflammation.
full_output.methodology: The study involved peptide synthesis, in vitro antimicrobial activity assays, stability testing, hemolysis and cytotoxicity assessments, biofilm inhibition and eradication experiments, and in vivo therapeutic evaluations in mouse models of infection.

full_output.paper_title: Data on draft genome sequence of stenotrophomonas sp. SAM-B isolated from a mineral cold spring located in Tyva, southern Siberia.
full_output.key_findings: The draft genome of Stenotrophomonas sp. SAM-B reveals the presence of beta-lactamase and quinolone resistance genes, indicating potential resistance to beta-lactam and fluoroquinolone antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing using Illumina MiSeq platform followed by bioinformatics analysis for genome annotation.

full_output.paper_title: Emerging Co-Pathogens: New Delhi Metallo-beta-lactamase producing Enterobacterales Infections in New York City COVID-19 Patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the emergence of New Delhi Metallo-beta-lactamase (NDM) producing Enterobacterales infections in COVID-19 patients in New York City, highlighting the risks of multidrug-resistant infections in hospitalized patients during the pandemic.
full_output.methodology: Detection of NDM genes through PCR testing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of avian-origin mcr-1-positive Escherichia coli with a potential risk to humans in Tai'an, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mcr-1 gene and bla CTX-M-14 and bla CTX-M-15 genes in avian-origin polymyxin-resistant Escherichia coli isolates, highlighting their potential risk to humans.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance genes and phenotypes.
full_output.sample_size: 87 poultry E. coli isolates and 356 human E. coli isolates

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of thyme oil against foodborne multiple antibiotics-resistant Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.key_findings: Thyme oil effectively inhibited the biofilm formation of E. faecalis by reducing cell motility and exopolysaccharide (EPS) production. It also inactivated E. faecalis cells in mature biofilms at high concentrations.
full_output.methodology: Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, crystal violet staining, qRT-PCR, and confocal laser scanning microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Success of Escherichia coli O25b:H4 Sequence Type 131 Clade C Associated with a Decrease in Virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes several AMR genes and mutations in E. coli O25b:H4 ST131 clades B and C, highlighting differences in virulence and resistance profiles between the clades.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping, phenotypic analysis, and in vivo virulence assays were conducted to identify and validate AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses various AMR genes and mutations associated with resistance to antibiotics, focusing on mechanisms such as enzymatic degradation, altered target sites, and efflux pumps. Key genes identified include aac(6')-Ie + aph(2'')-Ia, ant(4')-Ia, aph(3')-IIIa, aac(6')-Ie + aph(3''), vanA, vanB, vanC, vanE, vanD, vanG, vanM, vanL, blaOXA-23, blaOXA-24, blaOXA-51, blaOXA-58, blaKPC, mexR, gyrA, gyrB, parC, parE, qnr, cfr, mprF, arnBCADTEF operon, and pmrE.
full_output.methodology: The paper provides a comprehensive review of AMR mechanisms and associated genes, discussing their roles in resistance to various antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Sphaerostilbellins, New Antimicrobial Aminolipopeptide Peptaibiotics from Sphaerostilbella toxica.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the discovery of two new antimicrobial peptaibiotics, sphaerostilbellins A and B, from the fungus Sphaerostilbella toxica, which show potent antifungal activity against various pathogens including Cryptococcus neoformans, Candida albicans, Aspergillus fumigatus, and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: The research involved fermentation of S. toxica strains, bioassay-guided fractionation, and structural characterization using NMR and HRMS. Antimicrobial activity was evaluated through zone of inhibition assays and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) tests.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity of Selected Essential Oil Compounds Alone and in Combination with β-Lactam Antibiotics Against MRSA Strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA gene, which confers resistance to methicillin and penicillin G in MRSA strains. The research also explored the synergistic effects of essential oil compounds with β-lactam antibiotics against MRSA.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC testing, and checkerboard assays were used to evaluate the antibacterial activity of essential oil compounds and β-lactam antibiotics against MRSA strains.

full_output.paper_title: Optimal regimens based on PK/PD cutoff evaluation of ceftiofur against Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae in swine.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) cutoff for ceftiofur against Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae in swine, determining the optimal dosage regimens to achieve bacteriostatic, bactericidal, and elimination effects.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PK/PD modeling, MIC distribution analysis, and Monte Carlo simulations to determine the optimal ceftiofur dosage regimens for treating Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae infections in swine.

full_output.paper_title: Leclercia adecarboxylata causing necrotising soft tissue infection in an immunocompetent adult.
full_output.key_findings: The case presents the first reported instance of a monomicrobial necrotising soft tissue infection (NSTI) caused by Leclercia adecarboxylata in an immunocompetent individual. The isolate was pansusceptible to multiple antibiotics, including amoxicillin/clavulanate, piperacillin/tazobactam, and others.
full_output.methodology: Clinical case report with susceptibility testing of the isolated bacterium.

full_output.methodology: Growth curve-based method to measure sensitivity to sublethal HOCl stress, ICP-MS for intracellular copper concentration measurement, and biochemical assays to assess RclA activity.

full_output.key_findings: Indels in Mycobacterium tuberculosis are significantly enriched in antibiotic resistance genes, contributing to the evolution of multidrug resistance in an outbreak. Specific genes like pncA, mmaA3, ethA, espK, and nudC were identified as being disrupted by indels, leading to resistance against pyrazinamide, isoniazid, and ethionamide.
full_output.methodology: High-quality variant inference and phylogenetic analysis were used to study the evolution of point and segmental mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains from an outbreak.
full_output.sample_size: 353 MTB strains from the CAO and 64 from the Hamburg outbreak

full_output.paper_title: Surficial N+ charge density indicating antibacterial capacity of quaternary ammonium resins in water environment.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces the concept of surficial N+ charge density as a novel parameter to assess the antibacterial capacity of quaternary ammonium resins (QARs). It establishes a method to measure this charge density, demonstrating its effectiveness in predicting antibacterial efficacy against both gram-negative and gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study employed a method involving tetraphenylboron sodium standard solution (TS) to determine the surficial N+ charge density of QARs, correlating it with antibacterial efficacy through experiments with E. coli and S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: High Colonization Rate and Heterogeneity of ESBL- and Carbapenemase-Producing Enterobacteriaceae Isolated from Gull Feces in Lisbon, Portugal.

blaKPC-3.evidence_note: The gene blaKPC-3 was identified in the study as a carbapenemase gene in Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various ESBL and carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae in gull feces, including OXA-181, OXA-48, KPC-2, KPC-3, GES-5, GES-6, and multiple CTX-M variants. These findings highlight the role of gulls as potential reservoirs for multidrug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and plasmid analysis were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Structural insight into the Staphylococcus aureus ATP-driven exporter of virulent peptide toxins.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the PmtCD transporter, an ATP-binding cassette (ABC) exporter involved in the secretion of phenol-soluble modulins (PSMs) in Staphylococcus aureus. The research identifies the minimal functional unit of the transporter and provides structural insights into its mechanism of action.
full_output.methodology: Cryo-EM, x-ray crystallography, and functional ATPase assays were used to characterize the PmtCD transporter.

full_output.paper_title: Bacillus licheniformis strain POT1 mediated polyphenol biosynthetic pathways genes activation and systemic resistance in potato plants against Alfalfa mosaic virus.
full_output.key_findings: Bacillus licheniformis strain POT1 induces systemic resistance in potato plants against Alfalfa mosaic virus (AMV) by activating polyphenol biosynthetic pathways, leading to increased resistance and reduced viral accumulation.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antiviral activity of Bacillus licheniformis strain POT1, analyzed transcriptional levels of polyphenol biosynthetic pathway genes, and used HPLC and GC-MS for metabolite profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Sublethal Levels of Antibiotics Promote Bacterial Persistence in Epithelial Cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that sublethal levels of antibiotics promote bacterial persistence in epithelial cells by increasing toxin production, disrupting autophagy, and impairing lysosomal acidification, which leads to reduced antibiotic efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo models, including bacterial infection of epithelial cells, antibiotic treatments, and analysis of bacterial survival, autophagy, and lysosomal function.

full_output.paper_title: Screening of Lactobacillus plantarum Subsp. plantarum with Potential Probiotic Activities for Inhibiting ETEC K88 in Weaned Piglets.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Lactobacillus plantarum subsp. plantarum ZA3 as a potential probiotic with strong antimicrobial activity against ETEC K88 and other microorganisms. ZA3 showed resistance to norfloxacin and amikacin but was sensitive to several antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of LAB strains, analyzed their physiological and biochemical characteristics, and assessed their safety and resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of gramicidin A analogues with altered activities by multidimensional screening of a one-bead-one-compound library.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the discovery of 10 gramicidin A analogues with altered biological activities through a high-throughput screening approach. These analogues exhibit variations in cytotoxic, hemolytic, and antibacterial activities compared to the parent compound.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening of a one-bead-one-compound (OBOC) library of gramicidin A analogues, followed by functional assays and structural determination via MS/MS.

full_output.paper_title: Genomics of the Argentinian cholera epidemic elucidate the contrasting dynamics of epidemic and endemic Vibrio cholerae.

wbeT.notes: Mutations in wbeT lead to serotype Inaba or Ogawa depending on the specific mutation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several beta-lactamase genes (bla CTX-M-3, bla OXA-8, bla TEM) and mutations in the wbeT gene associated with serotype variation in the LAT-1 sub-lineage of Vibrio cholerae during the Argentinian cholera epidemic.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of 490 V. cholerae isolates, phylogenetic analysis, and identification of genetic variations.

full_output.paper_title: Piperacillin/tazobactam resistance in a clinical isolate of Escherichia coli due to IS26-mediated amplification of bla(TEM-1B).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IS26-mediated amplification of bla(TEM-1B) as the mechanism of piperacillin/tazobactam resistance in a clinical isolate of Escherichia coli, leading to hyperproduction of the beta-lactamase TEM-1B without a fitness cost.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MIC testing, qPCR, and PCR for junction detection.

full_output.paper_title: Validation of stable reference genes in Staphylococcus aureus to study gene expression under photodynamic treatment: a case study of SEB virulence factor analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ftsZ and gmk as the most stable reference genes under rose bengal and green light treatment, while ftsZ, proC, and fabD were the most stable under new methylene blue and red light treatment. It also showed that aPDI significantly downregulated the seb gene, indicating a potential effect on virulence factor expression.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR and various software tools (BestKeeper, geNorm, NormFinder, RefFinder) to evaluate the stability of reference genes under different photodynamic treatment conditions.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies tripodal peptidyl compounds that activate the DegP protease, leading to bacterial growth inhibition. These compounds bind to the substrate-binding sites of DegP and cause excessive degradation of newly synthesized proteins, demonstrating a novel strategy for antibiotic development by over-activating a non-essential bacterial enzyme.
full_output.methodology: The study used biochemical assays, crystallography, and bacterial growth inhibition experiments to characterize the activity of tripodal peptidyl compounds targeting the DegP protease.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance and genotyping of mecA-positive methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) from milk and nasal carriage of dairy water buffaloes (Bubalus bubalis) in the Philippines.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mecA-positive MRSA isolates from milk and nasal swabs of dairy water buffaloes in the Philippines, highlighting their resistance to penicillin and cefoxitin.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm forming potentiality of Escherichia coli isolated from bovine endometritis and their antibiotic resistance profiles.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple antibiotic resistance genes in E. coli isolates from bovine endometritis, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug-resistant strains and the association of fim H with biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, biofilm formation assessment via Congo red agar, and PCR-based detection of resistance and virulence genes.

full_output.paper_title: Mycolactone induces cell death by SETD1B-dependent degradation of glutathione.

full_output.paper_title: Synanthropic spiders, including the global invasive noble false widow Steatoda nobilis, are reservoirs for medically important and antibiotic resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various bacteria on the body surfaces and chelicerae of Steatoda nobilis, including several that show resistance to antibiotics. Notably, Pseudomonas putida, Staphylococcus capitis, and Staphylococcus edaphicus exhibited resistance to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolating and identifying bacteria from the body surfaces and chelicerae of Steatoda nobilis using 16S rRNA sequencing and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Co-infection With Chromosomally-Located bla (CTX-M-14) and Plasmid-Encoding bla (CTX-M-15) in Pathogenic Escherichia coli in the Republic of Korea.

blaCTX-M-15.genetic_context: IS Ecp1 - bla CTX-M-14 - IS903 transposon
blaCTX-M-15.evidence_note: All EAEC isolates carried the bla CTX-M-14 gene and all ETEC isolates the bla CTX-M-15 gene, as detected by multiplex PCR and sequencing analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first case of co-infection with chromosomally located bla CTX-M-14 and plasmid-encoding bla CTX-M-15 in pathogenic E. coli, highlighting the role of both chromosomal and plasmid-mediated resistance mechanisms in the spread of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes.
full_output.methodology: Molecular analysis, including antibiotic susceptibility testing, multiplex PCR, sequencing, MLST, PFGE, and whole-genome sequencing, was performed to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of Staphylococcal Bacteriophage Sb-1 as an Adjunctive Agent to Antibiotics Against Rifampin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the efficacy of phage Sb-1 in combination with antibiotics against rifampin-resistant S. aureus biofilms, highlighting synergistic effects with daptomycin and vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: The study used isothermal microcalorimetry and sonication/colony-counting to assess the antibiofilm activity of phage-antibiotic combinations.

full_output.paper_title: The Lung Microbiome of Three Young Brazilian Patients With Cystic Fibrosis Colonized by Fungi.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a variety of bacterial and fungal species in the lungs of three young CF patients, including several antibiotic resistance genes. Key findings included the presence of A. fumigatus, Candida albicans, and various bacteria such as S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, and B. cepacia complex. The study also noted the presence of virulence factors and antibiotic resistance genes, highlighting the complexity of the CF lung microbiome.
full_output.methodology: The study used culture isolation, metataxonomics, and metagenomics shotgun sequencing to analyze the lung microbiome of three CF patients. Virulence factors and antibiotic resistance genes were identified using bioinformatics tools and databases.

full_output.key_findings: Periplanetasin-2 enhances the antibacterial properties of vancomycin and chloramphenicol in Escherichia coli through synergistic interactions, leading to increased oxidative stress and apoptosis-like death.
full_output.methodology: Synergistic antibacterial activity of periplanetasin-2 with conventional antibacterial agents was examined using checkerboard assays and measurement of reactive oxygen species (ROS) production.

full_output.paper_title: Rescued chlorhexidine activity by resveratrol against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii via down-regulation of AdeB efflux pump.

adeB.validation_method: RT-qPCR and ethidium bromide accumulation assay

aceI.validation_method: RT-qPCR and ethidium bromide accumulation assay

full_output.key_findings: Resveratrol enhances chlorhexidine susceptibility by down-regulating the AdeB efflux pump in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.methodology: RT-qPCR, ethidium bromide accumulation assay, checkerboard and time-kill assays.

full_output.paper_title: EcDBS1R4, an Antimicrobial Peptide Effective against Escherichia coli with In Vitro Fusogenic Ability.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies EcDBS1R4 as an antimicrobial peptide effective against Gram-negative bacteria, particularly Escherichia coli, with a unique mechanism involving membrane fusion and hyperpolarization without pore formation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro assays, membrane model systems, and spectroscopic techniques to evaluate the antimicrobial activity and mechanism of EcDBS1R4.

full_output.paper_title: The Role of Efflux Pumps in the Transition from Low-Level to Clinical Antibiotic Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the role of efflux pumps in the transition from low-level to clinical antibiotic resistance, highlighting their contribution to bacterial persistence and the potential for developing high-level resistance through secondary mutations.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature and studies on efflux pumps and their role in antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Recent Advances in Zinc Oxide Nanostructures with Antimicrobial Activities.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the synthesis and antimicrobial properties of zinc oxide (ZnO) nanostructures, focusing on their photocatalytic activity and ability to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) for bacterial inactivation.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews the synthesis methods, photocatalytic properties, and antimicrobial activities of ZnO nanostructures, including the effects of metal and non-metal doping, carbon nanomaterial modifications, and semiconductor heterojunctions.

full_output.paper_title: A polymicrobial biofilm model for testing the antimicrobial potential of a nisin-biogel for canine periodontal disease control.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed an in vitro polymicrobial biofilm model for canine periodontal disease and evaluated the antimicrobial potential of a nisin-biogel. The model included five bacterial species: Neisseria zoodegmatis, Corynebacterium canis, Enterococcus faecalis, Porphyromonas cangingivalis, and Peptostreptococcus canis. The nisin-biogel showed effectiveness in inhibiting and eradicating the biofilm.
full_output.methodology: The study used a polymicrobial biofilm model, coaggregation assays, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and determination of minimum biofilm inhibitory (MBIC) and eradication concentrations (MBEC) of nisin-biogel.

full_output.paper_title: A bacteriocin-based antimicrobial formulation to effectively disrupt the cell viability of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: Garvicin KS and micrococcin P1 exhibit potent antimicrobial activity against S. aureus biofilms, including MRSA strains. Their combination enhances the effectiveness of penicillin G against MRSA by reducing biofilm resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity assays, BOAT assays, CFU counting, confocal microscopy, and SEM analysis were used to evaluate the effects of the bacteriocins on S. aureus biofilms.

full_output.key_findings: The study introduces a novel genome-editing method called 'Rock-Paper-Scissors' (RPS) that allows for efficient and robust iterative genome modifications in bacteria, particularly in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae. The method utilizes three sgRNA plasmids that can cure or be cured by each other, enabling simultaneous plasmid curing and genome editing without the need for separate steps.
full_output.methodology: The study describes the development and testing of the RPS genome-editing system, involving the construction of plasmids with specific sgRNA sequences, evaluation of plasmid curing efficiency through transformation and colony counting, and verification of genome edits via PCR and sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: miR-15a-5p and miR-21-5p contribute to chemoresistance in cytogenetically normal acute myeloid leukaemia by targeting PDCD4, ARL2 and BTG2.
full_output.key_findings: miR-15a-5p and miR-21-5p are overexpressed in chemoresistant AML patients and contribute to chemoresistance by targeting PDCD4, ARL2, and BTG2.
full_output.methodology: Small RNA sequencing, qRT-PCR, Western blotting, luciferase reporter assays, and siRNA transfections were used to analyze miRNA expression and target gene regulation.

full_output.paper_title: Extremely drug-resistant NDM-9-producing ST147 Klebsiella pneumoniae causing infections in Italy, May 2020.

blaNDM-9.genetic_context: bla NDM-9 gene, which presented one amino-acid substitution (E152K) with respect to bla NDM-1 gene identified in 2018–2019 isolates
blaNDM-9.evidence_note: The Kp-P1 and Kp-P2 strains carried the bla NDM-9 gene, which presented one amino-acid substitution (E152K) with respect to bla NDM-1 gene identified in 2018–2019 isolates.

sul2.evidence_note: The paper mentions the presence of sul2 in the context of resistance genes in K. pneumoniae strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of XDR ST147 K. pneumoniae strains carrying the blaNDM-9 gene and various resistance mechanisms, including chromosomal mutations in ramR, mgrB, and glpT that confer resistance to tigecycline, colistin, and fosfomycin.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, susceptibility testing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes and mutations in the studied strains.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and Antibiotic Susceptibility Pattern of Bacterial Uropathogens and Associated Factors Among Adult People Living with HIV/AIDS Attending the HIV Center at Wolaita Sodo University Teaching Referral Hospital, South Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified E. coli and S. aureus as the primary causes of urinary tract infections (UTIs) among HIV/AIDS patients. High rates of resistance to amoxicillin-clavulanic acid and ampicillin were observed, along with multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial isolates.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving 205 HIV/AIDS patients, with antimicrobial susceptibility testing performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, serotyping and drug susceptibility patterns of Escherichia coli isolates from kidney transplanted patients with urinary tract infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM, blaCTX-M, and blaSHV as the most common ESBL-encoding genes in E. coli isolates from kidney transplant patients with urinary tract infections, with high resistance rates to ampicillin, cefotaxime, and cefazolin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, serotyping, and polymerase chain reaction were used to analyze E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular and phenotypic characterization of Salmonella Typhimurium monophasic variant (1,4,[5],12:i:-) from Colombian clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the circulation of Salmonella Typhimurium monophasic variant (STVM) in Colombia, with a focus on genetic and phenotypic characteristics. It found that 61% of the isolates were STVM, with the European-Spanish clone being predominant. The study also noted variations in motility and membrane protein expression, particularly in urine-derived isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR, whole genome sequencing, and phenotypic analysis including growth curves, motility tests, and outer membrane protein evaluation.

full_output.paper_title: Chloroquine reverses chemoresistance via upregulation of p21(WAF1/CIP1) and autophagy inhibition in ovarian cancer.
full_output.key_findings: Chloroquine enhances cisplatin-induced cell death in ovarian cancer by upregulating p21(WAF1/CIP1) and inhibiting autophagy, leading to increased DNA damage and apoptosis.
full_output.methodology: Cell viability assays, Western blot, flow cytometry, immunofluorescence, and in vivo xenograft models.

full_output.paper_title: D- and Unnatural Amino Acid Substituted Antimicrobial Peptides With Improved Proteolytic Resistance and Their Proteolytic Degradation Characteristics.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on modifying antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) by substituting L-amino acids with D-amino acids and unnatural amino acids to improve their proteolytic resistance. Derivatives such as DP06 and UP09 showed improved in vitro stability, but their in vivo performance varied, highlighting the importance of optimizing AMPs for both stability and efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and characterization of AMP derivatives, assessing their stability towards proteases, antimicrobial activity, and toxicity using techniques such as RP-HPLC, CD spectroscopy, and MIC assays.

full_output.paper_title: Co-occurrence of Rapid Gene Gain and Loss in an Interhospital Outbreak of Carbapenem-Resistant Hypervirulent ST11-K64 Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the carbapenemase gene bla KPC–2 and the aminoglycoside modifying gene rmtB as key contributors to carbapenem and aminoglycoside resistance in ST11-K64 Klebsiella pneumoniae strains during an interhospital outbreak. Additionally, the loss of the 10-kbp fragment containing rmtB led to reduced aminoglycoside resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid analysis, PCR, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify and validate AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of enterotoxigenic Staphylococcus aureus harboring seb gene and enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (serogroups O18, O114, and O125) from soft and hard artisanal cheeses in Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified enterotoxigenic Staphylococcus aureus strains carrying the seb, sed, and see genes, as well as enteropathogenic E. coli serogroups O18, O114, and O125 in artisanal cheeses from Egypt.
full_output.methodology: Microbiological examination, PCR, and molecular characterization of isolates.

full_output.paper_title: L-Arginine Enhances Intracellular Killing of Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae ST258 by Murine Neutrophils.

wcaJ.notes: Associated with capsule biosynthesis and evasion of phagocytosis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the wcaJ gene in KP35 and KPPR1, which is involved in capsule biosynthesis and contributes to evasion of phagocytosis. l-arginine supplementation enhances neutrophil intracellular killing of KP35 by improving phagosome acidification, ROS production, and NO consumption.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of cps loci, neutrophil phagocytosis assays, and evaluation of intracellular killing mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: The potential therapeutic role of PTR1 gene in non-healing anthroponotic cutaneous leishmaniasis due to Leishmania tropica.

PTR1.validation_method: transfection with antisense plasmid and measurement of IC50

full_output.key_findings: The study found that the PTR1 gene reduces the efficacy of meglumine antimoniate, and its inhibition by antisense improves the treatment of non-healing cases of Leishmania tropica.
full_output.methodology: Transfection of Leishmania tropica with antisense plasmid and evaluation of drug susceptibility using IC50 measurements.
full_output.sample_size: Three isolates (two non-healing and one healing)

full_output.paper_title: Taking the next-gen step: Comprehensive antimicrobial resistance detection from Burkholderia pseudomallei.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents ARDaP, a new tool for comprehensive antimicrobial resistance (AMR) detection in Burkholderia pseudomallei. ARDaP accurately identifies various AMR determinants, including mutations in genes such as penA, bpeT, ptr1, metF, dut, bpsl3085, and amrR, which confer resistance to antibiotics like ceftazidime, meropenem, co-trimoxazole, and doxycycline.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized whole-genome sequencing and developed ARDaP to detect AMR determinants in B. pseudomallei, validating findings through experimental methods such as MIC testing and genetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of the agr System and Resistance to Antimicrobials in Biofilm-Producing S. epidermidis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA gene as a significant contributor to oxacillin resistance in biofilm-producing S. epidermidis strains, highlighting its role in antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, RT-PCR, MIC testing, PFGE, and MLST were used to analyze biofilm production and antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of OXA-Type β-Lactamase Genes among Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Clinical Isolates in Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of OXA-type β-lactamase genes among carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates in Thailand, highlighting the dominance of bla oxa-23-like genes and the lower prevalence of bla oxa-40/24-like and bla oxa-58-like genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and multi-locus sequence typing were used to analyze the prevalence and characteristics of OXA-type β-lactamase genes in CRAB isolates.

full_output.key_findings: Four tet(X) variants (tet(X3), tet(X4), tet(X5.2), and tet(X5.3)) were identified in Acinetobacter species, showing high-level resistance to tigecycline, tetracycline, eravacycline, and omadacycline. These genes were found in multiple Acinetobacter species and were associated with IS CR2 elements, facilitating their spread.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, cloning, susceptibility testing, and biochemical assays were used to characterize the tet(X) variants.

full_output.paper_title: Functional Characterization of the γ-Aminobutyric Acid Transporter from Mycobacterium smegmatis MC(2) 155 Reveals Sodium-Driven GABA Transport.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the GABA transporter GabP from Mycobacterium smegmatis, showing it is a sodium-dependent GABA transporter that can also transport β-alanine.
full_output.methodology: Expression in E. coli, radiolabeled transport assays, and reconstitution into liposomes.

full_output.paper_title: Dissociating antibacterial from ototoxic effects of gentamicin C-subtypes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies gentamicin C-subtypes and their ototoxicity profiles, demonstrating that C2b is the least ototoxic while maintaining antimicrobial activity, and highlights structure-activity relationships that can guide the development of safer aminoglycoside antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Purification of gentamicin C-subtypes, antimicrobial activity testing, and ototoxicity assessments in cochlear hair cells.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Action and Reversal of Resistance in MRSA by Difluorobenzamide Derivatives Targeted at FtsZ.
