penA.notes: PenA D192G mutation results in MEM sensitivity

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the class A beta-lactamase gene penA and efflux pump regulators bpeR and bpeT that contribute to extensive drug resistance in Burkholderia multivorans, and shows that antibiotic cycling can reverse this resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and mutational analysis were used to identify genetic changes associated with drug resistance in B. multivorans.
full_output.sample_size: Six XDR variants and their corresponding pan-CS variants

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a Novel Plasmid-Mediated Carbapenemase-Encoding Gene, bla(VMB-2), in Vibrio diabolicus.

bla(VMB-2).validation_method: cloning in E. coli BL21(DE3) and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel plasmid-mediated carbapenemase gene, bla(VMB-2), in Vibrio diabolicus, which confers resistance to β-lactam antibiotics including meropenem and ceftazidime.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, bioinformatics analysis, cloning, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: MAB_2355c Confers Macrolide Resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus by Ribosome Protection.

MAB_2355c.validation_method: gene knockout and complementation, antibiotic sensitivity assays

full_output.key_findings: MAB_2355c, an ATP-binding cassette F family protein, confers macrolide resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus through ribosome protection.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics analysis, gene cloning, protein purification, ATP hydrolysis assay, gene knockout and complementation, antibiotic sensitivity testing, and in vitro transcription-translation assays.

full_output.paper_title: WeFaceNano: a user-friendly pipeline for complete ONT sequence assembly and detection of antibiotic resistance in multi-plasmid bacterial isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents WeFaceNano, a user-friendly pipeline for assembling and analyzing long-read plasmid sequences from the Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) platform. It identifies various antibiotic resistance (AMR) genes in plasmids from multiple bacterial isolates, including beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, tetracycline resistance genes, and others.
full_output.methodology: WeFaceNano uses long-read sequencing data from ONT and integrates tools for assembly, annotation, and AMR gene detection. It includes BLAST, ResFinder, and PlasmidFinder for identifying AMR genes and plasmid incompatibility factors.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-Genome Sequencing and Machine Learning Analysis of Staphylococcus aureus from Multiple Heterogeneous Sources in China Reveals Common Genetic Traits of Antimicrobial Resistance.

maoC.evidence_note: The paper mentions that maoC was found to be highly discriminant between resistant and susceptible cefoxitin and oxacillin phenotypes, and that it was located in the SCC mec s of 332 isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from various sources in China, including mecA, cat, aacA-aphD, ugpQ, maoC, and tcaA, which are associated with resistance to oxacillin, cefoxitin, chloramphenicol, gentamicin, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and machine learning analysis were used to identify AMR genes and their associations with resistance phenotypes.

full_output.paper_title: Early Life Antibiotics Influence In Vivo and In Vitro Mouse Intestinal Epithelium Maturation and Functioning.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that early life antibiotic treatment in mice leads to changes in intestinal epithelial maturation and function, including decreased intestinal permeability, loss of vacuolated enterocytes, and alterations in gene expression related to maturation, digestion, defense, and sensing.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide gene expression analysis, qRT-PCR, immunohistochemistry, and fetal organoid culture experiments were used to assess the effects of early life antibiotic treatment on intestinal epithelial cells.

full_output.paper_title: Discrimination of hospital isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii using repeated sequences and whole genome alignment differential analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a polymorphic region in the DNA polymerase III subunit gamma/tau gene of Acinetobacter baumannii, which showed significant length polymorphism and was associated with imipenem susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, RFLP, and multiple genome alignments to identify polymorphic regions in Acinetobacter baumannii strains.

full_output.paper_title: A Bioengineered Nisin Derivative To Control Streptococcus uberis Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that nisin PV, a derivative of nisin A with S29P and I30V substitutions, shows enhanced resistance to proteolytic cleavage by NSR and is more effective in eradicating and inhibiting biofilms of Streptococcus uberis strains carrying the NSR system.
full_output.methodology: The study uses deferred antagonism assays, crystal violet assays, XTT assays, and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) to evaluate the bioactivity of nisin A and nisin PV against S. uberis biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Pigeons as Carriers of Clinically Relevant Multidrug-Resistant Pathogens-A Clinical Case Report and Literature Review.
full_output.key_findings: Three multidrug-resistant pathogens were isolated from a racing pigeon, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli, and Candida albicans resistant to multiple antifungals. The study highlights the potential public health concern of multidrug-resistant pathogens in pigeons.
full_output.methodology: Clinical examination, microbial culture, PCR for mecA gene detection, and disk-diffusion antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed.

full_output.paper_title: First Isolation and Molecular Characterization of bla (CTX-M-121) -Producing Escherichia coli O157:H7 From Cattle in Xinjiang, China.

blaCTX-M-121.evidence_note: The bla CTX-M-121 gene was detected in E. coli O157:H7 isolates, and it was transferable via plasmid transmission.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of the bla CTX-M-121 gene in Escherichia coli O157:H7 isolated from cattle in Xinjiang, China. This gene confers resistance to cephalosporins such as cefotaxime and ceftazidime.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and conjugation experiments were used to detect and characterize the bla CTX-M-121 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of mcr-1-positive multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli ST93, ST117, ST156, ST10, and ST744 isolated from poultry in Poland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1-positive multidrug-resistant E. coli strains from poultry in Poland, highlighting the presence of resistance genes including bla TEM, tetA, tetB, sul1, sul2, and sul3.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC testing, and MLST were used to characterize the resistance genes and sequence types of the E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid detection of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis based on allele-specific recombinase polymerase amplification and colorimetric detection.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed an allele-specific RPA/SYBR assay to detect major mutations in the rpoB and katG genes associated with rifampicin and isoniazid resistance in M. tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized allele-specific recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) combined with SYBR Green I detection to identify specific mutations in the rpoB and katG genes.

full_output.paper_title: Reinvestigation of the structure-activity relationships of isoniazid.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the structure-activity relationships of isoniazid (INH) and its analogs against various mycobacterial strains, identifying structural modifications that affect antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis and evaluation of INH analogs against mycobacterial and other bacterial strains using MIC assays.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic basis of molecular mechanisms in β-lactam resistant gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the genetic basis of β-lactam resistance in gram-negative bacteria, focusing on various β-lactamase genes such as CTX-M, TEM, SHV, KPC, and NDM. These genes confer resistance to a range of β-lactam antibiotics through hydrolysis.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews the molecular mechanisms of β-lactam resistance, including the characterization of β-lactamase genes and their impact on antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: Colistin-resistant and multidrug-resistant gram-negative bacteria were found in cloacal swabs of wild birds in a Ghanaian forest protected area, indicating potential for AMR spread from wildlife to humans and domestic animals.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing of 195 isolates, including colistin and multidrug resistance tests using disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Synthetic studies of cystobactamids as antibiotics and bacterial imaging carriers lead to compounds with high in vivo efficacy.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of cystobactamid derivatives with improved antibacterial activity against Gram-negative and Gram-positive pathogens, including the identification of compounds with high in vivo efficacy.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, antibacterial activity testing, gyrase inhibition assays, and in vivo pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic studies.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro Assessment of the Safety and Potential Probiotic Characteristics of Three Bacillus Strains Isolated From the Intestine of Hybrid Grouper (Epinephelus fuscoguttatus♀ × Epinephelus lanceolatus♂).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified three Bacillus strains (GPSAK2, GPSAK4, and GPSAK9) isolated from the intestine of hybrid grouper, evaluating their probiotic potential, including antibiotic susceptibility. GPSAK9 showed resistance to certain antibiotics, while others displayed susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation, identification, and characterization of Bacillus strains through biochemical tests, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and molecular analysis.

full_output.paper_title: In Vivo Evolution of GES β-Lactamases Driven by Ceftazidime/Avibactam Treatment of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infections.

blaGES-5.validation_method: cloning in PAO1 and susceptibility testing

blaGES-15.validation_method: cloning in PAO1 and susceptibility testing
blaGES-15.evidence_note: The paper describes the P162S substitution in bla GES-5 leading to bla GES-15, which confers resistance to meropenem and ceftazidime.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that a single amino acid substitution (P162S) in bla GES-5 leads to the formation of bla GES-15, which reverts the carbapenemase phenotype of GES-5 back to the ESBL phenotype of GES-1, demonstrating the dynamic nature of β-lactamase evolution in response to antibiotic pressure.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, cloning, and susceptibility testing of β-lactamase variants in PAO1.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in a Membrane Permease or hpt Lead to 6-Thioguanine Resistance in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the stgP gene, encoding a xanthine/uracil permease, and in the hpt gene, encoding hypoxanthine phosphoribosyltransferase, as mechanisms of 6-thioguanine resistance in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, complementation experiments, and disc diffusion assays were used to identify and validate mutations in stgP and hpt that confer 6-thioguanine resistance.

full_output.key_findings: Omadacycline showed superior in vitro and in vivo efficacy against multidrug-resistant Enterococcus faecium strains compared to daptomycin and vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: In vitro MIC testing and in vivo mouse peritonitis model experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanistic insights into translation inhibition by aminoglycoside antibiotic arbekacin.
full_output.key_findings: Arbekacin (ABK) inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by impairing the accuracy of tRNA selection and stabilizing dipeptidyl tRNA at the ribosomal A-site, leading to mistranslation and reduced translational efficiency.
full_output.methodology: In vitro translation experiments using a reconstituted E. coli system, GTP hydrolysis assays, and fluorescence-based mRNA translocation measurements.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic prescriptions and risk factors for antimicrobial resistance in patients hospitalized with urinary tract infection: a matched case-control study using the French health insurance database (SNDS).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies antibiotic exposure, particularly broad-spectrum antibiotics, as a significant risk factor for antimicrobial resistance in urinary tract infections. It highlights the importance of prudent antibiotic use to prevent resistance development.
full_output.methodology: A matched case-control study using the French national health data system (SNDS) to analyze risk factors for antimicrobial resistance in hospitalized patients with urinary tract infections.

full_output.paper_title: Burden of illness in US hospitals due to carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative urinary tract infections in patients with or without bacteraemia.
full_output.key_findings: Carbapenem-resistant (CR) Gram-negative pathogens, particularly Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae, were associated with increased healthcare burden, longer hospital stays, higher mortality rates, and greater hospitalization charges compared to carbapenem-susceptible (CS) pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of the Premier Healthcare Database from 2014 to 2019, including microbiology test results and patient outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Metallo-β-lactamases in the Age of Multidrug Resistance: From Structure and Mechanism to Evolution, Dissemination, and Inhibitor Design.

full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the role of metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs) in multidrug resistance, focusing on their structure, mechanism, and contribution to resistance against β-lactam antibiotics. It highlights the importance of MBLs in the spread of resistance and the challenges they pose for inhibitor design.
full_output.methodology: This is a review article summarizing existing research on MBLs, their mechanisms, and implications for antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Varied-shaped gold nanoparticles with nanogram killing efficiency as potential antimicrobial surface coatings for the medical devices.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes varied-shaped gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) with potent antimicrobial activity against a wide range of microbial pathogens, including multidrug-resistant strains. These nanoparticles exhibit high bactericidal and fungicidal efficiency at nanogram concentrations, effectively limiting biofilm formation on medical device surfaces.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), UV-Vis spectroscopy, zeta potential measurements, colony counting assays, and MIC/MBC/MBIC measurements to evaluate the antimicrobial activity of gold nanoparticles.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Sequence Analysis of Methicillin- and Carbapenem-Resistant Bacteria Isolated from Raw Sewage.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antibiotic resistance genes in methicillin- and carbapenem-resistant bacteria isolated from raw sewage, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant Bacillus strains carrying resistance genes for beta-lactams, fosfomycin, mupirocin, and vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of 100 bacterial isolates from wastewater treatment plants was used to characterize antibiotic resistance genes and their distribution.

full_output.paper_title: Peptides Affecting the Outer Membrane Lipid Asymmetry System (MlaA-OmpC/F) Reduce Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) Colonization in Chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies peptides that affect the MlaA-OmpC/F system in APEC, reducing its colonization in chickens. These peptides downregulate the expression of ompC, ompF, and mlaA genes, which are involved in maintaining outer membrane lipid asymmetry.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression analysis, bacterial cytological profiling, and immunoblotting were used to determine the effect of peptides on APEC.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Synergy Testing of Eravacycline in Combination with Clarithromycin and Rifabutin against Mycobacterium abscessus Complex.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the in vitro synergy of eravacycline with clarithromycin and rifabutin against Mycobacterium abscessus complex. The erm41 gene was identified as a key factor in clarithromycin susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Checkerboard testing was performed to assess synergy between eravacycline and other antibiotics against MabsC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of antibiotic susceptibilities of Brucella Strains isolated from various clinical samples in eastern Turkey.
full_output.key_findings: All Brucella strains were identified as B. melitensis. DOX, STR, CIP, and RIF were found to be effective against Brucella strains, with CIP showing the highest efficacy.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility was determined using the E test method.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting Antibacterial Effect and Promoting of Skin Wound Healing After Infected with Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus for the Novel Polyvinyl Alcohol Nanoparticles.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that BZK-loaded nanoparticles exhibit significant antibacterial activity against MRSA, both in vitro and in vivo, with improved biofilm disruption and wound healing properties compared to BZK aqueous solutions.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of BZK-loaded nanoparticles through in vitro MIC/MBC assays, biofilm disruption experiments, and in vivo wound healing models in mice.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a Potent Antimicrobial Peptide With Photodynamic Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development of a novel antimicrobial peptide, PcG3K5(RW)3, which exhibits potent antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including multidrug-resistant strains, when activated by red light.
full_output.methodology: The peptide was synthesized and characterized, and its antimicrobial activity was assessed using bioluminescent bacteria and standard bacterial strains, with evaluations of MIC, bactericidal kinetics, and photo-assisted antimicrobial effects.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the lsa(E) gene, which confers resistance to pleuromutilins, lincosamides, and streptogramin A, on a conjugative MDR plasmid pN7435-R3645. full_output.paper_title: Photoactive Silver Nanoagents for Backgroundless Monitoring and Precision Killing of Multidrug-Resistant Bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiology of methicillin-resistant and -susceptible Staphylococcus aureus from bloodstream infections.

full_output.paper_title: Peritoneal dialysis-related peritonitis caused by gram-negative organisms: ten-years experience in a single center.

full_output.paper_title: Reversing Antibiotic Resistance Caused by Mobile Resistance Genes of High Fitness Cost.

full_output.paper_title: Unacceptable Antibiotic Resistance Rates for Helicobacter pylori in Turkey: Something Must Change.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of the Staphylococcus aureus CA-MRSA USA300 in Belgium.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the epidemiology of Staphylococcus aureus CA-MRSA USA300 in Belgium, highlighting the presence of specific mutations in grlA and gyrA that confer resistance to ciprofloxacin, as well as the presence of acquired resistance genes such as mphC, msrA, and aph(3')-III that confer resistance to erythromycin and kanamycin.

full_output.paper_title: Long-read sequencing revealed cooccurrence, host range, and potential mobility of antibiotic resistome in cow feces.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in cow feces using long-read sequencing, revealing their cooccurrence, host range, and potential mobility. Key findings include the prevalence of multidrug resistance genes, the presence of specific ARGs like bla, erm, mph, lnu, tetM, tetL, tetA, APH, ANT, aac, qnrB, CTX-M, TEM, CMY, CARB, sul, dfr, ermB, mphA, ermA, ermC, ermF, ermX, mefA, mefE, lsa, vat, vgb, cat, cfr, optrA, poxtA, vanA, vanB, vanC, mcr, fos, acrAB, mexAB-OprM, and oqxAB, along with their associations with plasmids and mobile genetic elements.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized long-read sequencing (Nanopore and PacBio) to analyze the antibiotic resistome in cow feces, focusing on gene location, host range, and mobility. It involved sample enrichment with antibiotics, DNA extraction, sequencing, and bioinformatic analysis to identify and characterize ARGs.

full_output.paper_title: Prodigiosin inhibits bacterial growth and virulence factors as a potential physiological response to interspecies competition.
full_output.key_findings: Prodigiosin, a red tripyrrole pigment produced by Serratia marcescens, exhibits antimicrobial activity against several pathogenic bacteria, including MRSA, S. aureus, E. faecalis, and E. coli, but not against P. aeruginosa or S. Typhimurium. It inhibits protease activity and biofilm formation in some bacteria but does not affect hemolysis.

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin resistant Enterococci and its associated factors among HIV infected patients on anti-retroviral therapy in Ethiopia.

The study also identified factors associated with VRE colonization, including prior antibiotic exposure for more than two weeks and hospitalization for more than six months.

full_output.paper_title: Addressing the Antimicrobial Resistance of Ruminant Mycoplasmas Using a Clinical Surveillance Network.

full_output.paper_title: Modulatory Effects of Caffeine and Pentoxifylline on Aromatic Antibiotics: A Role for Hetero-Complex Formation.

full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the application of CRISPR-Cas systems in combating antimicrobial resistance in ESKAPE pathogens, focusing on gene editing strategies to target drug resistance and virulence genes.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature on CRISPR-Cas applications in treating ESKAPE infections.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Metagenomic Analysis of Chicken Gut Microbial Community, Function, and Resistome to Evaluate Noninvasive and Cecal Sampling Resources.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in chicken gut microbiota, including tetracycline, aminoglycoside, macrolide, lincomycin, chloramphenicol, valnemulin, and florfenicol resistance genes. The abundance of these ARGs varied depending on the sampling site, with fecal samples showing higher levels of certain ARGs compared to cecal and cloacal samples.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and analysis of microbial communities from fecal, cloacal, and cecal samples of broiler chickens.

full_output.paper_title: The Molecular Basis for Escherichia coli O157:H7 Phage FAHEc1 Endolysin Function and Protein Engineering to Increase Thermal Stability.

LysF1.evidence_note: The paper describes the characterization of LysF1, an endolysin from Escherichia coli O157:H7 phage FAHEc1, and its mutations. The mutations were studied for their effects on thermal stability and activity. The organisms observed include Escherichia coli, Salmonella typhimurium, and Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the endolysin LysF1 from Escherichia coli O157:H7 phage FAHEc1, identifies its structural and functional properties, and demonstrates that mutations in the hydrophobic core can improve its thermal stability and activity.
full_output.methodology: Structural and functional characterization of LysF1, including x-ray crystallography, mutagenesis, and activity assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a new variant of the New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase (NDM-29) in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, which confers resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and functional analysis of blaNDM-29 in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Core-Shell Capsules for Bacteriophage T3 Protection Against Acid and Thermal Stress
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that core-shell capsules effectively protect bacteriophage T3 from acid and thermal stress, enhancing its stability during animal feed processing and gastrointestinal transit.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a concentric nozzle encapsulator to produce core-shell capsules with T3 phages, assessing their stability under various acid and thermal conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Engineering of the CHAPk Staphylococcal Phage Endolysin to Enhance Antibacterial Activity against Stationary-Phase Cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the creation of a chimeric enzyme, CHAPk-SH3blys, by fusing the CHAPk endolysin with the SH3b cell-binding domain of lysostaphin, enhancing antibacterial activity against stationary-phase Staphylococcus aureus cells.
full_output.methodology: The study involved cloning, expression, and purification of recombinant enzymes, followed by evaluation of their lytic activity through turbidity reduction assays, colony plate counts, and MIC assays.

full_output.paper_title: Cheminformatic Profiling and Hit Prioritization of Natural Products with Activities against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on cheminformatics profiling of 111 natural products (NPs) with anti-MRSA activity, highlighting their drug-like properties and potential for optimization.
full_output.methodology: Cheminformatics profiling, structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis, and hit prioritization strategies were used to evaluate the drug-likeness and potential of the NPs.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Detection of Carbapenemases in Enterobacterales: A Comparison of Real-Time Multiplex PCR and Whole-Genome Sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study compares the performance of WGS and RT-qPCR for detecting carbapenemase genes in Enterobacterales, identifying blaNDM-1, blaKPC-2, blaVIM-1, and blaOXA-48 as the most prevalent carbapenemases.
full_output.methodology: The study used WGS, RT-qPCR, and the carbapenem inactivation method (CIM) to analyze 92 carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The Composites of PCL and Tetranuclear Titanium(IV)-oxo Complexes as Materials Exhibiting the Photocatalytic and the Antimicrobial Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antimicrobial and photocatalytic properties of PCL composites containing tetranuclear titanium(IV)-oxo complexes (TOCs). The composites showed significant antimicrobial activity against bacteria and fungi, particularly PCL + 20(2) with 9-fluorenocarboxylic stabilized ligand.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of TOCs and their integration into PCL matrices, followed by evaluation of photocatalytic and antimicrobial activities through various analytical techniques.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of integron genes (intI1, intI2) and extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes (bla TEM, bla CTX-M) in Proteus mirabilis isolates from catheters. full_output.paper_title: Determination of the frequency, species distribution and antimicrobial resistance of staphylococci isolated from dogs and their owners in Trinidad.

full_output.methodology: Staphylococci were isolated from dogs and their owners, identified using MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and tested for antimicrobial susceptibility using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Development of High-Level Daptomycin Resistance in Abiotrophia and Granulicatella Species Isolates from Patients with Infective Endocarditis.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the rapid development of high-level daptomycin resistance (HLDR) in Abiotrophia and Granulicatella species isolates from patients with infective endocarditis. HLDR was observed in 33% of A. defectiva and 78% of G. adiacens isolates after exposure to daptomycin, and the resistance was stable over time in G. adiacens but reversible in A. defectiva.
full_output.methodology: In vitro susceptibility testing, time-kill studies, and resistance screening were performed to evaluate daptomycin resistance in Abiotrophia and Granulicatella species isolates.

full_output.methodology: Cloning of β-lactamase genes into E. coli and susceptibility testing of the resulting strains.

full_output.paper_title: Wet-dry cycles protect surface-colonizing bacteria from major antibiotic classes.

full_output.methodology: Experiments and computational modeling were used to study bacterial response to antibiotics under wet-dry cycles with microscopic surface wetness (MSW).

tetB.genetic_context: Tn5432 flanked by two IS1249 elements transports the erm(X) gene (in green) to its corresponding right, region II of the pTP10 plasmid of C. striatum that contains the tetA/tetB genes (in light blue)
tetB.evidence_note: The presence of region II, the erm(X) gene, and ISCx1 in these studies suggests that in addition to resistance to lincosamides and macrolides, Tn5432 confers tetracycline resistance, which a past recombination event could have triggered.

tet(W).validation_method: genomic context and association with resistance mechanisms
tet(W).genetic_context: flanked by IS3504 element, close to the erm(X) gene
tet(W).evidence_note: The tet(W) gene product eliminates the inhibitory effect of tetracycline on protein synthesis through the non-covalent modification of the ribosomes. The gene is not transported by pTP10, suggesting another recombination event beyond pTP10 (or this plasmid acquired this gene in later events). It has been reported that IS3504 carried the tet(W) gene in isolates from the USA [16], but it could also be transported by IS3503 and IS3502 [33]. According to the ISfinder database [67], both IS3503 and IS3502 are part of C. jeikeium, and it has been transported to its plasmids and to C. urealyticum. On the other hand, IS3504 was described in the pNG2 plasmid of C. diphtheria [35] and the pJA144188 plasmid of C. resistens [42]. The tet(W) gene was first described for corynebacteria in plasmid pJA144188 of C. resistens. The gene was described in a genomic context similar to how it presents in C. striatum, with a close IS3504 element, as the studies by Nudel et al. (2018) [16] described it, and close to the erm(X) gene as was found in the studies by Wang et al., 2019 [33].

However, one isolate was found to have a D429V mutation in GyrB, which may be associated with zoliflodacin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Outer membrane permeability: Antimicrobials and diverse nutrients bypass porins in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that porins in Pseudomonas aeruginosa are not essential for the translocation of most antimicrobials and that hydrophilic compounds can permeate the outer membrane independently of porins. However, nutrients with multiple carboxylate groups require porins for efficient uptake.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic mutants, NMR spectroscopy, and antimicrobial susceptibility assays to investigate the role of porins in nutrient and antimicrobial translocation.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of the Rv3065, Rv2942, Rv1258c, Rv1410c, and Rv2459 efflux pump genes expression among multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified overexpression of Rv3065, Rv1410c, Rv1258c, Rv2459, and Rv2942 efflux pump genes in multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates, contributing to resistance against isoniazid and rifampin. full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR, DNA sequencing, and drug susceptibility testing were used to analyze efflux pump gene expression and mutations in MDR-TB isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence, distribution and pattern analysis of methicillin resistant (MRSA) and methicillin sensitive (MSSA) Staphylococcus aureus on fomites in public facilities.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and methicillin-sensitive S. aureus (MSSA) on various fomites in public facilities in northern Jordan. MRSA was found to be more prevalent on toilet door handles, student desks, and washrooms. The study also noted that MRSA isolates exhibited higher multidrug resistance compared to MSSA isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting swabs from various fomites, isolating S. aureus, and performing PCR to detect the mecA gene for MRSA identification. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibitory Compounds Targeting Plasmodium falciparum Gyrase B.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and risk factors for antimicrobial resistance among newborns with gram-negative sepsis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of antimicrobial resistance among gram-negative bacteria causing sepsis in newborns, particularly to ampicillin, gentamicin, and third-generation cephalosporins. Multidrug resistance was prevalent, with 88% of isolates showing resistance to multiple antibiotic classes.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed blood cultures from newborns with sepsis, using antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequencing to identify resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence characterization and clonal analysis of uropathogenic Escherichia coli metallo-beta-lactamase-producing isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence of an epidemic spread of KPC-producing Enterobacterales in Czech hospitals.

full_output.paper_title: Changing characteristics of S. aureus bacteremia caused by PVL-negative, MRSA strain over 11 years.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the resistance rate to erythromycin in ST72 MRSA decreased significantly over 11 years, and the vancomycin MIC also decreased. The incidence of ST72 MRSA bacteremia increased annually.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel IncC-IncX3 hybrid plasmid, pNUITM-VK5_mdr, which carries the carbapenemase gene bla(NDM-4), the tigecycline-inactivating enzyme gene tet(X), and the RND efflux pump gene tmexCD3-toprJ3, contributing to high-level resistance against multiple antimicrobials including carbapenems and tigecycline.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of Virulence and Antimicrobial Resistance Gene Carriage in Staphylococcus aureus Infections in Equids Using Whole-Genome Sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Silver Nanoparticles Using Eucalyptus or Willow Extracts (AgNPs) as Contact Lens Hydrogel Components to Reduce the Risk of Microbial Infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial potential of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesized using eucalyptus leaves (ELE) and willow bark (WBE) extracts, incorporated into pHEMA hydrogels. AgNPs(ELE) showed significant antimicrobial activity against P. aeruginosa, S. epidermidis, and S. aureus, with inhibition zones of 15.2, 17.0, and 15.2 mm, respectively. The materials pHEMA@AgNPs(ELE)_2 and pHEMA@AgNPs(WBE)_2 demonstrated reduced bacterial viability, with 28.3% and 6.8% for P. aeruginosa and S. epidermidis, respectively. The study highlights the effectiveness of AgNPs in reducing microbial infection risks in contact lenses.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar disc-diffusion method, XRF, XRPD, TG-DTA, DTG/DSC, ATR-FTIR, and UV-vis spectroscopy to characterize the materials. Antimicrobial activity was assessed against P. aeruginosa, S. epidermidis, and S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis of 3,5-Bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl-Substituted Pyrazole Derivatives as Potent Growth Inhibitors of Drug-Resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and antimicrobial evaluation of 30 novel pyrazole derivatives, which exhibit potent growth inhibition against drug-resistant bacteria, including MRSA and Enterococcus faecium. Compounds 11, 28, and 29 showed strong activity against S. aureus and E. faecalis biofilms, with minimum biofilm eradication concentrations (MBEC) as low as 1 µg/mL.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and evaluated for antimicrobial activity using microdilution techniques, cytotoxicity assays, time-kill assays, and biofilm eradication tests.

full_output.paper_title: Interest of Homodialkyl Neamine Derivatives against Resistant P. aeruginosa, E. coli, and β-Lactamases-Producing Bacteria-Effect of Alkyl Chain Length on the Interaction with LPS.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 3′,6-dinonyl neamine and 3′,6-di(dimethyloctyl) neamine as effective against resistant P. aeruginosa, E. coli, and β-lactamase-producing bacteria, showing low MIC values and potential as novel antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: MIC determination, BODIPY-TR-cadaverine displacement assay, and membrane permeabilization assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Peptides from Plants: A cDNA-Library Based Isolation, Purification, Characterization Approach and Elucidating Their Modes of Action.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a cDNA-library based approach for isolating, purifying, and characterizing antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) from plants using the Bacillus subtilis expression system. It highlights the importance of AMPs in plant immunity and their potential applications in agriculture.
full_output.methodology: The study utilizes a cDNA library constructed in the Bacillus subtilis expression system to isolate and characterize plant-derived antimicrobial peptides. Techniques such as Sanger sequencing, bioinformatics analysis, and purification methods like His-tag affinity chromatography were employed.

AWME3 shows dose-dependent bactericidal effects and enhances antimicrobial activity through sequential extraction.

full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of physicochemical properties, mechanisms of action, and resistance profiles of quinolone antibiotics.

full_output.methodology: PCR, phenotypic testing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to detect and characterize the CTX-M-15 gene and the O25-ST131 clone in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance and Virulence Genes of Escherichia coli Isolated from Patients with Urinary Tract Infections After Kidney Transplantation from Deceased Donors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance and numerous virulence genes in E. coli strains isolated from patients with urinary tract infections after kidney transplantation from deceased donors, with particular emphasis on hospital-acquired E. coli strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes and antibiotic susceptibility testing via the Kirby-Bauer method.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors for microbiologic failure in children with Enterobacter species bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies risk factors for microbiologic failure in children with Enterobacter species bacteremia, highlighting the importance of source control and the rarity of resistance development to third-generation cephalosporins (3GCs) during therapy.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective case-control study analyzing patients with Enterobacter species bacteremia, focusing on microbiologic failure and resistance development.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the dynamic behavior of hydrophobic nodes in class A β-lactamases, including KPC-2, SHV-1, TEM-1, and SME-1, revealing their roles in structural dynamics and resistance mechanisms against β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Adaptive sampling molecular dynamics simulations, Markov State Models, and structural analysis were used to investigate the dynamics of hydrophobic nodes in class A β-lactamases.

full_output.paper_title: Shewanella putrefaciens: A cause of bacteremia not to neglect.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first case of multidrug-resistant Shewanella putrefaciens bacteremia in Morocco, highlighting its resistance to multiple antibiotics except amikacin, colistin, polymyxin B, doxycycline, and tigecycline.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Upregulation of abeM, amvA, and qacEΔ1 efflux pump genes associated with resistance of Acinetobacter baumannii strains to disinfectants.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that upregulation of abeM, amvA, and qacEΔ1 efflux pump genes is associated with resistance of Acinetobacter baumannii strains to disinfectants such as MICROZED ID-MAX, NANOSIL D2, and OPIDEX OPA.
full_output.methodology: Real-time reverse transcriptase-PCR was used to investigate the expression levels of qacEΔ1, amvA, abeM, and adeB efflux pump genes in A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo Selection of Imipenem Resistance Among Ceftazidime-Avibactam-Resistant, Imipenem-Susceptible Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolate With KPC-33 Carbapenemase.

blaKPC-33.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the in vivo evolution of KPC-2 to KPC-33 and back to KPC-2 in Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting the dynamic nature of resistance mediated by bla KPC genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and population analysis profiling were used to analyze the resistance dynamics.

full_output.paper_title: Trend Analysis of Multidrug-Resistant Bacterial Pathogens Causing Neonatal Sepsis at University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia: A Retrospective Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens causing neonatal sepsis, with high resistance rates to commonly prescribed antibiotics. Key findings include high resistance levels in Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of bacterial isolates from neonatal blood cultures, including antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of Carbapenemase-Resistant Genotypes of Highly Virulent Klebsiella pneumoniae and Clinical Infection Characteristics of Different MLST Types.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified KPC, IMP, VIM, and NDM carbapenemase genes in 74 CR-KP strains, with KPC being the most prevalent. ST11 was the dominant MLST type and was associated with higher resistance to carbapenems and poorer patient outcomes.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection and DNA sequencing of carbapenemase genes, MLST typing, and drug susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptional and translational landscape of Candida auris in response to caspofungin.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that caspofungin induces significant morphological and transcriptomic changes in Candida auris, including upregulation of genes involved in cell wall synthesis and ribosome biogenesis, as well as alterations in cell wall composition.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RNA sequencing, quantitative RT-PCR, and proteomic analysis to investigate the cellular response of Candida auris to caspofungin treatment.

full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing, time-kill kinetic analysis, and CRISPR interference were used to identify and validate AMR genes in Mycobacterium abscessus.

full_output.paper_title: Newly identified parasitic nematode beta-tubulin alleles confer resistance to benzimidazoles.
full_output.key_findings: Four newly identified parasitic nematode beta-tubulin alleles (E198I, E198K, E198T, and E198stop) confer resistance to benzimidazoles in C. elegans.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing and high-throughput assays were used to introduce and test the resistance conferred by the beta-tubulin alleles.

full_output.paper_title: Na(+)-Coupled Respiration and Reshaping of Extracellular Polysaccharide Layer Counteract Monensin-Induced Cation Permeability in Prevotella bryantii B(1)4.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the Na+-translocating NADH:quinone oxidoreductase (NQR) and other sodium transport proteins as key players in counteracting monensin-induced cation permeability in Prevotella bryantii B14. It also highlights the role of the sodium/glucose cotransporter (D8DYQ7), Na+/H+ antiporter NhaD (D8DYG5), phosphate Na+-symporter (A0A1H9BJD7), and the YghO protein (D8DVZ9) in adapting to monensin stress.
full_output.methodology: The study employed proteomic analysis, enzyme activity measurements, and fluorescence microscopy to investigate the molecular mechanisms of monensin resistance in Prevotella bryantii B14.

full_output.key_findings: The study compared the metabolisms of two P. aeruginosa strains, revealing differences in amino acid metabolism and other metabolites that may relate to antibiotic resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Metabolomics analysis using 1H NMR spectroscopy combined with multivariate and univariate data analysis.

full_output.paper_title: An ArsR Transcriptional Regulator Facilitates Brucella sp. Survival via Regulating Self and Outer Membrane Protein.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ArsR6 as a transcriptional regulator involved in Brucella survival under stress conditions and during infection. It also shows that ArsR6 directly regulates the expression of omp25D, an outer membrane protein critical for Brucella virulence.
full_output.methodology: The research combined RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, EMSA, and mutagenesis approaches to investigate the role of ArsR6 in Brucella.

full_output.paper_title: TmSpz-like Plays a Fundamental Role in Response to E. coli but Not S. aureus or C. albican Infection in Tenebrio molitor via Regulation of Antimicrobial Peptide Production.
full_output.key_findings: TmSpz-like is crucial for the regulation of antimicrobial peptide (AMP) production in Tenebrio molitor larvae during E. coli infection, and its knockdown leads to reduced viability of E. coli-infected larvae.
full_output.methodology: Molecular cloning, qRT-PCR, and RNA interference experiments were conducted to analyze the expression and function of TmSpz-like.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity of Gemini Surfactants with Ether Group in the Spacer Part.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents the synthesis and evaluation of gemini surfactants with an ether group in the spacer part, demonstrating their antimicrobial activity against various microorganisms including bacteria, yeast, and molds.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of gemini surfactants, analytical methods including NMR, FTIR, and elemental analysis, and determination of antimicrobial activity via MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Membrane Transporters Involved in the Antimicrobial Activities of Pyrithione in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CopA, FepC, MetQ, and ZntA as membrane transporters involved in the uptake and efflux of pyrithione in E. coli, highlighting their roles in mediating pyrithione's antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening of E. coli Keio knockout strains, growth inhibition assays, and metal concentration measurements.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity of Biosynthesized Selenium Nanoparticles Using Extracts of Calendula officinalis against Potentially Clinical Bacterial Strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antibacterial activity of selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) synthesized using Calendula officinalis extracts against Serratia marcescens, Enterobacter cloacae, and Alcaligenes faecalis. SeNPs showed significant antibacterial effects, with complete inhibition of bacterial growth within specific time frames.
full_output.methodology: The antibacterial activity of SeNPs was assessed using disk diffusion and colony-forming unit (CFU) count methods against selected bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Unravelling the collateral damage of antibiotics on gut bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the effects of antibiotics on gut bacteria, identifying specific antibiotic classes that inhibit or kill commensal species, and screens for drugs that protect Bacteroides species from macrolide and tetracycline-induced harm.
full_output.methodology: The study uses MIC testing, growth curves, and high-throughput screening to assess antibiotic effects on gut bacteria and identify protective compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Predicting drug targets by homology modelling of Pseudomonas aeruginosa proteins of unknown function.
full_output.key_findings: The study predicts potential drug targets in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by analyzing proteins of unknown function using homology modelling. It identifies 41 potential drug targets, including enzymes, ligand-binding proteins, and transporters, which are involved in essential cellular processes, virulence, and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Homology modelling was used to predict the biochemical functions of Pseudomonas aeruginosa proteins of unknown function. The study integrated comparative sequence analysis and structural homology-based functional prediction.

full_output.paper_title: Ultrastructural changes in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) induced by metabolites of thermophilous fungi Acrophialophora levis.
full_output.key_findings: The ethyl acetate extract of Acrophialophora levis showed significant antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and MRSA, with MIC values of 1 μg/mL and 4 μg/mL, respectively. The extract caused cell wall disruption, membrane lysis, and cytoplasmic leakage in treated cells.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was assessed using agar well-diffusion and microdilution assays. SEM was used to observe structural changes in treated cells.

full_output.paper_title: Thinopyrum intermedium TiAP1 interacts with a chitin deacetylase from Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici and increases the resistance to Bgt in wheat.
full_output.key_findings: TiAP1, an aspartic protease from Thinopyrum intermedium, interacts with BgtCDA1, a chitin deacetylase from Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici, enhancing wheat resistance to Bgt. Silencing BgtCDA1 reduces Bgt invasion, and TiAP1 overexpression increases resistance in transgenic wheat.
full_output.methodology: Yeast two-hybrid, luciferase complementation imaging, bimolecular fluorescence complementary analysis, VIGS, transgenic wheat, HIGS, and qRT-PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Emergent Biological Endurance Depends on Extracellular Matrix Composition of Three-Dimensionally Printed Escherichia coli Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that 3D-printed biofilms of Escherichia coli expressing curli and/or cellulose exhibit increased resistance to disinfectants such as ethanol and Virkon S compared to those without these matrix components.
full_output.methodology: 3D printing of E. coli biofilms with different extracellular matrix compositions and assessment of their resistance to disinfectants.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the binding of vaborbactam to Pseudomonas aeruginosa PBP3, revealing that vaborbactam covalently binds to the catalytic S294 and forms various hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions within the active site of PBP3.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, biochemical assays, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze vaborbactam binding to PBP3.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of incidence and risk factors of the multidrug resistant gastrointestinal tract infection in children and adolescents undergoing allogeneic and autologous hematopoietic cell transplantation: a nationwide study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the incidence and risk factors for multidrug-resistant gastrointestinal tract infections (MDR GTI) in children undergoing hematopoietic cell transplantation, highlighting the prevalence of Clostridium difficile, extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacteriaceae, and high-level aminoglycoside-resistant Enterococcus.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance in colonizing group B Streptococcus among pregnant women from a hospital in Vietnam.

Multidrug resistance was also prevalent, with 60.66% of isolates showing resistance to at least three antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug Resistance Dynamics in Salmonella in Food Animals in the United States: An Analysis of Genomes from Public Databases.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed 22,102 Salmonella genomes from public databases to track antimicrobial resistance (AMR) trends in food animals in the United States. It found that the prevalence of multidrug resistance (MDR) decreased in bovines and swine but increased in poultry. Key AMR genes identified include bla CMY-2, bla CTX-M-65, floR, tetA, sul2, aadA2, aac(3)-VIa, qnrB19, qnrB2, bla SHV-12, bla TEM-1, bla CARB-2, aph(3")-Ib, aph(6)-Id, aph(3')-Ia, ant(3")-Ia, aph(4)-Ia, and aac(3)-IVa. A significant mutation, gyrA D87Y, was associated with quinolone resistance in poultry.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of publicly available Salmonella genomes to identify AMR genes and mutations.

Additionally, the study noted changes in antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, including reduced susceptibility of certain bacteria to specific antibiotics during the prophylaxis period.
full_output.methodology: The study was a single-center, observational cohort study analyzing data from pediatric AML patients receiving antimicrobial prophylaxis. It compared infection rates, antimicrobial exposure, and susceptibility profiles between preprophylaxis and prophylaxis periods.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic mutants, biochemical assays, and an experimental endocarditis model to investigate the role of purF and dacA in MRSA persistence.

full_output.paper_title: Practical approach to detection and surveillance of emerging highly resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis Beijing 1071-32-cluster.

Rv0373c.evidence_note: The paper mentions that Rv0373c has a synonymous mutation (C>T) at position 451510, which is part of the Beijing 1071-32-cluster specific SNPs. The mutation was detected using real-time PCR and is associated with the cluster.

katG.notes: Mutation in katG

rpoB.notes: Mutation in rpoB

embB.notes: Mutation in embB

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three synonymous SNPs in Rv0144, Rv0373c, and Rv0334 that are specific to the Beijing 1071-32-cluster. Additionally, six drug resistance mutations in katG, rpoB, rpoC, embB, and rpsL are associated with multidrug resistance in this cluster.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, real-time PCR, and molecular assays were used to identify SNPs and drug resistance mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic and Phenotypic Characterizations of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) on Frequently Touched Sites from Public Hospitals in South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes including tetM, tetK, ermC, blaZ, aac(6')-aph(2"), mecA, hld, and LukS/F-PV in MRSA isolates from public hospitals in South Africa.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and resistance profiles in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: An updated M. tuberculosis reference genome functional annotation
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a systematic approach to updating functional annotations of Mycobacterium tuberculosis genes using literature curation and structural modeling, revealing novel functions for numerous underannotated genes, including potential roles in drug resistance, metabolism, and virulence.
full_output.methodology: The study employed literature curation, structural modeling via I-TASSER, and validation through HHpred to infer and verify gene functions.

full_output.paper_title: The Two-Component System RstA/RstB Regulates Expression of Multiple Efflux Pumps and Influences Anaerobic Nitrate Respiration in Pseudomonas fluorescens.

rstA.notes: Phosphorylation of Asp52 is crucial for RstA function.
rstA.evidence_note: Experimental validation of mutations in RstA shows increased susceptibility to multiple antibiotics, indicating that phosphorylation of Asp52 is essential for RstA function.

full_output.key_findings: The TCS RstA/RstB regulates multiple efflux pumps (EmhABC and MexCD-OprJ) and contributes to antibiotic resistance in Pseudomonas fluorescens 2P24. Phosphorylation of RstA at Asp52 is essential for its DNA-binding activity and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Deletion mutants, MIC testing, qRT-PCR, EMSA, and proteomic analysis were used to validate the role of RstA/RstB in antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Maximum levels of cross-contamination for 24 antimicrobial active substances in non-target feed. Part 9: Polymyxins: colistin.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the resistance mechanisms of colistin, focusing on modifications of the LPS moiety, loss of LPS, porin mutations, and overexpression of efflux pumps. It also highlights the mcr-1 gene as a plasmid-mediated gene responsible for horizontal transfer of colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and data on colistin resistance mechanisms and its effects on bacterial resistance and growth promotion in food-producing animals.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance of Escherichia coli in broiler chickens, farmworkers, and farm sewage in Bangladesh.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of antimicrobial resistance in E. coli isolates from broiler chickens, farmworkers, and farm sewage in Bangladesh, with resistance to levofloxacin, doxycycline, cefotaxime, and ciprofloxacin being particularly prevalent. No isolates were found to carry the NDM-1 carbapenem resistance gene.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and identification of E. coli from 150 samples, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing and PCR-based detection of the NDM-1 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of NDM-1-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from hospitalized patients in Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaNDM-1, blaVIM-2, blaIMP-1, blaSPM, and blaOXA-10 as prevalent carbapenem resistance genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Iran, highlighting the complexity of resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: PCR, phenotypic testing, and DLST typing were used to characterize resistance genes and clonal relationships.

full_output.paper_title: Boosting Synergistic Effects of Short Antimicrobial Peptides With Conventional Antibiotics Against Resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that Nal-tagged antimicrobial peptides enhance the synergistic effects of conventional antibiotics against antibiotic-resistant bacteria, reducing lipopolysaccharide release and improving antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study used microbroth dilution, checkerboard assays, and fluorescence microscopy to assess antimicrobial activity and synergistic effects.

full_output.paper_title: Monitoring the Microevolution of Salmonella enterica in Healthy Dairy Cattle Populations at the Individual Farm Level Using Whole-Genome Sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes, including bla CMY-2, floR, sul2, and tetA, in Salmonella enterica isolates from dairy cattle. These genes confer resistance to various antibiotics such as cephalosporins, florfenicol, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in silico AMR determinant detection using multiple tools and databases.

full_output.key_findings: The paper highlights the prevalence of antibiotic resistance genes such as bla NDM-1, bla OXA-48, bla CTX-M, mcr-1, and mcr-2 in various pathogens in India, emphasizing their role in the spread of multidrug-resistant organisms.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of existing studies on antimicrobial resistance in India.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm formation and antibiotic susceptibility of Staphylococcus and Bacillus species isolated from human allogeneic skin.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the biofilm formation and antibiotic susceptibility of Staphylococcus and Bacillus species isolated from human allogeneic skin, highlighting the increased antibiotic tolerance of biofilm-forming bacteria compared to planktonic forms.
full_output.methodology: The study used crystal violet staining for biofilm quantification and broth microdilution with resazurin dye for determining MIC, MBIC, and MBEC values.

full_output.paper_title: Integration of metabolomics and transcriptomics indicates changes in MRSA exposed to terpinen-4-ol.
full_output.key_findings: Terpinen-4-ol exhibits antibacterial activity against MRSA and significantly inhibits biofilm formation by targeting purine and pyrimidine metabolism.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomics and metabolomics analyses were used to investigate the effects of terpinen-4-ol on MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriological profile, antibiotic susceptibility and factors associated with neonatal Septicaemia at Kilembe mines hospital, Kasese District Western Uganda.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant organisms causing neonatal septicaemia, highlighting the importance of antibiotic susceptibility testing and prudent antibiotic use.
full_output.methodology: Blood cultures, Gram staining, and Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method were used to determine bacterial isolates and their antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Changing microbiological profile and antimicrobial susceptibility of the isolates obtained from patients with infective endocarditis - The time to relook into the therapeutic guidelines.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Staphylococcus aureus was the predominant pathogen in infective endocarditis, with 90.2% of isolates being MRSA. Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates were 100% susceptible to carbapenems but showed variable resistance to other antimicrobials. All Enterococci were 100% susceptible to linezolid and daptomycin, but 25% were vancomycin-resistant. No AMR genes were experimentally validated in this study.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 66 isolates from patients with infective endocarditis, using CLSI 2017 guidelines for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Serum apolipoprotein A-I potentiates the therapeutic efficacy of lysocin E against Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA-I) and ApoA-II enhance the antimicrobial activity of lysocin E against Staphylococcus aureus. The study shows that ApoA-I and ApoA-II mediate the interaction of lysocin E with lipid II, leading to increased membrane disruption and bactericidal activity.
full_output.methodology: Microdilution assay, protein purification, genetic knockout experiments, and membrane potential measurements.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection in heterosexual men with reduced susceptibility to ceftriaxone, first report in Thailand.

full_output.paper_title: Novel colistin-EDTA combination for successful eradication of colistin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae catheter-related biofilm infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that a novel colistin-EDTA combination effectively reverses colistin resistance and eradicates catheter-related biofilm infections caused by colistin-resistant K. pneumoniae, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic strategy.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the synergistic activity of colistin and EDTA against colistin-resistant K. pneumoniae using in vitro and in vivo models, including time-kill assays, biofilm eradication tests, and animal infection models.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence of toxic metals and their selective pressure for antibiotic-resistant clinically relevant bacteria and antibiotic-resistant genes in river receiving systems under tropical conditions.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) and antibiotic-resistance genes (ARGs) in river systems receiving urban and hospital effluents in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It highlighted the correlation between heavy metal contamination and the prevalence of ARB and ARGs, emphasizing the need for improved waste management to mitigate environmental and public health risks.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed metal concentrations, ARB, and ARGs in water and sediment samples from two river systems using physicochemical measurements, microbial cultivation, and qPCR techniques.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses allogenous selection, where old antibiotics select for resistance to newer ones within the same family. It highlights the role of beta-lactamases like bla TEM-1, bla SHV-1, and CTX-M in expanding resistance to cephalosporins. Tetracycline resistance genes such as tet(M), tet(K), and tet(X) are noted for increasing resistance to newer tetracyclines. Quinolone resistance proteins like qnrB and qnrS1 contribute to resistance against fluoroquinolones. Macrolide resistance genes like ermB and efflux pumps like mexAB-OprM and acrAB-TolC are also identified as key players in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews experimental and computational studies on antibiotic resistance mechanisms, focusing on the evolution of resistance genes and mutations under selective pressures from different antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiological Species and Antibiotic Resistance in Diabetic and Nondiabetic Lower Extremity Wounds: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Gram-negative microorganisms, especially Enterobacteriaceae, were predominant in both diabetic and nondiabetic lower extremity wounds. Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing bacteria and carbapenem-resistant isolates were identified, but no significant differences in antibiotic resistance profiles were observed between diabetic and nondiabetic patients.
full_output.methodology: The study involved culturing tissue samples from 111 patients with lower extremity wounds, identifying microbial species, and assessing antibiotic resistance using automated systems.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial profile of high-touch surfaces, leftover drugs and antiseptics together with their antimicrobial susceptibility patterns at University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various bacterial isolates from high-touch surfaces, leftover drugs, and 80% ethanol, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant strains, including coagulase-negative Staphylococci (CoNS), Staphylococcus aureus, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Resistance to several antibiotics was observed, emphasizing the need for improved infection control measures.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting samples from high-touch surfaces, leftover drugs, and 80% ethanol, followed by bacterial isolation and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Polymerization of C9 enhances bacterial cell envelope damage and killing by membrane attack complex pores.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that polymerization of C9 enhances bacterial cell envelope damage and killing by MAC pores, and that a C9 TMH-1 lock mutant impairs C9 polymerization without affecting binding to C5b-8.
full_output.methodology: Flow cytometry, SDS-PAGE, and bacterial viability assays were used to assess the impact of C9 polymerization on bacterial cell envelope damage and killing.

full_output.paper_title: Optimization of five qPCR protocols toward the detection and the quantification of antimicrobial resistance genes in environmental samples.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents optimized qPCR protocols for detecting and quantifying five antimicrobial resistance genes (ermB, bla CTXM1-like, bla CMY-2, qnrA, and qnrS) in environmental samples, demonstrating their accuracy and reliability.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized qPCR with SYBR Green chemistry and melting curve analysis to optimize and validate the detection of antimicrobial resistance genes in environmental samples.

CPS type III remained the most prevalent, but there was a notable rise in CPS types Ib, II, and IV. Additionally, there was a significant increase in the incidence of late-onset GBS disease.
full_output.methodology: The study involved CPS typing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of 1,556 GBS isolates collected from 2014 to 2020. Antimicrobial resistance was assessed using disk diffusion methods.

full_output.key_findings: Nimbolide exhibits potent bactericidal activity against multiple strains of Helicobacter pylori, including multidrug-resistant strains, and effectively disrupts H. pylori biofilms. It shows synergistic effects with low pH and maintains efficacy under bacteriostatic conditions. Nimbolide is non-hemolytic and demonstrates irreversible bactericidal effects at high concentrations.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity of nimbolide was evaluated through MIC/MBC assays, bactericidal kinetics, pH-dependent activity, growth arrest experiments, and biofilm disruption assays.

full_output.paper_title: Predicted transmembrane proteins with homology to Mef(A) are not responsible for complementing mef(A) deletion in the mef(A)-msr(D) macrolide efflux system in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated whether spr0971, spr1023, and spr1932 could complement mef(A) deletion in the mef(A)-msr(D) macrolide efflux system in Streptococcus pneumoniae. None of these genes were found to significantly affect erythromycin resistance when deleted, indicating they are not involved in mef(A) complementation.

full_output.paper_title: Alcaligenes faecalis metallo-β-lactamase in extensively drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes two novel metallo-beta-lactamase genes, blaAFM-2 and blaAFM-3, from extensively drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, demonstrating their ability to confer resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Mobile Antimicrobial Resistance Genes in Probiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus pseudintermedius's PBP4 Is Directly Associated with the Dissociated Oxacillin and Cefoxitin Phenotype.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and Characterization of ESBL/AmpC Producing Escherichia coli from Fresh Meat in Portugal.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various ESBL and AmpC genes, including bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-32, bla CTX-M-55, bla CTX-M-65, bla CTX-M-27, bla CTX-M-9, bla CTX-M-14, bla SHV-12, bla TEM-52, bla CMY-2, qnrB, qnrS, aac(6')-Ib, and mcr-1, in E. coli isolates from fresh meat in Portugal.

Genomic analysis and susceptibility testing were performed to evaluate the properties of the resulting phages.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Isolated from the Intensive Care Unit in a Tertiary Teaching Hospital in Malaysia.

full_output.paper_title: Wastewater-Based Surveillance of Antibiotic Resistance Genes Associated with Tuberculosis Treatment Regimen in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) associated with tuberculosis treatment in wastewater samples from South Africa, including rrs (streptomycin resistance), pncA (pyrazinamide resistance), katG (isoniazid resistance), rpoB (rifampicin resistance), embB (ethambutol resistance), gyrA (ofloxacin resistance), gyrB (moxifloxacin resistance), atpE (bedaquiline resistance), ethR (ethionamide resistance), and eis (kanamycin/amikacin resistance).

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple extended-spectrum cephalosporin-resistant and bla(NDM-5)-harbouring uropathogenic Escherichia coli from cats and dogs in Thailand, highlighting the presence of various AMR genes such as bla CTX-M, bla NDM-5, mcr-3, aac(6')-Ib-cr, and mph(A).

full_output.paper_title: In Silico Detection of Antimicrobial Resistance Integrons in Salmonella enterica Isolates from Countries of the Andean Community.

full_output.paper_title: Is There a Difference in Clinical Features, Microbiological Epidemiology and Effective Empiric Antimicrobial Therapy Comparing Healthcare-Associated and Community-Acquired Vertebral Osteomyelitis?
full_output.key_findings: The study found that healthcare-associated vertebral osteomyelitis (HAVO) had a higher rate of methicillin-resistant isolates compared to community-acquired vertebral osteomyelitis (CAVO). Resistance to cefazolin and ciprofloxacin was higher in HAVO cases.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of Antibiotic Therapies on Resistance Genes Dynamic and Composition of the Animal Gut Microbiota.

full_output.key_findings: The study examined the impact of antibiotic therapies on the dynamics and composition of resistance genes in the animal gut microbiota, identifying several AMR genes such as blaTEM, tetA, strA, strB, intI1, tetM, mel, floR, mcr-2, oqx B, tetC, tetG, tetO, tetW, tetX, ermB, ermF, sul1, sul2, and others, which were experimentally validated in Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized qPCR to analyze the abundance of ARGs in fecal samples from calves and pigs, examining the effects of various antibiotics on the gut microbiota and resistance gene profiles.

full_output.paper_title: First Report of the Plasmid-mediated fosB Gene in Enterococcus faecalis from Pigs.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative RNA-Seq Analysis Reveals Potentially Resistance-Related Genes in Response to Bacterial Canker of Tomato.

full_output.paper_title: New Investigations with Lupane Type A-Ring Azepane Triterpenoids for Antimycobacterial Drug Candidate Design.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimycobacterial activity of twenty lupane type A-ring azepano-triterpenoids against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and non-tuberculous mycobacteria, identifying several compounds with high activity, including compound 7 with a MIC of 0.5 µM against M. tuberculosis H37Rv.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of Copper(II) Ion Binding by Porin P1 Precursor Fragments from Fusobacterium nucleatum on DNA Degradation.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the coordination of Cu(II) ions with model peptides from the outer membrane protein P1 precursor of Fusobacterium nucleatum and their effects on DNA degradation. It identifies the coordination modes and stability of Cu(II) complexes with the peptides, highlighting the role of histidine residues and carboxyl groups in metal binding. The research also demonstrates that the Cu(II)-peptide complexes can generate hydroxyl radicals, leading to DNA strand cleavage, particularly under oxidative conditions.
full_output.methodology: The study employs a combination of experimental techniques including mass spectrometry, potentiometry, UV-Vis, CD, EPR, gel electrophoresis, and computational methods such as density functional theory (DFT) to analyze the structural and thermodynamic properties of Cu(II) complexes with model peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical and Epidemiological Analysis of Children's Urinary Tract Infections in Accordance with Antibiotic Resistance Patterns of Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed antibiotic resistance patterns in children with urinary tract infections (UTIs), noting increasing resistance to amoxicillin with clavulanic acid, gentamicin, and ceftazidime. It also identified associations between inflammatory markers and antibiotic susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 525 children with UTIs, including microbiological testing and statistical analysis of resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Interplay between Sublethal Aminoglycosides and Quorum Sensing: Consequences on Survival in V. cholerae.

full_output.paper_title: Extraintestinal Pathogenic Escherichia coli: Virulence Factors and Antibiotic Resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of CTX-M Type ESBL E. coli from Sheep and Their Abattoir Environment Using Whole-Genome Sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: A Snapshot of the Genetic Diversity of Salmonella Enteritidis Population Involved in Human Infections in Romania Taken in the European Epidemiological Context.

full_output.paper_title: Colistin Induces Resistance through Biofilm Formation, via Increased phoQ Expression, in Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli.

full_output.paper_title: Two Novel Semisynthetic Lipoglycopeptides Active against Staphylococcus aureus Biofilms and Cells in Late Stationary Growth Phase.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Haemophilus influenzae Strains with Non-Enzymatic Resistance to β-Lactam Antibiotics Caused by Mutations in the PBP3 Gene in the Czech Republic in 2010-2018.

full_output.paper_title: Transformation of Tetracycline by Manganese Peroxidase from Phanerochaete chrysosporium.

full_output.paper_title: New Kendomycin Derivative Isolated from Streptomyces sp. Cl 58-27.
