full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the performance of a broth microdilution (BMD) assay for determining the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 14 anti-tuberculous drugs against Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) strains. The assay showed good agreement with genotypic drug susceptibility testing (gDST) results, with most discrepancies attributed to mutations in specific genes such as embB, atpE, Rv0678, ribD, ethA, cycA, and fbiC.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a broth microdilution assay based on the EUCAST reference protocol, combined with genotypic drug susceptibility testing via whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to identify resistance mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and virulent characterization of a duck-associated Salmonella serovar Potsdam from China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in Salmonella serovar Potsdam isolated from duck embryos, including aac(3')-Ia, aac(4')-IIa, aph(3')-IIa, aph(3')'-Ib, aph(6')-Id, blaTEM-116, blaTEM-1B, and tet(A), as well as gyrA and parC mutations associated with quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and ResFinder were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that nafcillin strongly inhibited biofilm formation by Salmonella Typhimurium, with MBIC and MBEC values of 8 µg/mL and 32 µg/mL, respectively. It also showed that nafcillin and diosmin reduced the expression of type II toxin-antitoxin (TA) system genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used biofilm assays, qRT-PCR, light microscopy, and FESEM to analyze the effects of nafcillin and diosmin on biofilm formation and gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Water source, latrine type, and rainfall are associated with detection of non-optimal and enteric bacteria in the vaginal microbiome: a prospective observational cohort study nested within a cluster randomized controlled trial.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that water source, latrine type, and rainfall are associated with the vaginal microbiome composition, with piped water and flush toilets linked to a higher proportion of L. crispatus-dominated CST-I, while traditional pit latrines and bush/field were associated with lower CST-I and higher alpha diversity.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to analyze the vaginal microbiome in a cohort of adolescent girls, along with statistical analyses to evaluate associations between environmental factors and microbiome composition.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiological and genetic characteristics of clinical carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales isolates from Batna hospitals in Algeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla OXA−48−like, bla NDM, bla VIM, and bla KPC genes as the primary carbapenemase genes in carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales isolates from Batna hospitals in Algeria. It also reported novel combinations of these genes, highlighting the complexity of resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection through real-time PCR and phenotypic screening for carbapenemase production.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular and clinical insights into extended-spectrum beta-lactamase genes of Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from neonatal sepsis in Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaCTX-M, blaTEM, and blaSHV as the most prevalent extended-spectrum beta-lactamase genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from neonatal sepsis in Ethiopia, with significant correlations between blaSHV and neonatal mortality.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and multiplex PCR were used to analyze resistance genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro resensitization of multidrug-resistant clinical isolates of Enterococcus faecium and E. faecalis through phage-antibiotic synergy.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that phage-antibiotic synergy can resensitize multidrug-resistant Enterococcus faecium and E. faecalis isolates to antibiotics, highlighting potential strategies for combating antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a comprehensive screening assay to evaluate phage-antibiotic synergy, transcriptome analysis, and gene expression profiling to understand the mechanisms behind the observed synergistic effects.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteria-activated macrophage membrane coated ROS-responsive nanoparticle for targeted delivery of antibiotics to infected wounds.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a ROS-responsive nanoparticle coated with bacteria-activated macrophage membranes (Sa-MM@Van-NPs) for targeted delivery of vancomycin to infected wounds, demonstrating enhanced antibacterial efficacy and wound healing.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized nanoparticle synthesis, in vitro and in vivo antibacterial assays, and imaging techniques to evaluate the performance of Sa-MM@Van-NPs.

full_output.paper_title: Diverse polysaccharide production and biofilm formation abilities of clinical Klebsiella pneumoniae.

mrkD.notes: Mutations in mrkD were prevalent in mucoid isolates

fimH.notes: Mutations in fimH were prevalent in mucoid isolates

full_output.paper_title: Decadal Evolution of KPC-related plasmids in Pseudomonas aeruginosa high-risk clone ST463 in Zhejiang, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaKPC-2 as a key gene responsible for carbapenem resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa ST463 clone, highlighting the evolutionary advantages of type I plasmids with fragment deletions.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid cloning, and MIC testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Structural insights into the enzymatic breakdown of azomycin-derived antibiotics by 2-nitroimidazole hydrolase (NnhA).

full_output.methodology: Expression and purification of NnhA, structural analysis via X-ray crystallography, and enzymatic activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Symbiotic microbial population composition of Apolygus lucorum under temperature and pesticide pressures.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that temperature and imidacloprid concentration affect the microbial community composition and abundance of Apolygus lucorum. Specifically, Aeromonas caviae and Akkermansia muciniphila show a strong correlation with imidacloprid concentration, suggesting their potential role in influencing the resistance of A. lucorum to imidacloprid.
full_output.methodology: 16S rRNA sequencing was used to analyze the microbial community composition of Apolygus lucorum under various temperature and imidacloprid concentration conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-wide phenotypic profiling of transcription factors and identification of novel targets to control the virulence of Vibrio vulnificus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 89 transcription factors (TFs) affecting multiple phenotypes of Vibrio vulnificus, including 59 TFs affecting in vitro survival and 64 TFs affecting virulence. Specifically, 27 TFs enhanced in vitro virulence, and 8 of these also increased in vivo virulence. HlyU, IscR, NagC, MetJ, and Tet2 were highlighted as potential drug targets for anti-virulence therapies due to their role in regulating major exotoxin genes without affecting bacterial growth.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide phenotypic profiling of TF mutants using 16 different assays, including in vitro survival, virulence, and in vivo infectivity tests.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic profiling of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii from a tertiary care center in Malaysia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla_OXA-23, bla_VIM, bla_ADC, and IS_Aba1/bla_OXA-23 as the primary resistance genes in multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from a Malaysian hospital, highlighting their role in carbapenem and other antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and MLST analysis were used to identify and characterize antibiotic resistance genes and genetic relatedness among isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriophage treatment is effective against carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (KPC) in a neutropenic murine model of gastrointestinal translocation and renal infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the effectiveness of a bacteriophage cocktail against KPC renal infection in a neutropenic murine model and shows a synergistic interaction with ceftazidime/avibactam.
full_output.methodology: Experiments involving bacteriophage treatment, MIC assays, and in vivo studies in a neutropenic murine model.

full_output.paper_title: Progression of ampC amplification during de novo amoxicillin resistance development in E. coli.

ampC.mechanism: ampC gene amplification and promoter mutations lead to increased AmpC activity and amoxicillin resistance
ampC.validation_method: qPCR, whole genome sequencing, AmpC activity measurement

ampC.notes: promoter mutations in ampC contribute to increased AmpC activity and amoxicillin resistance
ampC.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that mutations in the ampC promoter, specifically −11 G > A and −32 A > T, contribute to increased AmpC activity and amoxicillin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Cationic conjugated polymers with tunable hydrophobicity for efficient treatment of multidrug-resistant wound biofilm infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development of cationic conjugated polymers (CP_C n_TMA) with tunable hydrophobicity for treating multidrug-resistant wound biofilm infections. The polymer CP_C 11_TMA exhibited high antimicrobial efficacy against various multidrug-resistant bacteria, including Acinetobacter baumannii, Escherichia coli, and MRSA, with minimal toxicity to mammalian cells.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and evaluation of CP_C n_TMA polymers for antimicrobial activity, selectivity, and biofilm penetration using in vitro and in vivo models.

full_output.paper_title: Menaquinone-specific turnover by Mycobacterium tuberculosis cytochrome bd is redox regulated by the Q-loop disulfide bond.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that Mycobacterium tuberculosis cytochrome bd (Mtbd) exhibits menaquinone-specific turnover and that its activity is regulated by a unique Q-loop disulfide bond, which modulates enzyme activity in response to redox conditions.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biochemical assays, cryo-EM, and proteoliposome reconstitution to analyze the activity and regulation of Mtbd.

full_output.paper_title: The C-terminal α-helix is crucial for the activity of the bacterial ABC transporter BmrA.

full_output.key_findings: The C-terminal α-helix of BmrA is crucial for its ATPase and transport activity. Mutations in the C-terminal helix, particularly in the residues L569-R571 and Q576-L578, significantly reduce ATPase and transport activity.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, ATPase activity assays, Hoechst 33342 transport assays, BN-PAGE, and CD spectroscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Mutation on JmjC domain of UTX impaired its antitumor effects in pancreatic cancer via inhibiting G0S2 expression and activating the Toll-like signaling pathway.

UTX.notes: The UTX mutation leads to reduced G0S2 expression and activation of the Toll-like signaling pathway.

full_output.key_findings: A missense mutation in the JmjC domain of UTX impairs its antitumor effects in pancreatic cancer by inhibiting G0S2 expression and activating the Toll-like signaling pathway.
full_output.methodology: Exome sequencing, western blot, MTT assay, transwell assay, colony formation assay, and xenograft experiments were used to evaluate the role of UTX mutation in pancreatic cancer.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance of Escherichia coli in cats and their drinking water: drug resistance profiles and antimicrobial-resistant genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla TEM, bla SHV, and bla CTX-M as the most prevalent extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes in E. coli isolates from cats and their drinking water. Phylogroup B2 was the most common, and resistance to multiple antimicrobial agents was observed.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of beta-lactamase genes and Clermont phylotyping of E. coli isolates.
full_output.sample_size: 52 cat feces and 52 cat drinking water samples

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial purine metabolism modulates C. elegans development and stress tolerance via DAF-16.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the E. coli purE gene as a critical factor in C. elegans development, with its disruption causing developmental delays and activating the DAF-16 stress response pathway.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide screening of E. coli mutants and phenotypic analysis of C. elegans development.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in mexT bypass the stringent response dependency of virulence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: Mutations in mexT, a transcription factor, bypass the stringent response dependency of virulence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and are associated with resistance to aminoglycosides and colistin.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, genome sequencing, mutant construction, MIC testing, RNA-seq, and RT-qPCR.

full_output.paper_title: Screening and identification of antimicrobial peptides from the gut microbiome of cockroach Blattella germanica.
full_output.key_findings: AMP1, derived from the symbiotic microorganism Blattabacterium cuenoti, demonstrated broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, low cytotoxicity, and wound healing effects in mice, comparable to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Computational pipeline 'AMPidentifier' for AMP prediction, in vitro and in vivo testing, and mechanistic studies.

full_output.paper_title: Fusobacterium nucleatum-driven CX3CR1(+) PD-L1(+) phagocytes route to tumor tissues and reshape tumor microenvironment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Fn1792, a lysozyme inhibitor from Fusobacterium nucleatum, which suppresses apoptosis of host phagocytes by inducing CX3CR1 expression, contributing to tumor progression and immunosuppression.
full_output.methodology: Protein interaction assays, flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, Western blot, and in vivo experiments.
full_output.sample_size: n=22 for Fn-DNA levels in tumor tissues, n=432 for healthy subjects, n=10 for paired paraffin-embedded tumors, n=31 for fecal samples, n=21 for validation cohort

full_output.paper_title: A microaerobically induced small heat shock protein contributes to Rhizobium leguminosarum/Pisum sativum symbiosis and interacts with a wide range of bacteroid proteins.

RLV_1399.validation_method: pull-down assays, immunoblot analysis, and proteomic analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies rlv_1399 as a small heat shock protein (sHSP) that plays a crucial role in the symbiosis of Rhizobium leguminosarum with pea plants, enhancing bacterial tolerance to oxidative stress and NCR antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.methodology: Functional analysis of the sHSP RLV_1399, including gene deletion mutants, overexpression, and biochemical assays to assess its role in symbiosis and stress tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro potentiation of tetracyclines in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by RW01, a new cyclic peptide.

pmrB.notes: Mutations in pmrB were associated with resistance to colistin and cross-resistance to other antibiotics.

parS.notes: Mutations in parS were associated with resistance to colistin and cross-resistance to other antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: RW01 enhances tetracycline activity by permeabilizing the bacterial membrane, and resistance to the RW01-minocycline combination involves mutations in the pmrB gene, leading to cross-resistance to colistin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, checkerboard assays, whole-genome sequencing, and permeability assays were used to evaluate RW01's effect on P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Phage-mediated virulence loss and antimicrobial susceptibility in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.

yibH.validation_method: CRISPR/Cas9-based gene deletions and plaque efficiency assay

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, CRISPR/Cas9-based gene deletions, and phage susceptibility assays were used to identify and validate AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Patterns of spontaneous and induced genomic alterations in Yarrowia lipolytica.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified YALI1_E21053g as a gene negatively associated with Zeocin resistance in Yarrowia lipolytica. Deletion of this gene conferred increased Zeocin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and mutation accumulation experiments were used to analyze genomic alterations in Y. lipolytica under spontaneous and mutagen-induced conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of an antibiotic from an HTS targeting EF-Tu:tRNA interaction: a prospective topical treatment for MRSA skin infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MGC-10, a novel antibiotic targeting the EF-Tu:tRNA interaction, effective against MRSA and other Gram-positive bacteria with no observed resistance.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening (HTS) assay to identify inhibitors of EF-Tu:tRNA ternary complex formation, followed by in vitro and in vivo testing.

full_output.paper_title: Meningococcal C Disease Outbreak Caused by Multidrug-Resistant Neisseria meningitidis, Fiji.

gyrA.notes: All 23 strains were found to contain the gyrA point mutation T91I.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant Neisseria meningitidis serogroup C strains causing an outbreak in Fiji, with resistance mechanisms involving mutations in penA, gyrA, and rpoB genes.

full_output.paper_title: Phytochemistry, Antibacterial and Antioxidant Activities of Grewia lasiocarpa E. Mey. Ex Harv. Fungal Endophytes: A Computational and Experimental Validation Study.

full_output.methodology: Computational molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations, along with in vitro antibacterial assays.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen identifies AraC-daunorubicin-etoposide response modulators associated with outcomes in pediatric AML.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified BCL2, CLIP2, and VAV3 as drug-resistant markers associated with poor outcomes in pediatric AML treated with ADE, while GRPEL1, HCFC1, and TAF10 were identified as drug-sensitive markers linked to improved outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus endangers Egyptian dairy herds.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (VRSA) isolates with high prevalence of vanA and vanB genes, and methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) with mecA gene, highlighting the threat of multidrug-resistant strains in Egyptian dairy herds.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize AMR genes and resistance profiles in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Nosocomial transmission of NDM-1-containing Klebsiella pneumoniae ST147 in a Dutch pediatric oncology center associated with patients from Ukraine.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the nosocomial transmission of blaNDM-1-containing Klebsiella pneumoniae ST147 in a Dutch pediatric oncology center, highlighting the role of environmental contamination in the spread of multidrug-resistant organisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, phenotypic and genotypic characterization, and epidemiological analysis were used to investigate the transmission of blaNDM-1-containing K. pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: High Prevalence of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes in Multidrug-Resistant Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase-Producing Escherichia coli Clinical Isolates after COVID-19 Pandemic, North Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes, including blaIMP, blaTEM, AcrA, AcrB, blaCTX, blaOXA-58, aaclb, blaSHV, and aacla, in multidrug-resistant extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli isolates from Northern Iran.

full_output.paper_title: Engineering Salmochelin-Inspired Siderophore-Antibiotic Conjugates via IroB-Catalyzed Glucosylation
full_output.key_findings: IroB, a C-glucosyltransferase, was shown to effectively glucosylate non-native triscatecholates such as TC and MC, enabling the creation of salmochelin-inspired SACs with targeted antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: Enzymatic activity assays, HPLC, LC/MS, NMR, and antibacterial activity testing.

full_output.paper_title: Novel antibiotic resistance profiles in bacteria isolated from oil fly larvae Helaeomyia petrolei living in the La Brea Tar Pits.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel antibiotic resistance profiles in bacteria isolated from oil fly larvae, highlighting the presence of resistance genes and mechanisms not previously documented in the CARD database for the respective species.

full_output.sample_size: Six bacterial isolates from oil fly larvae.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus Tetracycline Resistance and Co-resistance in a Doxycycline Postexposure Prophylaxis-Eligible Population.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that tetracycline nonsusceptibility in Staphylococcus aureus is associated with co-resistance to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and clindamycin in a doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis-eligible population.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of S aureus cultures from patients with male sex, HIV, or HIV preexposure prophylaxis, assessing antimicrobial resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Developing novel indoles as antitubercular agents and simulated annealing-based analysis of their binding with MmpL3.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three novel indole-2-carboxamides (compounds 5c, 5f, and 5i) as potent antitubercular agents that inhibit MmpL3, a crucial protein involved in mycobacterial cell wall biogenesis. These compounds show strong activity against both drug-sensitive and drug-resistant strains of M. tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: The study employed rational drug design, molecular docking, simulated annealing-based molecular dynamics simulations, and biological evaluations including antitubercular activity assays and cytotoxicity assessments.

full_output.paper_title: Hybrid Cell Membrane-Engineered Nanocarrier for Triple-Action Strategy to Address Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces a novel nanocarrier, TTob@NPM, designed for targeted antibiotic delivery and toxin/bacteria clearance against Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections. TTob@NPM exhibits enhanced antibacterial activity, effective biofilm disruption, and immunomodulatory properties, demonstrating potential for treating multidrug-resistant infections.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro and in vivo experiments, including antimicrobial activity assays, biofilm disruption tests, and immunomodulatory evaluations, to characterize the performance of TTob@NPM.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of biofilm formation and carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from clinical samples at a rural hospital in western Uttar Pradesh.

full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, multiplex real-time PCR, and phenotypic tests (MHT, mCIM, eCIM) were used to identify carbapenem resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: A simple predictive model for puerperal infections: emphasizing risk factors and pathogen analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Escherichia coli as the primary pathogen causing puerperal infections and determined its susceptibility to several antibiotics, including Meropenem, Imipenem, Piperacillin/tazobactam, and Ceftazidime.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted a retrospective case-control analysis involving 525 pregnant women, utilizing logistic regression and LASSO methods to develop a predictive nomogram for puerperal infections.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of MDR1 Gene Variants and Their Impact on Translation Rates and Patient Survival
full_output.key_findings: The study uses computational methods to analyze the effects of MDR1 variants T1236C, T2677G, and T3435C on mRNA folding and translation rates, predicting that these variants may influence p-gp function without changing mRNA expression levels.
full_output.methodology: Computational modeling, Enformer, SpliceAI, Airliner, DeepM6ASeq, and catRAPID omics were used to assess the impact of MDR1 variants on gene expression and post-transcriptional regulation.

full_output.paper_title: ProQ-associated small RNAs control motility in Vibrio cholerae.
full_output.key_findings: ProQ interacts with hundreds of transcripts in V. cholerae, including the highly abundant FlaX small RNA (sRNA). FlaX base-pairs with multiple sites on the flaB flagellin mRNA, preventing 30S ribosome binding and translation initiation. V. cholerae cells lacking flaX display impaired motility gene expression, altered flagella composition and reduced swimming in liquid environments.

full_output.paper_title: Construction and characterization of bioluminescent Salmonella Reading outbreak and non-outbreak strains.

full_output.sample_size: Two strains of S. Reading: an outbreak strain (SRO) and a non-outbreak strain (SRN).

full_output.paper_title: Mitigating Antibiotic Resistance: The Utilization of CRISPR Technology in Detection.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the application of CRISPR technology in the detection of antibiotic resistance, focusing on its potential for identifying resistance genes and antibiotics. It highlights the development of CRISPR-based methods for both nucleic acid and non-nucleic acid targets, emphasizing their advantages in sensitivity, specificity, and speed.
full_output.methodology: The review covers the principles and applications of CRISPR/Cas systems in antibiotic detection, including various CRISPR-based platforms and their performance metrics.

full_output.paper_title: The characterization of outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) and their role in mediating antibiotic-resistance gene transfer through natural transformation in Riemerella anatipestifer.
full_output.key_findings: Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from Riemerella anatipestifer strain CH-1 were shown to transfer antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and plasmids to the sensitive strain RA ATCC11845 through natural transformation, leading to increased resistance to erythromycin, tetracycline, and aztreonam.

full_output.paper_title: Potential of nanopore sequencing for tuberculosis diagnosis and drug resistance detection.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of beta-lactamase genes and molecular genotyping of multidrug-resistant clinical isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Multi-label classification to predict antibiotic resistance from raw clinical MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry data.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive Analysis of Virulence Genes, Antibiotic Resistance, Biofilm Formation, and Sequence Types in Clinical Isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Association between clinical-biological characteristics of Klebsiella pneumoniae and 28-day mortality in patients with bloodstream infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that the presence of rfbA/B/D genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae strains is associated with increased 28-day mortality in patients with bloodstream infections, particularly in nosocomial cases.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical data, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, whole-genome sequencing, and statistical analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of bla(OXA-51-23-58), bla(VIM), bla(NDM), and bla(IMP) carbapenemase genes in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from hospitalized patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of carbapenemase genes blaOXA-23, blaOXA-51, and blaNDM in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates, highlighting the prevalence of carbapenem resistance in the studied population.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and characterize carbapenemase genes in A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity of camel colostrum against pathogenic strain of Escherichia coli F17-associated with calf diarrhea.
full_output.key_findings: Camel colostrum inhibits the growth of E. coli-F17 by impeding swarming and swimming motilities, and biofilm formation. It also reduces eDNA release.
full_output.methodology: Microbroth dilution, crystal violet assay, and motility assays were used to assess the antibacterial and antibiofilm effects of camel colostrum against E. coli-F17.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of antimicrobial resistance genes in multidrug-resistant-ESBLs-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae post-COVID-19 pandemic.

full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and multiplex PCR were used to detect resistance genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-function analysis of carrier protein-dependent 2-sulfamoylacetyl transferase in the biosynthesis of altemicidin.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structure and function of SbzI and SbzG, highlighting their roles in the biosynthesis of altemicidin, a sulfonamide antibiotic. full_output.methodology: Structural analysis, mutagenesis, enzyme assays, and computational modeling were used to investigate the function of SbzI and SbzG.

full_output.paper_title: A new type III effector from Bradyrhizobium sp. DOA9 encoding a putative SUMO-protease blocks nodulation in Arachis hypogaea L.

full_output.paper_title: The expression of different gene constructs in Escherichia coli SM lux biosensor after exposure to drugs.

full_output.methodology: Expression of gene constructs in E. coli SM biosensors was analyzed after exposure to various concentrations of antibiotics and diclofenac, measuring luminescence signals.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Enterobacter phage vB_EcRAM-01, a new Pseudotevenvirus against Enterobacter cloacae, isolated in an urban river in Panama.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the Enterobacter phage vB_EcRAM-01, isolated from an urban river in Panama, which exhibits lytic activity against Enterobacter cloacae. The phage is stable under various environmental conditions and lacks genes associated with resistance, virulence, or allergenicity.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, purification, morphological characterization, genome sequencing, and comparative genomics were employed to analyze vB_EcRAM-01.

full_output.paper_title: Reduced microtubule acetylation increases eribulin resistance in breast cancer cells
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ATAT1 as a key gene involved in microtubule acetylation, which is crucial for eribulin-induced cell death. full_output.paper_title: Morphogenetic penicillin-binding proteins control virulence-associated type III secretion systems in Salmonella.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a mutation in the gapA gene of E. coli that confers resistance to pentalenolactone, a sesquiterpenoid antibiotic. This mutation, Thr175Ser, was experimentally validated and can serve as a selectable marker for genetic engineering applications.
full_output.methodology: Genomic DNA sequencing, Sanger sequencing, and plasmid construction were used to validate the mutation in the gapA gene and its effect on pentalenolactone resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Organic vs. Conventional Milk: Uncovering the Link to Antibiotic Resistance in Bacillus cereus sensu lato.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that B. cereus s.l. isolates from organic milk had lower MIC values for most antibiotics compared to those from conventional milk, and identified the presence of nheA, hblA, and cytK genes associated with enterotoxin production.
full_output.methodology: The study used membrane ultrafiltration for bacterial isolation, disk diffusion and E-test for antibiotic resistance profiling, PCR and qPCR for gene detection and expression analysis, and MLST for phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Effects and Mechanisms of Action of Rutin with Conventional Antibiotics Against Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: Rutin exhibits antibacterial activity against E. coli and shows a significant synergistic effect when combined with amikacin, enhancing its bactericidal kinetics and disrupting the cell membrane and cell wall of E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was assessed using MIC, MBC, time-killing assays, SEM, AKP, K+, and protein leakage assays, along with CLSM for membrane integrity analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the distribution of exo virulotypes (exoU, exoS, exoT, exoY) in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains and links specific virulotypes (V1, V2) to increased mortality risk in pediatric patients.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and susceptibility profiling were used to analyze exo gene distribution and correlate virulotypes with clinical outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and Genotypic Analysis of Antimicrobial Resistance in Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae Isolated from Pigs with Enzootic Pneumonia in Australia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Australian M. hyopneumoniae isolates remained susceptible to most antimicrobials, with higher MICs observed for erythromycin, gamithromycin, and tilmicosin. No known genetic markers for resistance were identified, suggesting potential non-genetic resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, whole-genome sequencing, and PCR were used to analyze AMR profiles and genetic markers in M. hyopneumoniae isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies risk factors for carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) infection and mortality in children, highlighting hematopoietic malignancies, mechanical ventilation, and multiple antibiotic use as significant factors.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective case-control study analyzing clinical data from pediatric patients with CRKP and carbapenem-sensitive K. pneumoniae (CSKP) infections.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of Efflux Pump Contributions and Plasmid-Mediated Genetic Determinants in Ciprofloxacin-Resistant Salmonella.

aac(6')-Ib-cr.evidence_note: The gene aac(6')-Ib-cr was identified on transferable plasmids in S. Enteritidis, IncA/C plasmids in S. Typhimurium, and IncHI2 plasmids in S. Virchow.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies oqxAB, aac(6')-Ib-cr, and qnrS1 as key plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) genes in ciprofloxacin-resistant Salmonella. These genes contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance, with oqxAB and aac(6')-Ib-cr frequently co-occurring in strains. The role of efflux pumps and plasmid fusion in resistance dissemination is highlighted.
full_output.methodology: PCR, plasmid transfer experiments, MIC testing, and whole-genome sequencing were used to characterize resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance Trends in Carbapenem-Resistant Gram-Negative Pathogens and Eight-Year Surveillance of XDR Bloodstream Infections in a Western Greece Tertiary Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a high prevalence of extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Gram-negative bacteria, including Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, in a tertiary hospital in Western Greece. It highlights the increasing resistance to colistin and other antibiotics among these pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bloodstream isolates from 2016 to 2023, assessing their susceptibility to various antibiotics and determining XDR status based on resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Helicobacter pylori Inhibition, Gastritis Attenuation, and Gut Microbiota Protection in C57BL/6 Mice by Ligilactobacillus salivarius NCUH062003.
full_output.key_findings: Ligilactobacillus salivarius NCUH062003 reduces H. pylori colonization, alleviates gastric inflammation, and protects the gut microbiota in C57BL/6 mice.
full_output.methodology: Animal experiments, histopathological analysis, ELISA, and 16S rRNA sequencing were used to evaluate the effects of L. salivarius NCUH062003 on H. pylori infection and gut microbiota.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified high prevalence of multidrug-resistant bacteria, including S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, E. coli, and K. pneumoniae, in patients with otitis media in Ethiopia. Resistance to ampicillin, tetracycline, and other antibiotics was commonly observed.
full_output.methodology: Laboratory-based cross-sectional study involving 242 patients with otitis media, including bacterial culture, biochemical tests, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase 2 (IMPDH2) modulates response to therapy and chemo-resistance in triple negative breast cancer.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IMPDH2 as a contributor to doxorubicin resistance in triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) models. Elevated IMPDH2 expression is associated with worse prognosis and resistance to chemotherapy, and its inhibition reduces the growth of chemo-resistant lesions.
full_output.methodology: The study used public datasets, in vitro experiments with TNBC cell lines, and in vivo experiments with mice to investigate the role of IMPDH2 in chemotherapy resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Unveiling the photocatalytic and antimicrobial activities of star-shaped gold nanoparticles under visible spectrum.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that star-shaped gold nanoparticles (AuNSTs) exhibit significant photocatalytic activity in degrading rhodamine B dye and show potent antimicrobial effects against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of AuNSTs via seed-mediated growth, characterization using TEM and UV-Vis spectroscopy, photocatalytic degradation experiments, and antimicrobial activity assessment via disk diffusion and MIC tests.

full_output.paper_title: LEGO-Lipophosphonoxin membrane activity is enhanced by presence of phosphatidylethanolamine but hindered by outer membrane.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the membrane-active properties of LEGO-LPPOs, focusing on their ability to permeabilize bacterial membranes. It found that LEGO-LPPOs effectively permeabilize the cytoplasmic membranes of various bacteria, with activity influenced by the presence of phosphatidylethanolamine and the integrity of the outer membrane.
full_output.methodology: The study used antimicrobial activity assays, liposome leakage experiments, molecular dynamics simulations, and propidium iodide influx assays to evaluate the membrane-permeabilizing effects of LEGO-LPPOs.

full_output.paper_title: The assessment of chemical composition and biological activity of faba bean pods as a potential feed additive utilized in piglets nutrition.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that faba bean pods (FBP) contain high levels of polyphenols, including vestitol, piscidic acid, hydroxyeucomic acid, quercetin, and kaempferol glycosides. The methanolic extract of FBP showed significant antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Salmonella enterica, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 1 mg/mL for S. enterica and 0.5 mg/mL for E. coli. The extract also demonstrated low cytotoxicity against porcine intestinal IPEC-J2 cells.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the nutritional and phytochemical composition of FBP using proximate analysis, HPLC-MS, and evaluated the antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. enterica using broth dilution assays. Cytotoxicity was assessed using the MTT assay on IPEC-J2 cells.

full_output.paper_title: Facile Synthesis of Oxazolidinones as Potential Antibacterial Agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis of novel oxazolidinone derivatives and evaluates their antibacterial activity against M. smegmatis. Compound 18a1 showed potent activity with a MIC of 8 mg/L, comparable to Rifampicin.
full_output.methodology: The study employed microwave-assisted synthesis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to evaluate the compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Interplay between the Xer recombination system and the dissemination of antibioresistance in Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.methodology: Plasmid construction, EMSA, cleavage assays, and PCR-based recombination analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Linear Plasmids in Micrococcus: Insights Into a Common Ancestor and Transfer by Conjugation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the erythromycin resistance gene 'erm' on the linear plasmid pLMA1 in Micrococcus sp. A1, demonstrating its role in conferring resistance to erythromycin through experimental validation.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid isolation, sequencing, conjugation assays, and PCR confirmation were used to validate the resistance mechanism.

full_output.paper_title: DJK-5, an anti-biofilm peptide, increases Staphylococcus aureus sensitivity to colistin killing in co-biofilms with Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that DJK-5, an anti-biofilm peptide, enhances the effectiveness of colistin against Staphylococcus aureus in co-biofilms with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, demonstrating synergistic activity that reduces bacterial survival significantly.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro biofilm models and in vivo murine abscess models to evaluate the synergistic effects of DJK-5 and colistin against co-biofilms of P. aeruginosa and S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Influence of ESBL colonization status on gut microbiota composition during allogenic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the influence of ESBL colonization on gut microbiota composition during allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, highlighting differences in microbial abundance between ESBL-colonized and non-colonized patients.
full_output.methodology: Prospective pilot study analyzing gut microbiota through 16S rRNA sequencing and comparing microbial compositions between ESBL-colonized and non-colonized patients.

full_output.paper_title: Biophysical and biochemical evidence for the role of acetate kinases (AckAs) in an acetogenic pathway in pathogenic spirochetes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes acetate kinases TP0476 from Treponema pallidum and TV0924 from Treponema vincentii, demonstrating their enzymatic activity and structural properties.
full_output.methodology: Enzyme assays, crystallography, and biophysical analyses were used to characterize the acetate kinases.

full_output.paper_title: Cu2+ mediates the oxidation of the transcription factor MscA to regulate the antioxidant defense of mycobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MscA as a novel transcription factor that directly regulates the antioxidant defense in mycobacteria by modulating the expression of antioxidant gene clusters. Cu2+ binds to MscA, inhibiting its DNA binding activity and reducing the expression of antioxidant genes, leading to increased intracellular ROS and decreased mycobacterial growth under H2O2 stress.
full_output.methodology: The study employed EMSA, β-galactosidase activity assays, ITC, CD spectroscopy, and chemical cross-linking to investigate the role of MscA in antioxidant defense and its interaction with Cu2+.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli growing under antimicrobial gallium nitrate stress reveals new processes of tolerance and toxicity.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores the transcriptomic response of Escherichia coli K12 BW25113 under sublethal gallium nitrate stress, identifying 1372 differentially expressed genes, highlighting processes such as iron homeostasis, sulfur metabolism, and stress responses.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq analysis of E. coli K12 BW25113 exposed to sublethal gallium nitrate concentrations to identify differentially expressed genes and their functional implications.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring nagZ as a virulence biomarker and treatment target in Enterobacter cloacae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies nagZ as a critical gene involved in the virulence of Enterobacter cloacae. Deletion of nagZ significantly reduces virulence and enhances the antibacterial efficacy of ceftazidime against E. cloacae.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic manipulation techniques, including nagZ knockout and complementation, along with in vitro and in vivo infection models to assess the role of nagZ in E. cloacae virulence and antibiotic susceptibility.
full_output.sample_size: 6 pathogenic and 6 colonizing E. cloacae strains

full_output.paper_title: Comparative antibacterial activity of clove extract against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that clove extract exhibits antibacterial activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and enhances the effectiveness of antibiotics like imipenem and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid through synergistic effects.
full_output.methodology: The study used disc diffusion, agar well diffusion, and microdilution methods to assess antibacterial activity, along with UHPLC/MS analysis to identify components of the clove extract.

full_output.paper_title: Pilot study of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) in hospitals, Italy, September to December 2022.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 58.5% of C. difficile isolates were resistant to at least one antimicrobial class, with 75.3% being multidrug-resistant (MDR). Resistance to erythromycin (ERY), clindamycin (CLI), moxifloxacin (MXF), and/or rifampicin (RIF) was most common. No isolates exhibited resistance to metronidazole (MTZ) or vancomycin (VAN).
full_output.methodology: The study conducted antimicrobial susceptibility testing of C. difficile isolates using agar dilution method and analyzed PCR ribotypes to identify resistance patterns.

full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the antimicrobial resistance dynamics in Mycoplasma gallisepticum isolates, focusing on antibiotic and disinfectant interactions. It identified varying susceptibility patterns among 100 MG isolates to 15 antibiotics and 7 biocides, highlighting the complex resistance profiles and the potential for cross-resistance between antibiotics and disinfectants.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility was assessed using broth microdilution, and disinfectant susceptibility was evaluated similarly. Statistical analyses, including correlation coefficients and regression models, were used to explore relationships between antimicrobial and disinfectant resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Disseminated organ and tissue infection secondary to carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infection for acute lymphoblastic leukemia treated with ceftazidime-avibactam: Two case reports.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the effectiveness of ceftazidime–avibactam in treating disseminated organ and tissue infections caused by carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in patients with acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
full_output.methodology: Case reports with drug sensitivity testing and treatment outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: The interaction of Serratia bacteria and harmonine in harlequin ladybird confers an interspecies competitive edge.

The genes Spidey, Sca2, and Desat are involved in harmonine biosynthesis and are critical for the ladybird's resistance to S. harmoniae.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of microbiome analysis, RNA interference, and biochemical assays to investigate the role of S. harmoniae and harmonine in the harlequin ladybird's competitive advantage.

full_output.paper_title: A Pyrroloquinazoline Analogue Regulated Streptococcus mutans and Streptococcus sanguinis Dual-Species Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: SCH-79797 regulated the dual-species biofilm of Streptococcus mutans and Streptococcus sanguinis, reducing biofilm biomass, metabolic activity, EPS, and acid production, while altering gene expression related to polysaccharide synthesis and competition.
full_output.methodology: Biofilm biomass and metabolic activity were assessed using crystal violet and MTT assays, gene expression was analyzed via qRT-PCR, and biofilm composition was evaluated using FISH.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Antibacterial 4-Piperazinylquinoline Hybrid Derivatives Against Staphylococcus aureus: Design, Synthesis, and In Vitro and In Silico Insights.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified compound 5k as a potent inhibitor of Staphylococcus aureus with an MIC of 10 μM, demonstrating its antibacterial activity. full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and evaluation of 4-piperazinylquinoline derivatives. In vitro assays were conducted against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa, and in silico docking and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate the mechanism of action of compound 5k.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis of Pyrazole-Based Inhibitors of the Bacterial Enzyme N-Succinyl-l,l-2,6-Diaminopimelic Acid Desuccinylase (DapE) as Potential Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of pyrazole-based inhibitors targeting the bacterial enzyme DapE, which is involved in the biosynthesis of m-DAP and lysine, crucial for bacterial cell wall synthesis. full_output.paper_title: You Win Some, You Lose Some: Modifying the Molecular Periphery of Nitrofuran-Tagged Diazaspirooctane Reshapes Its Antibacterial Activity Profile.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on modifying the molecular periphery of a nitrofuran-tagged diazaspirooctane compound to enhance its antibacterial activity. full_output.paper_title: Negative DNA supercoiling enhances DARS2 binding of DNA-bending protein IHF in the activation of Fis-dependent ATP-DnaA production.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that negative DNA supercoiling is necessary for the activation of DARS2 through the stabilization of IHF binding and the promotion of ADP-DnaA dissociation. full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular cloning, mutagenesis, RT-PCR, Western blotting, and in vivo infection models to characterize the role of GrpP/GrpQ in UPEC pathogenesis.

full_output.paper_title: The antibacterial capabilities of alginate encapsulated lemon essential oil nanocapsules against multi-drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.

ALN significantly reduces the transcription of bacterial virulence genes and shows lower cytotoxicity compared to free lemon essential oil.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized SEM, DLS, FTIR, and PCR to characterize the nanocapsules and assess their antibacterial and anti-biofilm effects.

full_output.paper_title: A large geno-spatial cluster of multi-drug resistant tuberculosis outbreak in a western district of Thailand.

This sub-lineage was associated with MDR, pre-XDR, and XDR-TB cases, highlighting its role in the local transmission dynamics of tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and bioinformatic analysis of 188 MTB isolates were used to characterize the genomic profiles and geographical distribution of MDR-TB strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) was prevalent among medical students, with higher carriage rates in clinical students compared to pre-clinical students. Antibiotic resistance was primarily observed against erythromycin and clindamycin.

full_output.paper_title: Extended spectrum betalactamase and Carbapenemase producing gram negative bacteria from healthcare workers gowns at Debre Berhan Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Ethiopia.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Enterobacterales growing on selective CPE screening plates with a focus on non-carbapenemase-producing strains.

full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, spot tests, phage adsorption assays, and complementation experiments were used to characterize the role of bcsE in phage resistance.

cyp-35D1.evidence_note: The lysine allele at position 267 of CYP-35D1 was identified in a sensitive strain, and reciprocal allele replacement strains in different genetic backgrounds were used to show that the lysine allele conferred increased TBZ resistance.

CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, competitive fitness assays

cyp-35D1.notes: The lysine allele at position 267 of CYP-35D1 confers increased resistance to thiabendazole.

full_output.key_findings: Natural variation in the cytochrome P450 gene cyp-35D1 modifies thiabendazole (TBZ) responses in Caenorhabditis elegans independently of beta-tubulin. A lysine-to-glutamate substitution at position 267 (K267E) in CYP-35D1 increases TBZ resistance, while a lysine-to-aspartate substitution (K267D) also shows increased resistance. The lysine allele enhances TBZ metabolism in both C. elegans and yeast.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide association study, linkage mapping, CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, competitive fitness assays, yeast expression assays, HPLC-HRMS metabolite analysis.
full_output.sample_size: 214 wild C. elegans strains, 128 fenbendazole-resistant H. contortus samples

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the 23S rRNA gene at positions 2063 and 2064, which are associated with macrolide resistance in Mycoplasma pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted qualitative detection of 23sRNA A2063G and A2064G mutation sites resistant to MP macrolide antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Activation of three targets by a TAL effector confers susceptibility to bacterial blight of cotton.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies GhSWEET14a, GhSWEET14b, and GhPL1 as targets of the TAL effector Tal7b, which contribute to water-soaked lesion development in cotton. Silencing these genes reduces disease symptoms, demonstrating their role in susceptibility to bacterial blight.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, gene expression analysis, mutant analysis, and gene silencing techniques were used to characterize the role of GhSWEET14a, GhSWEET14b, and GhPL1 in cotton susceptibility to bacterial blight.
full_output.sample_size: Nine Xcm isolates from Texas, Mississippi, and Oklahoma

full_output.paper_title: Cryo-EM structure and evolutionary history of the conjugation surface exclusion protein TraT.
full_output.key_findings: TraT from IncF-like plasmids mediates plasmid-specific surface exclusion, forming a decameric structure critical for its function.
full_output.methodology: Cryo-EM structure determination and conjugation efficiency assays.

full_output.paper_title: Helicobacter pylori CagA promotes gastric cancer immune escape by upregulating SQLE.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that H. pylori CagA promotes gastric cancer immune escape by upregulating SQLE, which enhances PD-L1 palmitoylation and stability, leading to T cell dysfunction and immune evasion.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR, Western blotting, and functional assays to investigate the role of CagA and SQLE in gastric cancer progression and immune evasion.

full_output.paper_title: Constructing Activatable Photosensitizers Using Covalently Modified Mesoporous Silica.
full_output.key_findings: This study introduces DHUOCl-25, an activatable photosensitizer (aPS) that responds to hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and functions as a silica source for synthesizing mesoporous silica nanostructures (MSNs). DHUOCl-25 exhibits selective and sensitive responses to HOCl, releasing methylene blue (MB) upon activation. The synthesized MSNs, DHU-MSNs-2 and DHU-MSNs-6, demonstrate antibacterial and anticancer properties through photodynamic therapy (PDT) and chemotherapy.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the synthesis and characterization of DHUOCl-25, followed by the development of covalently modified MSNs (DHU-MSNs-1, DHU-MSNs-2, and DHU-MSNs-6) for biomedical applications. Techniques include fluorescence spectroscopy, FTIR, thermogravimetric analysis, and in vitro antibacterial and anticancer evaluations.

full_output.paper_title: Quorum sensing regulates virulence factors in the coral pathogen Vibrio coralliilyticus.

vcpR.validation_method: bioluminescence reporter assay, gene deletion studies

luxO.role_in_paper: key component of quorum sensing circuit

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies VcpR as a central regulator of quorum sensing in Vibrio coralliilyticus, demonstrating its role in regulating virulence factors such as biofilm formation and protease production. Key QS components including LuxO, CqsS, LuxN, and LuxP were shown to function analogously to those in other Vibrio species.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, comparative genomics, bioluminescence reporter assays, gene deletion studies, and biochemical assays were used to analyze the quorum sensing system in Vibrio coralliilyticus.

full_output.paper_title: Metabolite Profiling and Antimicrobial Activity of Endophytic Bacteria from Rauvolfia serpentina Leaves
full_output.key_findings: The study identified endophytic bacteria from Rauvolfia serpentina leaves, namely RSLB3 (Bacillus mojavensis) and RSLB18 (Bacillus wiedmannii), which exhibited significant antimicrobial activity against human pathogenic bacteria. Secondary metabolites from these isolates showed potent antibacterial effects, with RSLB3 demonstrating the highest zone of inhibition and lowest MIC values.
full_output.methodology: The study employed HPLC, UHPLC-HRMS, and biochemical assays to characterize metabolites and assess antimicrobial activity of endophytic bacteria from R. serpentina leaves.

full_output.paper_title: Single-cell microbiota phenotyping reveals distinct disease and therapy-associated signatures in Crohn's disease.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies distinct microbiota phenotypes and signatures associated with Crohn's disease (CD) and response to anti-TNF therapy, highlighting the potential of single-cell phenotyping for understanding disease mechanisms and therapeutic outcomes.
full_output.methodology: The study employed multi-parameter microbiota flow cytometry (mMFC) and 16S rRNA sequencing to analyze bacterial phenotypes and taxonomic compositions in CD patients and healthy controls.

full_output.paper_title: The fly route of extended-spectrum-β-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae dissemination in a cattle farm: from the ecosystem to the molecular scale.

blaCTX-M-15.evidence_note: The bla CTX-M-15 gene was found to confer resistance to ceftazidime, ceftriaxone, and ampicillin in ESBL E. coli isolates. The gene was located in a transposon carried by a non-mobilizing multi-replicative plasmid.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla CTX-M-15 and bla TEM-1B as key resistance genes in ESBL-producing E. coli and Enterobacter cloacae complex Taxon 4 isolates from a cattle farm, highlighting their role in resistance and the potential of flies as vectors for their dissemination.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MIC testing, and RT-qPCR were used to analyze resistance genes and their expression in ESBL-producing isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro antimicrobial susceptibility of clinical isolates from adult and paediatric patients in Jordan: Antimicrobial Testing Leadership and Surveillance (ATLAS) 2010-2021.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several beta-lactamase genes, including CTX-M-15, NDM-5, OXA-48, and CTX-M-9-type, which were associated with resistance to various antibiotics in clinical isolates from Jordan.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using CLSI broth microdilution methodology, and beta-lactamase genes were screened using multiplex PCR assays.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial burden and drug-resistant bacteria in healthcare workers' mobile phones: a study in Puerto Rican outpatient clinics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of drug-resistant bacteria on healthcare workers' mobile phones, including S. aureus carrying the pvl gene and the absence of mecA gene indicating no methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) in the isolates.
full_output.methodology: Swab samples from mobile phones were analyzed using biochemical, enzymatic, and molecular techniques including PCR for detection of resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Embedding a ribonuclease in the spore crust couples gene expression to spore development in Bacillus subtilis.
full_output.key_findings: KapD, a 3′-exoribonuclease, is essential for normal adhesiveness of spore surface layers and regulates the stability of sigK mRNA through CotY-mediated sequestration.
full_output.methodology: Fluorescence microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, in-vitro activity assays, genetic manipulation, and biochemical purification.

full_output.paper_title: Inactivation of glutathione S-transferase alpha 4 blocks Enterococcus faecalis-induced bystander effect by promoting macrophage ferroptosis.
full_output.key_findings: Inactivation of Gsta4 blocks E. faecalis-induced bystander effect by promoting macrophage ferroptosis, reducing inflammation and potentially preventing CRC.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the distribution of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and potential pathogens in different habitats of the Liaohe Estuary, highlighting the enrichment of aminoglycoside resistance genes in water and soil, and the dominance of certain pathogenic bacteria in specific habitats.
full_output.methodology: Meta-analysis of bacterial communities, taxonomic assignment of potential pathogens, prediction of functional profiles, and network analysis to explore interactions among microorganisms, ARGs, and MGEs.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluating the antibacterial efficacy of bee venom against multidrug-resistant pathogenic bacteria: Escherichia coli, Salmonella typhimurium, and Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antibacterial efficacy of bee venom (BV) against multidrug-resistant strains of Escherichia coli, Salmonella typhimurium, and Enterococcus faecalis, revealing high antibacterial activity with notable minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentrations (MBC).
full_output.methodology: The study utilized GC-MS for chemical analysis of bee venom, MIC and MBC assays, and disc diffusion method for comparing antibacterial activity against conventional antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Targeted sputum sequencing for rapid and broad drug resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a single 17-plex PCR assay covering 16 key resistance genes for rapid detection of drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis using nanopore sequencing. The method enabled accurate antimicrobial resistance predictions within a day of sample collection, with a cost under $35 per sample.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a single 17-plex PCR assay with thermo-protection buffer for DNA preparation, followed by nanopore sequencing and analysis with the ARapidTb tool.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel medium-throughput screening system for identifying and characterizing N-acyl L-homoserine lactonases (AHLs), which hydrolyze bacterial communication signals and interfere with quorum sensing. full_output.paper_title: Carbapenemase-Producing Enterobacterales: An Increasing Threat to Australian Liver Transplant Recipients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) as an increasing threat to Australian liver transplant recipients, with Klebsiella pneumoniae being the most common species carrying the New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase (NDM) gene. The study highlights the importance of enhanced screening for CPE colonization and infection in this vulnerable population.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing CPE isolates through whole genome sequencing and clinical data.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that ZnO@APTES quantum dots exhibit potent antibacterial activity against MRSA without inducing resistance, highlighting their potential as a novel treatment for antibiotic-resistant infections.
full_output.methodology: The study synthesized and characterized ZnO@APTES quantum dots using microwave-assisted methods and evaluated their antibacterial efficacy through MIC, MBC, biofilm inhibition, and resistance induction assays.

full_output.paper_title: Manipulated Slow Release of Florfenicol Hydrogels for Effective Treatment of Anti-Intestinal Bacterial Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed florfenicol hydrogels for slow release at intestinal infection sites, showing enhanced antibacterial activity against E. coli compared to free florfenicol.
full_output.methodology: Hydrogels were formulated using sodium alginate and calcium chloride, characterized for physical properties, stability, pH responsiveness, and antibacterial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Development and experimental validation of dephosphorylation-related biomarkers to assess prognosis and immunotherapeutic response in gliomas.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CDC25A as a key dephosphorylation-related gene that influences temozolomide (TMZ) resistance in glioma cells, with experimental validation showing that its overexpression increases TMZ sensitivity and knockdown decreases it.
full_output.methodology: The study used LASSO regression and Cox regression to identify 12 dephosphorylation-related genes, followed by experimental validation through overexpression and knockdown of CDC25A in glioma cell lines and assessment of TMZ sensitivity.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and antimicrobial evaluation of a new hybrid bis-cyanoacrylamide-based-piperazine containing sulphamethoxazole moiety against rheumatoid arthritis-associated pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated a new hybrid compound combining piperazine and sulphamethoxazole for antimicrobial activity against various pathogens associated with rheumatoid arthritis. The compound showed significant antibacterial and antifungal effects, particularly against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity was assessed using disc-diffusion and MIC methods, along with molecular docking studies to analyze interactions with target proteins.

full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, chitinase activity assays, growth experiments, and RT-qPCR for gene expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Development of novel broad-spectrum amphipathic antimicrobial peptides against multidrug-resistant bacteria through a rational combination strategy.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed P-α-02-B, a novel broad-spectrum amphipathic antimicrobial peptide with potent antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant bacteria, showing superior plasma stability and synergistic effects with levofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Peptide design, synthesis, and evaluation of antimicrobial activity, stability, and biofilm disruption through MIC assays, time-killing kinetics, and biofilm assays.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity-Oriented Synthesis and Antibiofilm Evaluation of Furan-2-Carboxamides.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of furan-2-carboxamides as antibiofilm agents against P. aeruginosa, highlighting carbohydrazide 4b as the most active compound with 58% biofilm inhibition. These compounds also showed reductions in quorum sensing-related virulence factors such as pyocyanin and proteases.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of various furan-2-carboxamides, their evaluation for antibiofilm activity using the crystal violet assay, and molecular docking studies to understand their mechanism of action.

full_output.paper_title: Gender-specific antibiotic-resistance patterns and characterization of bacterial flora of undergraduate students' mobile phones and associated factors at a Nigerian university.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial isolates from undergraduate students' mobile phones, highlighting the prevalence of antibiotic resistance among these isolates.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolates were identified using 16S rRNA sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion assay.

full_output.paper_title: Viral Mimetic Bacterial Outer Membrane Vesicles for Targeting Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of viral mimetic bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) displaying the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein receptor-binding domain (RBD) for targeting angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2). These OMVs were shown to block ACE2 interactions and induce neutralizing antibodies.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized E. coli-derived OMVs engineered with the Ag43 autotransporter system to display the SARS-CoV-2 RBD. Techniques included trypsin treatment, SDS-PAGE, SPR, ELISA, and in vivo experiments in mice.

full_output.paper_title: Increased rate of multidrug-resistant gram-negative bacterial infections in hospitalized immunocompromised pediatric patients.

full_output.paper_title: Botulinum neurotoxins exploit host digestive proteases to boost their oral toxicity via activating OrfXs/P47.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that OrfXs/P47 proteins, specifically OrfX1, OrfX2, OrfX3, and P47, play a critical role in enhancing the oral toxicity of BoNT/E. These proteins are necessary for the effective oral toxicity of BoNT/E, and their interaction with NTNH is vital for this process.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR/Cas9 engineering, cryo-EM, pull-down assays, and in vivo mouse bioassays were used to analyze the role of OrfXs/P47 in BoNT/E toxicity.

full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on ESBL- and carbapenemase-producing Gram-negative bacteria in UTIs in Ethiopia.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of antimicrobial resistance in Glaesserella parasuis in South China using whole-genome sequencing.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in Glaesserella parasuis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Pandemic one health clones of Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae producing CTX-M-14, CTX-M-27, CTX-M-55 and CTX-M-65 ESβLs among companion animals in northern Ecuador.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several mutations in genes associated with resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, streptomycin, levofloxacin, and para-aminosalicylic acid in Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains from TB-DM patients in Changping District, Beijing, China.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and drug susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains.

full_output.paper_title: LD-transpeptidase-mediated cell envelope remodeling enables developmental transitions and survival in Coxiella burnetii and Legionella pneumophila.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies lpg1386 as an LD-transpeptidase involved in cell envelope remodeling, leading to susceptibility to carbapenem antibiotics in survival variants of Legionella pneumophila.
full_output.methodology: Peptidoglycan extraction, HPLC, LC-MS/MS, RT-qPCR, and susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Fecal carriage of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli in South American camelids and biosecurity practices among farms in northern Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaCTX-M and blaTEM genes in ESBL-producing E. coli isolates from South American camelids in northern Italy, highlighting the presence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study involved PCR analysis to detect ESBL-encoding genes in E. coli isolates from fecal samples of South American camelids.

full_output.paper_title: The influence of depth on the global deep-sea plasmidome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antibiotic resistance genes such as aadA27, ANT3-PRIME, and TEM-116 in plasmid sequence contigs from deep-sea metagenomes, with aminoglycoside resistance being prevalent in the Atlantic Ocean and beta-lactamase resistance in the Pacific Ocean.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics pipeline for analyzing metagenomic data to detect and characterize plasmid sequences and their associated resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome evaluation and prophages characterization associated with genome of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii UOL-KIMZ-24-2.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in the carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii strain UOL-KIMZ-24-2, including blaOXA-66, blaOXA-23, blaOXA-25, aph(6)-Id, aph(3)-Ib, armA, mph(E), msr(E), and tet(B). These genes contribute to resistance against various antibiotics, including beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, macrolides, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mobile genetic elements in the strain UOL-KIMZ-24-2.

full_output.paper_title: Fecal carriage of carbapenemase and AmpC-β-lactamase producers among extended spectrum β-Lactamase-producing E. coli and Klebsiella spp. isolates in patients attending hospitals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified NDM-producing E. coli and Klebsiella spp. as carbapenemase producers, highlighting their role in multidrug resistance. AmpC-β-lactamase producers were also detected, contributing to resistance against various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic detection of carbapenemase and AmpC-β-lactamase production using immunochromatographic tests and disk diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial activity of adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cell secretome against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mecA, ermA, and ermB genes as contributors to resistance in MRSA isolates against AD-MSC secretome.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing of resistance genes in MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Azole Resistance and ERG11 Mutation in Clinical Isolates of Candida tropicalis.

ERG11.notes: Mutations in ERG11 were the main resistance mechanism identified in C. tropicalis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the ERG11 gene as the primary mechanism of azole resistance in C. tropicalis isolates, with Y132F and Y257N being the most prevalent.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of the ERG11 gene, antifungal susceptibility testing, and RT-qPCR for gene expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Deep-Sea Ecosystems as an Unexpected Source of Antibiotic Resistance Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a wide range of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in deep-sea environments, highlighting the diversity and distribution of these genes across different deep-sea ecosystems. It emphasizes the role of metagenomic approaches in uncovering ARGs and their potential hosts.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized metagenomic sequencing approaches, including short-read-based (SRB) and assembled-contig-based (ACB) methods, to analyze ARGs in deep-sea samples.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activities of Polysaccharide-Rich Extracts from the Irish Seaweed Alaria esculenta, Generated Using Green and Conventional Extraction Technologies, Against Foodborne Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the antimicrobial activity of polysaccharide-rich extracts from the Irish seaweed Alaria esculenta against Escherichia coli, with the highest activity observed in extracts prepared using ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE).
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of extracts from A. esculenta using microwave-assisted extraction (MAE), ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE), ultrasound–microwave-assisted extraction (UMAE), and conventional maceration, determining minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) against E. coli and L. innocua.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of Copper Electrodeposited Titanium Surfaces for Antimicrobial and Cytotoxic Effects
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimicrobial and cytotoxic effects of copper electrodeposited titanium (Cu-Ep-Ti) surfaces, demonstrating their ability to reduce bacterial viability and alter macrophage behavior.
full_output.methodology: The study uses microbiological assays, cell culture techniques, and imaging to analyze the effects of Cu-Ep-Ti surfaces on S. aureus and THP-1 macrophages.

full_output.paper_title: Supramolecular Optimization Strategy for Enhancing Antimicrobial Activity and Biosafety of Imidazolium Salts
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces a supramolecular material, NI6R@CB[7]@β-CD, which shows enhanced antibacterial activity against plant pathogens, including Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo), Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri (Xac), and Pseudomonas syringae pv. actinidiae (Psa). It effectively disrupts biofilms, inhibits bacterial motility, and reduces pathogenicity. The material also demonstrates good biosafety towards rice plants, zebrafish, and earthworms.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized supramolecular chemistry to create NI6R@CB[7]@β-CD, evaluating its antibacterial activity through in vitro and in vivo experiments, including biofilm inhibition, bacterial motility assays, and toxicity assessments on model organisms.

full_output.paper_title: Differential responses of Bradyrhizobium sp. SUTN9-2 to plant extracts and implications for endophytic interactions within different host plants.

degP.mechanism: degradation of misfolded or damaged proteins

gumC.mechanism: formation of protective barrier against CAMPs
