full_output.key_findings: Bradyrhizobium sp. SUTN9-2 exhibits resistance mechanisms against cationic antimicrobial peptides (CAMPs) from rice, chili, and tomato plants, including the upregulation of degP, acrAB-TolC efflux pump, and polysaccharide biosynthesis genes.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis, qRT-PCR, and flow cytometry were used to analyze gene expression and cellular responses to plant extracts.

full_output.paper_title: Activity of Aztreonam-avibactam and other β-lactamase inhibitor combinations against Gram-negative bacteria isolated from patients hospitalized with pneumonia in United States medical centers (2020-2022).
full_output.key_findings: Aztreonam-avibactam showed potent in vitro activity against a wide range of Gram-negative bacteria, including carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) isolates. The most common carbapenemase genes identified were blaKPC, blaNDM, and blaSME.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and broth microdilution susceptibility testing were used to identify carbapenemase genes and assess antimicrobial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Seasonal Determination of Antibiotic-Resistant Microorganisms and Ciprofloxacin Residues in Pork and Chicken Meats Collected from Fresh Markets in Chiang Mai, Northern Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ESBL-producing E. coli and K. pneumoniae in pork and chicken meat samples, indicating the presence of beta-lactam resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Microbial culture, MALDI-TOF MS identification, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect antibiotic-resistant organisms and ciprofloxacin residues.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) genes, including aac(6')-Ib-cr, qnrA, qnrS, and oqxAB, as well as GyrA mutations (S83Y, D87Y, S83Y-D87Y, S83R, D87N, D87G) in ciprofloxacin-resistant Salmonella enteritidis isolates. full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Glaesserella parasuis to Macrolides and Characterization of erm(T)-Carrying Mobile Elements on Chromosome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the macrolide resistance gene erm(T) and the A2059G mutation in 23S rRNA in Glaesserella parasuis. It also characterized ICEs carrying erm(T) for the first time in this species.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution, whole-genome sequencing, and bioinformatics analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Tracking the Prevalence of Antibiotic Resistance in Enterococcus Within the Spanish Poultry Industry: Insights from a One Health Approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanB and vanC genes in Enterococcus isolates, indicating vancomycin resistance. Low levels of vancomycin resistance were observed, with only one E. faecium strain showing phenotypic resistance. High resistance rates to tetracyclines and streptogramins were noted, while resistance to vancomycin and tigecycline was low.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic analysis of 215 Enterococcus isolates from Spanish poultry farms, including antimicrobial susceptibility testing and detection of vancomycin-resistant genes via RT-PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Emerging Resistance and Virulence Patterns in Salmonella enterica: Insights into Silver Nanoparticles as an Antimicrobial Strategy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in Salmonella enterica isolates, including blaTEM-1, aadA1, aadA2, aadA5, ant(2")-Ia, aph(3")-Ib, aph(6)-Id, mph(A), tet(A), tet(B), sul1, sul2, sul3, qnrA1, qnrB19, dfrA5, dfrA12, dfrA17, cmlA1, and cmlA5, which confer resistance to β-lactams, aminoglycosides, tetracyclines, sulfonamides, fluoroquinolones, trimethoprim, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in Salmonella enterica isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance Genes in Clinical Escherichia coli Strains from Livestock and Poultry in Shandong Province, China During 2015-2020.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes in clinical Escherichia coli strains from livestock and poultry in Shandong Province, including bla CTX-M, bla TEM, bla OXA, bla CMY-2, bla NDM-5, mcr-1.1, mcr-3.24, and tet(X4). These genes were associated with resistance to multiple antibiotics, highlighting the complexity of antimicrobial resistance in these isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and ResFinder database analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive Analysis of blaCTX-M1 Gene Expression Alongside iutA, csgA, and kpsMII Virulence Genes in Septicemic Escherichia coli Using Real-Time PCR.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaCTX-M1 as a key beta-lactamase gene contributing to resistance against several antibiotics in E. coli isolates from septicemic patients, alongside the upregulation of virulence genes like kpsMII and csgA.
full_output.methodology: PCR, real-time PCR, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to analyze gene expression and resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: First Detection and Genomic Characterization of Linezolid-Resistant Enterococcus faecalis Clinical Isolates in Bulgaria.

23S rDNA.evidence_note: The C2163T mutation in the 23S rDNA of Efs966-bg was identified through whole-genome sequencing and is associated with linezolid resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of linezolid-resistant Enterococcus faecalis isolates in Bulgaria, identifying the optrA gene and specific 23S rDNA mutations as key resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and phylogenomic analysis were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Advanced Large-Stokes-Shift Fluorescent Probe for the Detection of Biothiols: Facilitating Accurate Indirect Measurement of β-Lactamases.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel fluorescent probe, Bibc-DNBS, capable of detecting biothiols and indirectly measuring β-lactamase activity. The probe exhibits a large Stokes shift and shows high sensitivity and selectivity for biothiols, demonstrating potential for real-time monitoring of biothiols and β-lactamases in biological systems.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design and synthesis of the fluorescent probe Bibc-DNBS, along with its application in detecting biothiols and β-lactamases through fluorescence spectroscopy, HPLC, and mass spectrometry analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting Bacterial Cell Division with Benzodioxane-Benzamide FtsZ Inhibitors as a Novel Strategy to Fight Gram-Positive Ovococcal Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies benzodioxane-benzamide inhibitors that target FtsZ in Streptococcus pneumoniae, demonstrating bactericidal activity and affecting cell division and morphology.
full_output.methodology: The study determined MICs, assessed growth and viability, and analyzed FtsZ assembly under crowded conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance of Wolbachia to Trimethoprim: Insights into Genes Encoding Dihydrofolate Reductase, Thymidylate Synthase and Serine Hydroxymethyltransferase in the Rickettsiales.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that Wolbachia strain w Stri exhibits resistance to trimethoprim, with the DHFR enzyme containing amino acid substitutions associated with trimethoprim resistance in E. coli. Additionally, it was found that some Wolbachia genomes lack the folA gene encoding DHFR, indicating possible genomic streamlining.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics analysis, sequence alignment, and experimental validation of DHFR enzyme activity.

full_output.paper_title: A Four-Year Study of Antibiotic Resistance, Prevalence and Biofilm-Forming Ability of Uropathogens Isolated from Community- and Hospital-Acquired Urinary Tract Infections in Southern Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified differences in antibiotic resistance patterns between community- and hospital-acquired uropathogens, highlighting higher resistance rates in gram-negative bacteria. It also found an inverse correlation between biofilm production and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of urine samples from a university hospital in southern Italy, involving bacterial isolation, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and biofilm formation assessment.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriophage and Phage-Encoded Depolymerase Exhibit Antibacterial Activity Against K9-Type Acinetobacter baumannii in Mouse Sepsis and Burn Skin Infection Models.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and functional analysis of SAM-dependent N-methyltransferases involved in ovoselenol and ovothiol biosynthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology of Type F Clostridium perfringens Among Diarrheal Patients and Virulence-Resistance Dynamics - 11 Provinces, China, 2024.

full_output.paper_title: Interspecies interactions mediated by arginine metabolism enhance the stress tolerance of Fusobacterium nucleatum against Bifidobacterium animalis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various β-lactamase genes including bla CTX-M, bla SHV, bla OXY, bla VEB, bla CMY-59, and bla DHA-1 in ceftriaxone-resistant Enterobacterales. Additionally, mutations in the promoter or attenuator regions of the c-ampC gene in E. coli were investigated, but they did not significantly contribute to ceftriaxone resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Developing a clinical prediction model to modify empirical antibiotics for non-typhoidal Salmonella bloodstream infection in children under-five in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a clinical prediction model to guide the choice of empirical antibiotics for non-typhoidal Salmonella (NTS) bloodstream infections in children under-five in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The model showed good discrimination with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.79 and good calibration. The model can help clinicians choose between standard-of-care and alternative antibiotics for drug-resistant NTS.
full_output.methodology: The study used a prospective observational cohort design with multivariable logistic regression to develop a prediction model for NTS bloodstream infection. The model was internally validated using bootstrapping.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanistic insights into the haem degradation pathway of HemS

mutations_found.effect_on_function: The F104A mutation affects the double phenylalanine gate, which regulates NADH access to haem, thereby influencing the haem breakdown process.

The double phe-gate regulates NADH access to haem via a sophisticated set of interactions which extend outwards to the pocket edge, thus causing it to exercise tight control over the orientation which NADH is in before the hydride transfer event.

The F104I mutation has a lower E ‡ value than the WT which, at face value, would potentially suggest that this mutation will bring NADH and haem together at a faster rate. However, a comparison of the landscapes reveals that there are fewer low-energy configurations where NADH and haem are in close proximity for F104I, and its landscape has many more low-lying kinetic traps.

F104I.evidence_note: The F104I mutation was studied in the context of its effect on the NADH-regulating double phenylalanine gate in HemS, and its impact on the haem breakdown process was analyzed using computational and experimental methods.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the critical role of the double phe-gate (F104 and F199) in the haem degradation pathway of HemS, demonstrating that mutations in these residues significantly alter the NADH-haem interaction and reduce the efficiency of haem breakdown.
full_output.methodology: Computational modeling, stopped-flow spectroscopy, and X-ray crystallography were used to analyze the effects of mutations on HemS function.

full_output.paper_title: Plant Diversity Reduces the Risk of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Agroecosystems.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that increased plant diversity significantly reduces the abundance of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) in agricultural soils. full_output.methodology: High-throughput qPCR, metagenomic sequencing, and statistical analyses were used to evaluate the impact of plant diversity on ARGs and MGEs in different soil types.

full_output.paper_title: Deletion of ESX-3 and ESX-4 secretion systems in Mycobacterium abscessus results in highly impaired pathogenicity.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that ESX-3 and ESX-4 secretion systems are essential for the pathogenicity of Mycobacterium abscessus, affecting substrate secretion, macrophage infection, and in vivo virulence.
full_output.methodology: Generation of single and double mutants lacking eccC3 and eccC4, followed by characterization of their secretion profiles, subcellular localization, and effects on macrophage infection and mouse virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative microbial metagenomic analysis of drinking water plants and wastewater treatment plants in Istanbul.

Erm.mechanism: confers resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, and streptogramin B

full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial resistance gene markers such as ANT(3"), Erm, and Sul in raw wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) samples, indicating the presence of resistance to aminoglycosides, erythromycin, and sulfonamides. These genes were not detected in drinking water treatment plant (DWTP) samples.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis using next-generation sequencing and bioinformatics tools to identify microbial communities and antimicrobial resistance genes in water samples from DWTPs and WWTPs.

full_output.paper_title: Population genetic analysis of clinical Mycobacterium abscessus complex strains in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes and mutations in M. abscessus complex strains in China, including mtrA, RbpA, bla MAB, erm(41), and erm(46) for resistance to various antibiotics, as well as mutations in rrs, rrl, and gyrA contributing to aminoglycoside, macrolide, and fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of 360 MABC genomes using bioinformatics tools for AMR gene and mutation detection.

full_output.paper_title: Industrialization drives the gut microbiome and resistome of the Chinese populations.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies differences in the gut microbiome and resistome between eastern and western Chinese populations, with western populations showing higher abundance and diversity of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Key ARGs include tet(Q), erm(B), and erm(F).
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of 1,382 gut microbiome samples from Chinese populations.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the effect of sequential antibiotic exposure in resistant Escherichia coli causing urinary tract infections: a proof of principle study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaTEM-1 as a mecillinam resistance gene and non-synonymous substitutions in gyrA, parC, and parE as ciprofloxacin resistance mechanisms in E. coli isolates.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and susceptibility testing of E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The complex development of psoralen-interstrand crosslink resistance in Escherichia coli requires AcrR inactivation, retention of a marbox sequence, and one of three MarA, SoxS, or Rob global regulators.

acrR.notes: Deletion of the entire acrR coding region results in no resistance to psoralen-UVA.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that inactivation of the acrR gene, along with retention of the marbox sequence and the presence of MarA, SoxS, or Rob global regulators, is essential for psoralen-UVA resistance in E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, plasmid construction, and survival assays were used to investigate the role of acrR and its regulators in psoralen-UVA resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified E. coli as the most common pathogen in urinary tract infections (UTIs) among women with preterm labor, followed by Enterococcus, Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Proteus mirabilis. Antibiotic susceptibility patterns showed ceftriaxone and cefixime as the most effective agents against these pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed urine cultures and antibiotic susceptibility patterns of 385 pregnant women with preterm labor.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the antibacterial and anti-biofilm activity of two Iranian medical-grade kinds of honey on multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that both Thyme and Citrus honeys exhibited significant antibacterial and anti-biofilm activity against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) for both honeys was 6.25% v/v, and they showed effective biofilm inhibition, especially at higher concentrations.
full_output.methodology: The study used well-diffusion, broth microdilution, and crystal violet assays to evaluate the antibacterial and anti-biofilm properties of the honeys against P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting AI-2 quorum sensing: harnessing natural products against Streptococcus suis biofilm infection.

luxS.validation_method: virtual screening and in vitro enzyme activity inhibition assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies salvianolic acid A (SAA) and rhapontin (RH) as natural products that inhibit AI-2 quorum sensing in Streptococcus suis by targeting the LuxS protein, thus reducing biofilm formation and adhesion abilities.
full_output.methodology: Virtual screening, molecular docking, enzyme activity inhibition assays, biofilm inhibition assays, and Galleria mellonella larval model experiments.

full_output.paper_title: CAM/TMA-DPH as a promising alternative to SYTO9/PI for cell viability assessment in bacterial biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces CAM/TMA-DPH staining as a reliable alternative to SYTO9/PI for assessing bacterial biofilm viability, demonstrating strong correlations with CFU counts across multiple species.
full_output.methodology: The study used CLSM and ImageJ-based biofilm surface coverage quantification to compare CAM/TMA-DPH and SYTO9/PI staining methods for assessing biofilm viability.

full_output.paper_title: Decoding MexB efflux pump genes: structural, molecular, and phylogenetic analysis of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

MexB.validation_method: presence of MexB genes in resistant isolates, MIC reduction upon CCCP addition

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of MexB efflux pump genes in multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, which contribute to resistance against carbapenems such as meropenem and imipenem.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, Sanger sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and structural modeling were used to analyze MexB efflux pump genes in P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1C promotes EMT-associated cisplatin resistance in non-small cell lung cancer cells.

CPT1C.validation_method: knockdown and overexpression experiments showing altered cisplatin sensitivity

full_output.key_findings: CPT1C promotes cisplatin resistance in non-small cell lung cancer cells by inducing EMT.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockdown and overexpression experiments, western blot analysis, MTT assay, and wound healing assay.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro susceptibility pattern of Rhodococcus equi isolated from patients to antimicrobials recommended exclusively to humans, to domestic animals and to both.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all 41 R. equi isolates were susceptible to tigecycline and vancomycin, which are recommended exclusively for humans, while some drugs used in both humans and animals exhibited high efficacy. However, high multidrug resistance was observed, including resistance to florfenicol, ceftiofur, and enrofloxacin, which are used exclusively for animal therapy.
full_output.methodology: In vitro antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the disk diffusion method according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Study of the probability of resistance to phage infection in a collection of clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in relation to the presence of Pf phages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 12 Pf phages in clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa from cystic fibrosis patients. These phages encode various anti-phage defense systems, including Gabija, IetAS, Avs, PfsE, ShosTA, Kiwa, TA, and Retron, which contribute to phage resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, phylogenetic studies, and anti-phage defense system detection using PADLOC.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of sulopenem antimicrobial activity using in vitro time-kill kinetics, synergy, post-antibiotic effect, and sub-inhibitory MIC effect methods against Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antimicrobial activity of sulopenem against Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, focusing on its bactericidal effects and post-antibiotic effect (PAE).
full_output.methodology: The study employed in vitro time-kill kinetics, synergy testing, post-antibiotic effect (PAE), and sub-inhibitory MIC effect (PAE-SME) methods to evaluate sulopenem's antimicrobial activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the prevalence of ST131-O16 and ST131-O25b clones among extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing E. coli isolates causing bloodstream infections in Iran, highlighting the presence of resistance genes bla CTX-M−15, bla OXA−48, and bla CMY.
full_output.methodology: PCR screening for resistance genes and molecular characterization of E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Microbial Contamination of Percutaneous Endoscopic Gastrostomy Tube and Nasogastric Tube with Drug-Resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that PEGs and NGTs were contaminated with microorganisms, including drug-resistant bacteria. Specifically, 19.6% of PEGs and 23.7% of NGTs harbored drug-resistant bacteria. Among the resistant bacteria, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE) were identified in NGTs, while carbapenem-resistant, aminoglycoside-resistant, and fluoroquinolone-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Pseudomonas spp. were found in PEGs.
full_output.methodology: Microorganisms were cultured from PEGs and NGTs, and antimicrobial susceptibility was determined using the broth microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotics change the population growth rate heterogeneity and morphology of bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates how antibiotics affect bacterial growth rate heterogeneity and morphology, identifying that cell wall synthesis inhibitors induce the highest population growth rate heterogeneity (PGRH) and significant morphological changes. It introduces a novel morphological parameter, MOR50, for rapid MIC estimation.
full_output.methodology: Utilized the Multipad Agarose Plate (MAP) platform to track growth rates and morphology of E. coli, S. aureus, and P. aeruginosa under 14 antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Study of fluoroquinolones resistance in rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis patients in Beijing: Characteristics, trends, and treatment outcomes.

gyrA.notes: Assoc w R

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the gyrA gene associated with fluoroquinolone resistance in rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis patients in Beijing, highlighting the emergence of resistance and the need for targeted treatment strategies.
full_output.methodology: The study involved drug-sensitivity testing and sequencing of fluoroquinolone resistance genes in clinical isolates from patients with rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Emerging Resistance Mechanisms in Gram-Positive Bacteria Isolated From Septicemia Cases in ICUs: A Focus on Genotypic Insights.

mecA.validation_method: PCR detection of mecA gene in methicillin-resistant isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA, icaA, and icaD genes in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative Staphylococci isolates, emphasizing their role in methicillin resistance and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving PCR detection of resistance genes and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of concurrently transmissible mcr-9 and carbapenemase genes in bloodborne colistin-resistant Enterobacter cloacae complex isolated from ICU patients in Kolkata, India.

acrA.notes: Deletion in acrA was observed in mcr-9-producing colistin-resistant isolates.

phoP.notes: Mutations in phoP were found in mcr-9-producing colistin-resistant isolates.

phoQ.notes: Mutations in phoQ were found in mcr-9-producing colistin-resistant isolates.

pmrB.notes: high expression in colistin-resistant isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mcr-9 gene as a significant contributor to colistin resistance in Enterobacter cloacae complex isolates, alongside carbapenemase genes. Mutations in regulatory systems like phoP and phoQ were also linked to resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized qPCR, MIC testing, and sequencing to identify and characterize AMR genes and mutations in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic action of mucoactive drugs and phages against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the synergistic effects of mucoactive agents N-acetylcysteine (NAC) and ambroxol hydrochloride (AMB) with phages against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae, revealing that NAC and AMB can enhance phage efficacy under specific conditions.
full_output.methodology: The study used phage-host interaction experiments, bacterial growth assays, and phage stability measurements to evaluate the effects of NAC and AMB on phage activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies JMJD1B and JMJD1C as genes that promote PARPi resistance in ovarian cancer cells, and shows that their genetic depletion or pharmacological inhibition with methylstat enhances PARPi sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas9 loss-of-function screen, genetic depletion, and drug interaction analysis.

full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing, Raman-D2O labeling, and correlation analysis were used to identify and characterize antibiotic resistance genes in the gut microbiome of giant African snails under varying soil temperatures.

full_output.paper_title: No Emergence of Colistin Resistance in the Respiratory Tract of Lung Transplant Patients Treated With Inhaled Colistin.

pmrA.encodes: two-component system (PmrAB) associated with colistin resistance

mutations_found.validated_by: whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study found that inhaled colistin (IC) did not promote the emergence of colistin-resistant Gram-negative bacilli (GNB) in the respiratory tract of lung transplant patients. Mutations in the pmrA, pmrB, and parS genes were identified in some isolates, contributing to colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify mutations in colistin-resistant strains.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotype-Specific Semi-Mechanistic Modelling of Florfenicol Time-Kill Curves in G. Parasuis Compared to Other Respiratory Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that none of the isolates possessed resistance genes floR, cfr, fexA, or fexB, indicating susceptibility to florfenicol. However, distinct phenotypes ('slow-kill' and 'fast-kill') were observed in G. parasuis, affecting the required drug concentrations for bacterial eradication.
full_output.methodology: PCR screening for resistance genes and time-kill assays to evaluate bacterial response to florfenicol.
full_output.sample_size: A. pleuropneumoniae (n = 5), G. parasuis (n = 7), and P. multocida (n = 5)

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of two gradient diffusion tests to determine susceptibility to aztreonam and ceftazidime-avibactam in combination.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates two gradient diffusion methods for determining susceptibility to the aztreonam-ceftazidime-avibactam (ATM-CZA) combination, highlighting the strip cross (SX) method as highly accurate and reproducible for clinical use.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the performance of two gradient diffusion synergy testing methods (side-by-side and strip cross) against reference broth microdilution for ATM-CZA susceptibility testing in various bacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Interactions within higher-order antibiotic combinations do not influence the rate of adaptation in bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that neither net nor emergent interactions in three-drug combinations influenced the rate or frequency of adaptation in Staphylococcus epidermidis.

full_output.sample_size: Six populations were independently evolved for each drug treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive analysis of antimicrobial resistance dynamics among broiler and duck intensive production systems.

tetH.encodes: major facilitator superfamily antibiotic efflux pump

salA.organisms_tested_in: Ross 308 broiler chickens, Cherry Valley ducks

full_output.key_findings: The study identified numerous antimicrobial resistance genes in broiler and duck production systems, with tetracycline resistance being the most prevalent. Key genes included tet36, tetH, tetX3, tetX5, and tetT, which were associated with various bacterial species and conferred resistance to tetracycline. Other significant genes included mel, msrE, abaQ, OXA-921, and salA, which were linked to macrolide, fluoroquinolone, penam, and lincosamide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Next-generation shotgun sequencing was used to analyze antimicrobial resistance genes in biological and environmental samples from broiler and duck farms.

full_output.paper_title: Regional insights on the prevalence and antimicrobial susceptibility pattern of carbapenem and colistin-resistant gram-negative bacteria: an observational cross-sectional study from Karachi, Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 1.7% colistin resistance among carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacteria, primarily Klebsiella species, highlighting the therapeutic challenge posed by limited antibiotic alternatives.
full_output.methodology: Observational cross-sectional study analyzing antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Abundant geographical divergence of Clostridioides difficile infection in China: a prospective multicenter cross-sectional study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates to clindamycin (81.3%), erythromycin (63.6%), and moxifloxacin (24.0%) among C. difficile isolates in China, with multidrug-resistant strains detected in multiple regions.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing via E-test strips and molecular characterization through MLST and toxin gene profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Conflict-associated wounds and burns infected with GLASS pathogens in the Eastern Mediterranean Region: A systematic review.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights high rates of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) among civilians with conflict-associated wounds and burns in the Eastern Mediterranean Region, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review of literature focusing on GLASS priority pathogens in conflict-affected countries in the Eastern Mediterranean Region.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative functional analysis of a new CDR1-like ABC transporter gene in multidrug resistance and virulence between Magnaporthe oryzae and Trichophyton mentagrophytes.

MoCDR1.role_in_paper: involved in drug resistance and pathogenicity
MoCDR1.source: Comparative functional analysis of a new CDR1-like ABC transporter gene in multidrug resistance and virulence between Magnaporthe oryzae and Trichophyton mentagrophytes.
MoCDR1.evidence_note: MoCDR1 disruption caused hypersensitivity to multidrugs, and impaired conidiation, appressorium formation, and pathogenicity. TmCDR1 effectively rescued the drug sensitivity and virulence of ΔMocdr1 and mediated the drug resistance and animal skin infection in T. mentagrophytes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MoCDR1 and TmCDR1 as ABC transporter genes involved in multidrug resistance and virulence in Magnaporthe oryzae and Trichophyton mentagrophytes, respectively. Both genes confer resistance to various antifungal agents and are essential for pathogenicity.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, and phenotypic analysis were used to assess the role of MoCDR1 and TmCDR1 in drug resistance and virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Engineered Bacillus subtilis WB600/ZD prevents Salmonella Infantis-induced intestinal inflammation and alters the colon microbiota in a mouse model.

ZD.mechanism: bacteriostatic activity against various pathogenic bacteria
ZD.validation_method: fermentation broth supernatant inhibits bacterial growth

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the engineered Bacillus subtilis WB600/ZD strain effectively prevents Salmonella Infantis-induced intestinal inflammation and alters the colon microbiota in a mouse model by secreting the antimicrobial peptide ZD.
full_output.methodology: The study involved genetic modification of Bacillus subtilis to express ZD, followed by evaluation of its effects on Salmonella Infantis infection in mice through various physiological and molecular assays.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical and epidemiological differences in staphylococcal osteoarticular infections: insights for developing hospital-based infection control interventions.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the distinct epidemiological and clinical characteristics of osteoarticular infections (OAI) caused by Staphylococcus aureus and Coagulase-negative Staphylococcus (CoNS). It identifies significant differences in antimicrobial resistance patterns between these organisms, with CoNS showing higher resistance to gentamicin, linezolid, teicoplanin, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, while S. aureus exhibits higher resistance to clindamycin.
full_output.methodology: A single-center retrospective study analyzing 458 cases of OAI from 2011 to 2021, including microbiological analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: First whole genome sequencing of Staphylococcus aureus isolates from Iraq: Insights into zoonotic relations and biofilm-related genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the genomes of five Staphylococcus aureus isolates from Iraq, focusing on biofilm-related genes and their roles in biofilm formation. Several genes associated with biofilm formation were identified and characterized.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and biofilm formation assays were performed on the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and molecular detection of mecA and lukD genes from livestock-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolated in raw chicken meats sold in Abakaliki, Nigeria.

mecA.validation_method: polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and phenotypic testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of mecA and lukD genes in livestock-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (LA-MRSA) isolated from raw chicken meats in Abakaliki, Nigeria, highlighting a public health risk.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and identification of S. aureus, detection of LA-MRSA using disk diffusion, and molecular detection of mecA and lukD genes via PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Cefepime-taniborbactam and ceftibuten-ledaborbactam maintain activity against KPC variants that lead to ceftazidime-avibactam resistance.
full_output.key_findings: Cefepime-taniborbactam (FEP-TAN) and ceftibuten-ledaborbactam (CTB-LED) maintain activity against KPC variants that lead to ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) resistance. Mutations in KPC-2 and KPC-3, including D179Y, V240G, and T243M, reduce the effectiveness of CAZ-AVI but not FEP-TAN or CTB-LED.
full_output.methodology: Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing, kinetic analysis, and molecular modeling were used to assess the activity of beta-lactamase inhibitors against KPC variants.

full_output.paper_title: Differential producibility analysis reveals drug-associated carbon and nitrogen metabolite expressions in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies oxaloacetate (OAA) as a key metabolite upregulated across all four drugs (BDQ, INH, RIF, CLA) indicating a common metabolic response in Mtb to drug stress. It also highlights the reprogramming of central carbon and nitrogen metabolism in Mtb under drug exposure.
full_output.methodology: Genome-scale metabolic modeling combined with differential producibility analysis (DPA) and RNA-seq to identify drug-associated metabolite changes.

full_output.paper_title: Computational and in vitro evaluation of probiotic treatments for nasal Staphylococcus aureus decolonization.
full_output.key_findings: Probiotic treatment with D. pigrum and C. pseudodiphtheriticum effectively prevents S. aureus recolonization in nasal swabs, demonstrating superior decolonization performance compared to antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Computational modeling combined with in vitro experiments using nasal swabs to evaluate probiotic effectiveness against S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Innovative application of ceftriaxone as a quorum sensing inhibitor in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: Ceftriaxone (CRO) and its nickel complex (CRON) were found to inhibit quorum sensing (QS) in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, reducing virulence factors such as biofilm formation, hemolysin, protease, and pyocyanin without affecting bacterial growth. Molecular docking suggested interactions with QS receptors LasR, LasI, and PqsR.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the quorum sensing inhibitory activity of CRO and CRON using reporter strains and molecular docking analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and phenotypic characterization of Chryseomicrobium imtechense from canine pyometra.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of resistance genes to tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, beta-lactams, and multidrug resistance in the genome of Chryseomicrobium imtechense LBV029/19. Specifically, the blaB gene was found to confer resistance to cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and biofilm formation assessment were conducted.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and plasmid conjugation experiments were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms in Salmonella Thompson isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Potential of methanol extracts of Nephelium lappaceum (Sapindaceae) and Hyphaene thebaica (Arecaceae) as adjuvants to enhance the efficacy of antibiotics against critical class priority bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that methanol extracts from Nephelium lappaceum and Hyphaene thebaica had antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, with the leaf extract of N. lappaceum showing the highest activity. These extracts also showed synergistic effects with antibiotics like tetracycline, vancomycin, imipenem, ciprofloxacin, and cefixime, reducing their MIC values significantly.
full_output.methodology: The study used a 96-well microplate serial dilution technique to determine MIC and MBC, along with combination assays to assess synergistic effects with antibiotics. Phytochemical analysis was performed to identify bioactive compounds.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Determination of Colistin Susceptibility by Flow Cytometry Directly from Positive Urine Samples-Preliminary Results.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a rapid and accurate method for determining colistin MIC directly from urine samples using flow cytometry, achieving 99% essential agreement with traditional methods.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated a novel method for determining colistin susceptibility using flow cytometry with the FASTcolistin MIC kit, comparing results with traditional broth microdilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Simultaneous Detection of the Clinically Relevant Carbapenemase Resistance Genes blaKPC, blaOXA48, blaVIM and blaNDM with the Newly Developed Ready-to-Use qPCR CarbaScan LyoBead.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces the qPCR CarbaScan LyoBead assay, a robust and efficient tool for detecting clinically relevant carbapenemase resistance genes, including blaKPC, blaOXA48, blaVIM, and blaNDM. The assay demonstrated 100% specificity and sensitivity across a diverse range of bacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: Development and validation of the qPCR CarbaScan LyoBead assay using genomic DNA from various bacterial strains and comparative analysis with existing methods.

full_output.paper_title: Exploration of the Fusidic Acid Structure Activity Space for Antibiotic Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores modifications to fusidic acid to enhance its activity against Gram-negative bacteria. It identifies that mutations in the fusA and fusE genes confer resistance to fusidic acid.
full_output.methodology: The study involved synthesis and testing of fusidic acid derivatives against various bacterial strains, including S. aureus and E. coli mutants with altered permeability.

full_output.paper_title: Unlocking Antimicrobial Peptides: In Silico Proteolysis and Artificial Intelligence-Driven Discovery from Cnidarian Omics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 3130 Cnidaria Singular AMPs (CnSAs) with non-haemolytic and non-toxic properties, highlighting their potential for biomedical applications and antibiotic development.
full_output.methodology: In silico proteolysis, machine learning, and complex network analysis were used to identify novel antimicrobial peptides from Cnidaria omics data.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Modification of Queen Bee Acid and 10-Hydroxydecanoic Acid with Specific Tripeptides: Rational Design, Organic Synthesis, and Assessment for Prohealing and Antimicrobial Hydrogel Properties.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the creation of novel amphiphiles by modifying queen bee acid (hda) and 10-hydroxydecanoic acid (hdaa) with specific tripeptides, which exhibited antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus. The amphiphile hdaa-ILK-NH2 showed significant inhibition of S. aureus in a disc diffusion assay.
full_output.methodology: The amphiphiles were synthesized using solid-phase peptide synthesis and characterized using NMR and LC-MS/MS. Antimicrobial activity was evaluated using a disc diffusion assay.

full_output.paper_title: Phages carry orphan antitoxin-like enzymes to neutralize the DarTG1 toxin-antitoxin defense system.

adfN.validation_method: ectopic expression in E. coli and plaque assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AdfN as a novel anti-DarTG1 counter-defense element in T-even phages, which functions as a NADAR family DNA ADP-ribosylglycohydrolase to neutralize the DarT1 toxin and enable phage replication in DarTG1-containing bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, ectopic expression, plaque assays, and biochemical analysis were used to validate the function of AdfN.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of molecular resistance and associated risk factors in tuberculosis.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA were associated with fluoroquinolone resistance in MTBC strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the gyrA gene associated with fluoroquinolone resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) strains.
full_output.methodology: Molecular susceptibility testing and multicolor melting curve analysis were used to detect drug resistance mutations in MTBC strains.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular screening to track ceftriaxone-resistant FC428-like Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains' dissemination in four provinces of China, 2019 to 2021.

penA.notes: The A311V mutation is a key ceftriaxone resistance marker.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the penA-60.001, penA-195.001, and penA-232.001 alleles with the A311V mutation as critical for ceftriaxone resistance in FC428-like Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains in China.
full_output.methodology: The study used the HRM-FC428 assay and PCR-sequencing to detect and characterize ceftriaxone-resistant FC428-like strains.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence, Risk Factors, and Antibiotic Resistance Patterns of Salmonella Isolates Obtained From Dairy Farms in Gondar Town, Northwest Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Salmonella isolates from dairy farms in Gondar, Ethiopia, showed high resistance to ampicillin (100%) and tetracycline (96.7%), while being highly sensitive to ciprofloxacin (100%) and kanamycin (90%).
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving sample collection from dairy farms, isolation and identification of Salmonella, and antibiotic susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Staphylococcus aureus Causing Contamination in Raw Beef and Meat-Processing Environments in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.

mecA.validation_method: PCR detection of mecA gene in isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA gene, which confers methicillin resistance, in 27.4% of S. aureus isolates from raw beef and surface swabs in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. No vancomycin resistance genes (vanA or vanB) were detected.
full_output.methodology: PCR and disk diffusion methods were used to detect resistance genes and assess antibiotic susceptibility in S. aureus isolates.
full_output.sample_size: 156 raw beef samples and 131 surface swabs

full_output.paper_title: Sepsis in Internal Medicine: blood culture-based subtypes, hospital outcomes, and predictive biomarkers.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR+) sepsis and the association of specific biomarkers with sepsis outcomes. It notes a decline in resistance to certain antibiotics among Gram-negative bacteria but an increase in resistance to piperacillin/tazobactam and carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of sepsis patients in internal medicine units, utilizing clinical and microbiological data to assess outcomes and resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and therapeutic potential of newly isolated bacteriophages against Staphylococcus species in bovine mastitis.
full_output.key_findings: Three newly isolated bacteriophages (OPT-SA02, OPT-SC01, and OPT-SX11) were characterized for their lytic activity against Staphylococcus species, with genomic analysis revealing conserved lysis-related genes (holin and endolysin) responsible for their antibacterial properties.
full_output.methodology: Genomic characterization, TEM analysis, and lytic activity assays were used to evaluate the bacteriophages' properties and their ability to lyse Staphylococcus species.

full_output.paper_title: Phagocyte-Associated Microbes in Crohn's Disease: Pathobionts, Antimicrobial Resistance, and Host Immune Responses

ANT(3\")-Ia.validation_method: quantification of AMR genes among isolates

tet(B).validation_method: quantification of AMR genes among isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AMR genes such as ANT(3")-Ia and tet(B) in E. coli isolates from Crohn's disease (CD) patients, indicating higher expression of antibiotic inactivation enzymes in CD samples compared to controls.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing and quantification of AMR genes in E. coli isolates from CD and control patients.

full_output.paper_title: ACAT1-Mediated ME2 Acetylation Drives Chemoresistance in Ovarian Cancer by Linking Glutaminolysis to Lactate Production.

mutations_found.validated_by: Enzyme activity assay, cell survival and growth assays, lactate production measurements
Enzyme activity assay, cell survival and growth assays, lactate production measurements

ME2.notes: The wild-type ME2 is susceptible to cisplatin, but its acetylation at K156 leads to resistance.

full_output.key_findings: Acetylation of ME2 at lysine 156 is associated with platinum-based chemotherapy resistance in ovarian cancer. Acetylated ME2 promotes lactate production from glutamine, facilitating DNA repair and chemoresistance. Inhibition of ACAT1, the acetyltransferase responsible for ME2 acetylation, restores cisplatin sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: Proteome-wide acetylation analysis, enzyme activity assays, cell survival and growth assays, lactate production measurements, in vivo xenograft models, and targeted shRNA knockdown experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Piceatannol and its analogues alleviate Staphylococcus aureus pathogenesis by targeting β-lactamase biofilms and α-hemolysin.
full_output.key_findings: Piceatannol (pit) and its analogues inhibit β-lactamase activity, reducing the MIC of ampicillin against S. aureus USA300. Pit and pts also inhibit biofilm formation and hemolysis activity of S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: Inhibition experiments, molecular docking, MIC assays, biofilm assays, and hemolysis activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Deciphering the code of resistance: a genomic and transcriptomic exploration of the Cystoisospora suis Holland-I strain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified differential expression of mitochondrial genes CoI, CoIII, and Cytb in the toltrazuril-resistant Cystoisospora suis Holland-I strain, suggesting their potential role in drug resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome DNA sequencing and transcriptomic analyses were performed on C. suis strains to identify genetic variations and differentially expressed genes associated with toltrazuril resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of bacterial pathogens and antimicrobial susceptibility of early-onset sepsis (EOS) among neonates in Palestinian hospitals: a retrospective observational study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the most common gram-positive bacteria as alpha-hemolytic streptococcus, CoNS, GBS, Staphylococcus Aureus, and Enterococcus species, while the most common gram-negative bacteria were E. coli and Klebsiella spp. Resistance patterns showed high resistance to ciprofloxacin among gram-positive organisms and high resistance to ampicillin among gram-negative organisms.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational study analyzing blood cultures and antimicrobial susceptibility data from neonates with EOS.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the performance of targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) for detecting pathogens and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP). tNGS showed high sensitivity and specificity for pathogen identification and AMR detection, particularly for carbapenem, penicillin, cephalosporin, aminoglycoside, and sulfonamide resistance. Key AMR genes identified include ampC, APH, ANT, sul, blaOXA-51, blaOXA-23, blaTEM, blaCTX-M, blaSHV, and blaKPC.
full_output.methodology: The study used targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) combined with antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) to evaluate pathogen and AMR detection in VAP patients.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptome analysis reveals the molecular mechanism of γ-linolenic acid eradicating the biofilm of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium.
full_output.key_findings: γ-linolenic acid (GLA) downregulates the expression of several biofilm-associated genes in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium, including fruA, fruB, sgrA, lpxtg-cwa, tfpp, lafA, lafB, malP, fsrA, and fsrC', and upregulates the expression of fsrBD. GLA also inhibits the Fsr quorum sensing system by suppressing the function of FsrB.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome analysis and qRT-PCR were used to investigate the effects of GLA on gene expression in VRE-fm isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Six VRE-fm isolates and two E. faecalis isolates

full_output.paper_title: BTS1-knockout Saccharomyces cerevisiae with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity through lactic acid accumulation.
full_output.key_findings: BTS1-knockout Saccharomyces cerevisiae exhibits broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity through lactic acid accumulation, effectively inhibiting the growth of various pathogenic bacteria including E. coli and S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of MIC assays, growth curve analysis, biofilm inhibition assays, and in vivo models to evaluate the antimicrobial activity of BTS1-knockout S. cerevisiae.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity in Adaptive Evolution of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Clinical Isolates Under Exposure to Continuous Linezolid Stress in vitro.

23S rRNA.notes: Mutations in the domain V region of the 23S rRNA gene were identified as the main resistance mechanism.

rplC.notes: Mutations in the rplC gene were identified as a secondary resistance mechanism.

rplD.notes: Mutations in the rplD gene were identified as a secondary resistance mechanism.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the domain V region of the 23S rRNA gene and ribosomal protein-encoding genes (rplC and rplD) as the main mechanisms of linezolid resistance in MRSA clinical isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used sequencing and broth microdilution to detect mutations and determine linezolid resistance in MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance of Morganella clinical isolates between 2016 and 2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Morganella clinical isolates, including tet(B), sul1, catA2, sul2, floR, aadA1, and others, contributing to resistance against various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and genomic screening were used to identify AMR genes in Morganella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Improving the Activity and Selectivity of a Scorpion-Derived Peptide, A3a, against Acinetobacter baumannii through Rational Design.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on enhancing the activity and selectivity of the scorpion-derived peptide A3a against Acinetobacter baumannii through rational design. Two novel analogues, A3a[R7K] and A3a[I14W], were developed, showing improved antibacterial potency and selectivity. A3a[I14W] exhibited greater effectiveness against Gram-negative bacteria, particularly A. baumannii, compared to the parent peptide A3a.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, peptide synthesis, and in vitro antibacterial assays to evaluate the performance of A3a and its analogues.

full_output.paper_title: KRAS Mutations Confer NSCLC Drug Resistance Through ALKBH5 PTM-Mediated DNA Repair Pathways

DDB2.mechanism: Regulates nucleotide excision repair (NER) by recognizing and binding to damaged DNA
DDB2.validation_method: Gene knockdown experiments and mRNA stability assays

full_output.key_findings: KRAS mutations promote cisplatin resistance in NSCLC cells by enhancing the expression of DDB2 and XPC through m 6 A methylation, which stabilizes their mRNA and increases NER activity.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression analysis, mRNA stability assays, and xenograft experiments were used to evaluate the role of DDB2 and XPC in KRAS mutation-mediated cisplatin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Fe(3)O(4)@SiO(2)/Schiff-base/Zn (II) nanocomposite functioning as a versatile antimicrobial agent against bacterial and fungal pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces a Fe3O4@SiO2/Schiff-base/Zn(II) nanocomposite with potent antimicrobial activity against bacterial and fungal pathogens, showing significant inhibitory effects with MIC values of 8-64 µg/mL for Candida species and 64-512 µg/mL for bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The nanocomposite was synthesized and characterized using various techniques, and its antimicrobial activity was assessed using broth microdilution and disk diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: MoxR effects as an ATPase on anti-stress and pathogenicity of Riemerella anatipestifer.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MoxR as an ATPase involved in the anti-stress and pathogenicity of Riemerella anatipestifer. Deletion of moxR reduces pathogenicity and stress resistance, while overexpression increases stress resistance.
full_output.methodology: Construction of moxR knockout, complement, knockdown, and overexpression strains, qPCR, stress experiments, and pathogenicity analysis in ducklings.

full_output.paper_title: Diagnostics, resistance and clinical relevance of non-tuberculous mycobacteria unidentified at the species level by line probe assays: a bi-national study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a novel NTM species (CZ131/21) with inducible resistance to clarithromycin, likely due to the presence of an erm gene. Another isolate, M. branderi (CZ614/21), showed resistance to linezolid and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and targeted deep-sequencing (Deeplex Myc-TB) were used for NTM species identification, along with MIC testing for antimycobacterial drugs.

full_output.paper_title: Neonatal Sepsis Induces Acute Kidney Injury and Modulates Inflammatory Responses to Antibiotic and Anti-Inflammatory Treatments
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effects of antibiotic treatments (gentamicin, cefotaxime) with or without pretomanid (PTX) on renal injury markers and inflammatory responses in a murine model of neonatal E. coli sepsis. It found that combined treatment with gentamicin and PTX, as well as cefotaxime and PTX, significantly reduced the expression of various kidney injury biomarkers and chemokines, indicating potential therapeutic benefits in managing sepsis-induced acute kidney injury.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a murine model of neonatal E. coli sepsis, measuring cytokine and chemokine concentrations, renal injury biomarkers, and histological changes in response to different antibiotic and anti-inflammatory treatments.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial blood microbiome of Mastomys rodents: implications for disease spill-over at the animal-human interface within the Bushbuckridge-East community, South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Bartonella grahamii and Bartonella mastomydis as predominant bacterial species in the blood of Mastomys rodents, highlighting their potential role in zoonotic disease transmission.
full_output.methodology: 16S rRNA gene sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize bacterial diversity in rodent blood samples.

full_output.paper_title: Time-resolved proteomic profiling of Cupriavidus metallidurans CH34 in the copper-induced viable-but-nonculturable state.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies proteomic changes in Cupriavidus metallidurans CH34 during the copper-induced viable-but-nonculturable (VBNC) state and resuscitation, highlighting the dynamic nature of cellular responses to copper stress.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic profiling using LC-MS/MS analysis of protein extracts from cells exposed to copper stress at various time points.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of GS-omega/kappa-Hxtx-Hv1a and Bt toxins against Bt-resistant and -susceptible strains of Helicoverpa zea (Boddie) and Spodoptera frugiperda (J.E. Smith).
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy of GS-omega/kappa-Hxtx-Hv1a (omega/kappa-Hv1a) in combination with Bt toxins against Bt-resistant and -susceptible strains of Helicoverpa zea and Spodoptera frugiperda. It found that omega/kappa-Hv1a alone was not highly effective, but when combined with Cry1Ac, it significantly increased mortality in Cry-resistant H. zea. However, it did not enhance toxicity against Vip3Aa-resistant H. zea or Cry1F-resistant S. frugiperda.
full_output.methodology: The study used diet-overlay and diet-incorporated bioassays, along with corn leaf bioassays, to test the effects of omega/kappa-Hv1a and Bt toxins on insect mortality.

full_output.paper_title: Establishment and characterization of persistent Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections in air-liquid interface cultures of human airway epithelial cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the formation of non-attached aggregates of P. aeruginosa in the apical layer of human airway epithelial cells and identifies upregulated genes involved in virulence factors, biofilm formation, and secretion systems during prolonged infection.
full_output.methodology: Dual RNA sequencing and cytokine screening were used to analyze host-pathogen interactions in an air-liquid interface model.

full_output.paper_title: Carbon dioxide regulates Mycobacterium tuberculosis PhoPR signaling and virulence.

canB.validation_method: CRISPRi knockdown and macrophage survival assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that CO2 modulates PhoPR signaling in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with CanB playing a critical role in macrophage survival. PhoPR is shown to be responsive to CO2 levels, suggesting it may act as a CO2 sensor.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptional profiling, qRT-PCR, CRISPRi knockdown, and macrophage survival assays were used to investigate the role of CO2 and PhoPR in Mtb.

full_output.paper_title: Addressing carbapenemase-producing extensively drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa: the potential of cefiderocol and ceftazidime/avibactam plus aztreonam therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the activity of cefiderocol and the combination of ceftazidime/avibactam (CZA) plus aztreonam against carbapenemase-producing extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates. Cefiderocol showed consistent bactericidal activity against all isolates, while CZA plus aztreonam demonstrated synergistic effects in some cases. The study identified several carbapenemase genes, including blaIMP-1, blaVIM-1, blaVIM-2, blaVIM-20, blaVIM-47, blaGES-1, blaGES-5, blaNDM-1, and ampC, as well as the efflux pump mexAB-OprM, which contribute to resistance.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing, time-kill assays, and chemostat experiments were used to evaluate the antibacterial activity of cefiderocol and CZA plus aztreonam against XDR P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Anti-virulence effects of Diclofenac sodium in combination with gentamicin on Pseudomonas aeruginosa: attenuation of quorum sensing related traits and efflux pump systems.

mexXY-OprM.validation_method: qPCR and efflux pump activity assay

full_output.key_findings: Diclofenac sodium and gentamicin synergistically reduce efflux pump activity and quorum sensing related traits in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: qPCR, efflux pump activity assay, biofilm formation assay, motility assays, and MIC determination.
full_output.sample_size: 2 clinical P. aeruginosa strains and 1 standard strain

full_output.paper_title: Chemical Proteomics Reveals Human Off-Targets of Fluoroquinolone Induced Mitochondrial Toxicity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AIFM1 and IDH2 as human off-targets of fluoroquinolones, contributing to mitochondrial dysfunction and toxicity.
full_output.methodology: Chemical proteomics and affinity-based protein profiling were used to identify protein off-targets of fluoroquinolones.

full_output.paper_title: Blue benzoquinone from scorpion venom shows bactericidal activity against drug-resistant strains of the priority pathogen Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The blue 1,4-benzoquinone exhibits bactericidal activity against drug-resistant strains of Acinetobacter baumannii, including those resistant to carbapenems and colistin, and does not induce resistance even after prolonged exposure.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity was tested using broth microdilution and growth inhibition assays.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive genomic insights into a highly pathogenic clone ST656 of mcr8.1 containing multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae from Bangladesh.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple beta-lactamase genes (blaLAP-2, blaTEM-1, blaSHV-11, blaOXA-1) and the mcr8.1 gene, which confers resistance to colistin, in a multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae ST656 isolate from Bangladesh. Additionally, the qacEdelta1 gene, which contributes to resistance against disinfectants and antibiotics, was detected.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, biofilm formation assay, and serum resistance assay were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Lysis of Escherichia coli by colicin Ib contributes to bacterial cross-feeding by releasing active β-galactosidase.

cirA.notes: Spontaneous mutation of the ColIb receptor gene cirA leads to resistance to ColIb in E. coli.

cib.notes: Horizontal acquisition of the S. enterica colicin immunity gene imm confers resistance to ColIb in E. coli.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that spontaneous mutation of the ColIb receptor gene cirA or horizontal acquisition of the S. enterica colicin immunity gene imm leads to resistance to ColIb in E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Experiments included growth assays, qPCR, and β-galactosidase activity measurements.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic adaptation to amoxicillin in Escherichia coli: The limited role of dinB and katE.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in frdD and rpoD as significant contributors to amoxicillin resistance in E. coli, highlighting their roles in regulating ampC expression and stress response pathways.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and transcriptomic analysis were used to identify mutations and gene expression changes in E. coli strains during amoxicillin adaptation.
full_output.sample_size: Three biological replicates for each strain.

full_output.paper_title: Ex vivo oral biofilm model for rapid screening of antimicrobial agents including natural cranberry polyphenols.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed an ex vivo oral biofilm model to screen antimicrobial agents, demonstrating that cranberry juice inhibited a range of oral taxa, including Alloprevotella sp__HMT_473, Granulicatella adiacens, Lachnoanaerobaculum umeaense, Lepotrichia sp__HMT_215, Peptostreptococcus stomatis, Prevotella nanceiensis, Stomatobaculum sp__HMT_097, Veillonella parvula, and killed some targets. Vancomycin and penicillin G also inhibited subsets of Gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized an ex vivo oral biofilm model, analyzing 16S rRNA levels via next-generation sequencing to assess the effects of antimicrobial agents on oral bacterial communities.
full_output.sample_size: Three subjects initially, with a fourth subject added for validation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the significant role of insertion sequences (IS) in antimicrobial resistance (AMR) of Acinetobacter baumannii. It revealed that IS elements, when paired with antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), enhance the predictive accuracy of AMR phenotypes. Specific IS-ARG pairs were found to correlate with resistance to various antibiotics, demonstrating the importance of these interactions in AMR development.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, machine learning models, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and validate AMR genes and IS-ARG pairs in A. baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Enterobacter hormaechei replaces virulence with carbapenem resistance via porin loss.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies OmpC and OmpD porins as essential for the virulence of E. hormaechei ST78 clade D isolates. Loss of these porins leads to reduced virulence in immunocompetent hosts but provides a fitness advantage during carbapenem treatment. Disruptive mutations in ompC and ompD are common in some lineages, suggesting a trade-off between virulence and carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Comparative genomics, mutagenesis, complementation studies, and in vivo infection models were used to analyze the role of porins in virulence and carbapenem resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic characterization and in silico serotyping of 62 Salmonella enterica isolated from Korean poultry operations.

qacEdelta1.validation_method: Whole genome sequencing and gene annotation

full_output.paper_title: Infections caused by extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales in hospitalized neonatal foals: Can colonization predict infection?
full_output.key_findings: The study found that gastrointestinal colonization with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales (ESBL-PE) on hospital admission was associated with ESBL-PE hospital-acquired infections (HAIs) in neonatal foals. The main ESBL-PE species identified were Escherichia coli and Klebsiella spp.
full_output.methodology: Prospective cohort study of neonatal foals admitted to a veterinary hospital, with ESBL-PE colonization screening and infection analysis.

full_output.paper_title: H-NS controls the susceptibility of Escherichia coli to aminoglycosides by interfering its uptake and efflux.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: disruption of the gene leads to increased susceptibility to aminoglycosides
mutations_found.validated_by: broth microdilution method and time-kill curves assays

hns.notes: The hns gene is a regulatory gene whose mutation (deletion) affects the susceptibility of E. coli to aminoglycosides.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that deletion of the hns gene in E. coli increases susceptibility to aminoglycosides by altering membrane permeability, reducing efflux pump activity, and increasing proton motive force.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution, time-kill curves, real-time PCR, and membrane permeability assays to analyze the effects of hns deletion on E. coli susceptibility to aminoglycosides.

full_output.paper_title: A new bacteriophage infecting Staphylococcus epidermidis with potential for removing biofilms by combination with chimeric lysin CHAPSH3b and vancomycin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a new phage, IPLA-AICAT, which infects Staphylococcus epidermidis and shows potential for biofilm removal when combined with the lytic protein CHAPSH3b and vancomycin. The phage lacks antibiotic resistance genes and virulence factors.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, genome characterization, biofilm susceptibility testing, and combination therapy experiments with CHAPSH3b and vancomycin.
full_output.sample_size: 24 S. epidermidis strains and 6 S. aureus strains

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of bacteriophage against clinical isolates of AmpC beta lactamase-Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae from hospital wastewater.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolated and characterized bacteriophages specific to AmpC-beta-lactamase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae from hospital wastewater, demonstrating their efficacy and stability under various environmental conditions.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation and characterization techniques including spot assay, plaque assay, and transmission electron microscopy were employed.

full_output.paper_title: Intestinal short-chain fatty acids spatially regulate the antibiotic tolerance and virulence of avian pathogenic Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in the chicken intestine differentially regulate the antibiotic tolerance and virulence of avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC). Cecal SCFAs (c-SCFA) inhibit APEC growth, virulence gene expression, and ampicillin tolerance, while ileal SCFAs (i-SCFA) have minimal effects. The inhibitory effects of c-SCFA are linked to intracellular pH dysregulation and reduced tryptophan metabolism, which decreases indole production. Indole addition reverses these effects.
full_output.methodology: Experimental investigation of SCFA effects on APEC growth, virulence gene expression, and antibiotic tolerance using RT-qPCR and disk-diffusion assays.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the principles behind antibiotics with limited resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies limited resistance development against dual-target permeabilizer antibiotics, highlighting the importance of targeting both membrane integrity and another cellular pathway. It also reveals that resistance mechanisms for these antibiotics are distinct and less influenced by gene amplification or mobile resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized spontaneous resistance frequency assays, adaptive laboratory evolution, and functional metagenomic screens to analyze resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Leuconostoc lactis strain APC 3969 produces a new variant of cyclic bacteriocin leucocyclicin Q and displays potent anti-Clostridium perfringens activity.
full_output.key_findings: Leuconostoc lactis APC 3969 produces a new variant of cyclic bacteriocin leucocyclicin C, which shows potent anti-Clostridium perfringens activity. The bacteriocin has a molecular mass of 6,081.44 Da and is encoded by a genetic cluster of ten genes.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, mass spectrometry, and antimicrobial activity assays were used to characterize the bacteriocin and its genetic cluster.

full_output.paper_title: Major blood stream infection-causing bacterial pathogens, antimicrobial resistance patterns and trends: a multisite retrospective study in Asmara, Eritrea (2014-2022).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance among blood stream infection-causing bacteria in Eritrea, including multidrug resistance (MDR) in various pathogens such as Klebsiella spp., Escherichia coli, and CoNS. High resistance rates to antibiotics like ampicillin, gentamicin, and ciprofloxacin were noted.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of blood culture data from 3153 patients, including antimicrobial susceptibility testing and statistical analysis of resistance patterns.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies high levels of antimicrobial resistance in Coagulase-Negative Staphylococci (CONS), Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Acinetobacter spp. in neonatal intensive care units, with particular resistance to Gentamicin, Cotrimoxazole, and Ciprofloxacin. Amikacin shows lower resistance rates and may be a viable treatment option.
full_output.methodology: Mixed-methods study involving quantitative analysis of 420 clinical and environmental samples, along with qualitative interviews with healthcare providers to assess infection control practices and antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo Pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic relationship of florfenicol in combination with doxycycline against Riemerella anatipestifer in ducks and the effect upon resistance development.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified six mutated genes (fahA, pfam, TonB-dependent receptor gene, proS, porU, and RpiB) in Riemerella anatipestifer after serial passage under different antibacterial agents. These genes are involved in enzyme synthesis, antimicrobial sensitivity, virulence, and biofilm synthesis.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome resequencing and analysis of single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were performed to identify mutated genes in Riemerella anatipestifer.
full_output.sample_size: Nine strains induced for 30 generations and the primary strain
