full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and multidrug resistance patterns of bacterial pathogens in wastewater and drinking water systems from hospital and non-hospital environments in Ethiopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals high levels of bacterial contamination and multidrug resistance in Ethiopian wastewater systems, with significant variation across studies. Key findings include the high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, and Klebsiella spp., highlighting the urgent need for improved wastewater management and antimicrobial resistance monitoring.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on bacterial prevalence and antimicrobial resistance in Ethiopian wastewater systems.
full_output.sample_size: 848 wastewater and 325 drinking water samples and 2,961 bacterial strains

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance patterns of WHO priority pathogens at general hospital in Southern Ethiopia during the COVID-19 pandemic, with particular reference to ESKAPE-group isolates of surgical site infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high rates of multidrug resistance (MDR) among ESKAPE pathogens, particularly Acinetobacter baumannii (100% MDR), methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA, 90% MDR), and Klebsiella pneumoniae (88.23% MDR). Resistance to carbapenems, cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones was widespread.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method, and molecular detection of ESBL and MRSA was conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and genetic characteristics of Campylobacter jejuni from laying-hens in Hubei Province, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in Campylobacter jejuni isolates from laying-hens in Hubei Province, China, including blaOXA, tet(O), tet(M), tet(W), cmeR, and gyrA (T86I). High resistance rates were observed against ceftriaxone, enrofloxacin, doxycycline, and other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genomic resistance gene prediction, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and whole-genome sequencing were used to analyze the resistance profiles of C. jejuni isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting Acne: Development of Monensin-Loaded Nanostructured Lipid Carriers.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the effectiveness of monensin (MON) against acne pathogens, including resistant strains of Cutibacterium acnes, Staphylococcus aureus, and Staphylococcus epidermidis, when delivered via nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs).
full_output.methodology: The study used nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) to deliver monensin (MON) and evaluated its antibacterial activity against clinical isolates of acne pathogens using agar dilution methods.
full_output.sample_size: 30 clinical isolates of C. acnes, along with S. aureus ATCC 29213 and S. epidermidis ATCC 14990

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characteristics and phylogenetic analyses of colonization and infection with carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in multicenter intensive care units: a cohort study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC-2 and blaNDM-1 as the primary carbapenemase genes in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKp) isolates, highlighting their significant role in carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes in CRKp isolates.

full_output.methodology: Prospective, single-center study analyzing antibiotic concentrations and MICs in patients with Gram-negative bloodstream infections.

full_output.paper_title: Structural basis of siderophore export and drug efflux by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.key_findings: MmpL4 and MmpL5 are essential for mycobactin secretion and bedaquiline efflux in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The coiled-coil domain of MmpL4 is crucial for its function, and mutations in conserved residues affect substrate transport.
full_output.methodology: Cryo-EM structure determination, functional assays, and mutational analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Enhanced antimicrobial efficacy and biocompatibility of albumin nanoparticles loaded with Mentha extract against methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that Mentha-loaded albumin nanoparticles (MLAN) exhibit enhanced antimicrobial efficacy and biocompatibility against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) compared to the aqueous Mentha extract. MLAN showed larger zones of inhibition, lower MIC and MBC values, and downregulated key virulence genes (icaA, icaD, and eps) in MRSA.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized agar well diffusion, broth microdilution, and real-time PCR to assess the antimicrobial activity and gene expression effects of MLAN and Mentha extract against MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of new lytic bacteriophage PSA-KC1 against Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from cystic fibrosis patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolated and characterized a novel lytic bacteriophage, PSA-KC1, effective against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains from cystic fibrosis patients. The phage was found to lack antibiotic resistance genes, virulence factors, and toxins, making it a potential candidate for phage therapy.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and analysis of the phage PSA-KC1, including assessment of its lytic properties and host range.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial profile, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, and associated factors among lower respiratory tract infection patients attending at Debre Markos comprehensive specialized hospital, Northwest, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance among bacterial isolates from lower respiratory tract infections, with Klebsiella pneumoniae and Streptococcus pneumoniae being the most prevalent pathogens. Significant multidrug resistance was observed, highlighting the need for targeted antibiotic therapy and surveillance.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a hospital-based cross-sectional analysis of 305 patients, with bacterial isolates identified through culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE) isolates from dogs and cats in veterinary hospitals in Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanA, vanB, vanC, and vanE genes in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus isolates from dogs and cats in Brazil, highlighting the presence of these resistance mechanisms in veterinary settings.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic detection, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and molecular methods including PCR for gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Virulence Genes and Antimicrobial Susceptibility Profiles of Staphylococcus aureus Isolates From Bovine Mastitis in Chagni, Northwestern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified virulence genes such as seb, sec, seh, see, pvl, tst, and hlb in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from bovine mastitis. High resistance to cefoxitin was observed, suggesting possible methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA).
full_output.methodology: PCR for virulence gene detection and disk diffusion for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Mefloquine reduces the bacterial membrane fluidity of Acinetobacter baumannii and distorts the bacterial membrane when combined with polymyxin B.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that mefloquine (MFQ) reduces the membrane fluidity of Acinetobacter baumannii and causes membrane distortion, enhancing the effectiveness of polymyxin B. MFQ shows synergistic activity with polymyxin B and colistin against various gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized broth microdilution assays, electron microscopy, molecular dynamics simulations, and fluorescence assays to evaluate the antibacterial activity and membrane interactions of MFQ.

full_output.paper_title: Campylobacter jejuni resistance to human milk involves the acyl carrier protein AcpP.

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in the acyl carrier protein AcpP and the major outer membrane porin PorA contribute to Campylobacter jejuni resistance to human milk by altering cell membrane structure and function.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, mutagenesis, and growth assays in human milk were used to identify and characterize the role of AcpP and PorA mutations in C. jejuni resistance to human milk.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates occurring in optochin-susceptible and optochin-resistant variants by analyzing whole-genome sequencing data.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in ATP synthase genes (atpC and atpA) as the likely genetic basis for optochin resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae. Specifically, a novel mutation at position 143T > C in the atpC gene resulting in Val48Ala was reported for the first time.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and variation analysis were used to identify mutations in ATP synthase genes associated with optochin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Chromosomal genes modulating fosfomycin susceptibility in uropathogenic Escherichia coli: a genome-wide analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several chromosomal genes whose mutations enhance fosfomycin resistance in uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC), including mutL, mutS, purB, and hflD. These genes are involved in DNA repair, purine biosynthesis, and regulatory functions, and their inactivation leads to increased fosfomycin MICs and improved growth in the presence of the antibiotic.
full_output.methodology: The study used transposon-directed insertion site sequencing (TraDIS) to screen for chromosomal genes whose mutations improve bacterial growth in the presence of fosfomycin. Gene-deletion mutants were constructed and tested for fosfomycin susceptibility using MIC testing and growth curve assays.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic impact of macrolide resistance and H3N2 infection on M. pneumoniae outbreak in children.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae strains, primarily due to the A2063G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene. It also found a significant association between prior H3N2 influenza infection and increased susceptibility to M. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: PCR testing, sequencing of the P1 and 23S rRNA genes, and analysis of neutralizing antibody titers.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a rapid antimicrobial resistance (AMR) test combining MTT assay with Raman spectroscopy, enabling minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) determination within 1.5 hours. The method was validated using various antibiotic-resistant and susceptible strains of Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The study combined MTT assay with Raman spectroscopy to determine MICs of antibiotics, comparing results with traditional Etest methods.
full_output.sample_size: Several clinical strains of E. coli and K. pneumoniae

full_output.paper_title: Bacillus velezensis FiA2 as an Oxydifficidin-Producing Strain and its Effects on the Growth Performance, Immunity, Intestinal Microbiota, and Resistance to Aeromonas salmonicida Infection in Carassius carassius.
full_output.key_findings: Bacillus velezensis FiA2 produces oxydifficidin, which exhibits strong antibacterial activity against Aeromonas salmonicida and other aquatic pathogens. The strain enhances the growth, immunity, and intestinal microbiota of crucian carp and provides protection against A. salmonicida infection.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity, MIC, and MBC detection, HPLC, LC-MS/MS, and disc diffusion assay.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and photocatalytic potential of piperine-derived zinc oxide nanoparticles against multi-drug-resistant non-typhoidal Salmonella spp.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antibacterial and photocatalytic potential of piperine-derived zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONPs) against multi-drug-resistant (MDR) non-typhoidal Salmonella (NTS) strains, demonstrating their effectiveness in inhibiting bacterial growth and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of ZnONPs using piperine, followed by in vitro testing for antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and photocatalytic activities against MDR-NTS strains.

full_output.paper_title: Clonality, Virulence Genes, and Antimicrobial Resistance of Dairy Ruminants in Mastitic Milk-Associated Staphylococcus aureus in Sicily.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of spa, mecA, and pvl genes in S. aureus isolates from dairy ruminants in Sicily, highlighting the genetic diversity and antimicrobial resistance profiles of these isolates.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR, PFGE, and MLST were used for genetic characterization and analysis of antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Regulation of the H1 Type VI Secretion System by the Transcriptional Regulator NfxB in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

mutations_found.validated_by: paper disk assay and MIC determination

nfxB.notes: The deletion of nfxB leads to heightened carbenicillin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NfxB as a transcriptional regulator that negatively regulates the H1-T6SS in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Deletion of nfxB leads to heightened carbenicillin resistance, suggesting that NfxB plays a role in regulating antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study uses DNA pull-down assays, EMSA, Western blot, and antibiotic susceptibility assays to investigate the role of NfxB in regulating H1-T6SS and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Investigating Polyhydroxyalkanoate Synthesis for Insights into Drug Resistance in Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies phaC and phaZ as key genes involved in PHB synthesis and degradation, which are linked to drug resistance in Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae. Deletion of these genes reduces drug resistance to HN-2 n-butanol extract and bacitracin.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion experiments, PHB quantification, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted to assess the role of phaC and phaZ in drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, Antimicrobial Activity, and Tyrosinase Inhibition by Multifunctional 3,4-Dihydroxy-Phenyl Peptidomimetics.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of peptidomimetics with 3,4-dihydroxyphenyl scaffolds, which exhibit antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains, including E. coli and S. aureus. These compounds show promising antimicrobial properties with MIC values comparable to commonly used antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of peptidomimetics via the Ugi reaction, followed by assessment of their antimicrobial activity using MIC and MBC assays, and evaluation of their tyrosinase inhibitory effects.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance, Virulence Gene Profiling, and Spa Typing of Staphylococcus aureus Isolated from Retail Chicken Meat in Alabama, USA.

mecA.evidence_note: The mecA gene was identified in three MRSA isolates, and the plasmid carrying mecA was associated with resistance to penicillin, ampicillin, erythromycin, and oxacillin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from retail chicken meat, including mecA, blaZ, tetM, tetA, ermA, norA, chlA, ant(6)-Ia, aph(3′)-III, mph(C), and msr(A). These genes conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as tetracycline, beta-lactams, erythromycin, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, and macrolides.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection and plasmid sequencing were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology Clinical Manifestations, Decolonization Strategies, and Treatment Options of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Infection in Neonates.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various AMR genes in MRSA strains, including blaZ, ermC, dfrA, dfrK, tetK, tetL, and mecA, highlighting their roles in resistance to penicillin, erythromycin, clindamycin, trimethoprim, tetracycline, and methicillin.
full_output.methodology: The study reviews molecular characteristics, epidemiology, and treatment options for MRSA in neonates, focusing on AMR gene identification and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Quorum Quenching of P. aeruginosa by Portulaca oleracea Methanolic Extract and Its Phytochemical Profile.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of the methanolic extract of Portulaca oleracea and its effectiveness in blocking or attenuating the quorum sensing (QS) of P. aeruginosa. The extract showed significant growth inhibition of P. aeruginosa, reduced biofilm formation, pyocyanin production, and LasA staphylolytic activity. The phytochemical analysis revealed several compounds with antimicrobial and antioxidant effects.
full_output.methodology: Agar well diffusion method, determination of minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), biofilm formation assay, and Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS) for phytochemical analysis.

full_output.paper_title: New Bacteriophage Pseudomonas Phage Ka2 from a Tributary Stream of Lake Baikal.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a new bacteriophage, Pseudomonas phage Ka2, which effectively lyses 21 out of 30 P. aeruginosa clinical isolates and reduces the MIC of several antibiotics, including amikacin, gentamicin, cefepime, and colistin. The phage also shows synergistic effects with antimicrobials against biofilms.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, morphological analysis, genome sequencing, and assessment of lytic activity against P. aeruginosa isolates and biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of amino acid substitutions in penicillin-binding proteins associated with adaptation to D-Ala-D-Lac in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: shift in substrate preference from D-Ala-D-Ala to D-Ala-D-Lac

PBP1B.evidence_note: The paper states that the threonine-to-asparagine substitution at position 491 in PBP1B leads to a shift in substrate preference from D-Ala-D-Ala to D-Ala-D-Lac.

PBP2A.notes: A lysine-to-glycine substitution at position 336 of PBP2A affects the protein's flexibility and stability near the membrane interface.

PBP3.notes: Multiple substitutions in PBP3 affect the active site and may influence substrate binding.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific amino acid substitutions in penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis (VRE) that enable adaptation to D-Ala-D-Lac, a modified cell wall precursor. Key mutations include T491N in PBP1B, K336G in PBP2A, and multiple substitutions in PBP3, which alter substrate preferences and contribute to vancomycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study employed Sanger sequencing, bioinformatics analysis, structural modeling, and molecular docking to analyze PBP mutations and their impact on vancomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Silent pandemic
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the global crisis of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), highlighting its increasing prevalence and the challenges it poses to public health. It emphasizes the urgent need for coordinated efforts to address AMR through improved surveillance, responsible antibiotic use, and the development of new therapeutic strategies.
full_output.methodology: The paper provides a comprehensive review of the current state of AMR, drawing on various studies and reports to highlight the scope and impact of the issue.

full_output.paper_title: GrcC1 mediates low-level resistance to multiple drugs in M. marinum, M. abscessus, and M. smegmatis.

MMAR_2832.validation_method: overexpression in AlMmr, Msm WT, and Mab ΔembC

grcC1.notes: The A132V mutation in GrcC1 was shown to confer low-level resistance to multiple drugs.
grcC1.evidence_note: The A132V mutation in GrcC1 was shown to confer low-level resistance to multiple drugs.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel mutation (A132V) in the grcC1 gene that confers low-level resistance to multiple drugs in Mycobacterium species.
full_output.methodology: Overexpression, CRISPRi, CRISPR/Cpf1-assisted gene editing, and drug susceptibility testing were used to validate the role of grcC1 in drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Speeding up drug susceptibility testing in Mycobacterium tuberculosis using RNA biomarkers.

mmpR5.encodes: transcriptional repressor of the MmpS5-MmpL5 efflux pump

full_output.key_findings: The study introduces TRACeR-TB, a rapid drug susceptibility testing method for Mycobacterium tuberculosis that uses RNA biomarkers to detect resistance. It identifies specific mRNA biomarkers for different antibiotics and demonstrates improved sensitivity and specificity compared to traditional methods.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RNA sequencing to identify antibiotic-specific mRNA biomarkers and developed a quantitative assay to measure these biomarkers in crude cell lysates. The performance of TRACeR-TB was validated against conventional methods like MGIT DST.

full_output.paper_title: Incidence and in vitro acquisition of transferable drug resistance in Salmonella arizonae.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Salmonella arizonae isolates exhibited varying degrees of resistance to multiple antibiotics, including streptomycin, tetracycline, kanamycin, and ampicillin. Transferable resistance was observed through conjugation experiments, demonstrating the ability of S. arizonae to acquire resistance determinants from a multiply resistant E. coli strain.
full_output.methodology: The study used standardized disc susceptibility testing and conjugation experiments to assess antibiotic resistance and transferability in Salmonella arizonae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Berberine inhibits the tarO gene to impact MRSA cell wall synthesis.

tarO.encodes: a critical enzyme in the initial stage of wall teichoic acid (WTA) biosynthesis
tarO.validation_method: qRT-PCR analysis, WTA-PAGE electrophoresis, molecular docking

full_output.key_findings: Berberine inhibits the tarO gene, which reduces WTA synthesis and increases sensitivity to β-lactam antibiotics in MRSA.
full_output.methodology: qRT-PCR, WTA-PAGE, molecular docking, MIC/MBC determination, SEM, and bacterial viability assays.

full_output.paper_title: Serovar and multilocus sequence typing analysis of Pasteurella multocida from diseased pigs in Taiwan.

floR.validation_method: presence in strains with high resistance to florfenicol

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the floR gene as a significant contributor to florfenicol resistance in Pasteurella multocida isolates from diseased pigs in Taiwan.
full_output.methodology: Serotyping, MLST, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and detection of virulence and resistance genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed 10 cases of Neisseria-associated peritoneal dialysis-related peritonitis (PDAP) and found that Neisseria species, particularly Neisseria cinerea, Neisseria elongata, Neisseria sicca, Neisseria flavescens, and Neisseria mucosa, were responsible for the infections. The study noted that Neisseria infections had a favorable outcome similar to coagulase-negative staphylococci (CNS)-related PDAP but worse than Staphylococcus aureus (S)-related PDAP. Key risk factors for poor outcomes included hypoalbuminemia, hypokalemia, and elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP).
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical data from 10 patients with Neisseria-associated PDAP, including treatment regimens, clinical outcomes, and laboratory parameters.

full_output.paper_title: Disruption of zinc homeostasis reverses tigecycline resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that disrupting zinc homeostasis using PBT2 and zinc ions can reverse tigecycline resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae by inhibiting efflux pump mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study used MIC experiments, transcriptome sequencing, and gene knockout experiments to investigate the role of efflux pumps in tigecycline resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Exogenous plasmid capture to characterize tetracycline-resistance plasmids in sprouts obtained from retail in Germany.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance genes tet(A) and tet(D), along with quinolone, sulfonamide, and trimethoprim resistance genes qnrS1, sul1, and dfrA1 in plasmids from sprout samples.
full_output.methodology: Exogenous plasmid capture, whole genome sequencing, and disk diffusion testing.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance and virulence profile of Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from wild Sumatran Orangutans (Pongo abelii).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from wild Sumatran orangutans, including blaTEM, blaSHV, blaCTX-M, and tetA, indicating multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify antibiotic resistance genes and determine resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative metagenome-associated analysis of gut microbiota and antibiotic resistance genes in acute gastrointestinal injury patients with the risk of in-hospital mortality.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a novel antibiotic resistance gene, capO, associated with chloramphenicol resistance in gut microbiota of ICU patients with acute gastrointestinal injury. The gene was found to be enriched in the Death group compared to the Survival group.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify and compare gut microbiota and antibiotic resistance genes between Death and Survival groups of ICU patients with AGI.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic and phenotypic analyses of two distinct sets of Pseudomonas aeruginosa urinary tract isolates.

gyrA.notes: associated with high-level resistance to fluoroquinolones

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes and mutations in P. aeruginosa UTI isolates from the UK and Kuwait, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant strains, especially in Kuwaiti isolates. Key AMR genes included aac(3)-IV, aph(3')-Ib, aph(3')-IIb, aph(4)-Ia, aph(6)-Id, crpP, dfrB1, aac(6')-Ib7, aac(6')-ii, aaA61, blaPDC, and blaVIM-28. Mutations in gyrA were also found to contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, disc diffusion assays, and MIC testing were used to analyze AMR genes and mutations in P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Predominance of extensively-drug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii carrying bla OXA-23 in Jordanian patients admitted to the intensive care units.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla OXA-23-like, bla ADC, bla VIM, and bla NDM-1 as the predominant carbapenem resistance genes in extensively drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from Jordanian ICU patients.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Chemical Composition and Synergistic Antimicrobial Effects of Essential Oils From Four Commonly Used Satureja Species in Combination With Two Conventional Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antimicrobial effects of essential oils from four Satureja species and their synergistic interactions with gentamicin and amphotericin B. S. montana and S. hortensis EOs showed strong antimicrobial activity, while S. calamintha and S. alpina had weaker effects. All EOs demonstrated significant synergy with gentamicin, particularly against Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Gas chromatography and GC/MS analysis were used to determine the chemical composition of the essential oils. Antimicrobial activity was assessed using agar disc diffusion and microwell dilution methods. Synergistic effects were evaluated using the checkerboard method.

full_output.key_findings: This study developed random forest machine learning models to impute minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) for various antimicrobials using phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) data as predictors.
full_output.methodology: Machine learning models were built using cattle-associated Escherichia coli isolates from the National Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring System (NARMS) to predict MICs for 10 antimicrobials.

full_output.paper_title: Suppressive Effects of Kouboku on Methyl Mercaptan Production and Biofilm Formation in Porphyromonas gingivalis.
full_output.key_findings: Kouboku suppresses methyl mercaptan production and biofilm formation in Porphyromonas gingivalis by downregulating mgl and fimA expression.
full_output.methodology: Expression analysis, mutant construction, and biofilm assays.
full_output.sample_size: Five standard and five clinically isolated P. gingivalis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of aminoglycoside- and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus: phenotypic and genotypic insights from clinical specimens in Ardabil, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified aac(6')-Ie-aph(2''), aph(2'')-Ib, and ant(4')-Ia genes as the most prevalent aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes in MRSA and MSSA isolates from Ardabil, Iran.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize AME genes and resistance patterns in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug resistance of Pseudomonas aeruginosa: do virulence properties impact on resistance patterns?
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several beta-lactamase genes, including bla VIM-2, bla SPM, bla AIM, bla GIM, bla SIM, bla DIM, bla BIC, bla SHV, bla DHA, and bla OXA-48, which are associated with carbapenem resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Bangladesh. The toxA gene and twitching motility were significantly correlated with multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and gel electrophoresis were used to detect the presence of beta-lactamase and virulence genes in P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: CARPDM: cost-effective antibiotic resistome profiling of metagenomic samples using targeted enrichment.
full_output.key_findings: The paper introduces CARPDM, a software tool for designing targeted enrichment probes to profile antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in metagenomic samples. It describes two probe sets, allCARD and clinicalCARD, which significantly enhance the detection of ARGs compared to traditional shotgun sequencing.
full_output.methodology: The paper describes the development of CARPDM, a software tool for designing targeted enrichment probes, and evaluates the effectiveness of two probe sets (allCARD and clinicalCARD) for detecting ARGs in metagenomic samples through computational and experimental validation.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of isobavachalcone against Enterococcus faecalis clinical isolates from China.
full_output.key_findings: Isobavachalcone showed potent antibacterial activity against E. faecalis clinical isolates, with MICs ranging from 6.25 to 12.5 µM. It also inhibited biofilm formation at sub-MIC concentrations. Genomic analysis identified mutations in PurH and FlgJ associated with isobavachalcone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, growth curve analysis, biofilm assays, time-kill assays, persister assays, whole genome sequencing, and molecular docking.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that Listeria monocytogenes isolates from women with spontaneous abortion in Ugandan tertiary hospitals exhibited high resistance to ampicillin (81.40%) and amoxicillin (76.74%), with 46.51% of isolates resistant to more than three antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method on Listeria monocytogenes isolates from high vaginal swabs of women with spontaneous abortion.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization, genomic analysis and preclinical evaluation of the lytic Staphylococcus bacteriophage PSK against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus wound isolate.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the lytic bacteriophage PSK, which effectively targets methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and shows promise as an alternative to vancomycin for treating MRSA-induced wound infections.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and characterization of the phage PSK, including its genomic analysis, stability testing, and evaluation of its antibacterial activity in vitro and in a murine wound-infection model.

full_output.paper_title: Corynebacterium diphtheriae Infections, South Africa, 2015-2023.

pbp2m.validation_method: genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the pbp2m gene as a determinant of penicillin resistance in Corynebacterium diphtheriae isolates, highlighting the importance of monitoring penicillin resistance in diphtheria treatment strategies.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize resistance mechanisms in C. diphtheriae isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the emergence of macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MRMp) in Ohio, USA, with 24 (2.4%) of 995 sequenced samples carrying mutations associated with macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of M. pneumoniae isolates and analysis of resistance mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis strain (Ch strain) with a unique combination of resistance mutations, leading to resistance against multiple antibiotics including rifampin, isoniazid, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, streptomycin, kanamycin, amikacin, capreomycin, linezolid, bedaquiline, and clofazimine.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic drug-susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance mutations and confirm their impact on drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis of Derivatives of the Antibiotic Albicidin: The N-Terminal Fragment as Key to Control Potency and Resistance Mediated by the Binding Protein AlbA.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on synthesizing albicidin derivatives with modifications in the N-terminal building block to enhance antibacterial activity and overcome resistance mediated by the binding protein AlbA.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of albicidin derivatives, assessment of their antibacterial activity through MIC determination, and evaluation of their ability to evade AlbA-mediated resistance using growth inhibition and transcription activation assays.

full_output.paper_title: A novel Kayvirus species phage RuSa1 removes biofilm and lyses multiple clinical strains of methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel phage, RuSa1, capable of removing biofilm and lysing multiple clinical strains of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.methodology: The study utilized phage isolation, purification, and characterization techniques, along with biochemical and genetic analyses to assess the efficacy of RuSa1 against MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Therapeutic effect of pH responsive Magainin II modified azithromycin plus curcumin micelles in different depth models of MRSA infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed pH-responsive micelles containing azithromycin and curcumin modified with Magainin II, which showed strong antibacterial, anti-biofilm, and anti-inflammatory effects against MRSA in various infection models.
full_output.methodology: The study characterized the physicochemical properties of the micelles and evaluated their therapeutic effects in vitro and in vivo using different infection models.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic diversity of mcr-carrying plasmids and the role of type IV secretion systems in IncI2 plasmids conjugation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mcr-1, mcr-3, and mcr-9 as key genes responsible for colistin resistance in pMCRs, highlighting their prevalence and co-carriage with other resistance genes. T4SS P3 plays a critical role in the conjugative transfer of these plasmids.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, conjugation assays, and structural predictions were used to characterize the role of T4SS in plasmid transfer and resistance gene dissemination.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of resistance and biofilm genes of ESKAPE pathogens isolated from clinical samples: examination of the effect of boric acid on biofilm ability by cell culture method.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in ESKAPE pathogens, including vanA and vanC for vancomycin resistance, blaKPC and blaOXA-48 for carbapenem resistance, and others related to tetracycline, sulfonamide, quinolone, and aminoglycoside resistance. Additionally, biofilm-related genes such as icaA, icaD, gelE, asa1, and esp were detected in Staphylococcus and Enterococcus spp. Quorum sensing genes LasI and LasR were found in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and biofilm production genes like mrkA, wbbM, wzm, and luxS were identified in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: PCR and molecular analysis were used to detect AMR and biofilm-related genes in clinical isolates of ESKAPE pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiological profile and antimicrobial resistance trends of Staphylococcus aureus in Chinese pediatric intensive care units from 2016 to 2022: a multi-center retrospective study.
full_output.key_findings: Staphylococcus aureus is the most common gram-positive bacterium in PICUs, with high resistance rates to commonly used antimicrobials. No strains were resistant to vancomycin and linezolid. MRSA showed high resistance to erythromycin, clindamycin, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of S. aureus isolates from 17 PICUs in China from 2016 to 2022, with antimicrobial susceptibility testing performed according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance of bacterial pathogens isolated from cancer patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: This study highlights the high prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in bacterial pathogens isolated from cancer patients, with particular emphasis on E. coli, K. pneumoniae, S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, and A. baumannii. Resistance to penicillins, fluoroquinolones, and aminoglycosides was notably high across various cancer patient populations.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2000 and 2024, focusing on antimicrobial resistance in bacterial pathogens isolated from cancer patients.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and virulence in Klebsiella pneumoniae: a four-month study in Osogbo, Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of multidrug resistance in K. pneumoniae isolates, with all isolates showing resistance to ceftriaxone, cefotaxime, and colistin. Virulence genes K1, K2, and mrkD were prevalent, while other genes like fimH, ramA, traT, K3, and K5 were not detected.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing via Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion and molecular detection of virulence genes using multiplex PCR.

full_output.paper_title: A chionodracine-derived peptide, KHS-Cnd, as an anti-virulence agent against multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii clinical strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the anti-virulence properties of the chionodracine-derived peptide KHS-Cnd against multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii clinical strains, showing its ability to inhibit biofilm formation and reduce bacterial motility.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of KHS-Cnd through MIC and MBC determination, biofilm formation assays, motility assays, and synergy testing with ceftazidime/avibactam.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that ParE toxins from various bacteria induce loss of viability and increased mutation frequency, but do not lead to increased antibiotic resistance. Some ParE toxins, like PaParE1, are non-toxic and do not affect mutation frequency.
full_output.methodology: The study used fluctuation assays, MIC measurements, and expression of ParE toxins in different bacterial hosts to assess their effects on viability and mutation frequency.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-resistant Morganella morganii carrying bla(KPC-2) or bla(NDM-1) in the clinic: one-decade genomic epidemiology analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla(KPC-2) and bla(NDM-1) as the primary carbapenem resistance genes in carbapenem-resistant Morganella morganii (CRMM) isolates, highlighting their role in the spread of resistance through plasmid-mediated mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, transconjugation experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance genes and their impact on microbial fitness.

full_output.paper_title: Demographics, epidemiology, mortality and difficult-to-treat resistance patterns of bacterial bloodstream infections in the global US Military Health System from 2010 to 2019: a retrospective cohort study.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed bacterial bloodstream infections (BSIs) in the US Military Health System (MHS) from 2010 to 2019, identifying resistance patterns and mortality trends. It found that 0.5% of deaths were associated with difficult-to-treat resistance (DTR) GNB, with Acinetobacter spp, P. aeruginosa, and K. pneumoniae being the primary DTR pathogens. Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus and methicillin-resistant S. aureus were also noted.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing clinical and microbiological data from the MHS Data Repository and Defense Centers for Public Health-Portsmouth.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of Cigarette-Derived Compounds on the Spread of Antimicrobial Resistance in Artificial Human Lung Sputum Medium, Simulated Environmental Media, and Wastewater.
full_output.key_findings: Exposure to cigarette smoke condensate increased the transfer rates of a multidrug-resistance-encoding plasmid in artificial lung sputum medium, suggesting a role in promoting antimicrobial resistance spread.
full_output.methodology: Conjugation experiments with Pseudomonas putida and Escherichia coli strains, measuring plasmid transfer rates under exposure to cigarette-derived compounds.
full_output.sample_size: Six independent biological replicates for each concentration.

full_output.paper_title: Gold Nanoparticles Functionalized With 5-Amino-2-Mercaptobenzimidazole: A Promising Antimicrobial Strategy Against Carbapenem-Resistant Gram-Negative Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces 5-A-2MBI-functionalized gold nanoparticles (5-A-2MBI_Au NPs) as a novel antimicrobial strategy against carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacteria (CR-GNB). These nanoparticles show potent antibacterial activity with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 2 μg/mL against various CR-GNB strains, including those with resistance mechanisms such as NDM-5, NDM-7, KPC-2, and OXA-23.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of 5-A-2MBI_Au NPs through in vitro and in vivo experiments, including MIC determination, time-kill assays, SEM imaging, and transcriptome analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the clinical outcomes and molecular characteristics of Acinetobacter baumannii bloodstream infections: a study of sequence types, capsular types, and drug resistance in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenemase genes blaOXA-23, blaOXA-66, and blaNDM-1 in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAb) isolates, highlighting their association with multidrug resistance and higher mortality rates in bloodstream infections.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize AMR genes and mutations in A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of CMY-190, a novel chromosomally encoded AmpC β-lactamase, and plasmid-encoded KPC-2 in a clinical isolate of Citrobacter youngae.

blaCMY-190.validation_method: cloning in E. coli DH5α and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel chromosomally encoded AmpC β-lactamase gene, bla CMY-190, and a plasmid-encoded carbapenemase gene, bla KPC-2, in a clinical isolate of Citrobacter youngae.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, MIC testing, conjugation, transformation, and whole-genome sequencing were used to identify and validate the AMR genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the synergistic effect of combining polymyxin B and rifampicin in a murine neutropenic thigh infection model against E. coli and K. pneumoniae, with stronger synergy observed against K. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic analysis in a murine infection model.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Isolates of Antimicrobial-Resistant Enterobacter Species Can Persist in Human Macrophages Without Replication and Overt Cellular Cytotoxicity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that clinical isolates of Enterobacter species can persist in human macrophages without replication and with minimal cellular cytotoxicity, highlighting their ability to survive intracellularly without triggering significant immune responses.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized THP-1 macrophages and human monocyte-derived macrophages to investigate the intracellular trafficking and survival of Enterobacter clinical isolates, employing confocal fluorescence microscopy, bacterial enumeration, and cytotoxicity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence of vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, multidrug-resistant S. aureus, and Enterococcus faecium-causing mastitis in Thailand and Cambodia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) S. aureus and E. faecium causing mastitis in Thailand and Cambodia. While phenotypic vancomycin-resistant S. aureus (VRSA) was detected, none of the isolates carried the mecA, vanA, or vanB genes.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing via disk diffusion and PCR for detection of AMR genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that β-lactam antibiotic exposure led to changes in the oropharyngeal and fecal microbiota of infants with cystic fibrosis, including reduced bacterial loads and altered diversity, but no specific AMR genes or mutations were characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing and qPCR were used to analyze the microbiota and resistome of oropharyngeal and fecal samples.

full_output.paper_title: Deep-Learning-Based Approaches for Rational Design of Stapled Peptides With High Antimicrobial Activity and Stability.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed deep learning models to design stapled antimicrobial peptides with high stability and antimicrobial activity, demonstrating that certain stapled peptides effectively inhibited various bacteria with low concentrations and showed good serum stability and low hemolytic activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized deep learning and machine learning models, along with structural and sequence descriptors, to predict and validate the antimicrobial activity of stapled peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of different mechanisms on antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa: a strategic system for evaluating antibiotics against gram-negative bacteria.

mexS.notes: MexS mutation was identified as a cause of resistance to imipenem and relebactam in a KPC-producing P. aeruginosa strain.
mexS.evidence_note: The paper states that the Δ mexS mutant showed increased MICs for imipenem and meropenem, indicating that mutations in mexS confer resistance to these antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various AMR genes and mutations in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, including porin loss (oprD), efflux pump overexpression (mexR, nalC, nalD, nfxB, mexS, mexZ), chromosomal mutations in gyrA and parC, and plasmid-mediated resistance mechanisms (CTX-M-14, CTX-M-15, VEB-3, CMY-2, KPC-2, NDM-1, VIM-1).
full_output.methodology: The study used in-frame deletion mutagenesis, site-directed mutagenesis, and plasmid transformation to create genetically engineered strains with specific resistance mechanisms, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing to determine MICs.

full_output.paper_title: Resistome and virulome determination in Helicobacter pylori using next-generation sequencing with target-enrichment technology.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes mutations in 23S rDNA, gyrA, and rpoB genes associated with resistance to clarithromycin, levofloxacin, and rifampicin in Helicobacter pylori using next-generation sequencing with target-enrichment technology.
full_output.methodology: Next-generation sequencing with target-enrichment technology was used to analyze the resistome and virulome of H. pylori directly from gastric biopsies.

full_output.key_findings: The study introduces a high-throughput anaerobic method for viability assays using the Geometric Viability Assay (GVA) with Clostridium perfringens as a model. The method effectively measures viability, spore formation, and antibiotic susceptibility, offering a cost-effective alternative to traditional plate-based assays.
full_output.methodology: The study developed and validated a high-throughput anaerobic viability assay using the Geometric Viability Assay (GVA) with Clostridium perfringens, demonstrating its effectiveness in measuring viability, spore formation, and antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Sharp rise in high-virulence Bordetella pertussis with macrolides resistance in Northern China.

23S rRNA.notes: The A2047G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene is associated with erythromycin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a sharp rise in high-virulence Bordetella pertussis strains with macrolide resistance in Northern China, particularly noting the dominance of ptxP3-ERBP strains and the A2047G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene conferring erythromycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study involved PCR amplification, sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, MLVA typing, and whole-genome sequencing to characterize the genetic and resistance profiles of B. pertussis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Targeted insights into Aeromonas hydrophila biofilms: Surface preferences, resistance mechanisms, and gene expression.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of luxS, ahyR, and csgA genes in all four Aeromonas hydrophila strains, with csgA exclusively found in ATCC 7966. These genes are involved in quorum sensing and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study used gel electrophoresis, RT-PCR, and biofilm formation assays to analyze gene expression and resistance mechanisms in Aeromonas hydrophila strains.

full_output.paper_title: Nanobody-Targeted Conditional Antimicrobial Therapeutics.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that VHH16, a nanobody targeting Ly6G/C, enhances the activation of conditional antimicrobial therapeutics by proximity-induced reactivity with ADAM10, improving the efficacy of therapeutic peptides and proteins in bacterial infections.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro cleavage assays, in vivo biodistribution studies, and flow cytometry to evaluate the activation and efficacy of VHH-targeted antimicrobial therapeutics.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence genes, efflux pumps, and molecular typing of Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from North Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes including acrAB, tolC, mdtK, ompK35, and ompK36 in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from North Iran, which were associated with resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and resistance patterns in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Nanohybrid Hydrogel with Dual Functions: Controlled Low-Temperature Photothermal Antibacterial Activity and Promoted Regeneration for Treating MRSA-Infected Bone Defects.
full_output.key_findings: The study develops a nanohybrid hydrogel (FND-ZHD) that combines low-temperature photothermal antibacterial activity with bone regeneration capabilities, effectively targeting MRSA infections in bone defects.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the synthesis and characterization of ZHD nanoparticles and FND-ZHD hydrogels, evaluating their antibacterial properties, biocompatibility, and osteogenic potential through in vitro and in vivo experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology of Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates in Russia, 2015-2023: current trends and forecasting.

penA.mechanism: mutation leading to reduced susceptibility to ceftriaxone

mtrR.mechanism: mutation in promoter region leading to increased expression of mtrD

mtrD.mechanism: mutation leading to increased efflux of macrolides

penA.notes: mutations in penA contribute to reduced susceptibility to ceftriaxone

mtrR.notes: mutated mtrR promoter leads to resistance to macrolides

mtrD.notes: mutations in mtrD contribute to resistance to macrolides

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genetic determinants of resistance to ceftriaxone and azithromycin in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates in Russia, highlighting the emergence of mosaic alleles in penA, mtrR, and mtrD genes associated with reduced susceptibility and resistance.
full_output.methodology: Microarray-based assays and sequencing were used to identify genetic determinants of resistance in N. gonorrhoeae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypical and molecular characterization of Rhodococcus equi isolated from foals in the Agreste region of Pernambuco - Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of virulence plasmid genes (vapA, vapC, vapD, vapE, vapF, vapH, and traA) in Rhodococcus equi isolates from foals in the Agreste region of Pernambuco, Brazil. One isolate lacked the plasmid, likely due to loss after repeated passages at 37°C.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and molecular characterization including PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Development of early life gut resistome and mobilome across gestational ages and microbiota-modifying treatments
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies distinct trajectories of the gut resistome and mobilome in infants influenced by birth mode, gestational age, antibiotic use, and geographical location. It highlights the role of Escherichia coli as a major carrier of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and notes the gradual loss of ARG-associated plasmids during infancy.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a meta-analytical approach combining metagenomic data from 3981 stool samples of 1270 infants and 415 mothers, analyzed through reference-based and assembly-based methods to profile the resistome and mobilome.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of ceftriaxone-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae detected in Scotland, 2018-2024.

gyrA.evidence_note: The paper states 'gyrA and parC mutations conferring ciprofloxacin resistance'.

parC.evidence_note: Genotypic mechanisms conferring all detected phenotypic resistance were identified in the genomes, including the mosaic penA -60.001 conferring cephalosporin resistance, gyrA and parC mutations conferring ciprofloxacin resistance, and the rpsJ V57M polymorphism and tetM conferring tetracycline resistance

rpsJ.evidence_note: The paper mentions 'rpsJ V57M polymorphism and tetM conferring tetracycline resistance' but does not explicitly state that 'rpsJ' alone confers resistance to tetracycline.

tetM.evidence_note: The paper mentions 'tetM conferring tetracycline resistance' in the genomic investigation section.

23S rDNA A2059G.evidence_note: High-level azithromycin resistance was conferred by the 23S rDNA A2059G mutation (Escherichia coli numbering).

rpsJ.evidence_note: The rpsJ V57M polymorphism was explicitly mentioned in the genomic investigation section as conferring tetracycline resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes and mutations associated with ceftriaxone-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae in Scotland, including the mosaic penA-60.001 allele, gyrA and parC mutations, rpsJ V57M polymorphism, tetM, and the 23S rDNA A2059G mutation.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, MIC testing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the AMR profiles of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic profile of Staphylococcus spp., Enterococcus spp., and E. coli colonizing dogs, surgeons, and environment during the intraoperative period: a cross-sectional study in a veterinary teaching hospital in Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified resistance genes blaZ, mecA, tet(M), and aacA-aphD in Staphylococcus spp. and Enterococcus spp. isolates, indicating high rates of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus spp. and tetracycline-resistant Enterococcus spp. in a veterinary teaching hospital setting.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and PFGE analysis were used to detect resistance genes and assess genetic diversity among bacterial isolates from dogs, surgeons, and the environment.

full_output.paper_title: siRNA-AGO2 complex inhibits bacterial gene translation: A promising therapeutic strategy for superbug infection.

mecA.validation_method: silencing of mecA gene by siMecA-Exos leading to reduced PBP2a expression and increased susceptibility to methicillin

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that exosome-delivered siMecA can silence the mecA gene in MRSA, reducing PBP2a expression and increasing susceptibility to methicillin.
full_output.methodology: Exosome preparation, siRNA delivery, Western blotting, qPCR, and in vivo mouse infection models.

full_output.paper_title: Echinacoside reduces intracellular c-di-GMP levels and potentiates tobramycin activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm aggregates.
full_output.key_findings: SiaD is essential for P. aeruginosa auto-aggregation in SCFM2, and echinacoside reduces both auto-aggregation and intracellular c-di-GMP levels of PAO1 in SCFM2.
full_output.methodology: Virtual screening, molecular docking, RT-qPCR, ELISA, and microscopy were used to analyze the role of SiaD and the effects of echinacoside on P. aeruginosa biofilm aggregates.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of a fluorinated macrobicyclic antibiotic through chemical synthesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the discovery of BT-33, a novel fluorinated macrobicyclic antibiotic with broad-spectrum activity against multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens. It shows enhanced potency and metabolic stability compared to existing lincosamide antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, X-ray crystallography, and computational modeling were used to characterize BT-33.

full_output.paper_title: Pharmacodynamic target attainment of the synergism of ceftazidime-avibactam in combination with amikacin against OXA-producing extensively drug-resistant or pan drug-resistant (XDR/PDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several OXA-type beta-lactamase genes, including OXA-101, OXA-847, OXA-50, OXA-573, OXA-846, and OXA-488, which are prevalent in OXA-producing XDR/PDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates. These genes contribute to resistance against ceftazidime.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed to identify and characterize the resistance genes in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility and risk factors of uropathogens in symptomatic urinary tract infection cases at Dessie Referral Hospital, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) uropathogens, including Escherichia coli, Coagulase-negative Staphylococcus, Klebsiella spp., and others, showing high resistance to commonly used antimicrobials such as ampicillin, tetracycline, and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome sequencing identifies exotoxin and antimicrobial resistance profiles of Staphylococcus aureus from Maine dairy farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 14 antimicrobial resistance genes in 29 Staphylococcus aureus isolates from Maine dairy farms, with antibiotic efflux being the primary resistance mechanism. The genes included arIR, arIS, FosB, GlpT, kdpD, LmrS, mepR, mgrA, murA, norA, norC, sdrM, sepA, and vanT.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing was used to analyze the antimicrobial resistance and exotoxin genes in 29 S. aureus isolates from dairy farms in Maine.

full_output.paper_title: Fluoridated silver nanocomposites for caries management: an in-vitro assessment of the cytological and antibacterial profiles.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antibacterial efficacy of fluoridated silver nanocomposites (AgNPs) against Streptococcus mutans, demonstrating their potential as an anti-cariogenic agent with enhanced antimicrobial activity and reduced cytotoxicity compared to sodium fluoride (NaF).
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro assays including MTT cytotoxicity, mitochondrial stress assessment, and MIC determination to evaluate the safety and antibacterial properties of various AgNP formulations.

full_output.paper_title: Sodium ibuprofenate: antibacterial activities and potential β-lactamase inhibition in critical Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Sodium ibuprofenate (NaI) exhibits potent antibacterial and antibiofilm activities against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, with enhanced efficacy in hypertonic conditions. In silico studies suggest ibuprofen may inhibit β-lactamases (CTX-M-15, KPC-2, OXA-23).
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial and antibiofilm activities were assessed using MIC, MBC, time-kill assays, SEM, and in silico docking and molecular dynamics simulations.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity of the endophytic fungal extracts and synergistic effects of combinations of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified endophytic fungi with antibacterial activity against E. coli and P. aeruginosa, particularly highlighting the synergistic effects of combinations with EDTA.
full_output.methodology: Agar well diffusion, broth microdilution, time-kill assay, and molecular identification were used to assess antibacterial activity and synergy.
full_output.sample_size: Nine endophytic fungal isolates from various medicinal plants.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of O25B-ST131 clone and bla (CTX-M-15) gene in Escherichia coli isolated from patients with COVID-19.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the bla CTX-M-15 gene in E. coli isolates from COVID-19 patients, indicating the presence of ESBL-producing strains. The O25B-ST131 clone was also prevalent among these isolates.
full_output.methodology: Real-Time PCR for molecular detection of bla CTX-M-15 gene and O25B-ST131 clone.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and Spread of ESBL-Producing Enterobacteriaceae in Various Reservoirs
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the prevalence and spread of ESBL-encoding genes, particularly bla CTX-M-15, in various reservoirs including humans, animals, and the environment. It highlights the role of horizontal gene transfer and mobile genetic elements in the dissemination of these resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and analysis of environmental and clinical samples.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology and β-lactam resistance mechanisms of Enterobacter cloacae complex isolates obtained from bloodstream infections, Kyoto, Japan.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various β-lactam resistance mechanisms in Enterobacter cloacae complex isolates, including chromosomal AmpC β-lactamases, extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs), and plasmid-mediated AmpC. Additionally, ampD mutations were found to cause derepression of AmpC, leading to resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and mutation analysis were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, antibacterial activity, in silico ADMET prediction, docking, and molecular dynamics studies of substituted phenyl and furan ring containing thiazole Schiff base derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: The study synthesized and evaluated the antibacterial activity of eighteen thiazole Schiff base derivatives against gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, highlighting compounds 2d and 2n as showing high zone of inhibition against B. subtilis. The research also included in silico ADMET prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics studies to assess the compounds' properties and interactions.
full_output.methodology: The study employed synthesis, agar disk diffusion technique for antibacterial activity, in silico ADMET prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of anti-microbial and cytotoxic potential of Streptomyces werraensis GRS9 derived from the sediments of river Ganga.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several bioactive compounds from Streptomyces werraensis GRS9, including N-(4-Methyl-1-Piperazinyl)-1-Napthamide, Dodecanamide, 1,2-Benzenedicarboxylic Acid, Diethyl Ester, Nonanamide, Octanamide, N-Allyl-, Hexadecanamide, 1,4-Cyclohexanediol, (Z)-, TMS Derivative, and 2,4-Di-Tert-Butylthiophenol, which exhibited antimicrobial and anticancer activities.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation, characterization, and bioactivity testing of Streptomyces werraensis GRS9, along with GC-MS and FTIR analysis of its bioactive compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Characteristics, Virulence Profile, and Molecular Epidemiology of Klebsiella pneumoniae Infections in Kidney Transplant Recipients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified KPC-2 as the predominant carbapenemase gene in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) isolates from kidney transplant recipients, highlighting its role in carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and MLST were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms and molecular epidemiology of KP strains.

full_output.paper_title: Deficiency in peptidoglycan recycling promotes β-lactam sensitivity in Caulobacter crescentus.
full_output.key_findings: Deletion of sdpA and ampG leads to β-lactam sensitivity in Caulobacter crescentus, highlighting their roles in peptidoglycan recycling and resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genetic deletion, complementation, and antibiotic susceptibility assays were used to determine the role of sdpA and ampG in β-lactam resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Cytotoxicity and antibacterial activity of polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane modified Ti(3)C(2)T(x) MXene films.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that POSS-doped Ti3C2Tx MXene films exhibit significant antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus, with enhanced biocompatibility compared to pure PLA films.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized solution casting to prepare the films and assessed their antibacterial activity through colony counting and optical density measurements.

full_output.paper_title: Correcting promoter and beta-lactamase ORF orientation in a widely-used retroviral plasmid to restore bacterial growth.

bla.mechanism: The bla gene encodes the enzyme β-lactamase, which hydrolyzes the β-lactam ring in antibiotics such as ampicillin and carbenicillin.
bla.genetic_context: The orientation of the AmpR open reading frame (ORF) and adjacent sequences was inverted relative to expectations.
bla.source: The pBMN-I-GFP plasmid is a widely used retroviral vector for producing retroviral particles, utilized by thousands of laboratories worldwide.
bla.evidence_note: Sequencing, contrary to the available reference sequence, revealed an inversion of the beta-lactamase (bla) gene and part of its promoter, likely disrupting bla expression and, consequently, antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the pBMN-I-GFP plasmid had an inverted beta-lactamase (bla) gene and promoter, leading to lack of ampicillin and carbenicillin resistance. Correcting the orientation restored resistance.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing, restriction digest, and enzymatic assay were used to validate the restoration of beta-lactamase activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the MBT LipidART module for rapid detection of colistin resistance in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, showing good categorical agreement for E. coli but lower performance for K. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: MALDI-TOF MS-based lipid A profiling and broth microdilution susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence factors, molecular characteristics, and resistance mechanisms of carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from pediatric patients in Shanghai, China.

oprD.notes: Mutational inactivation of oprD leads to decreased production of outer membrane porin OprD, contributing to carbapenem resistance.

full_output.key_findings: Carbapenem resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from pediatric patients in Shanghai, China, is primarily mediated by mutational inactivation of the oprD gene, leading to decreased production of the outer membrane porin OprD. Additionally, several virulence factors, including toxA, lasB, exoS, lasA, pilA, and exoY, were widely present in the isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and qRT-PCR were used to detect virulence factors and resistance mechanisms, along with MLST for molecular characterization.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance and molecular characterization of clinical Shigella spp. isolated from hospitals located in Tehran and Qazvin cities, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high resistance rates to amoxicillin, tetracycline, and ampicillin among Shigella isolates, with 70%, 67%, and 60% resistance respectively. Moderate resistance was observed for nalidixic acid and chloramphenicol, while low resistance was noted for imipenem, cefepime, azithromycin, amikacin, kanamycin, gentamicin, norfloxacin, and cefoxitin. Approximately 27.5% of the isolates were classified as multidrug-resistant.
full_output.methodology: The study used pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) for genotyping and disc diffusion method for antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: The emergence of highly resistant and hypervirulent Escherichia coli ST405 clone in a tertiary hospital over 8 years.

blaNDM-5.validation_method: quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the ST405 clone of Escherichia coli as highly resistant and hypervirulent, with unique resistance genes mph(E) and msr(E) contributing to macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and genomic analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes and mutations in CREC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Pneumococcal genotype 23B1 as a driver of increased 23B serotype carriage, penicillin non-susceptibility, and invasive disease in Belgium: a retrospective analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 23B1 as a novel penicillin non-susceptible genotype driving increased 23B serotype carriage and invasive disease in Belgium. 23B1 is associated with higher penicillin MICs and contributes to the rise in penicillin non-susceptibility among 23B isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze 23B isolates from carriage and invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) cases.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-Resistant, Virulence Plasmid-Harboring Klebsiella pneumoniae, United States.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies six pVir-CRKP isolates from the United States, highlighting their multidrug resistance and enhanced virulence traits. These isolates exhibit resistance to various antibiotics, including carbapenems, cephalosporins, fluoroquinolones, and aminoglycosides, due to the presence of specific AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.methodology: The study uses a combination of experimental techniques (potentiometry, mass spectrometry, UV–vis, circular dichroism, electron paramagnetic resonance, and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy) and density functional theory calculations to analyze the coordination chemistry of the peptides with Cu(II) ions and their antimicrobial activity against various pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Interfering with proton and electron transfer enables antibacterial starvation therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel antibacterial strategy using a Schottky heterojunction film composed of gold and magnesium-iron mixed metal oxides (Au/MgFe-MMO) to disrupt bacterial energy metabolism by interfering with proton and electron transfer, leading to bacterial death without harming mammalian cells.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a Schottky heterojunction film composed of gold and magnesium-iron mixed metal oxides (Au/MgFe-MMO) to evaluate its antibacterial efficacy through in vitro and in vivo experiments, including bacterial culture, live/dead staining, SEM, TEM, and transcriptomic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of resistance patterns and genetic diversity of Escherichia coli isolated from geese in Northeastern China.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that over 70% of Escherichia coli isolates from geese in Heilongjiang Province were resistant to ampicillin, amoxicillin, imipenem, tetracycline, and doxycycline, with 92.66% of the strains showing resistance to 6 to 9 drugs.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the K-B paper diffusion method, and PFGE was used for molecular typing to assess genetic diversity.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the antibacterial efficacy of Opuntia monacantha in combatting methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of Opuntia monacantha against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and identified that the n-hexane and chloroform fractions exhibited significant inhibitory effects.
full_output.methodology: Phytochemical screening, GC-MS analysis, and well diffusion assay were employed to assess the antibacterial potential of Opuntia monacantha extracts against MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Global analysis of the metaplasmidome: ecological drivers and spread of antibiotic resistance genes across ecosystems.

full_output.paper_title: TROJAN-MDR: in vitro activity of cefiderocol and comparators against multidrug-resistant Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains in Southern France, evaluation of available testing methods performances.

full_output.paper_title: Iron-dependent mechanisms in Acinetobacter baumannii: pathogenicity and resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the iron acquisition mechanisms in Acinetobacter baumannii, focusing on siderophore-mediated iron uptake and the role of the TonB-dependent system in iron acquisition.

full_output.paper_title: Capsular Typing and Molecular Characterization of Streptococcus agalactiae Strains Isolated From Bovine Mastitis in Iran.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility of gram-negative strains isolated from bloodstream infections in China: Results from the study for monitoring antimicrobial resistance trends (SMART) 2018-2020.
