full_output.key_findings: This study identifies several mutations associated with drug resistance in multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MDR-MTB) strains from Hainan Island, including katG_S315T, rpoB_S450L, embB_M306I/V, gyrA_D94G/A94V, and others. These mutations are linked to resistance against isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, moxifloxacin, and other anti-TB drugs.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (DST) were used to identify and validate resistance-associated mutations in MDR-MTB strains.

full_output.paper_title: Diagnostic efficacy of Mycoplasma pneumoniae antibody and procalcitonin in children with Mycoplasma pneumonia.

23S rRNA.notes: Mutations at positions 2063 and 2064 of the 23S rRNA gene were detected in 22.5% of children with MPP.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the 23S rRNA gene at positions 2063 and 2064 in 22.5% of children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia, which are associated with macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR with TaqMan fluorescent probe technology was used to detect drug-resistance gene mutations in the MPP group.

full_output.paper_title: Optimizing Extracellular Products from Vibrio proteolyticus for Their Use as Postbiotics in Aquaculture.

aip56.mechanism: induces apoptosis of fish macrophages and neutrophils
aip56.validation_method: qRT-PCR showing downregulation of aip56 gene expression

full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial activity of extracellular products (ECPs) from Vibrio proteolyticus DCF12.2 against various fish pathogens, including Photobacterium damselae subsp. piscicida. The ECPs showed inhibitory effects on the growth of these pathogens and downregulated the aip56 gene, which is involved in virulence.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar well diffusion assays, hydrolytic activity tests, and qRT-PCR to evaluate the antibacterial activity and gene expression effects of V. proteolyticus ECPs.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic carry over is a confounding factor for cell-based antimicrobial research applications.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the antimicrobial activity observed in conditioned medium (CM) from various cell lines was due to residual antibiotics, specifically penicillin, adhering to tissue culture plastic surfaces rather than being secreted by the cells themselves.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the antimicrobial activity of conditioned medium (CM) from different cell lines, investigated the effect of cellular confluency, pre-washing, and sampling time points on antimicrobial activity, and tested the impact of antibiotic concentration and tissue culture plastic types.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of efflux pumps by FDA-approved drugs oxiconazole and sertaconazole restores antibiotic susceptibility in multidrug-resistant S. aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Oxiconazole and sertaconazole inhibit efflux pumps in multidrug-resistant S. aureus, restoring antibiotic susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Efflux pump inhibition assays, susceptibility testing, and synergy assays were used to evaluate the effect of oxiconazole and sertaconazole on S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: CRISPR/Cas9-targeted smpB mutation revealing roles in biofilm formation, motility, and antibiotic susceptibility in Acinetobacter baumannii.

smpB.notes: The smpB gene mutation affects antibiotic susceptibility profiles.

full_output.key_findings: The smpB gene mutation in Acinetobacter baumannii leads to reduced biofilm formation, impaired twitching motility, and altered antibiotic susceptibility profiles, indicating a critical role of SmpB in bacterial pathogenicity and stress response.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing was used to generate a targeted smpB mutant in A. baumannii, followed by assessment of growth, biofilm formation, motility, antibiotic susceptibility, and virulence.

full_output.paper_title: The inhibitory effect of M2 macrophage-derived exosomes on gefitinib resistant lung adenocarcinoma cells through the MIF/TIMP1/CD74 axis.

TIMP1.mechanism: interacts with CD74 and MIF, activating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway to promote gefitinib resistance
TIMP1.validation_method: qRT-PCR, ELISA, CCK-8, flow cytometry, Western blot

full_output.key_findings: M2 macrophage-derived exosomes inhibit the proliferation of gefitinib-resistant LA cells by delivering TIMP1, which interacts with CD74 and MIF to activate the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, promoting gefitinib resistance.
full_output.methodology: qRT-PCR, ELISA, CCK-8, flow cytometry, Western blot, co-IP, pull-down, and animal models were used to validate the role of TIMP1 in gefitinib resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Global soil antibiotic resistance genes are associated with increasing risk and connectivity to human resistome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in soil, highlighting their increasing risk and connectivity to the human resistome. Key findings include the identification of genes such as catI, catB3, eptA, mph(B), tet(M), aadA, erm(B), ANT(2")-Ia, AAC(3)-VIa, lsa(E), ANT(6)-Ia, mef(B), and dfrB1, which confer resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis and comparative genomics were used to characterize ARGs in soil samples and their association with human clinical resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial susceptibility of gram-negative bacteria in the urine of females in their reproductive ages in the Tamale Teaching Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Klebsiella spp, E. coli, Acinetobacter baumannii, Citrobacter freudii, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa as the most common gram-negative bacteria causing UTIs in females aged 15-45 years. Klebsiella spp was the most prevalent, followed by E. coli. The study also noted resistance patterns to various antibiotics, with Acinetobacter baumannii showing resistance to meropenem.
full_output.methodology: The study involved urine culture and susceptibility testing of 132 samples collected from females aged 15-45 years at Tamale Teaching Hospital. Antimicrobial susceptibility was assessed using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Use of the bacteriophage-derived endolysin CHAPK-SH3blys as a potent novel treatment for biofilm-associated Staphylococcus aureus wound infections.
full_output.key_findings: CHAPK-SH3blys endolysin exhibits potent antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, including biofilm-associated strains, with an MIC of 3.9 µg/mL. It effectively disrupts biofilms under various conditions and shows low cytotoxicity and hemolytic activity.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, biofilm disruption assays, and cytotoxicity evaluations were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Amino acid competition shapes Acinetobacter baumannii gut carriage.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: mutant grew with ornithine but not arginine as the sole carbon source
mutant grew with ornithine but not arginine as the sole carbon source

astO.evidence_note: The paper describes the role of AstO in ornithine catabolism and its importance for A. baumannii gut colonization, but does not explicitly state that the mutations L125A and H229A confer resistance to any specific drugs.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AstO as a key gene involved in ornithine catabolism, which is crucial for A. baumannii gut colonization. Dietary ornithine supplementation enhances long-term gut colonization by A. baumannii.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic manipulation, growth assays, and mouse models to investigate the role of AstO in A. baumannii gut colonization.

full_output.paper_title: Enhancement of carrimycin production in Streptomyces spiramyceticus 54-IA by the reporter-guided selection method with traditional mutagenesis.

mutations_found.validated_by: genomic sequencing and comparison between F2R-15 and 54-IA

bsm3.notes: bsm3 mutation leads to macrolide resistance

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antibiotic resistance profiles of ESKAPE pathogens in the neonatal intensive care unit of the women and newborn hospital in Lusaka, Zambia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) ESKAPE pathogens in the NICU, with K. pneumoniae, A. baumannii, and S. aureus showing significant resistance to multiple antibiotics, including carbapenems, cephalosporins, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method on selected bacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A Retrospective Analysis of Urinary Tract Infections With Special Reference to the Phenotypic and Genotypic Detection of Fosfomycin-Resistant Escherichia coli Isolates at a Tertiary Care Center in South India.

fosA3.encodes: protein that converts glutathione to fosfomycin

full_output.key_findings: The study identified fosfomycin-resistant Escherichia coli isolates, with the fosA3 gene detected in one of the three resistant isolates.
full_output.methodology: Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method and real-time PCR for detecting fosfomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Eco-friendly fabrication of ZnO quantum dots using Brassica rapa (L.): metabolomic profiling and antimicrobial efficacy against foodborne pathogens supported by in-silico insights.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antimicrobial efficacy of ZnO quantum dots (ZnO-QDs) synthesized using Brassica rapa root extract, highlighting their effectiveness against foodborne pathogens. Key phytochemicals in the extract show strong binding affinities to targets like DNA gyrase 2 and sterol demethylase CYP51B, suggesting potential mechanisms for their antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study uses GC/MS, LC-ESI-TOF-MS, and molecular docking to identify antimicrobial compounds and evaluate their interactions with microbial targets.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of a new bla(OXA-51-Like) variant (bla(OXA-1328)) and a novel sequence type (ST3457/2790) in Acinetobacter baumannii isolated from community sewage and an incinerator surface in Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a new bla(OXA-51-like) variant, bla(OXA-1328), in Acinetobacter baumannii from community sewage in Nigeria, along with a novel sequence type (ST3457/2790) from an incinerator surface. It also detects other bla OXA variants, including bla(OXA-707) and bla(OXA-120), and blaADC-25.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes and sequence types in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Postbiotics enhance the efficacy of derivative compound mouthwash against clinical Helicobacter pylori strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that postbiotic-glycerol monolaurate mouthwash was highly effective against Helicobacter pylori, reducing adhesion, biofilm formation, and cagA expression, with low cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the anti-H. pylori activity of postbiotics and derivative compounds through agar well diffusion, broth microdilution, and checkerboard assays, and assessed their effects on cell viability, adhesion, cytokine suppression, and biofilm eradication.

full_output.paper_title: Overview of changes in the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute Performance Standards for Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing: M100 32nd and 33rd editions.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses updates to CLSI M100 performance standards for antimicrobial susceptibility testing, focusing on revised breakpoints for aminoglycosides, piperacillin-tazobactam, and other antimicrobial agents, highlighting challenges in setting breakpoints for P. aeruginosa and the importance of considering pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic data.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews clinical data, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic literature, and evaluates breakpoints for antimicrobial agents against various bacterial species.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of how laser photostimulation at two wavelengths alters the antimicrobial potential of Streptomycetes spp.
full_output.key_findings: Laser photostimulation at 650 nm increased the antibacterial activity of Streptomyces lienomycini, leading to the identification of thiophene as a novel antibacterial compound.
full_output.methodology: GC-MS analysis and antibacterial sensitivity tests were used to evaluate the antimicrobial potential of Streptomycetes isolates after laser irradiation.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of drug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae phylogroups (K. quasipneumoniae and K. variicola) causing human infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the emergence of drug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae phylogroups K. quasipneumoniae and K. variicola, with significant resistance to carbapenems, colistin, and polymyxin B. Key resistance mechanisms included mutations in the PhoP and PhoQ genes and the presence of carbapenemase genes such as bla NDM, bla OXA-48, bla VIM, and bla IMP.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Ecological connectivity of genomic markers of antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli in Hong Kong.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates from Hong Kong, including blaTEM-1, floR, tet(A), aph(3')-Ia, blaNDM, tet(X4), and mcr, which confer resistance to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of 1016 E. coli isolates using Nanopore long-read sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of multidrug resistant gram-negative bacteria and associated factors among gram-negative blood culture isolates at Tikur Anbessa Specialized Hospital: a retrospective study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) gram-negative bacteria, with 81% of isolates being MDR. Carbapenem resistance was 58.1%, with higher rates in Klebsiella pneumoniae (77.4%) and Escherichia coli (47.8%).
full_output.methodology: Retrospective study analyzing 137 gram-negative blood culture isolates using disc diffusion method for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: High-fat and low-fiber diet elevates the gut resistome: a comparative metagenomic study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that a high-fat/low-fiber diet increases the gut resistome, virulome, and mobilome in mice and humans, while a high-fiber/low-fat diet reduces them. Several AMR genes, including vanD, vanG, vanR, vanS, lsa, vatB, vatC, bacA, bcrA, cat, blaTME-136, aph(3''')-III, cfr, tet(X), blaSHV, penA, tetM, tetL, tetW, and fexB, were identified as being associated with this dietary impact.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of gut microbiota from mice and human stool samples.
full_output.sample_size: 21 mice, 5 individuals with high-fat/low-fiber diet, 11 individuals with obesity

full_output.paper_title: Severe Staphylococcus aureus infection: associated factors and outcomes.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the prevalence of MRSA infections among PLHIV and notes that all MRSA isolates were susceptible to cotrimoxazole, doxycycline, and linezolid, indicating a community-associated MRSA (ca-MRSA) phenotype.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of patients with S. aureus infections, focusing on clinical and demographic data, antibiotic susceptibility, and outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Component characterization of Smilax glabra Roxb., and its inhibitory activity against Helicobacter pylori through targeted suppression of its secreted urease.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies astilbin and engeletin as the main active ingredients in Smilax glabra Roxb. (SGR) that inhibit urease activity in Helicobacter pylori, with astilbin showing stronger inhibitory effects compared to engeletin.
full_output.methodology: UPLC-ESI-MS/MS analysis, enzyme inhibitory activity assay, molecular docking analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of commensal Clostridium perfringens isolates from chickens in Hungarian poultry farms between 2022 and 2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high resistance rates to lincomycin (82.8%) and enrofloxacin (57.9%) among commensal Clostridium perfringens isolates from Hungarian poultry farms, highlighting the need for continued surveillance of antimicrobial resistance in these strains.
full_output.methodology: The study determined antimicrobial susceptibility using MIC values and PCR for toxin gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Trends in Antibiotic Resistance in Uropathogens at Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital (2019-2024): A Retrospective Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights high resistance rates to commonly prescribed antibiotics such as ampicillin (91.3%) and sulfamethoxazole (91.6%) among uropathogens, with Klebsiella spp. showing the highest resistance. Multidrug resistance (MDR) was prevalent, with 56.9% of isolates being MDR, and 70% of these MDR isolates were ESBL producers.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 939 urine culture-positive records with antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the disc diffusion method.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Enterococcus faecium as the predominant species causing bloodstream infections in critically ill patients, with high rates of multidrug resistance to ampicillin, aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing microbiological profiles and antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of Enterococcus isolates from critically ill patients.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatic tools powered by machine learning to identify antibiotic-resistant genes and virulence factors in Escherichia coli from sepsis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several known and novel antibiotic-resistant genes in E. coli isolates from sepsis patients using whole-genome sequencing and machine learning. Key findings include the presence of blaCTX-M, blaSHV, blaTEM, aac(6')-Ib, aadA, qnrS1, ermB, mexAB-OprM, acrAB-TolC, and oqxAB genes, which confer resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of 18 E. coli isolates followed by bioinformatic analysis and machine learning to identify antibiotic-resistant genes and virulence factors.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of potent endolysins against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and other gram-negative ESKAPE pathogens by an agar-based screening method.
full_output.key_findings: Three endolysins, L0779, L0782, and L0799, were identified and characterized for their bactericidal activity against Gram-negative ESKAPE pathogens, with L0782 showing the most potent activity.
full_output.methodology: Agar-based overlay assay, peptidoglycan hydrolysis assay, and lytic assay were used to evaluate the endolysins' activity.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant E. Coli in wastewater sources: a comparative study and identification of resistance hotspots.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla TEM, bla CTX-M, and bla OXA-48 as the most prevalent beta-lactamase genes in multidrug-resistant E. coli isolates from wastewater sources.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, conventional PCR, and phylogenetic analysis were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibitory effects of berberine against Streptococcus mutans: an in vitro insight on its anticaries potential.
full_output.key_findings: Berberine (BBR) inhibits the growth of planktonic Streptococcus mutans and its biofilm formation, reduces the expression of virulence genes such as gtfB, gtfC, gtfD, ldh, vicR, liaR, and comD, and exhibits good biocompatibility with human oral cells and macrophages.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity of BBR was evaluated using MIC, MBC, growth curve assays, crystal violet staining, CLSM, SEM, and qRT-PCR to measure gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of sulbactam in combination with other antimicrobial agents against extensively drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of sulbactam (SUL) in combination with other antimicrobial agents against extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Acinetobacter baumannii. SUL showed variable MICs, and combinations with fosfomycin (FOS), amikacin (AMI), and meropenem (MER) exhibited synergistic effects against a significant proportion of isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution and checkerboard methods to determine MICs and assess synergy, along with time-kill assays to evaluate bactericidal activity.

full_output.paper_title: ABCF protein-mediated resistance shapes bacterial responses to antibiotics based on their type and concentration.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TiaA and Are5sc as ABCF-ATPases that confer resistance to specific antibiotics, with TiaA playing a critical role in pleuromutilin resistance and Are5sc contributing to resistance against lincosamides and streptogramin A.
full_output.methodology: Genetic, OMICs, and biochemical approaches were used to analyze the role of TiaA and Are5sc in antibiotic resistance and regulation.

full_output.paper_title: CRISPR-Cas9 targeting the blaKPC gene in a clinical isolate of Klebsiella michiganensis: Reduction of imipenem resistance and changes in genomic carbapenem resistance determinants.

blaKPC.mechanism: targeted disruption of the blaKPC gene leads to reduced carbapenem resistance
blaKPC.validation_method: CRISPR-Cas9 mediated plasmid clearance and reduced gene expression
blaKPC.genetic_context: blaKPC gene is carried by an IncN plasmid
blaKPC.evidence_note: The paper demonstrates that targeting the blaKPC gene with CRISPR-Cas9 reduces carbapenem resistance in both E. coli and K. michiganensis.

ompK36.notes: Downregulation of ompK36 gene expression was observed in re-sensitized transformants.
ompK36.evidence_note: The paper states that "the expression of this gene was significantly downregulated in the KM S group" and that "ompK36 downregulation" was found.

mutations_found.protein_change: frameshift mutation (1970delT) and single nucleotide variant (1974C > A)

acrB.notes: Frameshift mutation and single nucleotide variant in acrB gene were identified in KM S transformants.
acrB.evidence_note: The paper states that a frameshift mutation and a single nucleotide variant in the acrB gene were identified in KM S transformants.

recN.notes: Insertion mutation in recN gene was observed in KM S transformants.
recN.evidence_note: The insertion mutation in the recN gene was observed in KM S transformants through whole genome sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: CRISPR-Cas9 targeting the blaKPC gene in Klebsiella michiganensis reduced imipenem resistance through plasmid copy number reduction and decreased blaKPC gene expression. Mutations in ompK36, acrB, and recN were observed, contributing to resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas9 system was used to target the blaKPC gene, with validation through plasmid clearance, gene expression analysis, and whole-genome sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: Natural transformation contributes to the acquisition of novel genes, including antimicrobial resistance genes such as bla, fosA, and ant(3")-IIA, in Acinetobacter baumannii and Legionella pneumophila.
full_output.methodology: Genome analysis, homologous recombination tracking, and transformation rate measurements.

full_output.paper_title: Is ampicillin plus cephalosporins a therapeutic option for Ampicillin-Susceptible Enterococcus faecium?
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the effectiveness of combining ampicillin with ceftriaxone or ceftaroline against ampicillin-susceptible Enterococcus faecium (ASEfm) strains, revealing that ampicillin combined with ceftaroline showed synergistic and/or additive effects in 7 out of 10 strains, whereas ampicillin combined with ceftriaxone showed less pronounced synergy.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing, time-kill assays, and genomic analysis were conducted to assess the effectiveness of antibiotic combinations against ASEfm strains.

full_output.paper_title: MexR and NalD are pyocyanin-responsive transcriptional repressors of the efflux pump MexAB-OprM in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MexR and NalD as pyocyanin-responsive transcriptional repressors of the efflux pump MexAB-OprM in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Pyocyanin binding to MexR and NalD leads to their dissociation from the mexA promoter, resulting in the derepression of mexAB-oprM expression and increased antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Electrophoretic mobility shift assay, microscale thermophoresis, surface plasmon resonance, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to characterize the interaction between pyocyanin and the transcriptional repressors MexR and NalD.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic decoding of drug-resistant tuberculosis transmission in Thailand over three decades.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the ddn Gly81Ser mutation associated with delamanid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Thailand.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize drug resistance and transmission dynamics of Mtb isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the efficacy of BNT331-EL, an endolysin, in reducing Gardnerella in vaginal samples from women with bacterial vaginosis (BV). BNT331-EL significantly reduced viable Gardnerella by ≥94% at 20-50 µg/mL over 19 hours, demonstrating selective targeting of Gardnerella without affecting commensal lactobacilli like L. crispatus.
full_output.methodology: Ex vivo treatment of vaginal samples with BNT331-EL, followed by FISH and viability qPCR to assess bacterial load and biofilm disruption.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic use in oyster hatcheries promotes rapid spread of a highly transferable and modular resistance plasmid in Vibrio.
full_output.key_findings: Chloramphenicol use in oyster hatcheries selects for a highly transferable and modular resistance plasmid, pAQU-MAN, which carries the chloramphenicol resistance gene catA2 and the tetracycline resistance gene tet(B).
full_output.methodology: Pool sequencing, qPCR, plasmid sequencing, and conjugation assays were used to analyze the resistance plasmid and its spread in Vibrio bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence and molecular evolution of carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent ST23 Klebsiella pneumoniae: The superbug phenomenon in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the emergence and molecular evolution of carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent ST23 Klebsiella pneumoniae in China, highlighting the presence of various carbapenemase genes such as bla KPC-2, bla NDM, and bla OXA-48, along with virulence factors like rmpA, rmpA2, iroN, iucA, and pagO.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a comprehensive literature review, genotyping, and phylogenetic analysis of ST23 CR-hvKP isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring antibiotic resistance in diverse homologs of the dihydrofolate reductase protein family through broad mutational scanning.

dhfr.mechanism: confers resistance to trimethoprim by restoring metabolic function in E. coli ΔfolAΔthyA cells
dhfr.validation_method: multiplexed in vivo assay testing ability to restore metabolic function and confer trimethoprim resistance

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial etiology of urinary tract infections and their sensitivity patterns towards commonly used antibiotics in port Sudan City, Sudan: a retrospective study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance among urinary tract infection (UTI) pathogens in Port Sudan, with Escherichia coli being the most common pathogen. High resistance to carbapenems and other antibiotics was observed, highlighting the need for updated treatment guidelines and surveillance.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of urine culture and antibiotic sensitivity data from 328 patients in Port Sudan.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and Antifungal Tannic Acid Coating on Plasma-Activated Titanium Alloy Surface.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that tannic acid coatings on plasma-activated titanium alloy surfaces exhibit strong antibacterial and antifungal activities against E. coli, S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, and C. albicans. The coatings with ≥5% tannic acid show significant bactericidal effects and inhibit fungal growth, making them promising for reducing implant-associated infections.
full_output.methodology: Surface characterization, tannic acid release profiling, cytocompatibility testing, and antimicrobial activity assessments were performed using SEM, XPS, Folin-Ciocalteu assay, MTT test, and culture-based methods.

full_output.paper_title: Assessing 5-Aminolevulinic Acid as a Natural Biocide Precursor for Light-Activated Eradication of Pseudomonas spp.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the efficacy of 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) in antimicrobial photodynamic inactivation (aPDI) against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Pseudomonas putida, showing that 5-ALA enhances the photodynamic effect when combined with glucose, leading to significant bacterial reduction.
full_output.methodology: The study uses photodynamic inactivation with 5-ALA and glucose, analyzing bacterial viability through fluorescence spectroscopy and light exposure experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Development and Evaluation of Graphene Oxide-Enhanced Chitosan Sponges as a Potential Antimicrobial Wound Dressing for Infected Wound Management.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed and evaluated chitosan-based sponges enhanced with graphene oxide (GO) as potential antimicrobial wound dressings. The results showed that GO-modified dressings exhibited enhanced antimicrobial activity against E. coli and S. aureus, although the effectiveness varied depending on the strain and the method of application. The study also highlighted the importance of optimizing GO concentration to maximize antimicrobial efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the fabrication of chitosan sponges with and without GO, followed by physico-mechanical characterization, cytocompatibility testing, and antimicrobial activity assessments.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibitory Effect of Allyl Isothiocyanate on Cariogenicity of Streptococcus mutans.
full_output.key_findings: Allyl isothiocyanate (AITC) inhibits the survival, growth, and biofilm formation of Streptococcus mutans. RNA sequencing analysis revealed that AITC alters the expression of numerous genes, including comYD, SMU_1980c, SMU_1141c, SMU_1671c, SMU_382c, and SMU_383c, which are involved in genetic competence and catalytic activity.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial survival, growth, and biofilm assays combined with RNA sequencing and bioinformatics analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Axially Disubstituted Silicon(IV) Phthalocyanine as a Potent Sensitizer for Antimicrobial and Anticancer Photo and Sonodynamic Therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimicrobial and anticancer properties of axially disubstituted silicon(IV) phthalocyanine (SiPc) as a photosensitizer and sonosensitizer, demonstrating its effectiveness in photodynamic and sonodynamic therapies.
full_output.methodology: The study uses photodynamic and sonodynamic therapy evaluations, including measurements of singlet oxygen quantum yields, photodecomposition, fluorescence, and antibacterial and anticancer activity assessments.

full_output.paper_title: Cloning, Heterologous Expression, and Antifungal Activity Evaluation of a Novel Truncated TasA Protein from Bacillus amyloliquefaciens BS-3.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a novel truncated TasA protein from Bacillus amyloliquefaciens BS-3, which exhibited potent antifungal activity against Colletotrichum acutatum and Alternaria heveae. The protein was successfully expressed and purified, showing significant inhibition of spore germination and mycelial growth of these pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, heterologous expression in E. coli, protein purification, and antifungal activity assays were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Amino Acid Substitutions in Bacteriocin Lactolisterin BU Reveal Functional Domains Involved in Biological Activity Against Staphylococcus aureus.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: increased antimicrobial activity but altered toxicity profiles
mutations_found.validated_by: LDH cytotoxicity assay, zebrafish embryo toxicity assay

G13A.notes: G13A variant showed increased toxicity towards mammalian cells and zebrafish embryos

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies amino acid substitutions in Lactolisterin LBU that enhance antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, with G3A, G7A, and G13A showing improved efficacy compared to the wild-type peptide.
full_output.methodology: Spot-on-the-lawn assay, MIC and MBC determination, hemolysis assays, and cytotoxicity assessments were conducted to evaluate the antimicrobial and toxicological properties of LBU variants.

full_output.paper_title: Pinene-Based Chiral Bipyridine Ligands Drive Potent Antibacterial Activity in Rhenium(I) Complexes.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of chiral rhenium(I) complexes with pinene-based bipyridine ligands, which exhibit potent antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus strains, including methicillin-resistant and methicillin-sensitive variants.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of rhenium(I) complexes, antimicrobial activity testing, and structural characterization using NMR, mass spectrometry, and X-ray diffraction.

full_output.paper_title: No Impact of Vancomycin MIC, AUC, or AUC/MIC in Enterococcus faecium Bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found no significant association between vancomycin MIC, AUC, or AUC/MIC and in-hospital mortality or recurrence in Enterococcus faecium bacteremia.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of E. faecium strains and their susceptibility to vancomycin, along with calculation of AUC and AUC/MIC ratios.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a Y323H substitution in the AZD5148 binding epitope of TcdB, which occurs in clade 4 and is associated with low-frequency occurrences in certain geographic regions.
full_output.methodology: Sequence analysis and in vitro neutralization assays were used to evaluate the conservation of the AZD5148 binding epitope in C. difficile isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic variability of Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli strains isolated from Paraguayan cattle.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the fosA7 gene, which confers resistance to fosfomycin, in four isolates, and the sitABCD gene, which confers resistance to hydrogen peroxide, in one isolate.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing was performed on 40 strains using the Illumina MiSeq platform.

full_output.paper_title: Combinations comprising dual β-lactams and a β-lactamase inhibitor achieve optimal synergistic inhibition of Mycobacterium abscessus growth.

blaMab.validation_method: experimental validation through MIC testing and FICI analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the β-lactamase BlaMab as a key factor in resistance to β-lactams in Mycobacterium abscessus, and highlights the synergistic effects of dual β-lactam combinations and β-lactamase inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: Checkerboard assay, MIC testing, and FICI analysis were used to evaluate synergistic effects of β-lactam and β-lactamase inhibitor combinations against Mycobacterium abscessus.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomics and untargeted metabolomics reveal antibiotic resistance dynamics in an anaerobic digestion-composting system treating organic fraction of municipal solid waste.

oleC.mechanism: efflux pump that leads to the excretion of chemical compounds, such as antibiotics, outside the bacterial cell
oleC.evidence_note: Most macrolides resistance genes consisted of the oleC gene (oleandomycin), whose mechanism of antibiotic resistance is efflux pump that leads to the excretion of chemical compounds, such as antibiotics, outside the bacterial cell

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in different matrices of an anaerobic digestion-composting system treating organic fraction of municipal solid waste. Key findings include the prevalence of glycopeptide, macrolide, and rifamycin resistance genes in mature compost, as well as the presence of fluoroquinolone and aminoglycoside resistance genes in digestate and its fractions.
full_output.methodology: The study used metagenomics and untargeted metabolomics to analyze the resistome and antibiotic compounds in different matrices of the waste treatment system.

full_output.paper_title: Advanced monolayer and layer-by-layer nanocapsule systems for sustained release of carvacrol and trans-cinnamaldehyde against multidrug-resistant Salmonella in poultry.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy of carvacrol and trans-cinnamaldehyde, in free and nanoencapsulated forms, as natural alternatives to chlorine for inactivating antibiotic-resistant Salmonella in chicken. The combination of monolayer and layer-by-layer carvacrol nanocapsules at a total concentration of 4% resulted in the highest Salmonella reduction (3.7 log CFU/g) after 11 days.
full_output.methodology: The study assessed the antimicrobial efficacy of various treatments against antibiotic-resistant Salmonella strains in poultry using microbial enumeration techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence of KPC-71 or the presence of NDM combined with a high expression of bla(SHV) contributes to low-level cefiderocol resistance in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in China.

bla(KPC-71).mechanism: enhances CFDC binding via a reduced K i and a potentially enlarged active-site pocket
bla(KPC-71).validation_method: cloning and expression in E. coli BL21(DE3) with MIC testing
bla(KPC-71).evidence_note: The paper states that KPC-71 enhances CFDC binding via a reduced K i and a potentially enlarged active-site pocket. It also mentions the key substitution Thr180_Ser181insSer and the genetic context Tn1721-IS Kpn6-bla KPC -IS Kpn27 -Tn3.

blaKPC-71.mechanism: enhanced affinity for cefiderocol and reduced affinity for avibactam
blaKPC-71.validation_method: expression in E. coli and MIC testing

KPC-71.notes: The Thr180_Ser181insSer mutation increases cefiderocol resistance and decreases avibactam inhibition.
KPC-71.evidence_note: The mutation was identified in Kp15 and Kp2 strains, and its effect on resistance was validated through cloning and expression experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies KPC-71 and NDM, in combination with high expression of bla(SHV), as contributors to low-level cefiderocol resistance in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. KPC-71 was shown to significantly decrease cefiderocol susceptibility, while NDM and bla(SHV) also played roles in resistance.
full_output.methodology: Cloning and expression of β-lactamase genes in E. coli BL21(DE3) followed by MIC testing and enzyme kinetics analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Sustainable Joullié-Ugi and Continuous Flow Implementation Led to Novel Captopril-Inspired Broad-Spectrum Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development of novel MBL inhibitors inspired by captopril, focusing on improving inhibitory activity against various MBLs while minimizing off-target effects on ACE-1.
full_output.methodology: The research involved the rational design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of indoline-based MBL inhibitors, along with computational docking and molecular dynamics simulations to understand their binding mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Thyme-synthesized silver nanoparticles mitigate immunosuppression, oxidative damage, and histopathological alterations induced by multidrug-resistant Enterococcus faecalis in Oreochromis niloticus: in vitro and in vivo assays.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of thyme-synthesized silver nanoparticles (thyme-AgNPs) against multidrug-resistant Enterococcus faecalis (MDR E. faecalis) in Oreochromis niloticus, demonstrating their ability to reduce immunosuppression, oxidative stress, and histopathological damage.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo assays, including agar diffusion, MIC/MBC determination, and histopathological analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology, antimicrobial resistance, and virulence characteristics of predominant methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus clones with strong biofilm-producing capability from a tertiary teaching hospital in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ST5-t2460, ST59-t437, and ST239-t030 as the predominant MRSA clones with strong biofilm-producing capability. These clones showed varying levels of antimicrobial resistance and virulence gene profiles, with ST5-t2460 and ST239-t030 displaying higher resistance to several antibiotics and more virulence factors compared to ST59-t437.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of phenotypic resistance profiling, biofilm formation assays, molecular typing (MLST and spa typing), and PCR for virulence gene detection to characterize the MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Determinants of indiscriminate antimicrobial use in commercial chicken farms in Bangladesh and their impact on food safety and public health.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the widespread and careless use of antimicrobials in Bangladesh's poultry industry, driven by inadequate knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) and insufficient veterinary oversight. It identifies factors associated with antimicrobial use, such as owner-managed farms, permissive beliefs about antimicrobial use, and the use of leftover antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted a cross-sectional survey of 340 commercial chicken farms in Bangladesh, analyzing antimicrobial use patterns and associated factors through questionnaires, statistical analyses, and logistic regression models.

full_output.paper_title: Performance of disc diffusion and gradient strip test on different Mueller-Hinton agar media plates and ComASP® and Bruker UMIC® Cefiderocol Microdilution Panels for cefiderocol susceptibility testing in carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaPAC-1 gene, an AmpC-type beta-lactamase, as contributing to cefiderocol resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Overexpression of PAC-1 increased cefiderocol MICs, indicating its role in reducing susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study involved cloning and expressing the blaPAC-1 gene in E. coli, followed by MIC testing to evaluate its impact on cefiderocol resistance.

full_output.paper_title: In-silico Analysis of a Novel MCR-1.1 Variant on an IncX4 Plasmid Attenuating Colistin Resistance in Multidrug-Resistant Escherichia coli ST131.

mcr-1.1.validation_method: in-silico structural analysis and molecular docking

mutations_found.validated_by: in-silico structural analysis and molecular docking

mcr-1.1.notes: The F265L substitution in MCR-1.1 impairs lipid A modification, reducing colistin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: A novel mcr-1.1 variant on an IncX4 plasmid in E. coli ST131 exhibits reduced colistin resistance due to a F265L substitution in the MCR-1.1 enzyme, which impairs lipid A modification.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, in-silico structural analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations.

full_output.paper_title: Development of triaryl antimicrobials by scaffold hopping from an aminopropanol hit targeting bacterial RNA polymerase-NusG interactions.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of triaryl inhibitors targeting the interaction between bacterial RNA polymerase (RNAP) and NusG, demonstrating potent antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacteria, especially Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and evaluation of triaryl compounds targeting the RNAP-NusG interaction, with antimicrobial activity tested against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of novel zinc-binding proteins in the cell wall of Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ZnuE, ZnuF, and ZnuG as part of the znu gene cluster involved in zinc metabolism in Corynebacterium diphtheriae. ZnuE is critical for growth in zinc-limited medium, and ZnuF and ZnuG bind zinc in vitro. ZnuF localizes to the cell wall independently of known sortase enzymes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic deletion mutants, plasmid complementation, thermal shift assays, and cell fractionation techniques to analyze the function and localization of ZnuE, ZnuF, and ZnuG.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of polyamine resistance in Staphylococcus aureus through modulation of potassium transport.

pgl.notes: mutations in pgl were not recovered in MN8, frequently recovered in both HFH-30364 and RN4850 strains

menD.notes: inactivation of menD increased resistance to spermine

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that mutations in the ktrA and ktrD genes of Staphylococcus aureus confer resistance to polyamines and various cationic antibiotics through alterations in membrane potential and cell surface charge.
full_output.methodology: Experimental evolution, mutagenesis, and MIC testing were used to characterize the role of ktrA and ktrD in polyamine and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Gastric microbiota transplantation enhanced the eradication of refractory Helicobacter pylori infection by modulating the gastric microbiota: a pilot study.
full_output.key_findings: Gastric microbiota transplantation (GMT) significantly enhanced the eradication rate of refractory Helicobacter pylori infection and improved symptoms in patients with H. pylori-positive atrophic gastritis.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis and clinical evaluation of gastric microbiota composition and H. pylori eradication rates following GMT.
full_output.sample_size: 13 H. pylori-positive patients and 8 H. pylori-negative patients

full_output.paper_title: Functional interplay between RND efflux pumps and GacS in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

gacS.notes: Frame-shift deletion in gacS leads to inactivation of the regulatory system.
gacS.evidence_note: The paper describes a frame-shift deletion in the gacS gene in P. aeruginosa strains PAO1-89 and P1116, leading to the deactivation of the gacS gene.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a frame-shift deletion in the gacS gene, which leads to the inactivation of the GacS regulatory system in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. This inactivation affects virulence and gene expression, but does not alter antibiotic susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, RNA-seq, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to analyze the effects of gacS inactivation and efflux pump deletions.

full_output.paper_title: Clindamycin-resistant among Staphylococcus aureus: Investigation into phenotypic and genotypic profiles.

ermC.evidence_note: ermC gene was detected in 60% of S. aureus isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified ermC and msr genes as the primary genetic determinants of MLSB resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates, with ermC being the most prevalent.
full_output.methodology: Conventional PCR and D-test were used to detect MLSB resistance phenotypes and corresponding genetic markers.

full_output.paper_title: Dissecting pOXA-48 fitness effects in clinical Enterobacterales using plasmid-wide CRISPRi screens.

blaOXA-48.role_in_paper: main contributor to pOXA-48 fitness costs
blaOXA-48.validation_method: CRISPRi screens and plasmid stability assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaOXA-48 as the primary gene responsible for the fitness costs associated with the pOXA-48 plasmid in clinical Enterobacterales.
full_output.methodology: CRISPRi screens and plasmid stability assays were used to analyze the fitness effects of pOXA-48 genes in clinical strains of Enterobacterales.
full_output.sample_size: 13 clinical strains of K. pneumoniae and E. coli

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and molecular characterization of multidrug resistant Campylobacter isolated from animals and humans as a one health approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high prevalence of multidrug-resistant Campylobacter isolates, with 90.1% exhibiting resistance to three or more antibiotic classes. The hipO, ceuE, and cadF virulence genes were detected in 77.8%, 22.2%, and 33.3% of isolates, respectively.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based molecular characterization and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Establishing the reference broth microdilution MIC method for cefepime-taniborbactam.
full_output.key_findings: The study establishes a reference broth microdilution MIC method for cefepime-taniborbactam, focusing on quality control ranges for specific bacterial strains to ensure reliable susceptibility testing.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized broth microdilution MIC testing following CLSI M07 and ISO 20776-1:2019 standards, evaluating various parameters and bacterial isolates to determine optimal conditions for susceptibility testing.
full_output.sample_size: Nine laboratories participated in the M23 tier 2 study, with additional testing conducted in surveillance studies and clinical trials.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiological evidence for the trisubstituted benzimidazoles targeting MmpL3 in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

mmpL3.mechanism: Targeting MmpL3, a transporter required for trehalose monomycolate (TMM) transport and mycolic acid biosynthesis
mmpL3.role_in_paper: The study demonstrates that SBZ compounds target MmpL3 as the primary mechanism of action, showing phenotypic similarities to known MmpL3 inhibitors and confirming resistance through mutations in mmpL3.
mmpL3.validation_method: Bacterial cytological profiling, whole-cell profiling assays, and molecular docking studies
mmpL3.genetic_context: Mutations in mmpL3 (F255L, V646M, F644I, S591I) confer resistance to SBZ compounds
mmpL3.evidence_note: The paper provides strong evidence that SBZ compounds target MmpL3, including phenotypic similarity to known MmpL3 inhibitors, MIC shifts in strains with regulated mmpL3 expression, and molecular docking studies.

mutations_found.validated_by: MIC shift in strain with mmpL3 mutations
MIC shift in strain with mmpL3 mutations
MIC shift in strain with mmpL3 mutations
MIC shift in strain with mmpL3 mutations

mmpL3.notes: Mutations in mmpL3 confer resistance to SBZ compounds.

full_output.key_findings: SBZ compounds target MmpL3, as evidenced by phenotypic assays and MIC shifts in strains with mmpL3 mutations.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial cytological profiling, whole-cell phenotypic assays, and molecular docking studies were used to investigate the mechanism of action of SBZ compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Multiplexed bacteriocin synthesis to combat and prevent antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the successful synthesis of bacteriocin cocktails using cell-free expression, showing effectiveness against multidrug-resistant E. coli strains and preventing resistance development.
full_output.methodology: Cell-free expression of bacteriocins using the PARAGEN collection, followed by activity assays on bacterial lawns and in vivo testing in Galleria mellonella.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomics reveals fibre fermentation and AMR pathways in red grouse (Lagopus scotica) microbiota.

vanG.encodes: glycopeptide resistance gene cluster; Van ligase

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple vancomycin resistance genes, including vanW, vanG, vanT, vanY, vanXY, vanH, and others, in the caecal microbiota of red grouse. Additionally, a tetracycline resistance gene (adeF) and a metronidazole resistance gene (nimJ) were detected.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in the caecal microbiota of red grouse.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial isolates and antibiotic resistance in critically ill sepsis patients at a tertiary hospital in Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens among critically ill sepsis patients, including ESBL and carbapenemase-producing bacteria. High resistance rates were observed against third- and fourth-generation cephalosporins, meropenem, and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study used the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method for antimicrobial susceptibility testing and MASTDISCS® for detecting ESBL and carbapenemase production.

full_output.paper_title: Sub-inhibitory concentrations of oxacillin modulate biogenesis and function of extracellular vesicles secreted by oxacillin-sensitive methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that sub-inhibitory concentrations of oxacillin enhance the secretion of extracellular vesicles (EVs) from oxacillin-sensitive methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (OS-MRSA), leading to increased expression of proteins such as beta-lactamase (BlaZ) and penicillin-binding protein 2 (PBP2), which contribute to beta-lactam resistance.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis using LC-MS/MS, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and biochemical assays.

full_output.paper_title: Dual mechanism of the OXA-23 carbapenemase inhibition by the carbapenem NA-1-157.

blaOXA-23.evidence_note: The paper describes the interaction of NA-1-157 with OXA-23, a class D carbapenemase, and demonstrates that NA-1-157 inhibits OXA-23, leading to reduced MICs against A. baumannii strains producing OXA-23.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies OXA-23 as a major carbapenemase in Acinetobacter baumannii and demonstrates that NA-1-157 inhibits OXA-23, reducing the MICs of carbapenems against clinical isolates producing OXA-23.
full_output.methodology: Kinetic studies, structural studies, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to evaluate the interaction of NA-1-157 with OXA-23.
full_output.sample_size: 40 genotypically characterized MDR CHDL-producing A. baumannii clinical isolates

full_output.paper_title: Kerstersia gyiorum infection in a patient with chronic suppurative otitis media identified by whole genome sequencing: a case report.

AcrE.source: Annotation of resistance genes using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database 13 revealed the presence of several resistance genes in the Kerstersia gyiorum genome. Of these, 16 Perfect Hits were identified (mdtE, AcrE, emrB, emrR, evgA, emrY, marA, H-NS, mdtH, mdtG, msbA, Escherichia coli acrA, acrB, ampH, FosA7.5, and cpxA), including targeted resistance to several classes of drugs, including fluoroquinolones, cephalosporins, tetracyclines, macrolides, coumarin antibiotics, and rifamycins, as well as genes associated with multiple drug-resistant efflux pumps.

full_output.key_findings: The case report identifies Kerstersia gyiorum as the causative agent of chronic suppurative otitis media through whole genome sequencing. The isolate was susceptible to multiple antibiotics, but genomic analysis revealed several resistance genes associated with efflux pumps and resistance to fluoroquinolones, cephalosporins, tetracyclines, macrolides, coumarin antibiotics, and rifamycins.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify the bacterium and predict resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Enhanced antioxidant and anti-Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae activities of combined Piper sarmentosum and guava leaf extracts.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the combined in vitro effects of Piper sarmentosum extracts (PSE) and guava extracts (GE) against Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae (Mhp) and their antioxidant activities. PSE and GE exhibited anti-Mhp effects, with their 1:1 combination showing additive effects and reducing MIC to 0.195 mg/mL. The combination also enhanced antioxidant activity.
full_output.methodology: The study used HPLC for phytochemical profiling, MIC assays for anti-Mhp activity, and ABTS and FRAP assays for antioxidant capacity.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and preclinical efficacy evaluation of two lytic bacteriophages targeting highly virulent and multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two lytic bacteriophages, vB_KpnP_XY3 and vB_KpnP_XY4, effective against multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. These phages demonstrate broad temperature and pH tolerance, chloroform resistance, and potent lytic activity against MDR K. pneumoniae strains, significantly reducing bacterial load and inflammation in a murine pneumonia model.
full_output.methodology: Phages were isolated, characterized using plaque assays, TEM, and WGS. Antimicrobial susceptibility and resistance genes were analyzed via broth microdilution and PCR. In vivo efficacy was evaluated in a murine pneumonia model.

full_output.paper_title: mAChR4 suppresses liver disease via GAP-induced antimicrobial immunity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that mAChR4 plays a critical role in suppressing liver disease by inducing antimicrobial immunity through GAP formation. Activation of mAChR4 or IL6ST signaling enhances GAP formation, leading to improved antimicrobial defenses and reduced bacterial translocation to the liver.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of human biopsy analysis, mouse models, and various molecular and cellular techniques including RNA-seq, immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, and bacterial culture to investigate the role of mAChR4 in liver disease.
full_output.sample_size: 44 patients with AUD and 16 control individuals

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of metallo-β-lactamases in carbapenem resistant Gram negative bacilli by omeprazole and pantoprazole.
full_output.key_findings: Omeprazole and pantoprazole inhibit metallo-beta-lactamases (MBLs) and reduce meropenem MIC in carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria. They downregulate MBL genes bla NDM, bla IMP, and bla VIM.
full_output.methodology: PCR, qRT-PCR, MIC determination, and molecular docking studies.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro and in vivo selection and cost of bacteriophage resistance on natural Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies waaO, emrR, and DBZ19_04325 as genes involved in phage resistance in Escherichia coli, with their deletion leading to reduced phage sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: Genetic deletion mutants were constructed and tested for phage resistance through growth curves and streak-spot assays.

full_output.paper_title: Systematic Evaluation of Helicobacter pylori Susceptibility to Antibiotics Before First-Line Treatment: A Cohort Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports that 22.6% of H. pylori cases showed clarithromycin resistance and 18.6% showed levofloxacin resistance, highlighting the importance of susceptibility-guided therapy for effective treatment.
full_output.methodology: The study involved systematic antibiotic susceptibility testing of H. pylori using PCR and culture methods.

full_output.paper_title: Ethnobotanical survey and evaluation of antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and cytotoxic activities of traditional medicinal plants from Swat, Pakistan
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and cytotoxic activities of 17 traditional medicinal plants from Swat, Pakistan. Several plant extracts showed significant antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity against various pathogens, with some demonstrating potent inhibition of biofilm formation. The results highlight the potential of these plants as sources of natural antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: The study involved phytochemical screening, antimicrobial and antibiofilm assays, and cytotoxicity testing of plant extracts.

full_output.key_findings: Defects in energy metabolism increase the susceptibility of Staphylococcus aureus and its small colony variants (SCVs) to Staphylococcus lugdunensis and lugdunin. full_output.paper_title: Predominance of gram-negative multidrug-resistant pathogens causing lower respiratory tract infections among gene X-pert negative presumptive tuberculosis patients in Dar Es Salaam, Tanzania.

High resistance rates were observed to ampicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, and third-generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving sputum sample analysis, bacterial culture, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence factors are preserved within carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii clades.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the distribution of virulence factors (VFs) in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) isolates, revealing that most VFs are preserved across sequence types (STs) and clades, with sporadic VFs showing homogenous patterns within clades. Notably, the bap gene was present in all ST2 isolates but absent in ST3, while ST3 isolates carried a novel BAP-like gene, blp3.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and biofilm formation assays were used to analyze the distribution of virulence factors in CRAB isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiology of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Wales.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the genomic epidemiology of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Wales, identifying low levels of drug resistance and factors associated with genomic clustering. Key findings include the predominance of Lineage 4, low resistance rates to various antibiotics, and significant associations between genomic clustering and factors such as being UK-born and having pulmonary disease.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized whole genome sequencing (WGS) data combined with epidemiological and demographic data to analyze genomic clustering and drug resistance patterns in Mycobacterium tuberculosis cases in Wales.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and machine learning analysis were used to identify mutations and clinical factors associated with delayed sputum culture conversion in rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antimycobacterial and antiproliferative activities of (E)-N'-benzylidenepyrazine-2-carbohydrazides and their derivatives, focusing on compounds 18, 21, and 22. These compounds exhibited antimycobacterial activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and other mycobacterial strains, with varying degrees of cytotoxicity against human cancer cell lines. The compounds also displayed iron-chelating properties, which may contribute to their biological activities.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of compounds, antimicrobial and cytotoxicity assays, iron-chelating activity evaluation, and structural analysis via X-ray diffraction.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and Bioinformatic Insights Into Enterococcus faecalis From Retail Meats in Nigeria.

full_output.paper_title: Integrating serotyping, MLST, and phenotypic data: decoding the evolutionary drivers of Salmonella pathogenicity and drug resistance.

full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis using ABRicate and VFDB, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Bacillus cereus-derived α-amylase disrupts biofilm formation and quorum sensing in multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that B. cereus-derived α-amylase effectively disrupts biofilm formation and quorum sensing in multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae, reducing biofilm thickness and inhibiting the expression of biofilm-associated genes fimH and mrkD.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the anti-biofilm, antibacterial, and quorum-quenching activities of B. cereus-derived α-amylase using MBIC, MBEC, MIC, MBC, CLSM, and qRT-PCR assays.

full_output.paper_title: A Promising Antibacterial Inhibition of Propolis Extracts Against Carbapenem-Resistant Bacteria Isolated From Clinical Samples.

full_output.paper_title: A Pseudomonas aeruginosa endolytic muramidase targets cell-wall peptidoglycan in bacterial competition.
